review.summary: B keeps the three-phase timing and loudness but swaps A's detailed, rattly mechanical reload for a flat noise burst, two lone ticks, and a boomy sub thump with a sustained whistle tone. It reads more like an error or loading sound than a rifle reload.

differences.a: Gritty, metallic, clicky handling. Many small rattles, scrapes and taps with natural variation.
differences.b: Phase 1 is a uniform, static-like noise block. There are no discrete clicks, and it sounds like hiss or scratch rather than mag handling.

differences.a: 13 onsets. Mag release rattles (0.21-0.8s), a series of light insert clicks (1.09-1.5s) building to a snap, then a bolt slam at 2.1s.
differences.b: Only 5 onsets: a noise block, two isolated ticks at 0.83s and 1.4s, and the slam. The mag-insert phase is reduced to a single faint tick and the click series is missing.

differences.a: Bright and broadband, centroid 5.6 kHz, mid 35% and presence 34%, with bass under 1%.
differences.b: Bass is 58% of energy from a heavy 20-150 Hz thump. Phase 1 is very bright (centroid about 10 kHz) and the mid band is thin, so the centroid is 2.9 kHz overall and the balance is bimodal.

differences.a: Noisy with metallic partials (flatness 0.31) and only a faint 3 kHz line late in the tail.
differences.b: Flatness is 0.04. A steady sine-like tone at about 1.1 kHz runs from 2.5s to 3.3s, with a comb of regularly spaced high-frequency ticks above it. This is a synthetic whistle that A does not have.

differences.a: The slam drops 20 dB in 0.1s and 40 dB in 0.27s. Every event is sharp and dry, with a quiet tail.
differences.b: The slam decays 20 dB in 0.36s and 40 dB in 1.19s, with a sub-bass sustain to about 2.7s and then the held tone. It is much longer and boomier than A's tight slam.

differences.a: Instant, crack-like transients on each click, with a sharp snap at 1.4s and a full-spectrum slam crack at 2.1s.
differences.b: Phase 1 has a soft, fade-in/out block with no transient definition. The ticks are tiny and the slam is a thump-dominated hit with a weaker crack.

differences.a: Active fraction 0.23. Phases sit at 0.21-0.8s, 1.09-1.65s and 1.97-2.5s, with gaps near 0.9-1.05s and 1.65-1.95s, then a faint tail and 0.98s of silence.
differences.b: Active fraction 0.53 because the noise block and held tone fill time. Phase starts line up with A (0.21s, 1.4s, 2.1s), but the content of each phase differs, and the tail is filled with tone rather than near-silence.

differences.a: Quiet residual rattle and a faint high line, essentially dry.
differences.b: A loud, sustained tail (-30 dB envelope) from the tone and ticks until 3.3s, which is far more prominent than A's tail.

differences.a: -16.4 LUFS, peak +0.2 dBFS, crest 22.7 dB.
differences.b: -16.9 LUFS, peak -1.4 dBFS, crest 20.9 dB. This is well matched overall, but the energy is concentrated in sub bass instead of mids and presence.

differences.a: Mono.
differences.b: Mono.

differences.a: One-shot.
differences.b: One-shot.

missing_elements: Distinct rattle and click series for mag release and handling at 0.2-0.8s
Mag-insert click series building to a snap with a small thump at 1.1-1.5s
Short metallic ring at 8-10 kHz on the slam
Mid-frequency (0.5-5 kHz) body that dominates A's energy
Dry, tight slam decay with a quiet tail
extra_elements: Continuous noise block from 0.2 to 0.75s that reads as static
Heavy sub and bass thump (20-150 Hz) under the slam, sustained to about 2.7s
Steady 1.1 kHz tone from 2.5 to 3.3s
Regular comb of high-frequency ticks from 2.4 to 3.3s
change_notes: Delete the 1.1 kHz sustained tone and the regular tick comb after 2.4s. Replace with a very quiet residual rattle (-45 dB relative to the slam) fading out by 2.9s, then keep the last 0.4s silent.

Replace the 0.21-0.75s noise block with 8-10 irregular clicks. Each is a 3-10 ms noise burst, bandpassed 1.5-6 kHz with a 300-900 Hz resonant body, spaced 30-120 ms, with amplitudes varying 6-12 dB. Put stronger taps at 0.30s and 0.52s (about -12 dB).

Build the mag-insert phase at 1.09-1.5s from 5-6 light clicks (-20 to -25 dB) leading to a louder snap at 1.4s. The snap is a 10 ms noise crack at 2-6 kHz plus a 150-300 Hz thump of 40 ms, 12 dB above the clicks.
Shorten and brighten the slam at 2.1s. Cut the sub thump: high-pass at 120 Hz, or cap the pitch drop at 220 Hz down to 120 Hz over 60 ms. Reduce its level so bass is under 10% of energy.

Add to the slam a 2-5 ms broadband crack, a 200-500 Hz body of 60-80 ms, and a short 8-10 kHz metallic ring of 80-100 ms. Set the decay to -20 dB at 0.1s and -40 dB at 0.3s, using an exponential envelope with a time constant of about 40 ms.
Add a bit of noise or granular texture to every hit by mixing in 10-15% bandpassed noise (1-8 kHz) so spectral flatness rises toward 0.25-0.3 and the centroid toward 5 kHz.
Keep the current timing anchors (0.21s, 1.4s, 2.1s), loudness near -16.5 LUFS and peak at or below -1 dBFS, and keep the output mono.

review.summary: B has the right length and loudness, but it is two separate events with a ~0.1 s dead gap in the middle. A is a continuous clanky rattle that builds to a heavy hinge thud, then a decaying scrape. B's front half is a tonal beep-and-hum latch, which reads more like a synth than a metal door, and its back half is a thin, dull rumble.

differences.a: Continuous sequence: latch rattle at 0.05 s, smaller knock at 0.13 s, then a heavy hinge/door body at 0.24-0.42 s with a click near 0.4 s, then a settling scrape.
differences.b: Two blocks: a noise burst plus a pure-tone ping at ~1 kHz (0.05-0.13 s), then a 150-250 Hz sine-like thump (0.13-0.31 s). After a gap, a click at 0.40 s and a low rumble.

differences.a: Energy builds through 0.05-0.25 s and peaks at 0.25 s. The tail is active until ~0.75 s, so the overall shape is a crescendo to the main hit.
differences.b: Loudest at 0.05-0.15 s, then a hard cutoff at ~0.31 s followed by ~0.1 s of true silence (-100 dB). The second event is quieter and starts at 0.40 s. The shape is front-loaded and fragmented.

differences.a: Noisy and semi-tonal (flatness 0.15), with dotted metallic resonance at 200-1000 Hz and only broad ringing.
differences.b: Contains clean, stationary sine lines at ~1.0 kHz, 1.2 kHz and 1.46 kHz, plus ~4 kHz and ~9 kHz, and a smooth sine-like sweep at 150-250 Hz (flatness 0.06). It sounds like a synth beep or tone, not a metal rattle.

differences.a: Centroid ~2.1 kHz, mid 38%, low-mid 29%, bass 13%, presence 15%. The bursts are bright to the top of the spectrum.
differences.b: Centroid ~1.1 kHz, rolloff 1.2 kHz. Bass 37% and low-mid 45%, with mid only 10% and presence 4%. This is dull, with no sizzle or bite.

differences.a: Soft-to-moderate rattle onsets build to a peak with a bright click at ~0.4 s. The crest factor is 23 dB, so it is spiky and clanky.
differences.b: The opening is a sustained noise block with a flat envelope, so there is no sharp click. The thump starts abruptly. The only true click is at 0.40 s. Crest factor is 17.8 dB.

differences.a: Gradual decay after 0.25 s, with -20 dB at +0.25 s and -40 dB at +0.49 s, a natural scrape-and-settle tail.
differences.b: The thump decays fast and is cut at 0.31 s. The second part decays over ~0.4 s with a bumpy low rumble. There is a faint high-frequency hiss tail.

differences.a: Peak -0.3 dBFS, -20.3 LUFS, peak in the middle (0.25 s).
differences.b: Peak -2.6 dBFS, -20.4 LUFS. The peak is at 0.13 s and the main loud part is early. This is the right integrated level, but the peak is below the -1 dBFS target.

differences.a: No pitch movement; resonances stay static.
differences.b: The 150-250 Hz thump glides down from ~300 Hz to ~150 Hz, which sounds like a tonal drone or boom.

differences.a: Dry, with a short natural scrape tail and a faint residual to 0.75 s.
differences.b: Dry, with a rumble tail to ~0.8 s and a faint sizzle after it. Roughly similar.

missing_elements: Second small metallic knock (~3-4 kHz) at 0.13 s inside a continuous rattle
Heavy hinge/door-body hit at ~0.25 s as the peak, with broadband resonant ringing at 150-800 Hz
Continuous scrape/creak bridging the events
Bright high-frequency content (2-8 kHz) across the body and tail
Noisy, inharmonic metal texture
extra_elements: Pure sine tones at ~1.0-1.5 kHz and harmonics at ~4 kHz and ~9 kHz
Smooth sine-like 150-300 Hz boom
About 0.1 s of digital silence at 0.31-0.40 s
Flat-topped noise block at 0.05-0.13 s
change_notes: Remove the dead gap: start the second event no later than 0.24 s and overlap it with the tail of the first. Fill 0.30-0.40 s with a decaying scrape (band-passed noise at 400-1500 Hz, -30 dB).

Reorder the energy so it builds: latch rattle at 0.05 s at about -14 dB relative to peak, knock at 0.13 s at -8 dB, main hinge hit at 0.24 s at 0 dB (peak -1 dBFS). Currently the loudest part is at 0.05-0.15 s.

Delete or heavily detune the static sine pings (1.0, 1.2, 1.46, 4, 9 kHz). Replace them with inharmonic metallic resonance: 4-6 detuned bandpass resonators at 220, 410, 680, 970, 1500 and 4200 Hz (Q 15-30) excited by 5-10 ms noise bursts, with 80-150 ms decays.
Rebuild the 0.05-0.12 s rattle as 3-4 rapid clicks (2-3 ms noise bursts, 8-15 ms apart, highpassed above 2 kHz), not a continuous noise block. Add a 1-2 ms click for a sharper crest factor (~22 dB).

Replace the 150-250 Hz sine boom with a short door-body thunk: noise plus a 120-200 Hz damped resonator, 120 ms decay, no downward glide. Keep it 6-8 dB below the mid content, since bass is currently 37% against A's 13%.
Raise the high end: add 2-8 kHz noise sizzle on each transient (20-40 ms) to bring presence to ~15% and mid to ~35-40%. Target centroid around 1.8-2.2 kHz, with rolloff ~4 kHz rather than 1.2 kHz.

Add the click at ~0.40 s as a bright 2-6 kHz tick (10 ms, -10 dB relative to the main hit). Follow it with a 0.3 s scrape and rumble tail that decays to -40 dB by ~0.75 s, centroid falling to ~700 Hz.
Normalise to peak -1 dBFS and keep ~-20.3 LUFS. Keep mono and 44.1 kHz. Add small random pitch/timing variants (±5%) for repeat opens.

review.summary: B hits the loudness (-12.9 vs -12.5 LUFS) and bass-heavy feel, but its structure is wrong. It has two separate blasts split by a gap at 0.5 s, then a long hole, then an unwanted steady noise bed from 2.0 to 2.95 s. A is a single splat with a thump, a squelchy body and sparse wet pops that die out by about 1.9 s.

differences.a: One continuous impact: a sub/bass thump with a dense noisy splat on top, then a squelchy body, then sparse wet pops.
differences.b: Two distinct hits (0-0.5 s and 0.5-1.0 s) separated by a hard dropout, followed by a steady noise bed at 2.0-2.95 s. It reads as a stitched sequence, not one gore burst.

differences.a: Falls to near silence after about 1.9 s, with about 1.1 s of trailing silence. The low block cuts off at 1.9 s and only faint specks remain.
differences.b: Has a quiet gap at about 1.2-1.9 s, then a flat, constant-level noise block from 2.0 s to about 2.95 s at roughly -25 dB. This is the opposite of A's quiet ending and reads as an artifact or hiss.

differences.a: Fast, ragged, clipped attack peaking at 0.22 s, with random crackly transients inside the splat.
differences.b: Starts at about -23 dB in the first tenth, then reaches its peak at 0.25 s. The second hit at 0.5 s is a re-trigger with a clean, smooth, synthetic onset and no crackle.

differences.a: Very noise-like and wet (flatness 0.012), with an irregular squelchy texture.
differences.b: Flatter and more uniform (0.075), with a constant hiss-like texture and a smooth, tonal sub swell at 0.5-0.9 s. It reads as synthetic or machine-like, not organic. Qwen even heard a machine gun.

differences.a: Steady decay: -20 dB at 0.54 s and -40 dB at 1.11 s, with a stuttering tail of pops to about 1.9 s.
differences.b: Slower decay (-20 dB at 0.68 s, -40 dB at 1.31 s) with no pulsing pops. The envelope then rises again at 2.0 s (-25 dB), so the shape is non-monotonic.

differences.a: Sub 25% and bass 43%. Sub energy is strong, with a block of low energy up to about 150 Hz that holds until 1.9 s.
differences.b: Sub only 0.9%, bass 57%, mid 20%. It lacks the 20-60 Hz thump and is more midrange-heavy. The low swell is centred around 100-250 Hz and drops pitch slowly between 0.5 and 1 s.

differences.a: About 1.9 s of active sound in a 2.99 s file, front-loaded.
differences.b: About 0.73 active fraction, with sound spread over the whole file and energy at the very end. The timing feels longer and more diffuse.

differences.a: Peaks at +4.8 dBTP with 681 clipped samples, -12.5 LUFS.
differences.b: Peak -1.1 dBFS with no clipping, -12.9 LUFS. This is within the target and arguably better.

differences.a: Static, with no deliberate pitch movement.
differences.b: Has a visible downward sweep in the low swell at 0.5-0.9 s (about 250 Hz to 100 Hz), which A lacks.

missing_elements: Sparse wet pops/drips at about 0.95-1.75 s, spaced about 80-100 ms apart
Deep 20-60 Hz sub thump
Abrupt low-end cutoff at about 1.9 s followed by a near-silent tail
Irregular crackly, squelchy broadband noise body
extra_elements: Second re-triggered hit at 0.5 s with a downward-sweeping low swell
Steady noise bed from 2.0 to 2.95 s
Dropout/gap at 0.48-0.5 s between the two hits
Smooth, synthetic tonal low swell
change_notes: Delete the 2.0-2.95 s noise block. Fade everything to below -60 dB by about 2.0 s, leaving about 1 s of silence or a very faint (-70 dB) tail like A.
Merge the two hits into one. Remove the gap at 0.5 s and the re-trigger. Make a single impact peaking at about 0.2 s, with the body decaying continuously.

Add a sub thump layer: sine at 45-60 Hz, with a quick drop from about 120 Hz to 50 Hz over 150 ms. Run it 0-0.4 s at about the level of the current bass, then lower it with a slow tail out to 1.8 s, to bring sub energy to about 20-25%.

Make the splat layer wet and crackly: band-passed noise at 0.5-4 kHz, amplitude-modulated with random 5-20 ms grains or a lowpass-filtered crackle. Keep it loud 0-0.5 s, with -20 dB at about 0.55 s and -40 dB at about 1.1 s.

Add 8-10 wet pops from 0.95 to 1.8 s, 80-100 ms apart (onsets about 0.95, 1.05, 1.13, 1.34, 1.42, 1.5, 1.58, 1.66, 1.75). Make each a 10-25 ms burst of 300-1500 Hz noise with a quick pitch-down chirp, at -30 to -40 dB below the peak and decreasing over time.
Hold a low rumble (40-150 Hz) at about -30 dB from 0.6 to 1.9 s and cut it sharply (about 10 ms) at 1.9 s.
Keep the peak at or below -1 dBFS and LUFS around -12.5. A's clipping isn't needed, so use soft saturation for a harsh edge instead. Keep it mono.

review.summary: B matches A's overall length (2.09 s), loudness (-22.4 vs -22.3 LUFS), peak position (0.95 s) and multi-event layout, but its events are too pure and tonal, pinging with sinusoidal resonances instead of rattly metal clacks. B also has a loud 0.35-0.7 s noise swath, a bass-heavy mag-seat boom and thin, tick-like bolt events.

differences.a: Noisy, broadband metal and plastic clacks with speckled harmonics at 1-4 kHz; flatness 0.004, so reads as resonant clatter rather than synthetic tones.
differences.b: Mag-seat and bolt events carry clean, sustained sine-like pings (about 1 kHz fundamental with harmonic lines up to 10 kHz) that sound like beeps or plucked notes. Flatness 0.265. The 0.35-0.7 s event is plain white-ish noise.

differences.a: The first 0.27 s is a soft click followed by a stronger clack, then a diffuse low-mid rattle-scrape at 0.36-0.72 s with weak clicks on top.
differences.b: The opening has 4-5 very short, thin ticks (0.05, 0.13, 0.25 s and so on) that read as clicks of equal weight. The scrape is a dense, flat noise burst with a hard onset at 0.35 s and no rattle texture.

differences.a: Almost no bass (0.1%). Energy is mid-dominant (41%), with presence 26% and air 24%. Centroid about 5.2 kHz.
differences.b: Bass 17% from a 100-300 Hz boom at about 0.95 s. Presence is lower (16%). Centroid about 4 kHz, with extreme swings between quarters (9.3k, 4.2k, 5.7k, 9.9k).

differences.a: Each hit is dry and fast, about 0.06 s to -20 dB and 0.13 s to -40 dB. There is a small low-mid thunk on the seat but no ringing tail.
differences.b: The mag-seat pings and the low boom ring on for 0.2-0.3 s (boom to about 1.1 s), and the bolt ping at 1.57 s sustains. The result is slower, more resonant and sounds reverberant, not dry.

differences.a: Rattly clack transients with soft pre-clicks (about 0.82 s before the 0.91-0.95 s seat).
differences.b: Hard, thin click transients with a pre-hit at 0.81 s and seat at 0.91 s. The seat is also a double hit (two pinged strikes close together), which sounds like a doubled note rather than a single seat.

differences.a: The bolt section is a cluster of sharp clicks (1.49, 1.57 s), a quiet tick at 1.7 s, then a louder broad clatter at 1.82-1.98 s that is the second-biggest event.
differences.b: The bolt section is sparse. A ping at about 1.5-1.6 s, then isolated narrow ticks at 1.67, 1.81 and 1.97 s with a pitched ring on the last. The 1.8-2.0 s clatter lacks body and width.

differences.a: Gaps at 0.27-0.36 s and 1.15-1.49 s. Events start at 0.01 s.
differences.b: Overall timing is close. The gap at 1.15-1.49 s matches, but the first gap is not clear because the tick train runs through it. The scrape starts at 0.35 s and ends at about 0.72 s, as in A.

differences.a: -25.2 dBFS RMS, peak -3.0, -22.3 LUFS. The seat is the loudest event.
differences.b: -25.4 dBFS RMS, peak -2.4, -22.4 LUFS. The seat is the loudest, but the scrape is relatively louder than A's, so the balance differs.

differences.a: Mono.
differences.b: Mono.

missing_elements: Rattly, noisy metal-on-metal clack texture on each hit
A soft pre-click and a single punchy seat clack with a short low-mid thunk
A diffuse, clicky rattle-scrape with modulated, speckled texture at 200-1000 Hz
A broad bolt-forward clatter at 1.82-1.98 s
A cluster of sharp ratchet clicks on the bolt pull
extra_elements: Pitched sine pings with harmonic lines (about 1 kHz fundamental, up to 10 kHz)
A 100-300 Hz sub-boom decaying over about 0.2 s after the mag seat
Extra thin ticks in the opening (0.25, 0.35, 0.44, 0.52 s)
Ringing pitched tail on the final tick near 2.0 s
change_notes: Replace the pinged mag-seat (0.91-0.95 s) with a single dry clack: 1.5-4 kHz band-passed noise burst plus a damped 1.2 kHz resonator (Q about 3), 60 ms total, -20 dB at 0.06 s and -40 dB at 0.13 s, with a soft pre-click at 0.82 s about 10 dB lower.

Remove or heavily damp the pure sine/ping layers (the 1 kHz and harmonics up to 10 kHz). If any resonance remains, use 3-4 inharmonic modes, each with a decay under 40 ms and -20 dB or lower, so flatness stays under about 0.05.
Cut the 100-300 Hz boom from about 17% bass to under 2%. Keep only a short thunk of 150-400 Hz, 30 ms, about -12 dB below the clack, with no ring past 0.1 s.

Rebuild the 0.36-0.72 s scrape as rattle: band-limit the noise to 200-1000 Hz, amplitude-modulate it with 15-30 random micro-clicks, soften the onset over 20 ms, and drop it about 6 dB so it sits below the seat by 8 dB or more.

Simplify the opening to two events: a soft click at 0.05 s (about -12 dB) and a stronger metallic clack at 0.13 s with a 60 ms rattly decay. Remove the ticks at 0.25 s and 0.35-0.52 s so the 0.27-0.36 s gap stays silent.
Add presence and air to the clacks: boost 4-8 kHz by about 4 dB on the transients, and raise the centroid from about 4 kHz to about 5 kHz. Avoid 9-10 kHz swings between sections.
Bolt pull (1.49 and 1.57 s): two sharp 3-6 kHz noise clicks of 10-15 ms each with a 50 ms clacky tail, 3-4 dB below the seat. Remove the sustained 1 kHz ping at 1.5-1.6 s.

Bolt release (1.82-1.98 s): replace the thin ticks with a broad 80-120 ms clatter of 1-6 kHz noise with 4-6 sub-clicks, peaking about -6 dB below the seat. Add a tiny tick at 1.7 s about -20 dB and a final small tick near 2.03 s with no pitched ring.
Keep the total length at 2.09 s, with a silent gap at 1.15-1.49 s. Keep the peak at 0.95 s at about -3 dBFS and the loudness at about -22.3 LUFS.

review.summary: B is the same length (2.99 s) and similar integrated loudness, but it is a sparse, synthetic series of isolated events separated by near-silent gaps, with long sustained tonal drones in the second half. A is a dense, continuous, gritty handling sequence with a short rising whine only at the very end, so B does not read as a busy mechanical reload.

differences.a: Dense mechanical handling: a loud clack at 0.05 s, a double heavy clack at 0.68/0.75 s, a single latch clack at 1.35 s, rattles and clicks at 1.8/1.89/1.98 s, and a snap pair at 2.43/2.52 s. Rattle fills the gaps.
differences.b: A 0.25 s white-noise burst opens it, followed by a low thump, a few isolated pings and ticks, and long tonal drones. Almost no handling or rattle texture.

differences.a: Mostly noisy, gritty broadband metal (flatness 0.29), with tonal content only in the final whine.
differences.b: Flatness 0.58 with a hiss-heavy opening, plus pure sine-like tones at about 1 kHz and 2.2 kHz from 1.5 to 2.4 s. The tones are loud and sustained and sound like an alarm or synth drone, not a reload.

differences.a: Continuous activity, active fraction 0.9. Loudness stays within about 10 dB from 0 to 2.5 s, and every hit decays in 50-100 ms over a low rattle bed.
differences.b: Gated, with deep silence of -85 to -91 dB from about 0.3 to 0.6 s and 0.8 to 1.0 s. Events are islands and the tone blocks are flat rectangular sustains with abrupt cutoffs at 2.4 s.

differences.a: Many sharp, bright clacks with broadband snaps and low-mid bodies. The loudest are at 0.74 s, with a peak near 0 dBFS.
differences.b: The loudest part is the sustained noise burst at 0-0.25 s, a soft swell and not a crisp clack. The later ticks and pings are thin, very quiet and pure-tonal. There is no heavy double clack at 0.7 s.

differences.a: A thin rising whine at about 2.6-3.0 s, sweeping from about 1 kHz to 5 kHz or higher, with a faint hint from 2.1 s.
differences.b: The tones glide only slightly (about 1 kHz to 1.1 kHz) and then drop to about 750 Hz at 2.45 s before a gentle rise. Their long duration (about 0.9 s plus about 0.6 s) is wrong, and there is no clear rising charge-up sweep.

differences.a: Centroid about 5.8 kHz, mid/presence dominant with 24.7% air, and low-mid thuds at 150-300 Hz in the middle.
differences.b: Centroid about 7.9 kHz with 47% air energy, which makes it hissy. The tonal sections drop to a centroid of about 1.3-1.5 kHz, so brightness swings between extremes. Only two soft 200 Hz thumps at about 1.75 and 1.95 s.

differences.a: -20.1 LUFS, peak +0.3 dBFS with clipping.
differences.b: -20.6 LUFS, peak -3.7 dBFS. Level matches and is cleaner, but it is driven by the noise burst and the tone drones instead of transient peaks, so crest is lower (18.2 vs 22.5 dB).

differences.a: Events spread across the whole 3 s, with the loudest at 0.74 s and the final snaps at 2.43/2.52 s.
differences.b: Same total length, but the event placement differs. The first big event is a 0.25 s noise burst, and there is a dead zone from 0.9 to 1.3 s with only tiny ticks.

differences.a: Very little tail. Short reverb on the early clacks, then the whine fades out by 3.0 s.
differences.b: The ends of the pings ring with a clean tonal decay, and the final tone holds at nearly full level to the file end with no fade.

differences.a: Mono.
differences.b: Mono.

differences.a: One-shot.
differences.b: One-shot.

Heavy double clack at about 0.68/0.75 s with a low-mid body
Single bright latch clack at about 1.35 s

extra_elements: 0.25 s white-noise burst at the start

Held tone at about 750 Hz to 1.1 kHz from 2.45 s to the end
Pure-tone pings with harmonic stacks at 0.7-0.9 s and 1.35 s
Deep silent gaps (-85 to -91 dB)
change_notes: Delete the 0-0.25 s white-noise burst and the 1.5-2.4 s and 2.45-3.0 s drones. Replace them with percussive handling hits.
Make a heavy clack at 0.05 s: a 1-8 kHz noise crack of 10-15 ms plus a damped metal resonance at 2-3 kHz with a 60-80 ms decay, plus 3-4 small clicks at 0.12-0.3 s that are 10-15 dB quieter.
Make a double heavy clack at 0.68 s and 0.75 s, the loudest events at about -3 dBFS peak. Each is a 2-4 kHz noise crack of 15 ms plus a 200-400 Hz thunk of 80 ms, and the second is 2 dB louder.
Add a single bright latch clack at 1.35 s: 15 ms transient, ring at 3-4 kHz, 100 ms decay, at about -4 dBFS.

Add a continuous rattle bed from 0.3 to 2.4 s: band-passed noise at 1-6 kHz with random 20-60 ms grains, level -30 to -35 dB, so no gap drops below about -45 dB. Fill the dead zones at 0.3-0.6 s and 0.8-1.3 s with it.
Add 150-300 Hz thuds at 0.37 s, 1.55 s, 1.75 s and 1.95 s, each 100-150 ms with an exponential decay and a pitch drop from 300 Hz to 120 Hz.
Add click clusters at 1.80, 1.89 and 1.98 s (5-10 ms clicks at 2-6 kHz, plus ring) and a snap pair at 2.43 and 2.52 s, 3-5 dB above the rattle bed.

Rebuild the ending as a rising charge whine from 2.55 to 3.0 s: a sine or thin saw sweeping 1 kHz to 5 kHz, with a faint second line an octave up. Fade in over 100 ms, then fade out so it ends by about -50 dB at 2.99 s. Keep it 15-20 dB below the clacks.

review.summary: B matches A's length (1.21 s), loudness (-17.2 vs -16.9 LUFS) and low-end weight, but its envelope is wrong. It opens with a short tonal blip, drops into a near-gap, then builds to a late peak at 0.48 s and cuts off abruptly at about 0.5 s. A is a dense rumble that peaks at about 0.1-0.3 s and decays smoothly, so B reads as a different, segmented event instead of a steam-thrust burst.

differences.a: Fast noisy thump that rises to its peak by about 0.1 s, with a second surge near 0.3 s. The loudest region is 0.05-0.5 s.
differences.b: Starts with a pitched blip at 0-0.1 s (-11 dB), then a deep dip to -33 dB at 0.1-0.2 s. The true peak comes late, at 0.48 s, so the attack is backwards compared with A.

differences.a: Sustains high until about 0.45 s, then decays smoothly: -20 dB at 0.63 s, -40 dB at 1.03 s. Active fraction 0.86.
differences.b: Builds to 0.5 s, then drops about 16 dB abruptly, with a hard edge at 0.5 s. It reaches -20 dB by 0.1 s and -40 dB by 0.52 s, with a low-level wash afterward. Active fraction 0.69, with 0.14 s of trailing silence. The shape is gap-then-swell-then-cliff rather than burst-then-decay.

differences.a: No audible pitch. It is a noise-like rumble with no discrete peaks.
differences.b: A clear tonal glide at about 500 Hz falling to about 250 Hz over 0-0.15 s, then holding near 250 Hz until about 0.17 s. This reads as an electronic blip or zap that A does not have.

differences.a: Sub-heavy: 53% sub and 26% bass, centroid about 257 Hz, with grit and speckle up to 5-10 kHz in the first half.
differences.b: Bass-heavy: 17% sub and 72% bass, centroid 155 Hz, with a very dark top end. Less sub weight, and almost no mid or presence content (1.5% mid, 0.2% presence). The 0.5-1.0 s section has a steady noise band that makes the centroid jump to over 2 kHz in the last half.

differences.a: Dense, churning, chuffing noise with fast amplitude pulsing, which gives the steam texture.
differences.b: Low tonal and pulsed content at 0.2-0.5 s, with a distinct hard band edge at 0.5 s and a thin hiss from 0.5 to 1.0 s. The rhythmic pulses are slower and more discrete than A's churn, and they build instead of staying constant.

differences.a: Continuous rumbling decay that fades gradually into a quiet low tail.
differences.b: Tail is thin and quiet after the 0.5 s cutoff, then abruptly gated off at about 1.01 s, which is audible as a cutoff. The 0.5-1.0 s part is about 20-30 dB below the peak.

differences.a: Peaks at +3.8 dBFS with 87 clipped samples. RMS -13 dB, high sustained energy.
differences.b: Peak -1.7 dBFS, RMS -17.4 dB, no clipping. Integrated loudness matches, but energy is concentrated at 0.3-0.5 s instead of spread over 0.05-0.6 s. The tail is much quieter.

differences.a: Single dense noise-and-rumble mass, with no separate blip or gap.
differences.b: Three separate segments: a tonal blip, a gap, and a pulsed swell. Onsets at 0.16, 0.25 and 0.48 s are different from A's onsets at 0.05 and 0.3 s.

Add steam-hiss grit: band-passed noise at 1-5 kHz, level about -25 dB below the body, 0-0.5 s, then a low-pass sweep from 5 kHz down to 1 kHz over 0.5-1.0 s. This restores the mid and high speckle.
Replace the gate at 1.0 s with a smooth fade: a 150-200 ms fade-out to silence by about 1.15 s, with a 0.06 s silent tail. Keep the 1.21 s length.

review.summary: B matches A's length, loudness and opening noise burst, but it behaves like a sustained, tonal sub-bass drone with a second re-trigger at 0.3 s, not a short punchy impact with a thin tail. Energy is concentrated at 20-200 Hz for about 0.6 s, so it reads as a hum or energy-weapon pulse more than a bullet hit.

differences.a: Fast decay: -20 dB by 0.12 s after the peak, -40 dB by about 0.5 s. The body is mostly gone by 0.35 s, followed by a very quiet thin tail.
differences.b: Slow decay: -20 dB at 0.36 s, with a flat 80-200 Hz plateau held to about 0.62 s and then cut off abruptly. It sounds like a sustained drone, not a hit.

differences.a: Broadband: sub 16%, bass 22%, low-mid 29%, mid 22%, presence 9%. Centroid is about 1.3 kHz and rolloff about 2.3 kHz.
differences.b: Bass is 82% and sub is only 2%, with rolloff at 258 Hz. The low-mid and mid bands are nearly empty, so the body lacks the crunchy 300-2000 Hz content. The centroid is similar only because of the early hiss.

differences.a: Main layers are a noisy burst, double low thumps at about 0.08-0.12 s and 0.17-0.3 s, a falling 400-250 Hz mid sweep, and a faint steady 800 Hz ring.
differences.b: Main layers are a 0.06-0.25 s noise burst, a continuous 80-200 Hz tone-like block, a second bass onset at 0.3 s, and a 1.2 kHz tone that falls slightly (about 1.3 to 1.0 kHz) from 0.27 to 0.5 s. There is no mid sweep, and the ring is higher and louder.

differences.a: Very quiet pre-tick at 0-0.05 s, then a sudden gritty burst. One detected onset at 0.05 s, with two thump pulses inside the burst.
differences.b: Onset at 0.05 s is similar, but a hard second onset at 0.3 s adds a re-trigger that sounds like a separate hit. There is no pre-tick, only a dark gap before 0.06 s.

differences.a: Thin, quiet tail of faint 800 Hz ring and sparse noise, fading to silence by about 0.9 s, with about 0.3 s of near-silence at the end.
differences.b: Hard cutoff at about 0.5-0.62 s, with a visible vertical edge on the spectrogram. After it there is only faint broadband hiss, with 0.25 s of silence at the end.

differences.a: Noisy and gritty (flatness 0.19). The tone is limited to a thin ring, and the thumps are noisy.
differences.b: Low band is smooth and periodic, visible as pulsing LF waveform cycles (flatness 0.069). It sounds like a sine or sub hum instead of a noisy thud.

differences.a: Faint falling mid sweep (about 400 to 250 Hz) and a steady 800 Hz ring. Thumps have no clear pitch.
differences.b: Ring sits at about 1.2 kHz and falls slightly. The bass is static, with no downward pitch drop.

differences.a: Peak +0.4 dBFS (clipped), RMS -20.2 dB, -19.0 LUFS, crest 20.6 dB.
differences.b: Peak -3.6 dBFS, RMS -19.4 dB, -19.5 LUFS, crest 15.8 dB. Overall loudness matches, but the energy is spread over a longer time, so it feels heavier and less punchy.

review.summary: B matches A's length and loudness but is a sustained, bass-heavy drone with a constant ~1 kHz sine whistle, not a short crunchy bullet hit with a fast-decaying tail. Its role as an impact is weakened: the hit is smeared, the tail is too long and tonal, and the spectral balance is wrong.

differences.a: Peaks around 0.12 s, falls about 20 dB by 0.25 s and 40 dB by about 0.5 s, then a very quiet tail. Envelope by tenth: -14, -15, -29, -38, -43, -47 dB.
differences.b: Stays near -15 dB for 0.4 s, then sits at a flat plateau around -33 dB from 0.5 s to 0.95 s and cuts off abruptly. -20 dB is reached at 0.39 s and -40 dB at 0.73 s. It sounds like a sustained drone, not a hit.

differences.a: Broad spread: sub 16%, bass 22%, low-mid 29%, mid 22%, presence 9%. Centroid about 1.3 kHz, rolloff 2.3 kHz.
differences.b: Bass is 80% of energy, with low-mid and mid at 3-4% each. The rolloff is 323 Hz, so it is boomy and muffled, with no body in the 300 Hz-2 kHz range.

differences.a: Mostly noisy, crunchy debris, flatness 0.19. The tone is only a faint ~800 Hz line late in the sound.
differences.b: Flatness 0.055 with strong steady sine lines at ~1 kHz and ~2 kHz, plus faint high pings at ~4.5, 9 and 12 kHz. It reads as an electronic whistle or UI tone instead of a physical impact.

differences.a: Low thud fades by 0.4 s. A very faint ring near 800 Hz sags slightly to 0.9 s and is far below the body. The last 0.3 s is silent.
differences.b: The ~1 kHz tone and a 100-200 Hz hum run at a high level to 0.95 s, then stop abruptly (a hard cut at 0.57 s on the low band, a click at ~0.57 s, and a cutoff at 0.95 s). The tail is loud and static, not a quiet fade.

differences.a: Near-instant noisy onset at 0.05 s with a crack and debris. Peak 0.4 dBFS, crest 20.6 dB.
differences.b: Onset at ~0.06 s but the low end builds into a wall. Peak -5.4 dBFS, crest 15 dB. Less snap and no distinct crack.

differences.a: Two or three discrete bass thump pulses (~0.08-0.12 s, ~0.18-0.25 s and ~0.3 s), a noise crunch up to 6 kHz+, and a faint metallic ring.
differences.b: A continuous low rumble, a noise burst lasting 0.06-0.28 s, and sustained sine tones. There are no clearly separated thump pulses.

differences.b: Tone fixed at ~1055 Hz with an overtone at ~2.1 kHz and a 1120-1486 Hz partial. Bass hum ~100-200 Hz. The ring is higher and does not sag.

Remove the 2 kHz and 4.5/9/12 kHz partials, or put them at -50 dB or lower.

Add a 2-6 kHz noise crack of 10-15 ms at 0.05 s, +6 dB over the body, with a 6 kHz high shelf of about -6 dB afterwards to keep the air band near 2%. This should raise the crest factor toward 20 dB.
Raise the peak to about -1 dBFS using a short limiter on the transient, and then trim the body so that integrated loudness stays around -19 LUFS.
Remove the click at 0.57 s and the cut-off at 0.95 s by fading all layers with at least a 20 ms fade-out. Make 2-3 variants by randomising the thump timing by ±10 ms and the ring pitch by ±5%.

review.summary: B matches A's length (2.97 s), loudness (-25.9 vs -25.4 LUFS) and rough event layout (clicks at 0.34/0.6 s, big hit at 1.4 s, whirr to 2.2 s). It reads as clean, tonal and gappy where A is a continuous, rumbly, noisy mechanical handling sound, and the 1 kHz whirr is a pure steady tone.

differences.a: Continuous low mechanical handling rumble and scuffs with small bumps from 0 to 1.3 s, so there are no true gaps. The sound is 93% active.
differences.b: Isolated short blips separated by near-silent gaps (about -75 dB) at 0.25-0.34, 0.5-0.6 and 1.3-1.4 s. Only 68% active, so it sounds like discrete beeps rather than handling.

differences.a: Mostly broadband noise and granular texture. Flatness is low only because of the strong bass.
differences.b: Pitched sine-like blips (1 kHz harmonics, 250 Hz sweeps) and a steady 1 kHz sine whine during the whirr. The result is beepy and reads like an error or notification tone.

differences.a: Sharp broadband clicks at 0.34 and 0.6 s, with vertical strokes up to 15 kHz over a thumpy body. A loud bright clack at about 1.4 s. Peak -4.5 dBFS.
differences.b: The early clicks are soft tonal pings with a decaying 300 Hz sweep and no broadband snap. The 1.4 s hit is a low thump with a few tonal partials and is the loudest event (peak -8.4 dBFS). The clack is not bright and noisy.

differences.a: Sub and bass about 60% of energy (14.6% sub, 45.1% bass), with 11% air from the clicks. Centroid swings 240 Hz to 2 kHz.
differences.b: Sub is almost absent (0.1%). Mid is 40%, from the 1 kHz tone and hiss. Air is only 3%, and the final-quarter centroid is 9 kHz, far above A's 275 Hz.

differences.a: Level stays about -23 to -30 dB through the first half. There is a strong clack at 1.4 s and a mid-level whirr to 2.2 s. It then fades smoothly to the -40 dB point at 2.3 s.
differences.b: The first 1.3 s sits near -53 to -73 dB, 25-30 dB quieter than A, so the first half is almost empty. Level jumps at 1.4 s and holds flat to 2.2 s, then drops abruptly. The sound reaches -40 dB at 1.5 s.

differences.a: The 1.55-2.2 s whirr is granular and slightly warbling, 150-250 Hz bass plus 1-3 kHz grain, with gradually rising energy.
differences.b: A static, flat-amplitude 1 kHz sine with a hissy noise bed above 2 kHz. There is no modulation and it ends in a hard cutoff at 2.2 s.

differences.a: Quiet, smooth fading tail with faint low rumble and hiss from 2.2 to 2.97 s.
differences.b: Tail after 2.2 s is a very quiet low hiss that fades, but it is separated from the whirr by an abrupt cut. The effect is dry apart from the cutoff.

differences.b: Audible pitch sweeps (250-400 Hz down) on each blip and fixed 1 kHz tones.

Add 3-5 small bumps and scuffs between 0.66 and 1.3 s: 10-30 ms filtered noise ticks at 500 Hz-3 kHz, -30 to -35 dBFS, with a gentle low-end rumble.

Replace the 1 kHz sine whirr (1.55-2.2 s) with a granular, modulated noise whirr: band-pass noise 300 Hz-3 kHz plus a 150-250 Hz bass layer, with 8-15 Hz amplitude and filter wobble (+/-30%). Fade it in over 0.15 s, hold at about -28 dBFS, and fade it out from 2.0 to 2.4 s. Do not cut abruptly. Cut any steady sine to under -35 dB.
Boost sub and bass: add a 40-120 Hz layer to reach about 14% sub and 45% bass. Cut mid from 40% to about 14%. Keep air at about 10% by adding hiss above 8 kHz on the clicks only, not the whole file.
Add a quiet fading tail of 2.2-2.97 s: low rumble at 100-200 Hz plus faint hiss, fading from -45 to -65 dB. Keep it mono and set the final peak at about -4.5 dBFS.

review.summary: B is a plausible bass-heavy explosion of the right length and loudness, but it is a sustained, sub-heavy plateau with a regular amplitude-modulated flutter, not A's sharp-peaked, gritty, irregular blast that decays steadily. It reads as a rumbling engine drone more than a detonation.

differences.a: Near-instant onset peaking at 0.08 s with a hard clipped crack and bright upper-mid crackle, so it hits as a detonation.
differences.b: Slower, softer onset peaking at 0.15 s with no distinct transient, so it swells in rather than hitting.

differences.a: Hot for about 0.3 s, then a steady, uneven decay: -20 dB at 0.56 s and -40 dB at 1.06 s, so the shape is front-loaded.
differences.b: Flat plateau of about -7 dB for 0.4 s, then a slow fade that only reaches -23 dB at 0.9 s and cuts abruptly at about 1.12 s. It is much more sustained and ends with a hard edge.

differences.a: Centroid about 338 Hz, 69% bass, 12% sub, with highs darkening steadily over time.
differences.b: Centroid about 612 Hz, 40% sub, 35% bass, with more mid and air energy (about 14% mid and above versus 8%). It is subby and boomy and the highs persist.

differences.a: Irregular, grainy debris and crackle with a mottled, random amplitude texture.
differences.b: Regular, periodic pulsing (about 15-20 Hz comb-like vertical striations) that gives a motor, engine or tremolo feel, not debris. Qwen's 'vehicle' note agrees.

differences.a: Almost entirely noise with a faint 3 kHz line, and a burst of broadband energy at the start.
differences.b: Sustained low tonal and sub-bass drone with a periodic modulator layered under the noise, so it sounds more tonal and mechanical.

differences.b: Peak -1.9 dBFS, no clipping, -12.4 LUFS, crest 7.9 dB. It is slightly quieter and less punchy but within tolerance and cleaner.

review.summary: B matches A's 2.29 s length, loudness and rough three-act structure (clack, quiet middle, rattle, rising end tone), but it is built from sustained synthetic blocks with hard silent gaps. A is a sparse series of sharp foley transients. B sounds more like a synth sequence than a handled weapon reload.

differences.a: Several sharp, bright, broadband metallic clacks (0.04 s, 0.18 s, a strong clunk at 0.64 s, small clacks at 1.7-1.85 s), each with a fast decay (-20 dB in 0.05 s).
differences.b: Opens with a flat-topped buzzy block of about 0.1 s, then a band-limited noise burst. Almost no distinct clack transients. The only click-like events are one at 0.12 s and a tick near 1.12 s.

differences.a: Layered foley: eject clack, handling clicks, insertion clunk, slide/rack rattle, then a rising whine.
differences.b: Three synthetic blocks: a tone-plus-noise burst (0-0.4 s), a sub thump with decaying low sweep (0.6-0.9 s), and a dense noise wash (1.34-1.9 s). The two-tone end whine is present. No recognisable insert or rack foley.

differences.a: Events at 0.05, 0.18, 0.45, 0.64, 0.86, 1.1, 1.3, 1.69 and 1.82 s. Continuous low-level activity (active fraction 0.72) with no true digital silence.
differences.b: Only 6 onsets. Hard digital-silent gaps at about 0.42-0.6 s and around 1.3 s, and a quiet stretch from 0.9 to 1.3 s. Total length is right, but the gaps read as dropouts rather than natural room tone.

differences.b: Smooth synthetic noise bursts and a pure ~1 kHz tone with harmonics at 0-0.1 s. The 1.34-1.9 s rattle is a uniform, fairly steady noise bed with stuttered amplitude, not discrete clacks.

differences.b: A ~600 Hz tone and a ~1.1 kHz tone rise only slightly from 1.9 s. They are louder, more prominent and lower. They are wider in pitch and glide less than A's.

differences.a: Spiky envelope with the peak at 0.04 s and -40 dB at 0.77 s. The loudest element is the 0.64 s clunk.

differences.a: Peak -0.9 dBFS, -23.0 LUFS, crest factor 23 dB.

differences.b: Dry. The thump decays smoothly over about 0.3 s, and the noise blocks cut off abruptly (about 1.34 s and 1.9 s).

differences.b: Mono.

review.summary: B is a similar-length, similar-loudness explosion, but it is much brighter and more tonal than A, with a smooth steady-level body, regular click-like pulses and an abrupt cutoff. A is a dark, clipped, bass-dominated roar with irregular debris and a natural fade.

differences.a: Very dark: centroid ~196 Hz, 85% rolloff ~172 Hz, about 90% of energy below 250 Hz (25% sub, 65% bass), almost nothing above 2 kHz after the first 0.5 s.
differences.b: Much brighter: centroid ~923 Hz, rolloff ~1.66 kHz, only ~63% in sub+bass, with ~16% mid, ~3.6% presence and ~2.2% air. Broadband noise is visible up to 10 kHz throughout.

differences.a: Irregular, turbulent amplitude with random fluctuation and debris bursts. Dense chaotic low rumble, centroid falling 232 to 107 Hz.
differences.b: Very flat, smooth amplitude body that looks like a steady noise bed with a linear fade. Centroid wanders 1088, 467, 1040, 1365 Hz, so it brightens late instead of darkening.

differences.a: Peak at 0.08 s with near-full level held to ~1.0 s, then a stepped ~6 dB drop at ~1.1 s. -20 dB at 1.24 s, -40 dB at 2.03 s, and a natural fade to silence.
differences.b: Peak at 0.05 s and a gradual slope: -20 dB only at 1.81 s, -40 dB at 2.23 s. The decay is slower and more linear, with no stepped drop, and the sound is cut abruptly at ~2.2-2.27 s with a visible end click.

differences.a: Distorted, clipped, rumbly roar with sparse crackle and debris pulses at ~0.6, 1.4, 1.5, 1.8, 1.9 and 2.1 s.
differences.b: Regular, comb-like vertical striations every ~50-80 ms across the full spectrum from ~0.3 s on. This reads as a machine-gun or fluttering/tremolo pulse train rather than random debris, and it gets denser and more rhythmic late on.

differences.a: Sharp broadband blast burst in the first ~0.1 s, clipping, with a strong crack reaching the top of the spectrum.
differences.b: Soft attack, with no distinct crack or transient spike. It starts at near-full level with only a slight hump, so the initial blast lacks punch.

differences.a: Peak +0.7 dBFS (1265 clipped samples), RMS -9.7 dB, -10.3 LUFS.
differences.b: Peak -1.5 dBFS, no clipping, RMS -10.7 dB, -11.6 LUFS. This is within tolerance and meets the peak target, but the loudness is carried by mids and highs rather than sub and bass.

differences.a: 2.47 s, with 0.28 s trailing silence and an active tail until ~2.19 s.
differences.b: 2.47 s, with 0.19 s trailing silence. Duration matches, but the sound stays active about 0.1 s longer and then stops abruptly.

differences.a: No pitch movement, just a low rumble with sub energy (the written profile suggests a sub sweep of ~100 to 40 Hz).
differences.b: The sub-bass region is strong (35% sub) but largely static. There is no clear downward sweep, though the Qwen notes claim a drop. The high-frequency pulse train adds a pitched flutter impression.

differences.a: The tail is low rumble that darkens with a closing low-pass and dies into silence by ~2.2 s, with little bright content after ~0.5 s.
differences.b: The tail keeps wideband hiss and bright pulses until the cutoff, so it sounds more like a fizzling or firework-like crackle than a dark rumbling decay.

change_notes: Low-pass the main noise roar: 12-24 dB/oct at ~400-500 Hz, with the cutoff sweeping from ~1.5 kHz at 0 s down to ~250 Hz by 2.0 s. This should bring the centroid to ~200-250 Hz and the rolloff to ~200-400 Hz. Cut the 1-10 kHz noise bed by ~20-30 dB after 0.3 s.

Remove or randomise the periodic pulse train. If there is an LFO or retrigger at ~12-20 Hz, delete it. Replace it with 5-7 sparse debris crackles (5-20 ms, bandpassed 1-4 kHz, -15 to -25 dB relative to the body) at ~0.6, 0.7, 1.4, 1.5, 1.8, 1.9 and 2.1 s, with jittered timing and level.

Add a blast transient: 80-100 ms of full-band noise (broadband to ~10 kHz), attack <5 ms, decaying -30 dB over ~100 ms, ~+6 dB above the body. Soft-clip or saturate lightly so the peak sits around -1 dBFS.
Strengthen the bass: sine/triangle boom swept 100 Hz to 40 Hz over ~300-400 ms, plus noise at 40-250 Hz. Target ~25% sub and ~60% bass of the energy, and reduce the low-mid/mid share to ≤8% combined.

Reshape the envelope: hold near full level to ~1.0 s, drop ~6 dB at ~1.1 s, reach -20 dB by ~1.25 s (currently 1.81 s) and -40 dB by ~2.0 s, then fade to zero by ~2.2 s. Use a 100-150 ms smooth release instead of a hard cut so there is no end click.
Add random amplitude turbulence (non-periodic) of ±3 dB at 3-10 Hz to the roar, using slow filtered noise rather than a regular LFO, so it no longer sounds like a flat steady noise bed.
Keep the overall loudness near -10.3 LUFS. After the brightness cut, the level will fall because the mids are removed, so raise the low band gain by ~2-3 dB and keep the peak ≤ -1 dBFS.

review.summary: B matches length (0.76 s) and integrated loudness (-10.6 vs -10.1 LUFS), but the structure and timbre differ. A is one loud noisy slap, a quiet gap with faint ticks, then a low pulsing hum. B is a sequence of tonal beeps and sweeps with a dead gap at 0.5-0.58 s and a pitched, sustained ending.

differences.a: Event reads as one heavy slap (0-0.25 s), then quiet ticks, then a low hum. The slap is the dominant event.
differences.b: Four or five separate events: two noisy bursts (0.04 s and 0.21 s), a descending tonal sweep (0.27-0.5 s), a gap, then a rising tonal tone burst (0.58-0.76 s). There is no single dominant slap.

differences.a: Broadband noise to 5-10 kHz plus thick 20-250 Hz body. Centroid is ~1 kHz, rising to ~2 kHz in the middle quarters. Bass 27%, low-mid 29%, mid 23%, sub 4.5%.
differences.b: Low-mid heavy (58%), almost no sub (0.5%) and bass at 18%. Rolloff is 1.2 kHz. Centroid is 504 Hz in the second quarter, then 6.9 kHz in the third quarter, where only the sparse high-frequency ticks are active.

differences.a: Mostly noise and crunchy broadband. The tail is a low hum. Nothing reads as a pure tone.
differences.b: Strong narrow tonal lines at ~1.0-1.2 kHz, 3.3 kHz and 6.5 kHz, plus a descending tone and a ~700 Hz tone. This sounds like a synth beep (Qwen heard a 'sine wave').

differences.a: Peaks at 0.04 s, sustains to ~0.2 s, then falls steeply by 0.25 s into a quiet floor of ticks (-25 to -38 dB). The hum then swells in the last 0.2 s.
differences.b: Roughly flat -8 to -10 dB for 0-0.5 s with no clear decay after the first hit. It dips only at 0.38-0.5 s, goes silent at 0.5-0.58 s, then holds a loud block (-7 dB) to 0.76 s. The envelope is block-like.

differences.a: A hard, clipped slap transient at ~0.04 s (peak +2.6 dBFS, crest 13 dB), with small click transients at 0.35, 0.5 and 0.62 s.
differences.b: Softer, more sustained noise onsets (crest 8 dB, no clipping). Clicks at 0.38, 0.44 and 0.5 s are brief but vertical stripes. The ending has no transient, only an abrupt start after the gap.

differences.a: No clear pitch movement. The ending is a low, ~25-30 Hz-pulsed rumble below ~200 Hz.
differences.b: Clear pitch movement: a descending sweep from ~500 Hz to ~150 Hz over 0.27-0.5 s, and a gently rising tone from ~600 to ~750 Hz in the ending.

differences.a: The first 0.25 s holds the main hit, then there are sparse ticks at 0.35, 0.5 and 0.62 s, with the hum beginning around 0.55 s and swelling to 0.7 s.
differences.b: Total length matches, but the timing is different. The dominant events run 0-0.5 s and 0.58-0.76 s, and the final block starts around 0.58 s and is far louder and more tonal.

differences.a: Peak +2.6 dBFS (clipped, 728 samples), RMS -10.5 dB, -10.1 LUFS. Dynamic contrast is large (-2.8 dB peak to -25 to -46 dB in the gaps).
differences.b: Peak -2 dBFS, RMS -10 dB, -10.6 LUFS. Overall level is similar, but the dynamic contrast is far smaller. The quiet portion is only the 0.38-0.5 s dip and the silence at 0.5-0.58 s.

differences.a: No reverb. A low rumbling pulse fades by 0.76 s.
differences.b: No reverb. The ending cuts off hard after the gap and fades only in the last ~30 ms.

change_notes: Rebuild the opening as one slap, 0-0.25 s: white noise band-passed 200 Hz-5 kHz with a 5 ms attack, held ~0.15 s, then an exponential decay to -20 dB by 0.17 s and -40 dB by 0.25 s. Remove the second burst at 0.21 s.
Add a body under the slap: sine/triangle at 150 Hz falling to 60 Hz over 120 ms, plus a 40 Hz sub thump, 100 ms, around +3 dB. Target bass+sub at ~30% of band energy.
Remove the 1.0/3.3/6.5 kHz tonal lines: delete the fixed sine-like partials or replace them with a filtered noise click. Keep the tail non-melodic.
Delete the 500 to 150 Hz descending tone at 0.27-0.5 s. Replace this region with a low-level floor (-30 to -40 dB) holding only small clicks.
Place three quiet mechanical clicks at 0.35, 0.50 and 0.62 s: 1-4 kHz noise, 5-10 ms each, 20 dB below the slap peak (~-25 dB), with the first slightly louder.

Replace the 0.58-0.76 s tone with a low hum: 80-120 Hz saw/square lowpassed at 200 Hz, amplitude-modulated at 25-30 Hz, fading in from 0.55 s to a peak at ~0.68 s (about -12 dB relative to the slap), then fading out over 0.08 s. Keep it pitched flat or very slightly rising.
Fill the 0.5-0.58 s silence with the hum rise and clicks so there is no dead gap.

Raise the slap crest factor to ~12 dB with a hard peak (+0 dB soft clip) while keeping the output at or below -1 dBFS, and maintain ~-10 to -12 LUFS integrated by leaving the middle quiet instead of loud.

review.summary: B has the right blaster character, with a low thump and a descending zap, but it is much shorter and its tail is far thinner. It decays to silence by about 1.0 s, where A's boomy, noisy wash runs for 2 s. B's sub is weak and it has no mid resonance band.

differences.a: Audible for about 2.07 s and the file is 2.76 s. It falls to -20 dB at 1.5 s and -40 dB at 2.04 s. Active fraction is 0.68.
differences.b: Audible for only about 0.7-1.0 s, then digital silence for 1.93 s. It falls to -20 dB at 0.49 s and -40 dB at 0.82 s. Active fraction is 0.25.

differences.a: Slow, nearly flat decay. It sits at about -18 to -28 dB through 0.5 s and is still at -33 dB at 0.6 s, with no steep drop until about 1.5 s.
differences.b: Fast, steep exponential fall: -15, -19, -30, -48, -77 dB per tenth. It reads as a short pop with no sustained body.

differences.a: Long, dark, noisy reverb-like rumble. High end dies first and the low rumble lingers.
differences.b: Almost no tail. The low end cuts off hard at about 0.7 s, visible as a vertical edge in the spectrogram, followed by a faint low fade to about 1.4 s.

differences.a: Broad low end: sub 16%, bass 35.5%, low-mid 14%. Mid 12%, presence 9%. Sub energy extends down to 20 Hz.
differences.b: Bass 71%, sub only 1.3%, low-mid 3.6%. It is concentrated at about 100-300 Hz and lacks real sub weight and the low-mid body.

differences.a: Thump, a diagonal falling zap line from several kHz to about 400 Hz over 0.3-0.4 s, a sustained 450-1000 Hz resonant band to about 1.5 s, and a noisy wash.
differences.b: Thump plus clean, discrete, harmonic zap sweeps. Several parallel curved lines fall from 10 kHz to about 700 Hz over about 0.5 s. There is no sustained mid band.

differences.a: Dense, gritty, distorted noise and granular texture. Flatness is 0 and tonality is low.
differences.b: The zap is clean and tonal, with visible harmonic lines. Noise is limited to the first 0.5 s, so it sounds more synthetic and less gritty.

differences.a: Peak at 0.03 s, with a dense blast and a broad noisy onset.
differences.b: Peak at 0.01 s. Crest factor is 21 dB against A's 17 dB, so it is spikier and more clicky.

differences.a: RMS -21.9 dBFS, peak -4.4 dBFS, -21.5 LUFS. Energy is spread over time.
differences.b: Also -21.5 LUFS, but this comes from a louder initial burst (-14.8 dB first tenth) over a much shorter duration. RMS is -24.8 dBFS and peak is -3.6 dBFS. It will feel punchier and less sustained.

differences.a: The zap falls from several kHz to about 400 Hz, then the body holds around 450-1000 Hz resonances.
differences.b: The zap falls from about 10 kHz to about 700 Hz, higher and wider in range, and it stops at about 0.5 s.

change_notes: Extend the main body and tail. Replace the exponential decay with a two-stage envelope: hold at about -18 to -28 dB through 0.5 s, reach -20 dB at about 1.5 s and -40 dB at about 2.0 s. Make the total audible length about 2.1 s.
Remove the hard cut at 0.7 s. Fade the low layers with a smooth 1.5 s exponential release and no gate or vertical edge.
Add a noise tail layer: low-passed noise, about 4 kHz corner falling to 800 Hz over 1.8 s. Add a 0.3 s pre-delay-free dark reverb or comb diffusion at -18 dB relative to the thump.
Add sub weight. Use a sine at 40-60 Hz, with a pitch drop from 90 to 45 Hz over 150 ms, held with 1.2 s decay, at about +6 dB over the current bass. Target sub about 15% and bass about 35%.

Add a mid resonant band of 3-4 band-passed noise or FM partials at 450, 600, 800 and 1000 Hz, Q about 8, starting at 0.3 s, at -25 dB relative to peak and lasting until 1.4 s, with slow random amplitude modulation at about 8-12 Hz.

Reduce the zap's tonal purity. Cut the harmonic sweep from 10 kHz to a start of about 5 kHz, falling to 400 Hz over 0.35 s. Use a single saw or square sweep and mix it with noise at -6 dB. Lower its level by about 4 dB.
Add mild saturation or tanh drive (about 6 dB) on the sum, plus 20% bit-crush or noise-modulated grit, so the texture is gritty and distorted.

Soften the transient. Use a 20-30 ms attack-to-peak instead of 10 ms and cut the click to bring crest factor to about 17 dB. Keep the peak at about -4 dBFS and about -21.5 LUFS after the longer tail raises the RMS.

review.summary: B matches A's length, loudness and the overall reload layout (clicks, mid thunk near 1.1 s, gap, clacks, big hit near 1.87 s), but it sounds synthetic: it adds sustained whistling tones and heavy low-end, has a long smooth tail instead of dry clacks, and lacks A's sharp, dry metallic foley.

differences.a: Final hit at 1.87 s decays fast (-20 dB in 0.06 s, -40 dB in 0.39 s) into a faint ringing tail with small pulses and a few late clicks to about 2.65 s.
differences.b: Final hit at 1.87 s is followed by a long sustained tail of about 0.8 s that stays audible to the end, with a flat tonal line under it (decay measured at -20 dB 0.76 s).

differences.a: Almost no sub or bass (0.2% combined). Energy is mid, presence and air, with a 1 kHz click body and 2-5 kHz content.
differences.b: 29% of energy is in bass, with a big 50-200 Hz bloom at 1.87-2.1 s and a low rumble bed in 0.3-1.0 s. Bass is far heavier than A.

differences.a: Noise-based metallic impacts. Only a faint tonal line near 2.3-3 kHz in the tail.
differences.b: Prominent steady sine-like partials at about 1.1-1.5 kHz, plus a long held tone at about 1.3 kHz from 1.95 s to 2.7 s. These read as electronic whistles or beeps, not metal.

differences.a: Dry, clicky, gritty foley with broadband transients: mag release, rattle, seating thunk.
differences.b: Smooth, synthetic and electronic-sounding (Qwen: 'static', 'short-circuit'). The 1.05-1.4 s hit is a bright noise burst with a smooth decaying envelope, more like a hiss or whoosh than a metal thunk.

differences.a: Many sharp, short clicks. 15 onsets, including clusters at 0.09-0.23 s, 1.63-1.82 s and late clicks at 2.03-2.55 s.
differences.b: 11 onsets. Early clicks are sparse and thin, and the 1.67-1.83 s cluster has less snap. Late clicks are absent as distinct events and replaced by regular tick lines.

differences.a: Quiet friction bed 0.65-1.0 s with small clicks. The 1.06 s thunk decays by about 1.4 s. Gap 1.45-1.62 s.

Make the early clicks at 0.09, 0.15 and 0.23 s sharper and louder: 3-8 ms noise bursts, band-passed around 1 kHz and 2-5 kHz, peaks at about -15 dB relative to the main hit. Use short resonant ping decays of about 30 ms.
Change the 0.65-1.0 s rattle bed to very low-level band-passed noise (500 Hz-5 kHz, about -45 dB) with irregular tiny clicks. Remove the rhythmic ticking at a regular rate and randomise the timing.

Shape the 1.63-1.82 s cluster into 4 distinct clacks at about 1.63, 1.71, 1.76 and 1.82 s, each 10-20 ms, with a 1 kHz click body. Make the 1.87 s slam the loudest event, with a broadband noise crack of about 20 ms, then a fast decay.

review.summary: B matches A's total length (5.29 s) and rough integrated loudness, but it is a flat, sustained noise bed with three repeated sweeping-thump cycles, where A is a hot burst that decays over about 4 s into sparse crackles. It reads as a looping drone or alarm rather than a disintegration.

differences.a: Peak at 0.05 s, then a steady exponential decay: -20 dB at about 2.0 s, -40 dB at about 4.0 s, near silence after 4.6 s.
differences.b: Almost flat at about -11 to -14 dB for 4.0 s, then a slow fade to -18 dB at 4.4 s and a sudden cutoff. The -20 dB point is at 4.6 s, so there is no real decay.

differences.a: Heavy sub thump at the start (sub 12%), dense noise burst, and crackle/pop ticks that thin out (14 onsets, 2.5-4.6 s).
differences.b: Continuous noise bed plus a repeating downward-sweeping tone at roughly 300 Hz to 60 Hz, restarting at about 0 s, 1.4 s and 2.4 s. There are no discrete crackles, only 2 onsets (a seam click at 1.4 s and an end click at 4.6 s).

differences.a: Hot, burning, crackly and sizzling, sparse and brittle toward the end, with an irregular organic feel.
differences.b: Smooth, uniform, synthetic noise with a tonal sweep, which Qwen heard as a sine and chirp or an electronic alert. It does not sound like burning or dissolving.

differences.b: Opener with a sub thump and two tones, then a continuous ~1 kHz sine drone from 0.1 s to 0.96 s, plus a noise bed and spiky clicks at roughly 0.1 s spacing.

differences.a: Opener is clean, harmonic and tonal (flatness 0.006). The ticks are narrow-band chirp clicks, and the gaps are silent.
differences.b: Wideband noise floor throughout (flatness 0.345) and a constant sine drone, so there is no silence anywhere.

differences.a: Flat, loud sustain to 0.08 s, then a hard gate: -20 dB by 0.08 s and -40 dB by 0.13 s. Ticks sit at about -60 dBFS and every gap is empty.

differences.a: Instant, hard-gated buzzy burst at 0 s (peak at 0.01 s). Ticks are soft, short and very quiet.

differences.b: Spread across low-mid (31%), mid (26%) and air (31%), with peaks at 818, 1163 and 1637 Hz. Sub-bass thump is about 40-200 Hz. The ~1 kHz drone dominates the body.

change_notes: Delete the 1 kHz sine drone (0.1-0.96 s) completely. It is the main reason B no longer reads as a countdown.
Remove the broadband noise floor. Gate everything to true silence (below -90 dB) between the clicks, so flatness drops and active fraction goes from 0.95 to about 0.2.

Rebuild the opener as a buzzy burst starting at 0 s with a 1-2 ms attack. Use a square or saw at about 1.1 kHz with stacked partials at 2.2k, 4.6k and 7-11k Hz, held flat for 80-90 ms with a hard gate (about 5 ms release). Set its peak to about -1.5 dBFS.
Shorten the sub thump to 50-150 Hz for about 80 ms, and cut the low rumble tail (currently about 0.3 s). Keep only a little thump under the opener and nothing after the gate.

Make the clicks uniform: eight band-passed bursts (6-10 kHz, Q about 3), 20-30 ms each with a 1 ms attack and a fast exponential decay, at exactly 0.1, 0.2, ... 0.9 s. Keep the total length at 1.0 s and target about -21.8 LUFS integrated. Because the ticks are so quiet, the opener has to carry the loudness (peak at or below -1 dBFS).

review.summary: B is a similar-length, similar-loudness rifle shot, but it is much darker and more bass-heavy, with a softer, slower attack and no sharp crack or mechanical second transient. It reads more like a boomy thud than the bright, noisy SCAR blast of A.

review.summary: B matches the 5 s length, the ~-19.5 LUFS loudness and the rough four-stage layout of A. Its character is wrong: A is sparse, dry foley made of clicks, clacks and thumps with sharp transients, while B is sustained, synthetic and tonal, built from noise-and-sine blocks with a steady pad-like body.

differences.a: Many sharp, discrete transients (about 30 onsets): rustles, clicks, clacks and metal slams, each with a fast attack and a decay of 0.2-0.5 s.
differences.b: Only about 14 onsets. Most events are blocky sustained plateaus with a soft or squared-off onset. Little click or impact definition apart from a decaying thump at 1.2 s.

differences.a: Each event decays quickly (-20 dB by 0.22 s, -40 dB by 0.48 s) and leaves a dynamic, varied envelope.
differences.b: Events hold level as flat-topped blocks (0-0.9 s, 2.6-3.3 s, 4.15-5.0 s) and cut off abruptly. The 4.15-5.0 s block is a sustained slab with no distinct slam decays. Decay is slower (-20 dB at 0.48 s, -40 dB at 0.71 s).

differences.a: Quiet handling rustle and clicks (0-1 s), clack at ~1.25 s, sparse ticks, rattle and thump at ~2.9 s, then two separate loud metal slams at ~4.2 s and ~4.6 s.
differences.b: 0-0.9 s is a continuous low-frequency pulsing buzz instead of rustle and clicks. The 1.2 s thump is well placed. 2.6-3.3 s is a flat ~800 Hz tone, and the final section has only one onset at 4.15 s with a steady ~1.4 kHz tone, not two slams.

differences.a: Mostly noisy, metallic broadband, with only a faint ~1 kHz ring after the 2.9 s event and after the last slam.
differences.b: Prominent, loud, steady sine-like tones at ~800 Hz (2.6-3.3 s) and ~1.4 kHz (4.15-5.0 s), plus a ~1 kHz beep at 1.25 s. These read as beeps or sirens, not metal.

differences.a: Mid-dominant (45% mid, 21% presence, 15% air), with sub thumps under the main hits. Centroid ~3.9 kHz.
differences.b: 39.6% bass energy, with long low-frequency slabs, so it is bass-heavy and boomy. Mid is 26% and low-mid is weak. Centroid ~3.2 kHz, but it swings from 371 Hz to 8 kHz between quarters, which makes the balance uneven.

differences.a: ~5.0 s with 0.04 s trailing silence. Events at ~0.2-0.9 s, 1.25 s, 2.9 s, 4.2 s and 4.6 s. A near-silent gap at 3.4-4.1 s with one tiny click at ~3.7 s.
differences.b: 5.0 s. Gap structure is similar (silence 3.35-4.1 s, a click at 3.7 s). The 0.9-1.2 s and 1.6-2.6 s sections are near-silent or have sparse ticks, which is plausible. The overall stage timing is reasonably close.

differences.a: Organic, close and dry foley: cloth, metal, a rattly insertion, heavy slams.
differences.b: Clearly synthetic. Hiss-like noise at 2-16 kHz sits on top of tones and low-frequency slabs, so it reads as static plus beeps (as Qwen heard) and not as a rifle reload.

differences.a: Peak -3.4 dBFS, RMS -24.4 dB, crest 21 dB, -19.5 LUFS.
differences.b: Peak -4.7 dBFS, RMS -22.4 dB, crest 17.7 dB, -19.6 LUFS. Integrated loudness matches, but the higher RMS and lower crest come from sustained blocks, not peaky hits.

differences.a: Dry, with short ringing tails under 0.5 s.
differences.b: Also dry, but with abrupt gating at the block ends (~0.9 s, ~3.3 s) and hard sustained tones in place of natural short tails.

differences.a: Mono, centered.
differences.b: Mono, centered.

Rattly insertion and thump build at 2.6-3.1 s
Two separate loud metal slams at ~4.2 s and ~4.6 s, each with a sub thump and short decay

Fast, natural decay on every event

Steady ~800 Hz tone plateau at 2.6-3.3 s
Steady ~1.4 kHz tone held through 4.15-5.0 s

change_notes: Rebuild the 4.15-5.0 s section as two slams. Slam 1 at 4.15 s and slam 2 at 4.6 s, each with a 2 ms noise click, a 1-6 kHz noise burst of 80 ms that decays -30 dB in 250 ms, a 60->45 Hz sine thump of 150 ms, and a metallic ring made from 2-3 inharmonic partials near 900-1500 Hz. Drop the ring to -35 dB below the hit and decay it in ≤0.4 s. Remove the sustained 1.4 kHz tone.

Replace the 0-0.9 s buzz with 6-8 discrete events at about 0.1, 0.23, 0.31, 0.43, 0.53, 0.62, 0.71 and 0.81 s. Use 5-15 ms bandpassed noise clicks at 2-6 kHz plus a soft 50-90 Hz thump of 80 ms. Keep the level 15-25 dB below the main hits (about -35 to -30 dBFS). Fade the rustle in and out irregularly, not as a constant buzz.

Make the 1.2 s clack bright and short. Add a 1-8 kHz noise crack of 30 ms at +6 dB over the body, keep the 60-100 Hz thump but shorten it to ≤150 ms (-20 dB by 0.2 s, not 0.48 s), and keep a short 1 kHz ring (≤150 ms) at -30 dB. Remove the 1.2-1.4 s low-frequency slab.

Rework 2.6-3.3 s: use 4-6 small rattle clicks of 10-20 ms from 2.6 to 2.85 s (bandpass 1-5 kHz) rising in level, then a thud at 2.9-3.0 s (70 Hz, 120 ms, -6 dB re the final slams). Make the ~1 kHz ring a faint sine at -40 dB, decaying over 0.3 s, instead of a steady 800 Hz tone at full level. Fade it out by ~3.4 s.

Cut bass: reduce the 20-200 Hz share from ~40% to ~10-15% of band energy by shortening thumps and keeping them to the main hits. Raise the 500 Hz-5 kHz noise content so that mid is ~45% and presence ~20%, then aim for a centroid near 3.5-4 kHz.
Fill 1.7-2.6 s with 3-5 sparse ticks (5-10 ms, 2-5 kHz, -45 to -35 dBFS) at about 1.78, 1.88, 2.07, 2.29 and 2.37 s. Keep the gap 3.4-4.1 s silent apart from one tick at 3.7 s.

Raise the crest factor from 17.7 to ~21 dB by making the loudest slam peak at about -3.4 dBFS and keeping the rest of the file much quieter. Keep -19.5 LUFS. Use a 2-5 ms fade-in or out on every event to avoid clicks, and give every event an exponential decay, not a gate.

review.summary: B captures the low thump and the downward zap sweep, but it is a much shorter, faster-decaying shot. Its audible tail is about 1.0 s against A's roughly 1.9 s, with 1.8 s of dead silence at the end, so it lacks the long rumbling tail and the gritty noisy body.

differences.a: Audible energy for about 1.9 s, then 0.76 s of silence. Active fraction 0.6, -40 dB at 1.73 s.
differences.b: Audible energy only to about 1.0-1.5 s, then 1.8 s of digital silence. Active fraction 0.28, -40 dB at 0.83 s.

differences.a: Slow, smooth decay: -20 dB at 0.75 s, -40 dB at 1.73 s. The body holds at about -23 to -28 dB for 0.2-0.5 s.
differences.b: Fast decay: -20 dB at 0.45 s, -40 dB at 0.83 s. The envelope falls steeply after 0.3 s, with levels of -44 dB at 0.3 s and -67 dB at 0.4 s.

differences.a: Long, dull, pulsing low rumble with reverb-like decay, still audible out to about 2 s.
differences.b: Short tail of low rumble that is gone by about 1.3 s. It has little pulsing or reverb feel.

differences.a: Peak at 0.11 s with a bright, broadband noisy burst and a sweep starting at the top of the spectrum.
differences.b: Peak at 0.02 s with a sharper, more immediate onset and a cleaner, more tonal burst.

differences.a: Sub 21%, bass 16%, low-mid 15%, mid 15%, presence 10%, air 5%. Broad and weighty, with a centroid that dips to 870 Hz then rises to 2.6 kHz late in the tail from the noise floor.
differences.b: Sub only 1.5%, bass 63%, low-mid 5%, mid 15%. It is bass-heavy at roughly 60-250 Hz and lacks real sub. The centroid falls steadily from 1.4 kHz to 220 Hz. No low-mid body.

differences.a: Bright diagonal zap from about 10+ kHz down to about 1 kHz over about 0.3-0.5 s, with a few fainter streaks in the body.
differences.b: Several parallel harmonic sweeps falling from about 10 kHz to about 500 Hz over about 0.6 s. They are clean, tonal and sweep slower and lower.

differences.a: Dense and gritty with noisy broadband texture throughout. Flatness is 0.002 but skewed by the lows.
differences.b: More tonal and clean with discrete harmonic streaks and a smoother noise floor. It has less grit and flutter.

differences.a: Heavy, boomy, gritty, with fluttering mid texture and sustained mid-range noise up to about 1.7 s.
differences.b: Cleaner, more synthetic, with a thinner body. It reads more like a zap plus a thump than a heavy blast.

differences.a: Sub boom, noisy burst, zap sweep, mid texture, long rumble tail.
differences.b: Bass thump, harmonic zap sweep and short tail only. A narrow vertical click or glitch appears at about 0.7 s.

differences.a: Peak -4.1 dBFS, RMS -21.7, LUFS -20.9.
differences.b: Peak -4.4 dBFS, RMS -24.4, LUFS -20.9. Integrated loudness matches, but energy is more front-loaded with a higher crest factor (20 vs 17.5 dB), so it feels punchier but less sustained.

differences.a: Mono.
differences.b: Mono.

differences.a: One-shot.
differences.b: One-shot.

change_notes: Lengthen the tail: keep the audible decay to about 2.0 s (-20 dB at 0.75 s, -40 dB at 1.7 s) instead of -20 dB at 0.45 s and -40 dB at 0.83 s. Use a lowpassed noise rumble at 80-400 Hz with an exponential decay of about 0.5 s time constant, fading to silence by about 2.0 s, leaving about 0.6 s of trailing silence.

Add a sub boom: a sine at 70 Hz dropping to 35 Hz over 250 ms, with a 400 ms decay at about the same level as the bass. Raise the sub to about 18-20% of energy and cut the 100-250 Hz bass emphasis by about 6 dB so the bass drops from 63% to about 16%.
Add a pulsing, reverb-like tail: send the rumble through a dense reverb or comb network with RT60 of about 1.5 s and 4-6 Hz amplitude flutter of about 3 dB, so it sounds like a decaying room.
Add a gritty noise body: pink or white noise bandpassed at 300-2500 Hz, starting at about -24 dB at 0.15 s and decaying over about 1.2 s. Raise the low-mid and mid content to about 15% each.

Soften the attack slightly: use a 5-10 ms attack ramp on the noise burst and let the body peak at about 0.05-0.1 s. Keep a 2-3 ms noise click at 0 s for the transient. This puts the sound closer to A's broadband blast.

Modify the zap: make it a single dominant sweep rather than 4-5 parallel harmonics. Run it from 10 kHz to 1 kHz exponentially over 0.4 s at about -12 dB relative to the body, with added noise or FM grit so it is less pure. Remove the 0.7 s glitch.
Keep peak at about -4 dBFS and integrated loudness at about -21 LUFS. Lowering the sweep level and raising the sustained body will reduce crest factor from 20 dB to about 17-18 dB.

review.summary: B is a darker, smoother, bass-dominated boom that lasts a bit longer in its low tail but lacks A's sharp noisy crack, bright first 100 ms, mid body and mechanical bump. It matches the loudness, but it reads as a muffled thud or drum rather than a rifle shot.

differences.a: Centroid ~1.1 kHz, rolloff85 ~1.7 kHz. Bass 42%, low-mid 21%, mid+presence+air ~18%. Broadband energy reaches the top of the spectrum early.
differences.b: Centroid ~600 Hz, rolloff85 only ~711 Hz. Bass 70%, low-mid 5%, air 1%. Highs are gone very early and the sound is muffled.

differences.a: Sharp, noisy, near-clipping crack peaking at 0.04 s, with a ragged secondary burst around 0.2-0.27 s and a discrete bump at 0.41 s.
differences.b: Immediate but soft-edged onset with no distinct crack, a smooth blocky envelope and no secondary events (onset_count 0). It sounds like a thump or drum hit.

differences.a: Noisy, distorted and broadband (flatness 0.089), with no stable tones.
differences.b: Cleaner and more tonal-sounding sub/bass with low flatness (0.021). The 100-200 Hz energy reads as a pitched boom, and Qwen heard a drum roll.

differences.a: Very loud for ~0.2 s, -20 dB at 0.29 s, -40 dB at 0.78 s. The tail is a long, gradual fade of low-mid rumble and lasts about 0.85 s.
differences.b: Slower early fall (-20 dB at 0.41 s) and then a steep collapse (-40 dB at 0.7 s, -80 dB by 0.7 s). The tail is thin, and the active portion is similar in length, but its body is fatter than A's in the first 0.4 s and its tail is emptier.

differences.a: Reverberant low-mid tail with mid energy fading slowly. There is some highs decay over ~0.8 s.
differences.b: The tail is only sub/bass, with no mid-range room character, and it ends cleanly around 1.3 s. A single thin vertical line at ~0.72 s looks like an artifact.

differences.a: Crack, sub/bass thump, mid body, secondary burst, mechanical bump and room tail.
differences.b: Essentially one low boom layer with some noise on top, so it is much simpler.

differences.a: Peak 0 dBFS, RMS -15.9, ~-15.6 LUFS, one clipped sample.
differences.b: Peak -2.5 dBFS, ~-15.9 LUFS, no clipping. Integrated loudness is matched, but perceived punch is lower because the energy is all low-frequency.

differences.a: No obvious pitch movement, noise-based.
differences.b: Energy sits at 80-200 Hz and the centroid falls from 600 to 80 Hz. This reads as a pitched drop, giving a kick-drum feel.

differences.a: File 1.60 s with ~0.85 s active and 0.72 s trailing silence.
differences.b: File 1.60 s with ~0.75 s active and 0.85 s trailing silence. The timing is close.

change_notes: Add a noise crack layer: white noise bandpassed at 2-9 kHz, 40-60 ms long, exponential decay, at 0 s, about +8 dB over the bass body. Add a 1-3 ms hard click at the front for the transient.
Reduce the bass/sub dominance: cut the 80-200 Hz layer by ~6-8 dB so bass falls from 70% to ~42% and sub stays near 11%. Aim for a centroid near 1.1 kHz and rolloff85 near 1.7 kHz.
Add a low-mid body: noise lowpassed at ~1.5 kHz plus 300-900 Hz content, ~-6 dB under the crack, decaying from 0 to 0.5 s. Aim for ~20% of energy in low-mid and ~8% in mid.
Add a secondary noise burst at 0.2-0.27 s, 40 ms long, -8 dB re the main blast, bandpassed at 500 Hz-3 kHz, for the doubled, ragged feel.
Add a mechanical click at 0.41 s: 5-10 ms burst bandpassed at 1-3 kHz, about -25 dB re peak.
Add 2-4x soft-clip saturation on the sum, and raise the peak to about -1 dBFS, since the original is distorted and touches 0 dBFS.
Give the sub thump a faster fall: sine drop from 100 Hz to 45 Hz over ~120 ms with a 150 ms decay, rather than a held 100-200 Hz boom.
Lengthen and fill the tail: use a lowpassed noise reverb (2-3 kHz cutoff, closing to ~800 Hz) with ~-40 dB at 0.78 s. Avoid the steep drop and make sure it is smooth, with no click near 0.72 s.

review.summary: B matches A's length and loudness, but it is built from distinct, sequenced blocks (a long noise slab, a hissy second section, a pitched 1 kHz beep with ticks) instead of A's single dense burst decaying into sparse splats. It reads as electronic and synthetic, not a wet gore impact.

differences.a: One continuous gory event: a dense wet crunch plus bass thump that decays into 5 small splat clicks and a faint tail.
differences.b: Three separate sections: a 0-0.85 s noise/bass slab, a 0.85-1.7 s hissy section with pitch-dropping thumps, and a 1.8-2.2 s steady ~1 kHz tone with ticks.

differences.a: No pitch movement and no tonal peaks; it is pure noise and thump.
differences.b: A sustained ~1 kHz sine/square beep from 1.8 to 2.2 s, plus 3 descending ~300-150 Hz thumps at 1.0-1.35 s, which sound like sci-fi and read as an alert.

differences.a: Peaks at 0.02 s and decays smoothly: -20 dB at 0.83 s, -40 dB at 1.84 s. No sustain.
differences.b: Held flat at near-full level for 0.85 s, then drops abruptly at 0.85 s and again at 1.8 s. The waveform has a block shape with no natural decay. The -40 dB point is at 2.19 s.

differences.a: Sub 20%, bass 29%, mid 20%, presence 18%, air 3%. The centroid is about 1.9 kHz and rolloff85 about 4.8 kHz, so it is bright and crunchy.
differences.b: Sub only 1%, bass 55%, low-mid 27%, presence 3%, air 7%. The early section is dark (centroid about 370 Hz) and the later sections are hissy (centroid 7-9 kHz). The sub thump is missing.

differences.a: Instant, clipped, transient-heavy attack at 0.02 s (+4 dBFS peak, crest 20 dB).
differences.b: Soft attack: the first tenth of the envelope is -25.6 dB and it peaks at 0.03 s. Crest is only 12 dB, so it is compressed and lacks snap.

differences.a: Gritty wet broadband noise with low flatness (0.02).
differences.b: Smoother, more uniform noise (flatness 0.115) plus a pure tone. It lacks the wet squelch texture.

differences.a: Splat clicks at 0.93, 1.03, 1.13, 1.22 and 1.31 s, spaced about 0.1 s apart.
differences.b: No distinct splats. Instead there is a bright hiss wash from 0.85 s and a thin picket of vertical ticks around the beep (1.8-2.2 s).

differences.a: Active content for about 1.85 s, near-silence after that, 0.81 s of trailing silence.
differences.b: Active content up to about 2.25 s (active fraction 0.74 vs 0.53), 0.53 s of trailing silence. The tail is too long and too busy.

differences.a: -15.9 dB RMS, -13.3 LUFS, clipped.
differences.b: -14.9 dB RMS, -13.7 LUFS, peak -2.9 dBFS, no clipping. Loudness is close, and the lack of clipping is good.

differences.b: Mono.
