change_notes: Delete the 1 kHz beep (1.8-2.2 s) and its ticks completely. Nothing tonal should remain.

Delete the three descending thumps at 1.0-1.35 s. Replace them with one sub thump: sine 90 Hz falling to 45 Hz over 150 ms, with an exponential decay of about 0.5 s and a fade to nothing by 1.8 s. Add a quieter 100-200 Hz layer decaying over 1.2 s.

Rebuild the main body as one wet crunch burst: a 1-8 kHz noise band, 0 to about 0.5 s, with an attack under 5 ms and an exponential decay (-20 dB by 0.8 s). Use a bandpass sweep of 6 kHz down to 1.5 kHz and amplitude-modulate it at 30-60 Hz for squelch.
Add a transient crack at t=0: 2-6 kHz noise, 10-15 ms, +6 dB over the body. Use a soft clipper so the peak reaches about -1 dBFS without hard clipping.
Remove the block structure. Delete the abrupt cuts at 0.85 s and 1.8 s and the flat sustain. Use one continuous decay with -20 dB at about 0.8 s and -40 dB at about 1.8 s.

Replace the hiss wash with 5 splat clicks at 0.93, 1.03, 1.13, 1.22 and 1.31 s. Make each a 10-25 ms bandpassed noise burst at 1.5-4 kHz, with levels falling from -20 to -32 dB relative to the peak and slight pitch variation between them.
Cut the air band: lowpass at about 9 kHz, and keep the 5-10 kHz content below -50 dB after 0.9 s. Aim for a band split of roughly sub 20%, bass 28%, mid 20%, presence 18%.
Fade everything below -60 dB by 2.0 s. Leave only 2 or 3 very faint ticks until 2.2 s, then silence to 2.99 s (trailing silence of about 0.8 s).

review.summary: B has the right length and a two-hit structure, but it sounds like a low bass thump followed by a pure-tone whistle rather than a creaky, rattly metal door. Its energy sits in the bass instead of the low-mid/mid, it lacks A's noisy scrape texture, and it adds an artificial sustained sine at about 1.2 kHz.

differences.a: Low-mid (44%) and mid (38%) dominate, with bass at about 9%. The body sits around 200-800 Hz and the centroid is about 1.6 kHz, mostly from the noisy, woody-metallic body.
differences.b: Bass is 52% and low-mid 22%. The first hit is a steady 60-200 Hz block, and the first-quarter centroid is only about 286 Hz. The overall centroid matches only by coincidence, because the later whistle and tones are bright.

differences.a: Noisy and broadband (flatness 0.12), with a rattly, scrapey, resonant texture and no sustained pure tone, apart from a faint thin line near 8-9 kHz.
differences.b: More tonal (flatness 0.067). It has a held low-frequency tone block, a sustained sine near 1.2 kHz from 0.33 to 0.67 s, and harmonic lines at about 3.6, 5.5 and 9 kHz. It reads as an electronic beep or controller sound rather than metal.

differences.a: Sharp broadband thunk transient at 0.05-0.09 s, peak near -2 dBFS, crest 21 dB. The transient is crisp and wideband, with a second clunk at 0.26 s that is brighter and reaches several kHz.
differences.b: The first hit has a soft, slow onset and no crack, just a low thud rising from 0.05 s. Its peak lands at 0.32 s on the second hit, so the loudest event is in the wrong place. The peak is -5.9 dBFS, crest 18.7 dB.

differences.a: Fairly steady moderate level through about 0.6 s with a second bump at 0.26 s. -20 dB at 0.42 s, -40 dB at 0.64 s, a gradual rattly decay.
differences.b: The first block is flat-topped and cuts off abruptly at about 0.28 s. Decay to -20 dB and -40 dB both happen by 0.3-0.33 s relative to the peak, so the tail drops off a cliff, then a thin sine tone lingers to 0.67 s. The envelope has a gated, synthetic shape.

differences.a: Latch thunk, rattly metal scrape or creak, second hinge clunk, then a decaying rattle tail with a faint high whistle.
differences.b: Low thud, a short noisy burst, a second hit with a pitched ping, and a sustained sine. There is no real scrape, creak or rattle detail, and the pings are too clean.

differences.a: 0.83 s, onset 0.05 s, second onset 0.26 s, 0.1 s trailing silence.
differences.b: 0.83 s, onsets 0.05 and 0.27 s, so the timing is close. The first hit starts a little softly, and active sound stops at about 0.68 s, leaving 0.13 s of silence.

differences.a: Slow rattly decay with sparse mid and high texture to about 0.65 s, then fading.
differences.b: Almost dry after 0.5 s apart from the whistle line, with little rattling decay. The tail is thin and sparse.

differences.a: Peak -2.1 dBFS, -22.2 LUFS, RMS -23.4.
differences.b: Peak -5.9 dBFS, -22.6 LUFS, RMS -24.6. The LUFS match is fine, but the peak is lower than the brief's -1 dBFS ceiling suggests, and the loudness is carried by the sustained bass.

differences.a: No pitch movement and no clear pitch, just resonant noise.
differences.b: A static low tone and a prominent fixed 1.2 kHz sine make it sound pitched, which is not part of the original character.

change_notes: Remove or heavily reduce the 1.2 kHz sustained sine and its harmonic pings. If a metallic ring is kept, make it a short 3-4 mode inharmonic partial set (for example 780, 1310 and 2150 Hz), 60-120 ms decay, at -25 dB under the clunk.

Rebuild the first hit as a latch thunk. Add a 2-5 kHz noise crack of 10-15 ms at 0.05 s, with a 3 ms attack, at +6 dB over the body. Follow it with a 250-500 Hz band-passed noise and sine body, 100 ms decay, and peak it near -2 dBFS at 0.09 s.
Cut the bass block. High-pass the thump at about 120 Hz, drop the 40-100 Hz content by 12-15 dB, and target roughly 9% bass, 44% low-mid and 38% mid. Move the body centre up to 300-600 Hz.

Add a scrape or creak layer from 0.15 to 0.26 s: band-passed noise at 800-2500 Hz, with 15-25 Hz amplitude modulation or a stick-slip pulse train, and a slowly sweeping resonant filter (900 to 1400 Hz). Level about -10 dB under the thunk.

Make the second clunk at 0.26 s a brighter metal knock, with a 1-6 kHz noise burst of 20 ms plus a 400 Hz body decaying in 120 ms. Keep it about 3 dB below the first hit so the loudest event is at about 0.09 s, not 0.32 s.

Replace the abrupt gate with a rattle tail from 0.35 to 0.65 s: 5-8 sparse micro-clicks, band-passed at 1-4 kHz, with random spacing of 20-50 ms and falling in level by about 20 dB by 0.42 s and 40 dB by 0.64 s. Fade smoothly to silence by 0.73 s.
Optionally add a very quiet, thin 8-9 kHz whistle line at 0.4-0.55 s, at about -45 dB, to echo the original. Add per-trigger variation of +/-5% pitch and +/-10 ms timing.
Keep the render at 44.1 kHz and the length at 0.83 s. Normalise to -22 LUFS with the peak at or below -1 dBFS (about -2 dBFS, in line with A's -2.1).

review.summary: B is a similar-length, similar-loudness impact, but it is a single smooth boom with a decaying noise tail and one sustained tonal tick. A is a crunchy noise burst with stuttered low thuds, a downward sweep and a thin 780 Hz ring. B fills the role roughly but lacks A's multi-thud punch and metallic ring.

differences.a: Noise crack with a faint descending sweep (300-600 Hz) and 2-3 separate heavy thuds below 150 Hz at about 0.08-0.12, 0.17-0.24 and 0.26-0.33 s.
differences.b: One continuous low-frequency block (about 40-250 Hz) running from about 0.06 s to 0.41 s, with no separate thuds and no downward sweep.

change_notes: Delete the 1 kHz tone layer (1.5-3.0 s) completely. If a tonal element is wanted, use a low 60-90 Hz sine that pitch-drops, not a mid-range whistle.

Add a sustained sub/bass body: sine or filtered noise at 30-120 Hz, with pitch dropping from 120 Hz to 40 Hz over 0.4 s, held at full level until 1.4 s, then faded to -20 dB by 1.6 s. Aim for sub (20-60 Hz) at about 25% of the energy and bass at about 18%, down from B's 73% in the 100 Hz region.

Add a wet granular layer: band-passed noise at 500 Hz-8 kHz, amplitude-modulated with random 10-40 ms grains (crackle density about 30-60/s), at -6 dB under the body from 0.05 to 1.5 s. Use a higher centroid early (about 3-5 kHz) and sweep the low-pass from 8 kHz to 2 kHz over 1.5-3.0 s.
Add 3 churn bursts: 40-80 ms noise at 0.87, 1.15 and 1.23 s (+3 dB over the bed), then 2 weaker ones at 2.39 and 2.58 s (-8 dB).

Replace the hard-edged tail: a single continuous dark noise/rumble (low-pass 400 Hz to 150 Hz) decaying exponentially to -40 dB at about 2.9 s and to silence at about 3.5 s. Do not restart the noise at 3.0 s, and add 20-50 ms fades at all layer boundaries.
Increase the spectral flatness from about 0.09 to about 0.3 by raising the noise-to-tone ratio, and lift the 85% rolloff from 1.8 kHz to about 6 kHz.

Keep the final level at about -16 LUFS with peak at or below -1 dBFS, and widen the loudness range from 2.4 to about 8 LU through the front-loaded decaying envelope. Keep mono and the 3.99 s length, with trailing silence from about 3.5 s.

review.summary: B matches A's overall length, loudness and initial noise burst, but its low end is a sustained 100-200 Hz drone lasting about 0.5 s instead of a short, punchy sub thud. It also adds a second ping hit, a click at about 0.55 s and a noisy burst at about 0.73-0.98 s that A does not have, so it reads as a different, longer, less focused impact.

differences.a: The tail fades smoothly to near silence. It is about -40 dB by 0.5 s, then quiet, with the last 0.3 s essentially empty.
differences.b: The body is cut off hard at about 0.55 s, followed by a dead gap from 0.56 to 0.72 s. A new broadband noise burst then appears from about 0.73 s to the end (centroid about 2.8 kHz in the last quarter, active_fraction 0.72), which reads as a stray artifact or second event.

differences.a: The energy is spread across sub 16%, bass 22%, low-mid 29% and mid 22%. It has strong thumps below 100 Hz plus noisy body up to about 6 kHz, and the centroid is about 1.3 kHz.
differences.b: Bass is 73%, sub only 1.6% and low-mid 6%. A dense 100-250 Hz hum dominates. The spectral rolloff is only about 1 kHz, so it sounds boomy and muddy, lacking both true sub weight and midrange body.

differences.a: A hit with a quick drop. The main body ends around 0.25-0.35 s and is -20 dB by about 0.12-0.25 s, then it falls steadily to -40 dB by 0.5 s.
differences.b: The level is held roughly flat at -13 to -16 dB from 0.05 to 0.35 s, then runs on as a sustained low drone to 0.55 s, followed by a sudden cliff to about -67 dB. It feels sustained and gated rather than a natural decay.

differences.a: One dense noise burst with a double sub thud at about 0.08-0.12 s and 0.18-0.3 s, a falling 600-250 Hz tonal sweep and a faint steady 800 Hz ring in the tail.
differences.b: Noise burst plus a long low drone, a short 1 kHz tone with a glide at 0.05-0.24 s, and a second ping at about 0.37-0.5 s with harmonic lines at about 1, 3.5, 7 and 10 kHz. It also has a pre-hit falling sweep from 450 to 250 Hz before 0.07 s and a click at about 0.55 s. The elements are more numerous, synthetic and tonal.

differences.a: There is a very quiet lead-in tick up to about 0.05 s, then an abrupt full-band noise attack with an edgy crack. The peak is about 0 dBFS at about 0.12 s.
differences.b: The attack also starts at about 0.05 s with a broadband burst, which is good, but it is preceded by an audible falling-tone pre-sweep (450 to 250 Hz) rather than a tick. The transient is less crack-like and more smeared by the low drone. The peak is -3 dBFS.

differences.a: A brief falling tonal sweep from about 600 Hz to 250 Hz inside the body, then a faint steady ring at about 800 Hz.
differences.b: A static, slightly falling 1 kHz tone during the burst, a separate 1 kHz ping later, and an extra pre-hit sweep from 450 to 250 Hz. The pitch events are in the wrong place and register.

differences.a: Noise-dominated with some tone (flatness 0.19).
differences.b: More tonal and pulsing (flatness 0.058). The drone shows a periodic amplitude beat or buzz in the waveform, and the late pings are sine-like.

differences.a: The active sound is about 0.7 s, with 0.3 s of trailing silence. There is a single event cluster.

Replace the 100-250 Hz sustained drone with two short sub thumps: a sine falling from 100 Hz to 45 Hz over 120 ms at 0.07 s, and a second at 0.19 s falling from 90 to 40 Hz over 150 ms, about 2 dB quieter. Use an exponential decay (time constant about 60 ms) so they are gone by about 0.35 s. This should raise sub energy to about 15% and cut bass from 73% to about 22%.

Rebuild the body as band-passed noise (300 Hz to 6 kHz, centroid about 1.5 kHz) from 0.05 to 0.25 s. Use a 2 ms attack, about 80 ms decay to -20 dB, and a 0.35 s tail to -40 dB. Add a low-mid emphasis of +4 dB at 400-900 Hz to lift low-mid to about 29% and mid to about 22%.
Add a quick noise crack of 2-5 kHz, about 15 ms, at 0.05 s, +4 dB over the body. Replace the pre-hit falling tone with a very quiet 2-3 ms click at 0.0-0.04 s, about -35 dB.

Remove the 1 kHz static tone and the second ping at 0.37 s. Add a falling sine sweep from 600 Hz to 250 Hz over 150 ms at 0.06 s, -18 dB under the noise. Add a faint 800 Hz sine ring from 0.25 to 0.7 s, decaying to -45 dB, at about -35 dB relative to the peak.

Reduce the noisiness gap: raise the noise floor of the body so flatness is about 0.15-0.2, and drop the sine harmonics at 3.5, 7 and 10 kHz. Keep the rolloff 85% near 2.3 kHz with a low-pass at about 6 kHz.
Keep the peak at about -1 dBFS and the integrated loudness at about -19 LUFS. Raise the peak by 2 dB after reshaping, since the crest factor will rise with sharper thumps.

review.summary: B follows A's rough event order (thud, clicks, thumps with beeps, long beep, tail) and matches length and RMS, but it is darker, tonally pitched and sustained, with a loud white-noise hiss tail and a wrong-pitch beep. It reads as a synthy sequence rather than a crunchy stick-on plant with sparse foley.

differences.b: No rustle or foley. 0.38-0.5 s has a few narrow high-frequency ticks only, then a gap.

change_notes: Replace the tail: start the hiss tail at 0.97 s at about -40 dB (not -14 dB), lowpass at 4 kHz, and fade to under -60 dB by 1.4 s. Do not use a bright 10 kHz+ noise burst, and leave ~0.09 s of silence at the end.

Retune all beeps to ~4.5 kHz square or sine. Use three 40-50 ms beeps at 0.69, 0.75 and 0.80 s, then one 80-100 ms beep at 0.89-0.97 s with 3 ms fades. Remove the 1.05 kHz sustained line and the 650 Hz final beep, or drop them 25 dB.

Rebuild the opening 0-0.15 s as a noise slap: white noise bandpassed 300 Hz-6 kHz with a 2 ms attack and 80 ms exponential decay (-20 dB by 0.1 s), plus a 60-150 Hz sine thump (150 to 50 Hz over 120 ms) at +3 dB. Add 1-2 kHz crunch and a soft clip so the peak stays around -1 dBFS.

Make the 0.21 and 0.28 s events real clicks: 5-10 ms bursts of noise highpassed at 2 kHz (extending to 10 kHz), each with a 80-120 Hz thump body of ~60 ms. Replace the descending 300 to 150 Hz tone sweeps (shorten them to under 100 ms and lower them by ~15 dB).

Under the beeps (0.62-0.88 s) use 3-4 separate 100-200 Hz thumps (60-80 ms each) with 1-3 kHz noise bursts at about -20 dB, and drop the continuous flat wall of sound. Bring that section down from -12 dB to about -18 to -22 dB so the opening hit is the loudest event.

review.summary: B is a reasonable sci-fi blaster with similar length, loudness and overall decay, but its energy sits in a narrower bass band with a clean downward-sweeping zap, and it lacks A's sub weight, gritty noise, mid-range metallic body and the secondary bump. Its tail also fades earlier and darker.

differences.b: Almost no sub (0.6%) with bass at 48%, concentrated at roughly 40-250 Hz, and low-mid only 6.5%, giving a hollow gap between the bass and the mids.

differences.a: Metallic mid tonal smears at ~700-1500 Hz from 0.4 to 1.0 s, plus thin 4-8 kHz zap streaks near 0.35-0.5 s that give the sound its character.

differences.a: Noisy, crackly broadband burst; the peak comes at ~0.1 s and the level stays strong until ~0.3 s (-14.7, -13.1 dB per tenth).

differences.a: Holds strong for ~0.3 s, then -27 dB at 0.3 s, -39 dB at 0.5 s, and a long gentle tail reaching -66 dB at 0.9 s.

differences.a: Rumbling noise tail with a bump near 0.66 s, highs lasting to ~1.4 s, and a centroid of ~550-800 Hz in the tail.

Reduce the sweep layer: lower the falling sweeps by ~6 dB and shorten them to 0.2 s, and add a short 4-8 kHz zap of 100-150 ms at 0.35 s (falling 8 kHz to 4 kHz) so the laser reads as an accent, not the main body.

review.summary: B matches A's length (1.75 s) and rough loudness, but it is a flat, sustained noise bed with a slow 0.06 s swell and no discrete blast, where A is a punchy, heavily clipped, bass-heavy explosion that decays steadily into a rumble. B is brighter, less punchy and less dynamic, and its tail is abruptly cut.

differences.a: Near-instant blast peaking at 0.04 s, with a bright crack over the boom. Opening 10% is -28.7 dB, then -1.9 dB, so the hit is a sharp spike.
differences.b: Starts at about -7 dB with no punch and a 0.06 s attack. It reads as a continuous noise bed, with no distinct crack or boom hit.

differences.a: Holds near full level to about 0.5 s, then falls steadily: -20 dB at 0.96 s, -40 dB at 1.5 s, natural rumble fade.

differences.a: Bass-dominated: bass 70%, sub 16%, centroid 250 Hz, rolloff 215 Hz. Mids and highs are minimal.
differences.b: Sub 50%, bass only 17.5%, mid and above about 28%. Centroid 876 Hz, rolloff 1270 Hz, so it is much brighter and hissier, with a hollow region between 100 and 400 Hz and bright vertical bands to 10 kHz.

differences.a: Crack, then a saturated bass roar with irregular debris crackle, then secondary bumps at 0.68, 0.82 and 1.22 s.

differences.a: Heavily clipped, saturated and dense, with an organic crackly rumble.
differences.b: Clean, with a lower crest factor (6 dB against 10 dB), uniform and synthetic. Reads as a droning or buzzy noise, not a blast.

change_notes: Add a blast transient at t=0: a 30 ms broadband noise burst with a 1-3 ms attack and a fast exponential decay. Make it about 6 dB above the body, with the first 0.04 s peaking near -1 dBFS. Cut the current 60 ms swell-in.
Replace the flat noise bed with a decaying envelope: hold about 0.4 s near full level, then fall about -20 dB by 0.95 s and -40 dB by 1.5 s. Use an exponential curve, not the current 1.0-1.55 s ramp.

Add a bass boom: a sine plus soft-clipped triangle falling from about 110 Hz to 40 Hz over 0.5 s, with a decay of about 0.8 s. Make bass (60-250 Hz) about 65-70% of the energy and reduce sub to about 15%, shifting weight up from the current 50% sub.

Low-pass the noise layer: start at about 4 kHz, sweep to about 300 Hz over 1.2 s, and cut the sustained 4-10 kHz hiss. Target a centroid of about 250-300 Hz and a rolloff of about 250 Hz, and cut mid and above to under 5% of the energy.

Remove the regular amplitude modulation. Replace it with irregular random crackle bursts (5-15 ms grains at random times through 0.1-0.7 s, 1-3 kHz, dropping in level over time), and add 3 small bumps at 0.68, 0.82 and 1.22 s (+4-6 dB, 40-80 ms low-passed noise or thump).
Drive the sum through a soft-clip or limiter for a crest factor of about 9-10 dB and a loudness of about -9 LUFS, peak at -1 dBFS. Don't hard-clip; avoid DC offset.
Finish with a 150-250 ms fade-out ending by about 1.6 s so the cut has no click, and keep the last 0.13 s silent.

review.summary: B matches A's overall length (1.4 s), loudness (-18.0 vs -17.5 LUFS) and noisy broadband gunshot role, but is built differently: it carries a strong, sustained 60-200 Hz tonal boom with an amplitude-modulated, humming tail, while A is a dense noise rumble with a bright crack and a hard cutoff at about 1.25 s.

differences.a: Energy spread across sub, bass and low-mid (8.9/29/27.7%), mid 18%, presence 9.5%. Centroid is about 1.6 kHz and rolloff about 3.7 kHz, with bright content to a 10 kHz lowpass throughout the first half.
differences.b: 74.5% of energy in a single bass band, with almost no sub or low-mid (0.5/4.3%). Rolloff is 2.5 kHz, and the centroid falls from 1080 Hz to about 60 Hz by the last quarter. Highs decay much faster and the sound ends up as a pure low hum.

differences.a: Almost entirely noise, with a dense, chaotic rumble and no steady tones.
differences.b: A clear tonal band at about 80-250 Hz with a regular pulsing, comb-like vertical striping. The tail reads as a sustained low sine or buzz, a synth-like boom rather than a blast.

differences.a: Loud for the first 0.15 s, then a steady smooth decay (-20 dB at 0.66 s, -40 dB at 1.09 s) that stops abruptly at about 1.25 s.
differences.b: -20 dB at 0.72 s and -40 dB at 1.22 s, so a slightly longer decay. It fades gradually to the end with no hard cutoff, and the waveform shows visible amplitude beating or pulsing in the tail.

differences.a: Near-instant broadband burst with a bright crack up to about 10 kHz. It is dense, sustained noise rather than a single click.
differences.b: A fast attack (peak at 0.02 s) and bright content in the first 100 ms, but the crack is shorter and weaker. The low boom dominates the onset, and the early high-mid body is thinner.

differences.a: A fluttering, reflection-like low-mid rumble (200-1000 Hz) fading out over about 1 s, with highs dying first.
differences.b: The tail is a narrow sub-100 Hz hum with sparse mids and highs. It lacks the diffuse reflection-like rumble, and the high-frequency noise falls away early (below -75 dB past about 0.9 s).

differences.a: No pitch movement; unpitched noise.

differences.b: Strongly tonal: a persistent ~1.3 kHz ping on nearly every event, a ~4.5 kHz partial, a ~900 Hz and ~2.3 kHz bar around 0.58 s, and harmonic lines up to 12 kHz. Flatness 0.39.

differences.b: A big 20-300 Hz thump around 0.53-0.65 s, the loudest part of the spectrogram, plus 16.6% low-mid. Centroid 5.0 kHz and rolloff 10 kHz, so a bit darker overall.

differences.a: Two swells: a first burst peaking ~0.52-0.56 s, a quiet lull at 0.64-0.72 s, a second long burst 0.78-0.9 s with rattly texture, and a final click at 0.94 s. Each decays in ~0.05 s.

A is a sustained, turbulent, noisy rumble that holds near peak for about 0.3 s and keeps a bright haze and secondary bumps through about 1.2 s. B ends too early and is too smooth and too dark.

review.summary: B has the right length, one-shot structure and overall loudness, but it is darker and much more bass-heavy than A, with a duller crack and a shorter, thinner tail. It reads as a boomy cannon or explosion, not A's bright, mid-rich rifle report.

differences.b: Centroid about 1.0 kHz, rolloff85 only 1.7 kHz. Bass is 62% and sub 12.5%, and low-mid/mid are only 7-9% each. It sounds boomy and muffled.

review.summary: B follows A's rough 3.4 s, multi-stage layout (three ticks, a noisy burst near 0.5 s, a middle section, a late low hit), but it is built from different material. A is a set of crisp, bright clacks and a rattly mid-heavy thunk with a long hiss tail. B has near-inaudible ticks, a sustained noise-and-tone plateau, and two big sub-bass thumps that dominate the spectrum.

differences.a: Almost no bass (0.4%). Energy is mid 29%, presence 25% and air 36%. The late thud sits at about 200-500 Hz.
differences.b: 39% of energy is in the bass band, mostly two big 40-150 Hz thumps at 1.4 s and 1.65 s. Mid energy is only 8%, so the sound is much more sub-heavy and the mid-range mechanical body is thin.

differences.a: Discrete clacks and snaps at 0.89, 1.01, 1.09 and 1.17 s, plus a wet slide with a 200-2000 Hz body at 0.53 s.
differences.b: A sustained, flat noise block from 0.9 to 1.2 s, with a few narrow tonal beeps near 1.6 kHz (peak at 1641 Hz). It reads as an electronic hiss, not as snapping parts. Sparse clicks only start after the thumps.

differences.a: Every event has a sharp, bright transient. Crest factor is 26 dB and the loudest event is the clack at 1.09 s.
differences.b: The three opening ticks are tiny, thin vertical lines that are barely audible. The 0.5 s burst has a soft onset. Crest factor is 18.6 dB and the peak is only -11.8 dBFS, compared with -4 dBFS for A.

differences.a: Each hit decays over tens of ms to about 0.3 s. The tail is a rattly mid-high hiss that fades by about 2.9 s.
differences.b: The noise block has a plateau envelope and then cuts off abruptly. The sub thumps ring for about 0.3 s each, and the tail after 1.9 s is a thin hiss with a hard stop at about 2.9 s. The shape is blocky, not a set of snappy hits.

differences.a: No pitch movement. All content is noise and clicks.
differences.b: Narrow tonal beeps at about 1.6 kHz and a pitched sub-bass tone make it sound synthetic or sci-fi. The thumps hold a steady low pitch with no decay sweep.

differences.a: Almost pure broadband noise and clicks (flatness 0.003, skewed by the clicks).
differences.b: Flatness is 0.043, with a noise plateau plus tonal beeps and bass tones. It sounds more electronic than mechanical.

differences.a: The click cluster at 0.89-1.17 s is followed by a thud at 1.25-1.8 s. Sparse clicks run to 2.5 s. Duration is 3.42 s, with a 0.63 s silent tail.

B also has a more pulsed, rattly texture and less bass weight.

differences.a: Fast onset at 0.05 s, with a loud rev reached by about 0.1 s (-16.6 dB in the 0.1 s bin) and peak at 0.19 s.
differences.b: Slow fade-in: -38 dB at 0.1 s, -29 dB at 0.2 s, and the attack is 0.57 s with peak at 0.59 s. It reads as a swell, not a rev-up hit.

review.summary: B has a similar punchy onset and matching loudness (-22.4 vs -22.3 LUFS), but it is bass-heavy and darker, with a tail that dies by about 1.3 s. A has a long, bright, noisy, reverberant tail lasting about 2 s, so B is a boomy thud rather than a rifle crack plus room.

B is a recognisable single rifle shot at a similar peak and loudness, but it is bassier and darker, and its tail dies about 0.6 s sooner. It lacks A's long, smooth reverberant decay and its bright, noisy crack.

differences.a: Long, smooth, dark reverb tail. Falls to -40 dB at about 1.15 s, with audible energy to roughly 1.3 s and a faint residual beyond that, which is a room-like decay.
differences.b: Tail collapses sooner. -40 dB at about 0.75 s, and the envelope hits digital silence by about 0.8-0.9 s. The spectrogram shows content ending around 1.7 s, which is much quieter than A's tail.

differences.a: -20 dB at 0.4 s and -40 dB at 1.15 s. A gradual, smooth slope with a long low-level shoulder (-47 to -78 dB across 0.5-0.9 s of the active region).

review.summary: B matches A's length (1.31 s) and loudness (-13.2 vs -13.0 LUFS) but is a clean, tonal, rising sine-like sweep that builds slowly to a late peak and cuts off. A is a noisy, turbulent sub rumble that swells in 0.1 s, holds, then decays. The role and feel do not match.

differences.a: Jumps from -36 dB to about -9 dB within 0.1 s, holds -9 to -14 dB until about 0.7 s, then falls to -20 dB at 0.73 s and -40 dB at 0.98 s, with a faint tail to 1.3 s.

differences.b: Almost purely tonal: two clean sweeping partials, flatness 0.004, peaks at 352, 773 and 1547 Hz. It sounds like a synth or laser tone, not a rumble.

differences.b: Peak -1.8 dBFS, RMS -26.5 dB, -22.1 LUFS. The loudest hit is the bolt group at 2.76 s, and the noise bed raises the RMS. The overall level is close, but the hierarchy is wrong.

differences.a: The 2.0 s magazine seat is the loudest, most prominent event. The 2.59-2.84 s bolt group is strong, and the 0.54-0.71 s group is a rattly mag release.
differences.b: The 2.0 s event is a single ping, quieter than the 2.6-2.9 s group. The bolt group is louder and ringier. The 0.5-0.8 s group has 4 pings. The late 2.97 s onset has no counterpart in A.

differences.a: Centroid 6.8 kHz and rising over the clip (4.3 to 7.6 kHz). Energy is 25% mid, 29% presence, 42% air and very little below 250 Hz.
differences.b: Centroid 5.8 kHz and falling (6.6, 10.0, 5.2, 4.1 kHz). Energy is 42% mid, 23% presence, 27% air and 8% low-mid. It is heavier in the mids because of the 0.9-1.5 kHz ping resonances, with less air.
Onsets match closely, with the main groups within 10-20 ms. It adds 0.81 and 0.97 s onsets, and the early clicks at 0.08-0.19 s are barely audible. The overall timing skeleton is good.

review.summary: B matches A's length (2.95 s), loudness (-19.9 vs -19.6 LUFS) and rough event layout, including the gap near 1.2 s and a two-hit finish. But the events are clean, ringing tonal pings with big silent gaps, where A is a dense, gritty cluster of noisy metallic handling transients. It reads as synthetic bells and beeps rather than a shotgun reload.

differences.a: Gritty, noisy metallic and plastic handling clacks with broadband scrape and rattle; flatness 0.005 in the measurements, but the sound is a dense mechanical cluster.
differences.b: Clean synthetic pings with sustained pure partials near 1.1 kHz, 2.2 kHz, 3.3 kHz and 4.5 kHz and harmonic lines up to 10 kHz. Qwen heard sine/beep-bleep tones. Flatness is 0.354.

differences.a: Sharp fast-attack transients with 0.2-0.3 s decays and tiny tails.
differences.b: Percussive hits with long smooth exponential ring-outs, bell- or pluck-like. The final hits ring audibly longer. -20 dB decay is 0.12 s, but the tonal ring is perceptually longer.

differences.a: Continuous sequence of many small events: handling ticks, a cluster of shell-insert clacks, a click-clack at 1.34 s, a scraping rattle at 1.6-2.3 s, then a heavy two-part pump finish. 23 onsets.
differences.b: Only 17 onsets, sparse and clearly separated. The 0.4-0.7 s clack cluster is missing entirely, with a hole from 0.35 to 0.74 s. A 200-300 Hz sine-like boom at 0.75 s has no counterpart in A. Little scrape or rattle texture.

differences.a: Activity runs almost continuously from 0.05 to 1.2 s, then from 1.3 to 2.8 s. The only gap is a short one near 1.2 s. Final clacks at 2.51 s and 2.67 s, followed by a short tail.
differences.b: Long dead gaps at 0.35-0.74 s and 0.9-1.19 s, and a gap at 2.3-2.45 s. Final hits at 2.49 s and 2.69 s are well placed, but the gaps make the reload feel disjointed.

review.summary: B is a similar-length (1.62 s) low chainsaw drone at near-matching loudness, but it swells smoothly over about 0.75 s with a fairly steady pulse. A has a quick fade-in and 4 distinct rev surges with deep dips and a clear 700 Hz harmonic band. B has the right role and weight but lacks A's surge structure and harmonic definition.

differences.a: Reaches full level within about 0.05-0.1 s, then holds at roughly -18 to -23 dB with a gentle fade from about 1.2 s to the end of the clip.
differences.b: Slow fade-in from -37 dB at 0.1 s to -20 dB at 0.3 s, peaking at 0.76 s, then a symmetrical fade-out. It looks like a lens or spindle shape.

differences.a: 4 distinct rev surges (about 0.05-0.3, 0.38-0.5, 0.56-0.8, 0.85-1.2 s) with dips of 3-6 dB or deeper, especially the one near 0.8 s. This gives a swing and rev feel.
differences.b: A single continuous swell with fast, shallow flutter (about 20-25 Hz striations) and no clear surge or dip structure.

differences.a: Bass and low-mid are 66% of energy with a strong 60-200 Hz body. A bright harmonic band near 600-800 Hz and harmonics up to 2-3 kHz give a clear pitched ladder.
differences.b: Energy leans to the mid band (40% vs 23% in A). Bass is lower (24% vs 33%) and sub is almost absent. The harmonic band is smeared with no distinct 700 Hz line, so it sounds darker and more muddy.

differences.a: Very tonal (flatness about 0). Rough, buzzy harmonics with a high-frequency noise layer that is weak but present.
differences.b: More noise-like (flatness 0.015) with a broadband smeared texture. Weaker tonal definition.

differences.a: Starts quickly with an onset at 0.05 s, so the swing feels immediate.

differences.a: Wobbling pitch, with the drone around 70-100 Hz moving a few Hz between surges, which gives a rev feel.
differences.b: Steady pitch with no audible rev movement.

Raise the level by about 1-2 dB so the peak is near -4.5 dBFS and loudness is about -18.6 LUFS. Keep it mono.

review.summary: B is a steady, rhythmically pulsing bass drone at near-constant level for about 1.2 s that ends in an abrupt fade, while A is a one-shot bite with a swell to a peak at 0.23 s and a long, thinning decay. Length and loudness match, but the envelope, sub weight and overall role (a single impact) do not.

differences.a: Swells from near silence to a peak at about 0.23 s, then decays steadily: -20 dB at 0.72 s, -40 dB at 1.04 s, fading into a thin tail.
differences.b: Sustained plateau at -12 to -18 dB from 0 to about 1.2 s with no real decay, then a sudden drop to silence in the last 0.1-0.15 s (-20 dB at 0.87 s, -40 dB at 0.94 s). Reads as a running engine, not a hit.

differences.a: Soft swell of about 0.2 s with a single onset at 0.05 s, with no click. The densest, loudest grit falls at 0.2-0.5 s.
differences.b: Starts at full level (-16 dB in the first tenth), with no onset and no bite or impact moment. The peak comes at 0.37 s but is barely above the plateau.

differences.a: One continuous growl: heavy sub/bass rumble plus gritty mid noise up to about 2 kHz with irregular chain-like modulation, and a fluttering tail.
differences.b: Regular periodic pulse train, about 50-60 pulses over 1.2 s (roughly 45-50 Hz), like a mechanical motor idle or comb pattern. No distinct impact or chop layer and no irregular grit.

differences.a: Sub 22.5%, bass 33%, low-mid 25%, mid 13%. Strong energy down to 20 Hz and a centroid of about 693 Hz that rises to about 1.3 kHz mid-sound and falls to about 516 Hz in the tail.
differences.b: Sub only 1.8%, bass 67%, low-mid 19%, mid 8%. Heavy energy at about 60-200 Hz but little true sub. Centroid is static at about 650-720 Hz. Rolloff is 732 Hz versus 1184 Hz in A, so the midrange grit is thinner.

differences.a: Rough, random, chewing, with vertical streaks of uneven width. It sounds like a saw biting into something.
differences.b: Clean, regular and tonal-buzzy (flatness 0.033). Reads as a uniform engine hum or comb filter. A faint narrow tone near 1 kHz and a few thin lines at 4-12 kHz appear early on.

differences.a: Long, thinning, lowpassed tail with highs fading over time, ending near 1.27 s.
differences.b: No tail: the body stops abruptly at about 1.2 s with only about 0.1 s of fade. Highs stay broadband up to the end.

differences.a: 1.335 s total, about 0.01 s of leading silence and 0.06 s trailing.
differences.b: 1.34 s, no leading silence and 0.03 s trailing. Total length matches, but the energy is spread evenly where A's is front-loaded.

change_notes: Replace the flat amplitude with an explicit envelope: 0.01 s start from -50 dB, ramp to peak at 0.23 s (about 0.2 s exponential rise), then decay -20 dB by 0.72 s and -40 dB by 1.04 s, ending at about 1.27 s. Drop the 1.2 s plateau and the abrupt cutoff.
Add a sub layer: sine or lowpassed saw at 40-60 Hz (LPF at 120 Hz) to lift sub energy from 2% to about 20%, level about +6 dB over the current bass at the peak, decaying with the main envelope.
Make the pulse modulation irregular: jitter the pulse rate at 40-70 Hz by +/-30% with random depth of 30-60%, and slow it toward the tail (to about 25 Hz by 1 s) so it flutters rather than idles.

Add a mid grit layer: bandpassed noise at 500 Hz-2 kHz with random chop modulation at 15-30 Hz, rising to peak with the body at 0.2-0.5 s (+3 to +4 dB over the current mid), then decaying faster than the bass.
Add a short 40-80 ms impact (noise burst 300 Hz-3 kHz plus a 100 Hz thump) at about 0.05 s, +4 dB over the body, to give the bite a defined moment.
Apply a time-varying lowpass: cutoff about 3 kHz at the peak sweeping to about 600 Hz by 1.1 s, so the tail darkens and the centroid falls from about 1.2 kHz to about 500 Hz.

Remove the narrow 1 kHz tone and filter everything above about 8 kHz (12 dB/oct) so highs stay minimal. Keep peak near -3 dBFS and about -16 LUFS integrated, with a 10-20 ms fade-in at the start and no click.

review.summary: B is a flat, constant, midrange-buzzy drone with harmonic structure, while A is a sub-heavy churning rumble that swells in over 0.3 s and fades out by the end. Length and loudness match, but the envelope, tonal balance and character differ a lot.

differences.a: Symmetrical swell: starts near silence (-44 dB), reaches about -8 dB by 0.2-0.3 s, holds, then fades to -20 dB by 0.9 s and -34 dB at the end.
differences.b: Flat from 0 s to the end (about -10.5 dB, within ±1.5 dB). There is no fade-in or fade-out, and it is on at full level from sample 0.

differences.a: Sub and bass dominated: 56% sub, 33% bass, centroid about 290 Hz, rolloff 141 Hz. Almost nothing above 500 Hz.
differences.b: 0% sub, 58% bass, 28% low-mid, 9% mid. Centroid about 874 Hz and rolloff 938 Hz, so it is much brighter and thinner, with no deep rumble.

differences.a: Centroid rises from about 150 Hz to about 450 Hz as the swell opens. There are no discrete tonal peaks.
differences.b: Fixed harmonic stack with peaks at about 305, 328 and 656 Hz, and visible harmonic lines up to about 2 kHz. The centroid drifts only from 729 to 1000 Hz. It sounds like a pitched engine or hum.

differences.a: Gritty, churning rumble with irregular, deep amplitude modulation (vertical striations, crest 7.8 dB, spiky waveform). It reads as an energy beam or boomy rumble.
differences.b: Uniform, stationary buzz with a regular fine comb or striation pattern and a low-contrast noise-like waveform. It reads as an idling engine, with no churn or irregular bursts.

differences.a: Noise-like rough rumble with only a faint hissy veil above 1 kHz (about 4% of energy).
differences.b: Tonal and harmonic in the 300-2000 Hz region, with a steady noise floor above 2.5 kHz that is clearly stronger (5% in presence and air). The spectrum has a hard cutoff at about 2.3 kHz.

differences.a: 1.008 s, with about 0.01 s of leading silence and a faded start and end.
differences.b: 1.01 s, with no silence and a hard start and end. The length matches.

differences.a: Faded ends, so the loop has a pulsing seam, which is intended for chained variants.
differences.b: The loop has a constant level but a hard-cut start and end. Repeats may click or phase-jump, but the level is steady.

differences.a: -11.0 LUFS, peak -0.6 dBFS, RMS -8.4 dB.

change_notes: Add a sub rumble layer: filtered noise or a saw with a lowpass at 100 Hz and a sine or triangle at 40-60 Hz. Make it about 55% of the energy, so the overall centroid is about 290 Hz and the rolloff is about 140 Hz.
Cut the 300-700 Hz harmonic buzz by about 20 dB and lowpass it at 400 Hz. Remove the 305/328/656 Hz peaks and the harmonics above 1 kHz. Target under 5% of energy above 500 Hz.
Apply an amplitude envelope: 0.3 s ease-in from -44 dB to -8 dB, hold at -5 to -8 dB until 0.8 s, then fade to -20 dB at 0.9 s and about -35 dB at 1.0 s. Add a small dip around 0.8 s.

Add churn: modulate the bass layer's amplitude with random or noise-driven LFO at 20-40 Hz, depth 50-70% (about 10-15 dB), to raise the crest factor from 9 to about 7.8 dB. Use random modulation instead of a periodic comb.
Sweep the lowpass cutoff on the bass layer from about 150 Hz at 0 s to about 450 Hz at 0.4 s, then hold. This reproduces the rising centroid.
Add a faint hiss above 2 kHz at -35 to -45 dB relative to the body, 4% of energy, and fade it with the main envelope. Remove the hard 2.3 kHz cutoff.
Keep the 1.0 s length. Make the fade shapes match so chained variants crossfade smoothly. Normalise to about -11 LUFS with the peak at or below -1 dBFS.

review.summary: B is a flat, steady, mid-heavy buzz with no fade in/out, while A is a sub-heavy rumble that fades in and out of near silence with irregular crackly pulses. Loudness and length match, but the spectral balance and envelope differ, and B would not crossfade or loop like A.

differences.a: Dominated by sub and bass: 60% sub, 28% bass, centroid ~261 Hz, 85% rolloff ~141 Hz. Almost nothing above 1 kHz.
differences.b: No sub energy (0%), 51% bass, 32% low-mid, 11% mid. Centroid ~974 Hz, rolloff ~1.2 kHz, about 3.7x brighter. The spectrogram shows a strong band at 600-1000 Hz and a comb of harmonics up to ~2.5 kHz.

differences.a: Fades in from about -39 dB in the first tenth, sustains around -6 to -10 dB, peaks near 0.52 s, then fades to about -35 dB in the last tenth.
differences.b: Flat at -10 to -13 dB from the first sample to the last, with no fades. Active fraction is 1.0 and the peak at 0.54 s is incidental.

differences.a: Both ends fade to near silence, so it crossfades or alternates smoothly with other loop variants.
differences.b: Starts and ends at full level. Looped back to back it will likely click or sound like a hard seam, and it can't be crossfaded the way A is.

differences.a: Rough, crackly, irregular amplitude flutter in the low band. Vertical streaks in the spectrogram and large waveform bursts give an organic, unstable energy-beam rumble.
differences.b: Regular, tight, machine-like pulsing (visible as evenly spaced ticks and a harmonic comb). It sounds like an engine or idle machinery, as Qwen noted, rather than an energy beam.

differences.a: Irregular bursts, including onsets at 0.05, 0.17 and 0.89 s, with crest factor 7.8 dB.
differences.b: No onsets, but a constant fine pulse train in the waveform. Crest factor is 9.7 dB, with narrow spikes over a constant noise bed.

differences.a: No pitch movement. Centroid rises from ~190 Hz to ~400 Hz as the sound swells, with no distinct tonal peaks.
differences.b: No pitch movement, but it has distinct tonal peaks at 234, 352 and 375 Hz with a fixed harmonic structure. The centroid is ~860-1100 Hz.

differences.a: Mostly low-frequency rumble with only a faint noisy haze above 1 kHz (about 4% of energy above 500 Hz).
differences.b: Brighter noise bed plus harmonic tone. 16% of energy is in mid/presence/air, with a visible hiss band up to 10 kHz+.

differences.a: -11.4 LUFS, peak -0.7 dBFS, RMS -8.6 dB.
differences.b: -11.6 LUFS, peak -1.6 dBFS, RMS -11.3 dB. Integrated loudness matches, though B is carried by mids, which would sound louder and harsher at the same LUFS, and it has less sub weight.

differences.a: No true tail; the fade-out at the end is about 0.1 s.
differences.b: No tail and no fade, so it ends abruptly.

change_notes: Rebuild the spectral balance: add a sub layer of 40-70 Hz sine/triangle at about -6 dB relative to the full mix, then a bass layer at 80-200 Hz. Together these should be about 85-90% of the energy. Low-pass everything else at ~300 Hz with a 24 dB/oct slope, and bring the centroid down from ~974 Hz to ~260-400 Hz.
Remove or cut by 20 dB or more the 600-1000 Hz band and the harmonic comb at 234/352/375 Hz. Keep mids and highs at a combined 5% or less of energy.

Add fades at both ends: a 0-0.1 s fade-in from about -40 dB to full, and a 0.9-1.01 s fade-out back to about -35 dB. Start and end at zero crossings, with the fade shape the same at both ends so the loop crossfades cleanly.

differences.b: The 0.38 s hit has a long, flat low-frequency sustain of ~0.3 s (to ~0.68 s) and then a slow linear decay, like a synth drone. The waveform shows a smooth triangular tail instead of a snap. The decay to -20 dB takes 0.19 s versus A's 0.13 s.

differences.a: Stage 1 is a rattle and click-clack. The 0.38 s hit is a thunk plus metallic click. Then come many small irregular clicks and rattles (0.55-1.0 s). The swelling scrape at 1.0-1.27 s is noisy. The finale is a rattle, a click and a heavy snap.
differences.b: The elements are in the right places but are simplified. Stage 1 is a few evenly spaced ticks. The 0.55-1.0 s section has only two low pitched blips (0.59 s and 0.78 s) plus sparse ticks. The 1.0-1.27 s scrape is a smooth swelling tone-noise burst with a pitched onset at 1.0 s. The finale is a regular descending-spacing series of ticks (1.5, 1.59, 1.68, 1.76 s) with a ringing 1.1 kHz tone.

differences.b: Transients are present but thin, mostly vertical ticks with little body. The ending clicks decay with a tonal ring instead of a crack, and the 0.38 s hit leads with a low sine and not a metal clack.

differences.a: Organic and irregular, with real metal and plastic foley, rattles and micro-variation between hits.

Add 8-10 small rattle and click events between 0.45 and 1.0 s at -15 to -25 dB under the main hit: 5-15 ms noise grains clustered in 2-3 groups, at ~0.48, 0.57, 0.69, 0.82, 0.9, 1.0 s. Fade to near silence by ~1.0 s.

Rework the 1.0-1.27 s scrape: use pure band-passed noise (1-6 kHz) with a slow 100-150 ms swell then a fast cut at ~1.27 s, with grit from a 40-80 Hz amplitude modulation at 50% depth. Remove the pitched onset. Keep it at around -18 dB under the thunk.

Rebuild the finale (1.5-1.81 s): a 60-100 ms rattle (dense 3-5 ms noise grains) at 1.5 s, a sharp click at ~1.63 s, and a heavier snap at ~1.7 s with a 100 Hz-body thud (30 ms) plus a bright click, with a ~100 ms dry tail. Drop the ringing 1.1 kHz tone.

Rebuild the stage-1 rattle at 0-0.17 s as an irregular rattle plus a click-clack pair (~0.05 s and ~0.13 s) with noise grains, not four equal ticks. Keep silence from 0.17-0.38 s and 1.27-1.5 s at digital zero.
Keep the overall level at about -22 LUFS, with the peak at the 0.38 s hit at roughly -3 dBFS. After the changes, lift the click layers by ~2-3 dB so the loudness holds with the bass sustain gone.

Remove the regular low-frequency pulsing in the tail: stop using a fixed-frequency resonator or AM, and use a noise-driven or randomly modulated low-passed rumble at 60-250 Hz instead.
Add light saturation or soft clipping (about 3-6 dB of drive) on the body for the rough, distorted character, and keep the peak at about -1.9 dBFS and the loudness at about -17.6 LUFS.

review.summary: B is a close structural match to A: a boomy revolver shot with a decaying tail, same duration and loudness. It is darker and more bass-heavy, with a shorter tail and a flatter sub-bass block in place of A's broadband crack and mid body.

differences.b: Bursts 2 and 3 are clean exponential ring-outs of roughly 100-250 ms each, like struck bells or pings. They are much smoother and more regular than real handling clacks.

differences.b: In burst 2 two thumps fall from about 500 Hz to 200 Hz, like toms or sci-fi drops. This is a clearly audible pitch sweep that A does not have.

differences.a: Peak -1.3 dBFS, RMS -24.6 dBFS, -19.7 LUFS. The loudest hit is the final rack at about 2.28 s.

Drop the 1 kHz tones at 0.3-0.45 s.

review.summary: B captures the boomy low-end launcher thump and matches overall loudness, length and trailing silence, but it is darker, smoother and less transient-rich than A. It lacks A's noisy crack, mid-range grit and secondary bumps, so it reads as a muffled drum boom.

differences.a: Centroid about 554 Hz and 85% rolloff about 431 Hz. Bass is 66%, with real mid, low-mid and presence energy (about 18% combined), and a bright noisy block up to about 5 kHz in the first 0.3 s.
differences.b: Centroid about 361 Hz and rolloff only about 129 Hz. Bass is 81% and mids and presence are only about 7%. Reads as dark and subby, with the energy squeezed into 20-130 Hz.

differences.a: Sharp broadband crack at about 0.04-0.05 s with tall spikes in the waveform, followed by a second bright bump around 0.25 s. Gives a hard, explosive onset.

differences.a: Noise-dominated, gritty, with broadband blast noise on top of the thump and a faint resonance line near 1 kHz.
differences.b: Mostly smooth tonal low boom with a slight noise wash that fades quickly. Highs fade steadily from the start, so it has little grit.

differences.a: Peak at 0.04 s. -20 dB at 0.31 s, -40 dB at 0.72 s. Sustained bright low block to about 0.55 s, then a fast drop. Envelope: -18, -14, -26, -30, -44 dB per tenth.
differences.b: Peak at 0.04 s. -20 dB at 0.26 s, -40 dB at 0.62 s. Slightly faster decay, and the 0.3-0.4 s region is about 11 dB lower (-40.8 vs -29.8). Hotter in the first 0.1 s (-11 vs -18 dB) with less body in the mid-tail.

differences.a: Crack and noise burst, a sub thump, a second small bump near 0.25 s, a mid resonance near 1 kHz, and a low rumble tail.
differences.b: Essentially a single low boom layer with a high-frequency hiss decaying across the spectrum. No mechanical or launcher thoomp detail and no secondary event.

review.summary: B matches A's length (2.21 s), onset count (14), gap near 1.1 s and loudness (-24.0 vs -23.7 LUFS), but sounds synthetic: it has sine-like pitched drops, a sustained organ-like tone at 0.8-1.05 s and a boomy 1.2-1.5 s thump, where A is dry, noisy metal clatter with a sharp thunk. differences.b: At 0.8-1.05 s there is a sustained flat ~500-600 Hz tone, a square or organ-like hum lasting about 0.25 s with a hard cut-off. It is the most unnatural element and the wrong shape for a thunk.

differences.a: Hits are percussive and decay quickly (-40 dB in about 0.18 s). The energy is in transients.
differences.b: The sustained tone and the long low thump (1.2-1.5 s, decay about 0.26 s to -20 dB) are held for too long. The 0.3-0.75 s pitched drops ring out like tom or boing sounds.

differences.b: Bass-heavy: 36% bass and 39% low-mid, only 15% mid. Centroid is about 1.4 kHz and rolloff about 2.1 kHz. Too dark and boomy, with a flat low-end plateau down to 20 Hz.

Find and remove the click at ~1.22 s (likely a buffer or segment boundary); apply a 5-10 ms crossfade or fade.
Keep the output mono per the brief, but make the mid and low-mid content slightly wider in the design logic (e.g. decorrelated noise) if stereo is later allowed.

review.summary: B matches A's length, peak level and loudness and has the same heavy low-end boom, but it is a much darker, tonal, sub-heavy thump. It lacks A's broadband noisy body, mid and high content, and gritty distorted texture, and its attack and decay shapes differ.

Level it ~6-8 dB above the current mid content, so the 85% rolloff moves from 151 Hz to ~1 kHz and the centroid from 418 to ~600 Hz.

review.summary: B follows A's overall layout (clicks, mag events, slam near 1.05s, rack at 1.64s, bolt release at 1.85s, three settling ticks) with matching length and loudness. review.summary: B has the right overall role, a bass-heavy laser blast with a falling zap, and matches loudness and file length. It is more tonal and synthetic: clean falling sine partials, a stuck ~200 Hz drone, and an abrupt cutoff near 0.9 s, where A has a noisy, gritty body with a smooth rumble fade.

review.summary: B matches the length (6.24 s), loudness (-24.0 vs -23.7 LUFS) and the rough layout of discrete events, but it sounds synthetic and gappy. It has a tonal sine-like thud, beeps and a hard noise burst in place of A's dry, noisy Foley clacks, and its low-frequency energy is far heavier.

differences.a: Broadband, noisy and dry, with no stable tonal peaks (flatness 0.057). It reads as metal and plastic Foley.
differences.b: Has clear tonal elements: pitched pings at about 1.2, 1.6 and 3.3 kHz, falling sine-like thumps at 1.1 s and 2.5 s, and a pitch-swept boom. Qwen hears beeps and bleeps, so it feels sci-fi rather than a mechanical minigun.

differences.a: Continuous handling and cloth rustle, many different clunks and clacks, a mag slide, and a ratchet rattle at 4.1-5.3 s ending in a low-mid thump.
differences.b: Isolated synthetic blocks separated by dead digital silence (about 1.0-1.1 s, 1.7-2.3 s, 2.6-3.1 s). It has a steady 1 s noise bed, a 1.5-1.7 s hiss burst, two boom hits, and a regular comb of 0.08 s ticks for the ratchet.

differences.a: Near-instant attacks with fast, irregular decays (-20 dB in 0.12 s, -40 dB in 0.41 s). The gaps are filled with low-level room and handling noise, so the clip feels continuous.
differences.b: The two big booms ring out smoothly like an exponential sine decay (0.19 s to -20 dB). Gaps fall to digital silence (-200 dB), so it sounds gated and unnatural.

differences.a: Sharp, dry, metallic clack transients, with the loudest slam at 3.72-3.8 s (peak -3.4 dBFS). The 1.57-1.65 s clack is bright and broadband.

differences.b: B is more tonal and cleaner. The sweep lines are clearly resolved, with less broadband grit above 1 kHz and a visibly lower noise floor.

differences.a: A starts with a bright, noisy transient and then swells into a sustained body. It has no hard click.
differences.b: B hits at full level straight away with a 0.04 s attack. It is louder in the first 0.1 s (-8 dB vs -20 dB at the start) and has no bright noise crack.

review.summary: B matches A's 3.05 s length and three-part layout, but it replaces A's clacky mechanical handling with a continuous noise wash, three clean pinging tones and a sustained steady whistle. The result reads as a synthetic beep sequence rather than a tactile reload, and the timing and texture are both off.

differences.a: Burst 1 is 4-5 discrete, sharp mechanical clacks between 0.1 and 0.55 s, at about 0.1, 0.28, 0.36, 0.45 and 0.53 s, with gaps between them.
differences.b: Burst 1 is one continuous broadband noise block from 0.08 to about 0.6 s with no separate hits, ending in a faint tonal tail at about 1.1 kHz. It reads as a hiss or static wash, not clicks.

differences.a: Woody-plastic and metallic handling sounds with a noisy, organic, irregular texture and mid-heavy transients (800 Hz-3 kHz).
differences.b: Synthetic and clean. The noise is flat (flatness 0.39 vs 0.10) and the later hits are pure pinged sine partials with harmonics, which sound like beeps or bells, not metal clunks.

differences.a: Each transient decays in under 0.15 s. The final latch at about 2.04 s is a bright burst that decays over about 0.8 s into a quiet tail that ends by about 2.8 s.
differences.b: The 0.08-0.6 s block is a flat sustained plateau. The final element (1.95-2.85 s) is a steady constant-level whistle with almost no decay until it cuts off at about 2.85 s, so it reads as a held tone rather than a settling charge-up.

differences.a: Strong, varied clack transients with a high crest factor of 26.5 dB and peak -3.8 dBFS.
differences.b: Weaker transients. Burst 1 has almost none, the 3 clunks are soft pings, and the crest factor is 21.5 dB with peak -8.2 dBFS (about 4.4 dB lower).

differences.a: The tail has a faint, thin narrow-band whine at 8-9 kHz that rises slightly, mixed low in a noisy tail.
differences.b: A strong, prominent tonal whistle at about 1 kHz with a 2nd partial at about 2.2 kHz, rising slowly. It is much lower than A's whine and far louder, so it dominates the tail. The 3 pings fall in pitch, from about 1.1 kHz to 0.9 kHz, with harmonics.

differences.a: Onsets at 0.1, 0.28, 0.36, 0.45, 0.53, 0.78, 1.58, 1.69, 1.80, 1.96, 2.04 and 2.53 s (12 in all). Burst 2 is the loudest at about 1.69 s and the final latch hits at 2.04 s.

differences.b: Strongly tonal ringing partials in bursts 2 and 3, plus a hissy noise bed in bursts 1 and 3. This is a different balance.

change_notes: Burst 1: delete the continuous noise block. Build 5 separate clicks at 0.10, 0.28, 0.36, 0.45 and 0.53 s. Each is a 3-8 ms noise burst bandpassed at 1.5-4 kHz, mixed with a 600-900 Hz damped resonant ping (decay 40-80 ms). Vary level by ±3 dB and pitch by ±10% per hit. Keep the 0.28-0.53 s hits about 6 dB louder than the first.

Burst 2 (1.58, 1.69, 1.80 s): replace the pure sine pings with clunks. Use a 10 ms noise crack bandpassed at 0.8-3 kHz, plus a 300-600 Hz damped body with 60-100 ms decay, and a short 2-5 kHz metallic ring at -18 dB. Make this the loudest section at about -4 dBFS peak (raise it about 4 dB from now), with the middle hit (1.69 s) strongest.

review.summary: B is a close match to A in length, loudness (-13.5 vs -13.0 LUFS) and bass-heavy burst-plus-tail shape. It decays gradually through the burst instead of holding a flat level and then dropping, and it is darker, with a softer top end and a less defined cliff at 0.3 s.

differences.a: Level is held roughly flat and pulsing from 0 to 0.3 s (-7, -12, -6 dB per tenth), then drops about 12-20 dB abruptly at 0.3 s into a smooth exponential tail.
differences.b: Starts hot (-5.4 dB) and slopes down steadily (-8, -10, -19 dB per tenth), so the 0.3 s cliff is softer and the burst reads as a decaying single boom, not a sustained rapid-fire burst.

differences.a: Near-instant onset, with the peak at 0.15 s in the middle of the burst. Individual shots are lumpy and overlapping, with strong broadband crack throughout.
differences.b: Peak at 0.06 s, with a strong initial thump at 100-200 Hz in the first 50 ms. Pulse bands are visible but weaker and more regular, with less crack per pulse.

differences.a: Onsets at 0.19, 0.33, 0.43, 0.66, 0.84, 0.92, 1.11, 1.33 s, with a dead gap of ~1.17-1.33 s. Early events are spaced and sparse, with a quiet tick at 0-0.08 s.

Add a 60-90 Hz thump with a 120 ms decay. Drop the flat 0.35 s gate and the hard cutoff at 0.6 s.

Fill 0.6-1.5 s with a continuous gritty rattle instead of silence. Use bandpassed noise (300-2000 Hz) with ~25 Hz amplitude modulation at -20 to -25 dB, sitting about 20 dB under the hit. Remove the regular comb of ticks, or randomise them to 3-4 sparse ticks at -35 dB.

Cut the air band: low-pass the whole mix at ~6-8 kHz so air falls from 6.3% to ~2.5%. Soft-limit the peak at -1 dBFS. Keep the integrated level at about -12 LUFS, and aim for a crest factor of about 17-19 dB so the hit stands out more.

review.summary: B is a flat, seamless 4 s machine loop that matches A's length and loudness (-17.7 vs -17.2 LUFS), but it is much brighter and more tonal, with a distinct 300-900 Hz band and a lot of hiss. A is a dark, sub-heavy rumble (centroid 151 Hz) with a slow swell and irregular bumps, so B reads as a lawn-mower or engine rather than a heavy heat-ray hum.

differences.b: A distinct tonal band at ~300-900 Hz with a hard ceiling near 900 Hz, plus a broadband hiss bed up to 20 kHz (flatness 0.066). This sounds like an engine or motor plus static.

differences.b: Very uniform, with a fast regular vertical striping (~25-30 Hz amplitude flutter) and no onsets. It feels mechanical and static, like a steady motor.

review.summary: B has the right length, loudness and low-end weight, but its structure is wrong: a gated block of noise from 0.12-0.5 s, a pre-bump, a gap, and a stray blip at 1.06 s, instead of A's single smooth swell and fade. It reads as stuttering segments rather than one continuous press churn.

differences.b: Blocky gated envelope: a weak bump at 0-0.1 s, near silence at 0.1 s (-47 dB), a sudden jump at 0.12 s to a plateau until 0.5 s, a hard cut at 0.5 s, then a low ragged tail.

differences.a: Single continuous churn layer with faint high ticks near 0.13-0.45 s.

differences.b: Very regular amplitude-modulated pulses (~18 per 0.5 s, about 35-40 Hz) that sound like a mechanical tremolo or ratchet, with visible comb-like harmonic banding.

differences.b: Strongly tonal: a bright harmonic stack near 0.9, 1.8 and 2.6 kHz that sags slightly in pitch over 0.5 s, over a noise bed. Sounds metallic and synthetic.

differences.b: Metallic and mechanical, like a laser or gun ring. Qwen heard a gun with a shell drop. No wetness or crunch.

differences.b: Broadband hiss with two clean swept sine-like whistle lines (about 2.1-3 kHz and 4.5-5.5 kHz) and nothing in the growl region.

differences.a: Envelope by tenth: -41, -22, -10, -19, -25, -25, -33, -40, -52, -62. The decay is smooth and rattly.
differences.b: Envelope by tenth: -36, -34, -12, -18, -25, -25, -31, -40, -46, -40. Similar overall, but there is a rebound at 0.9 s and a slower fade at 0.7-0.8 s.

change_notes: Rebalance the body: cut the 50-200 Hz thump block by about 8-10 dB and add a band-passed noise grind (150-900 Hz, mild distortion) of about 0.3 s under the 0.2 s peak. Target bass about 30%, low_mid about 40%, mid about 25%.
Replace the sine whine at 0-0.13 s with a soft low rumble that fades in from -35 dB to -20 dB. Optionally keep a very quiet 450 Hz triangle/square band at -30 dB. Remove the 650-850 Hz glide.

Shape the thump as a decaying hit, not a flat block. Use a sine at 120 Hz falling to 60 Hz over 150 ms with an exponential decay of about 150 ms starting at 0.2 s. Add a short metallic clank at 0.2 s: 1-3 kHz noise, 20 ms, +4 dB over the body, with 450 Hz resonance.

Low-pass the tail at about 1.5 kHz, a 12 dB/oct slope, and sweep the cutoff down to 400 Hz by 0.8 s. Replace the click/pops with 8-12 amplitude-modulated rattle pulses (about 25 Hz) that decay from -25 dB at 0.4 s to -60 dB at 0.85 s.
Remove the onset at 0.87 s and the hiss after the cutoff. Fade to digital silence by 0.85 s, leaving about 0.2 s of silence. Keep the 0.05 s precursor as a faint 20 ms blip at -28 dB.

Reduce energy above 4 kHz by 10-15 dB. Aim for centroid about 850 Hz, rolloff85 about 1.8 kHz and a final-quarter centroid of about 250 Hz. Raise the peak to about -3 dBFS while keeping about -20 LUFS.

review.summary: B is a flat, steady wall of mid-heavy noise for the whole 2.2 s with no burst structure, no impact, and no decaying low tail, whereas A is a loud, pulsing, clipped burst that cuts off at ~0.85 s and falls into a bass rumble. B fills the 'rumbling noise' idea but not the role or timing.

differences.a: Loud plateau 0-0.85 s (peak ~0.42 s), sharp drop of about 20 dB by ~0.9 s, then a long decay to -40 dB at ~1.56 s and silence by ~2.07 s.
differences.b: Flat sustain at about -8 dB from 0.1 s to ~1.4 s, only a slight fall to -11 dB, then an abrupt fade in the last ~0.1 s. No real decay; reads as a drone or loop.

differences.a: Instant, hard loud onset with a strong low thump and a heavily clipped, punchy transient.
differences.b: Soft ~0.05-0.1 s fade-in from -29 dB with no transient. The only onset is a weak one at 0.05 s.

differences.a: Regular pulse train (~0.09 s spacing, ~11 Hz) of rotor or gun chop in the first 0.85 s, with secondary onsets at 1.33 s and 1.72 s in the tail.
differences.b: Continuous noise and rumble with no discernible rhythmic pulsing or secondary events; the spectrogram is a uniform smear. Waveform ripples appear only in the last 0.4 s.

differences.a: Bass-dominated: sub 12.8% and bass 49.5%, centroid 1.1 kHz, rolloff 2 kHz. The tail falls below ~250 Hz (centroid 178-214 Hz).
differences.b: Mid-heavy: sub 4.4%, bass 26.7%, low-mid 33%, air 8.6%. Centroid 2.2 kHz, rolloff 4.4 kHz, and the centroid stays ~1.5-2.4 kHz throughout.

differences.a: Long low-passed rumble tail (~1.2 s) with a crackly debris texture, and the high end dies after ~0.9 s.
differences.b: No tail. Full-bandwidth noise (up to 10 kHz+) persists until the end, so there is no darkening over time.

differences.a: Extremely loud and clipped (19k clipped samples, +15 dBFS peak as measured, +2 LUFS, crest 15.7 dB).
differences.b: Sustained at -7.7 LUFS with a peak of -1.5 dBFS, crest 7.1 dB. Lower in level, and it reads as constant rather than punchy. Peak is compliant, but with no dynamics it will feel less impactful.

differences.a: Distorted broadband noise with crackle and a strong low thump; low flatness (0.064).
differences.b: More noise-like and flatter (0.234) with a hollow, synthetic mid-range character; no thump.

differences.a: 2.22 s with 0.15 s trailing silence; activity front-loaded in the first ~40%.
differences.b: 2.22 s total but 100% active, no trailing silence, and energy spread evenly. Duration matches but the timing distribution is wrong.

differences.a: No clear pitch; chop rate is the only rhythmic element.
differences.b: Static, with no pitch or rate movement.

change_notes: Restructure the envelope: 0-0.85 s loud burst plateau at about -3 dBFS, then fall 20 dB by ~0.95 s, to -40 dB by ~1.55 s, and silence from 2.07 s. Remove the 1.4 s sustain.

Add a pulse train: amplitude-gate the noise with ~10-11 sharp pulses at ~0.085-0.09 s spacing (about 11 Hz, 10 ms attack, 50-60 ms decay, ~20 dB depth) across 0-0.85 s. Give each pulse a slight random level and timing jitter of ±5 ms.
Add a sub thump at 0 s: a sine sweep from 110 Hz down to 45 Hz over 150 ms, +6 dB over the noise body. Repeat at about -6 dB on every second pulse for chop weight.
Rebalance the spectrum toward bass: low-shelf +8 dB below 250 Hz and cut 1-4 kHz by ~8 dB. Target about 13% sub, 50% bass and centroid ~1.1 kHz. Keep light 4-10 kHz noise only in the first 0.85 s.
Make the tail a low-passed rumble: after 0.85 s sweep a lowpass from ~6 kHz down to 300 Hz over ~0.8 s, with a gain fade of ~1.2 s.
Add 2-3 crackle or debris ticks (3-6 ms noise bursts at 1-3 kHz, -15 dB) near 1.33 s and 1.72 s, and add 0.15 s of trailing silence.

Add soft saturation (tanh, drive ~3-4 dB) for grit, with a limiter at -1 dBFS. Don't hard clip. Aim for roughly -10 to -14 LUFS integrated, since a +2 LUFS target is only reachable by clipping. Keep it mono with DC removed.

review.summary: B matches A's length, loudness (-17.2 vs -17.1 LUFS) and mid-bright centroid, but it is a regular train of about 20 discrete pulses that sounds like a motor or a ticking clock. A is one continuous gritty swell with a quick fall-off and a sparse, clicky tail, so B only partly fills the role.

differences.a: A single ragged, continuous rasp with irregular granular grit, like an insect vocalization.
differences.b: A very regular train of about 20 evenly spaced pulses at roughly 45-50 Hz, giving a mechanical buzz or tick. Qwen heard a clock ticking.

differences.a: Swells from 0.05 s to a peak at about 0.15 s, holds to about 0.23 s, then drops 20 dB by about 0.27 s and 40 dB by about 0.39 s.
differences.b: The envelope plateaus at about -16 to -19 dB from 0.1 to 0.7 of the clip, then cuts off sharply around 0.46 s. Individual pulses dip to near silence between hits.

differences.a: A sparse tail from 0.25 to 0.40 s with faint ticks and residual hiss, fading smoothly to roughly -70 dB.
differences.b: No tail. Everything stops abruptly at about 0.46 s, followed by digital silence (-200 dB) for the last 0.1 s.

differences.a: Soft swell with a single onset at 0.05 s and no hard transient. The waveform shows a few isolated spikes inside the body.
differences.b: Each pulse has its own attack, giving 4 detected onsets and a repeating amplitude pattern. There is also a low-frequency thump near 0.11 s and 0.2 s that is not in A.

differences.a: Noise-dominated and fairly dense (flatness 0.15) with mottled resonance bands at 1-6 kHz.
differences.b: Flatness is 0.42, but the spectrogram shows a harmonic or pulse-comb structure with strong 1-3 kHz bands, so it sounds more buzzy and tonal than noisy.

differences.a: Presence-heavy: about 32% mid, 55% presence and 13% air. Rolloff85 is 7.8 kHz. The body centres on 3-6 kHz and nothing sits below 300 Hz.
differences.b: Shifted down and wider: about 45% mid, 32% presence and 20% air, plus 3% low-mid. Rolloff85 is 9.4 kHz. Energy sits at 1-3 kHz with a visible 20-100 Hz thump.

differences.a: 0.555 s with about 0.16 s of quiet trailing silence. Active energy runs about 0.05-0.25 s (active fraction 0.62).
differences.b: 0.56 s total with active content spread over about 0.02-0.46 s (active fraction 0.76). The body is longer and more evenly filled, so the sound feels longer.

differences.a: Peak -1.0 dBFS, RMS -21.2 dB, LUFS -17.1, crest 20.2 dB.
differences.b: Peak -3.5 dBFS, RMS -21.2 dB, LUFS -17.2, crest 17.7 dB. Overall level matches, with slightly less peakiness.

change_notes: Replace the regular pulse train with a continuous band-passed noise layer (3-6 kHz, Q about 1.5). Amplitude-modulate it with filtered random noise at 20-60 Hz, depth 40-60%, with jittered rates, instead of a fixed 48 Hz LFO.
Reshape the envelope: 0 to -40 dB at 0-0.05 s, ramp to peak at 0.15 s, hold to 0.23 s, then drop 20 dB by 0.27 s and 40 dB by 0.39 s. Use exponential curves, no plateau and no hard stop at 0.46 s.
Remove the sub/bass thumps at 0.11 s and 0.2 s and high-pass at about 300 Hz (12 dB/oct). Low-mid should be under 0.5%.
Shift the balance up: lower the 1-3 kHz emphasis by about 6 dB, boost 3-6 kHz by about 4 dB, and low-pass the air around 8-9 kHz so rolloff85 is about 7.8 kHz.
Add 4-6 tiny clicks (1-3 ms, 2-5 kHz, -30 to -35 dB relative to the body) between 0.25 and 0.37 s, plus a faint hiss tail at -45 to -60 dB out to about 0.40 s.
Add 1-2 soft formant-like resonances at about 3.5 kHz and 5 kHz (Q 3-5) with slow random drift of ±10% across the body for an organic feel.
Lift the peak to about -1 dBFS and increase crest factor to about 20 dB with a couple of small random spikes of +4-6 dB inside the body, keeping LUFS at about -17.
Keep the file at 0.555 s and make the final 0.1-0.15 s very quiet (below -60 dB) but not digital-silence, with a short fade.

review.summary: B is a flat, brighter, mid-heavy noise bed of the right length and loudness, but it lacks A's low-end rumble, its slow mid-clip swell and its darker edges. It reads as a hissy stream or surf wash rather than wind buffeting past a glider.

differences.a: Centroid about 1.15 kHz and rolloff85 about 1.3 kHz. Bass 31% and low-mid 39%, with strong 20-500 Hz energy and little above 5 kHz.
differences.b: Centroid about 1.8 kHz and rolloff85 about 3 kHz. Mid 57% and low-mid 29%, with bass only 6% and sub 0.3%. The result is bright and hissy, with energy extending to about 6 kHz.

differences.a: Slow swell of about 4 dB to a peak near the middle (4-7 s), with quieter, darker edges (about -30 dB at 1 s and -29 dB at the end). Loudness range 4 LU.
differences.b: Almost flat envelope within about 1 dB, a small bump near 4 s, and a loudness range of 1.1 LU. There is no real swell or fade at the edges.

differences.a: Buffeting, fluttering rumble with vertical streaks below 500 Hz, plus a mid haze that brightens mid-clip. Reads as air rushing past the player.
differences.b: Uniform, dense, grainy noise with no low-frequency flutter. Reads as a steady water or surf wash, and Qwen heard waves and rushing water.

differences.a: Partial decorrelation: L/R correlation 0.43 and side-to-mid -4 dB, so the image is wide but still has a coherent centre.
differences.b: Nearly fully decorrelated: correlation 0.007 and side-to-mid -0.1 dB. It is very wide and phasey, and will thin out when summed to mono.

differences.a: Centroid moves over time: about 490 Hz in the first quarter, 1.1 kHz in the middle and about 515 Hz in the last quarter. The brightness arc follows the swell.
differences.b: Centroid is static at about 1.78 kHz across all quarters, with no spectral evolution.

differences.a: Integrated -19.2 LUFS, peak -5.9 dBFS, RMS -23.8 dB.
differences.b: Integrated -19.1 LUFS, which matches, but peak -9.5 dBFS and RMS -26.6 dB. The loudness is the same because the energy sits in the more audible mids, so the bed will feel more present and less rumbly.

differences.a: Faint tick-like flecks near 8 s and slight onsets at 1.0 s and 8.7 s, giving subtle irregularity.
differences.b: No onsets or transients, perfectly smooth.

differences.a: Quieter, darker edges suggest a designed loop, though the seam may still be audible.
differences.b: Uniform level and spectrum at both ends, so the loop will be seamless if the noise is crossfaded. It sounds static as it repeats.

differences.a: 9.41 s, active throughout.
differences.b: 9.41 s, active throughout.

change_notes: Re-balance the spectrum: use brown/pink noise with a low-pass at about 1.5 kHz (12-24 dB/oct) and a high-pass at about 35 Hz. Aim for bass+low-mid about 70%, mid about 20%, presence under 2%. Cut the current 2-6 kHz content by roughly 12-15 dB.
Add a rumble layer of low-passed brown noise at 60-300 Hz, about 6-8 dB above the current bass level, with sub (20-60 Hz) at about 3%.

Add a slow amplitude envelope over the 9.41 s: -4 dB at 0-1 s, rising to 0 dB at about 4.5-6.5 s, falling to -4 dB by 9.4 s. Make it start and end at the same level so the loop is seamless, with a dip of about 1-2 dB near 1 s.

Make the brightness follow the swell: sweep a band-pass or low-pass cutoff from about 600 Hz at the edges to about 1.5 kHz at the centre, so the centroid moves from about 500 Hz to about 1.1 kHz and back.
Add buffeting: amplitude-modulate the low band (under 500 Hz) with smoothed random noise at 5-15 Hz, depth about 3-5 dB, to create the vertical streaky flutter.
Mid haze layer: band-pass noise at 1-3 kHz, gain about -12 dB relative to the body, swelling by +4 dB in the middle 3-7 s.

Reduce the stereo width: generate L and R from shared noise plus independent noise at about 40-50% mix, targeting L/R correlation about 0.4 and side-to-mid about -4 dB. Keep the low-end below 150 Hz closer to mono.
Optionally add 2-3 very quiet 2-4 kHz noise ticks, about 10 ms and -25 dB relative to the body, around 1 s and 8-8.7 s for organic irregularity.
Raise the final level so the peak is about -6 dBFS and the integrated loudness stays at about -19.2 LUFS. Raising the low-end weight will need the mids dropped by about 6 dB to hold the loudness.

review.summary: B matches A's length and overall loudness but reads as a smooth sustained noise bed with a clean whistling tone, not a gritty rasp breaking into chittering clicks. Its second half is almost silent with sparse faint blips, where A keeps crackling clicks until about 1 s.

differences.a: Dense rasping screech body, then discrete shell-like chitter clicks with a faint crackle tail.
differences.b: Steady noise bed with a pure swept sine whistle (about 2.2 kHz with a harmonic near 4.5 kHz), then tiny faint blips.

differences.a: Semi-noisy with mottled, fluttering partials and no stable peaks, so it sounds organic and vocal.
differences.b: Two clear stable tonal lines (4436 and 4737 Hz peaks, slowly rising) on top of noise, so it sounds like a beep or electronic whistle.

differences.a: Loud rasp for 0-0.3 s, then a sharp drop and a long run of decaying clicks. It is -40 dB by about 0.55 s, and the clicks stay audible to about 1.0 s.
differences.b: Smooth swell to a peak at 0.18 s, flat sustain to about 0.45 s, then a fast fade. Energy is -55 to -87 dB from 0.6 s onward, so the tail is effectively silent.

differences.a: Immediate gritty attack, with very sharp high-peak spikes at 0.28 and 0.39 s (crest 18.7 dB, clipping).
differences.b: Soft attack with a few small pulses at the start and no strong transients (crest 15.6 dB, peak -4.8 dBFS).

differences.a: Fluttering, rasping vocal quality with fast amplitude modulation, hostile and organic.
differences.b: Smooth, uniform noise with little amplitude modulation, synthetic and flat.

differences.a: Low body at 200-500 Hz and strong 2-5 kHz. The centroid rises from 3.4 to 6.9 kHz as clicks take over.
differences.b: Almost no energy below 500 Hz (low_mid 0.5% against 4.3%). The centroid is 3.3 kHz and jumps to about 9 kHz in the last half, where only HF blips remain.

differences.a: Nine onsets from 0.05 to 0.99 s, spread across the clip.
differences.b: Seven onsets, with the clicks clustered at 0.53-1.02 s and none between 0.08 and 0.53 s. Active fraction is 0.64 against 0.79.

differences.a: -15.1 LUFS, peak +1 dBFS with clipping.
differences.b: -15.6 LUFS, peak -4.8 dBFS, so the loudness is close and the peaks are cleaner. B's energy sits in the first half only.

differences.a: Dry, with a short natural crackle tail.
differences.b: Dry, with a very quiet, sparse tail of isolated blips.

change_notes: Delete the sine whistle and its harmonic (about 2.2 kHz and 4.5 kHz). Replace it with a formant-filtered noise rasp: band-pass 300 Hz-5 kHz, with peaks near 2.5-4 kHz and 350 Hz.
Apply fast amplitude modulation to the rasp: 40-80 Hz, 60-80% depth, with random jitter of about ±20%. Add slight ring or FM flutter so it reads as a vocal rasp, not a smooth bed.
Cut the rasp to 0-0.30 s with an instant attack (under 3 ms) and an exponential fall to -20 dB within about 0.07 s after 0.3 s. Currently it sustains to 0.45 s.
Add two hard click transients at 0.28 s and 0.39 s: 3-8 ms bursts of noise high-passed at 2 kHz, +8 to +10 dB over the body, with a 1 ms attack.

Build a chitter chain of 6-8 clicks at about 0.45, 0.53, 0.61, 0.73, 0.81, 0.89 and 0.99 s. Each is a 10-25 ms band-passed noise burst (3-6 kHz) with a short exponential decay. Reduce their level 3-4 dB per click, starting at about -25 dB relative to the rasp, and sweep the center frequency up toward 6-7 kHz.
Fill the 0.45-1.0 s region so the envelope tracks A's: about -30 dB at 0.6 s and -40 dB at 0.9 s. Currently B drops to -55 to -87 dB there.
Add low body: 150-500 Hz noise or a 200-300 Hz pulsed layer at about -6 dB relative to the mid band for 0-0.3 s, to bring low_mid from 0.5% toward 4%.
Raise the peak to about -1 dBFS using the click transients and keep clipping at 0. Target -15 to -16 LUFS.

review.summary: B matches A's length (0.6 s) and integrated loudness (-14.8 vs -14.6 LUFS) but is a sustained, low-passed ~60-150 Hz boom with a slow tremolo-like pulse, not a punchy, noisy, crackling gunshot that decays into silence. It lacks the full-band crack and fast decay and needs a rework.

differences.a: Instant peak, then falls fast: -20 dB by 0.23 s, -40 dB by 0.48 s, last 0.12 s silent. Short and punchy.
differences.b: Slow, held envelope: stays within about -8 to -11 dB through 0.3 s, reaches -20 dB only at 0.5 s, and is active for 97% of the file with almost no trailing silence. Reads as a sustained boom.

differences.a: Instant full-band attack at 0 s with a noisy crack reaching about 10 kHz in the first 0.1 s. Peak -0.9 dBFS.
differences.b: Soft 10 ms attack with a weak broadband click. The spectrogram shows no distinct crack, so the onset reads as a thud.

differences.a: Broad spectrum: sub 25%, bass 19%, low-mid 23%, mid 10%, presence 4%. Centroid ~907 Hz, rolloff85 ~1.2 kHz.
differences.b: Narrow low end: bass 79%, sub 9%, and almost nothing above 200 Hz (low-mid 3.5%, mid 4.6%). Centroid ~515 Hz, rolloff85 only 151 Hz, and the centroid drops to ~60 Hz by the last quarter. Muffled and boomy.

differences.a: Noise-dominated (flatness 0.08): crackly, dense, rattling texture with vertical striations.
differences.b: Tonal and sine-like (flatness 0.02). The waveform shows a regular amplitude beating, about 25-30 pulses across 0.6 s, like a low oscillator with AM or a detuned pair, which sounds like a hum or throb.

differences.a: Irregular crackle and rumble, with faint rattle and room residue in the tail. Sounds like a real SMG shot.
differences.b: Smooth, regular pulsing, more like a bass drone or a reverberant explosion (Qwen heard heavy reverb). It lacks the grit and randomness of a gunshot.

differences.a: Three layers: a sub thump, a bright noise crack, and a crackly low-mid body and tail.
differences.b: Effectively one layer: a low sustained sine/boom with a little noise on top. No distinct crack and no mid-range body.

differences.a: 0.60 s file with about 0.5 s of audible content and 0.12 s of trailing silence. Short enough for high fire rates.
differences.b: 0.60 s file filled to the end (0.01 s trailing silence), so it would smear and overlap in rapid fire.

differences.a: Dry, with a quiet low-frequency tail and faint rattle that dies out by about 0.5 s.
differences.b: A long, loud low-frequency tail that sounds reverberant and hangs on until the end of the file.

differences.a: No audible pitch movement, although the thump layer drops quickly.
differences.b: Roughly static low pitch, with the centroid sliding down from ~700 to ~60 Hz. The pulsing makes it sound pitched.

differences.a: Peak -0.9 dBFS, RMS -13.0 dB, -14.6 LUFS, crest 12.2 dB.
differences.b: Peak -1.6 dBFS, RMS -13.4 dB, -14.8 LUFS, crest 11.8 dB. Matches on paper, but the energy is spread evenly over time rather than front-loaded.

differences.a: Mono.
differences.b: Mono. Matches.
