change_notes: Rebuild the envelope. Give the whole sound an exponential decay reaching -20 dB at ~0.23 s and -40 dB at ~0.48 s, and fade to true silence by ~0.5 s, leaving ~0.1 s of trailing silence. Currently -20 dB is reached at 0.5 s.

Add a noise crack layer: white or pink noise high-passed at 1 kHz and low-passed at ~10 kHz, 0 s attack, 40-60 ms exponential decay, level about +3 to +6 dB over the body. Set the attack to 0 ms, not 10 ms.
Make the sub thump short: a sine sweeping 120 Hz to 45 Hz over ~100-150 ms, with an amplitude decay of ~0.15 s. Do not hold it for 0.6 s. It should supply about 25% of the energy in the sub band.
Remove the slow AM/beating on the low oscillator, or detune and randomize it. Replace it with irregular noise bursts.

Add a crackly body layer: band-passed noise at 200-1200 Hz with a random amplitude flutter of about 30-60 Hz, decaying over ~0.3 s, at about -6 dB relative to the crack. This should raise the centroid from ~515 Hz to ~900 Hz and the 85% rolloff from 151 Hz to ~1.2 kHz.
Rebalance the band energies to about sub 25%, bass 20%, low-mid 23%, mid 10%, presence 4%. Cut bass-band sustain by about 10 dB after 0.15 s.
Keep a dry sound with no reverb. Tail the low end with a short rattle at about -40 dB under 300 Hz.

Keep the peak at about -1 dBFS and target -14.6 LUFS. Because the energy is now front-loaded, the crest factor will rise to about 12 dB. Make 2-4 variants by randomizing the noise seed and the sweep start by ±10%.

review.summary: B is a sustained, near-stationary bass-and-noise drone that ends abruptly at about 2.05 s, while A is a sharp electrical blast with a bright crackly top end, a 0.13 s peak and a collapsing rumble tail out to about 2.7 s. Overall loudness and the bass weight are roughly comparable, but the shape, brightness and ending are different.

differences.a: Loud body for about 1 s, then -20 dB at 1.09 s and -40 dB at 2.5 s. This is a smooth, long, natural tail that fades to silence by about 2.7 s.
differences.b: Slow, near-linear decline from -8 to -20 dB over 2 s, then a cliff drop to silence at about 2.05 s (-20 to -40 dB within 0.01 s). The ending is a hard cutoff.

differences.a: 3.44 s file with about 2.7 s of audible sound and 0.75 s of trailing silence.
differences.b: 3.44 s file but only about 2.05 s audible, with 1.38 s of trailing silence. It is about 0.65 s too short, with a noticeably longer silent end.

differences.a: Sub 19% and bass 41%, with a clear sub thump. Bright hiss to about 6 kHz (rolloff 6.2 kHz), centroid about 2 kHz, and strong energy above 10 kHz in the first 0.5 s.
differences.b: Sub only 0.6% and bass 60%, so the sub is missing and everything sits at 80-250 Hz. Rolloff is only 3.6 kHz, there is a visible hard low-pass shelf at about 2.2 kHz, and the upper range is thin and flat.

differences.a: Broadband burst peaking at 0.13 s, brightest at the start, with a crackling discharge character.
differences.b: Peak at 0.02 s with no distinct transient crack. It starts as a stationary block of noise and tone.

differences.a: Fast swell with a sharp transient spike near 0.11-0.12 s, plus small clicks later. Crest factor 22.4 dB.
differences.b: Soft, symmetrical burst swells with no distinct sharp transient. Only a minor click-like spike appears near 0.25 s. Crest factor 19.6 dB and peak 3 dB lower.

A is a gradual motor-rumble swell with a warm 400-450 Hz band and a gritty, lingering decay. B lacks A's early build and mid body, and its tail is thinner and ends sooner.

differences.b: Impact is smeared across a flat 0.25-0.5 s bright noise burst with a ~950 Hz tone, followed by a separate low thump with a 1 kHz ping at 0.53 s. The peak is later and softer (-1.5 dBFS), with no clipping or punch.

differences.a: Peak at 0.26 s, falls ~20 dB by 0.6 s, then a low-level churn at about -24 dB until ~1.6 s, fading out by ~2.2 s.

change_notes: Move the main impact to 0.25 s: delete the 0.25-0.5 s noise plateau and put the thump/clank there. Keep 0.0-0.2 s as near-silence (about -55 dB) and remove the 0.05 s tick, or reduce it to a faint -50 dB tick at 0.07 s.

Build the impact from a broadband noise crack (1-8 kHz, 15-30 ms attack-to-peak, 120 ms decay) plus a sine thump sweeping 120 Hz to 45 Hz over 150 ms with a 250 ms decay. Peak at about -1 dBFS (soft clip for grit), about +6 dB over the bed.

Add a metallic ring: two resonant partials at 2.15 kHz and 2.9 kHz, 150-250 ms exponential decay, -12 dB relative to the crack. Delete or drop the pure 950 Hz / 1 kHz pings, or detune and noise-modulate them.

Reshape the envelope: after the hit, fall about 20 dB by 0.6 s, then hold a grinding bed at about -20 to -25 dB relative to the peak from 0.6 to 1.6 s. Make the bed lower than the hit, not the loudest section. Remove the 1.5-1.7 s swell, or limit it to +3 dB at 1.3-1.6 s.

Rebalance the bed: band-pass noise at 100-250 Hz with 8-15 Hz slow modulation, plus 600 Hz-3 kHz band-passed noise at -12 dB (about 40% of energy in the mid) to give machinery grit. Lift rolloff85 from ~800 Hz to about 2.5 kHz.
Cut the isolated high-frequency clicks at 1.3 s and 1.65 s, or replace them with 3-4 small low-level servo ticks (-30 dB, 2-4 kHz, 5 ms) in the 0.4-1.2 s range.
Fade out smoothly: apply a 0.5 s exponential fade from 1.7 s to -60 dB by 2.2 s, low rumble first (low-pass sweep 400 to 150 Hz). Keep the 0.3-0.4 s silence at the end and a total length of 2.57 s.
Target -15.5 LUFS with the peak at or below -1 dBFS, raising crest factor toward 18-20 dB by making the impact stronger relative to the bed.

review.summary: B matches A's length, overall loudness and rough envelope shape (0.4 s body then a sparse click tail), but the body is a clean, tonal, whistly synth with two sweeping sine-like lines instead of a gritty, formant-rich growl. Its tail is too regular and too long. B reads as a synthetic chirp or alarm, not a creature snarl.

differences.a: Gritty, rasping, noise-heavy snarl with flatness 0.15 and a dense, irregular spectrogram with no stable partials.
differences.b: Very tonal and clean, flatness 0.016, with two bright, narrow, rising lines near 2.2->3 kHz and 4.5->5 kHz sitting over a comb-like pulse texture. It sounds like a whistle or beep.

differences.a: Vocal, throat-like creature screech with organic formant movement and a ragged amplitude.
differences.b: Synthetic, buzzy, regularly pulsed (AM-like vertical striations) with a pure-tone sweep. It reads as a mechanical alarm or ticking, not an organic bug.

differences.a: Strong low body at 100-700 Hz (bass+low_mid about 11%) plus a broad 1.5-3.5 kHz formant band. Centroid 2.4 kHz, rolloff 3.4 kHz.
differences.b: Almost no energy below 500 Hz (bass 0.1%, low_mid 2.7%). Mid is 86% and is concentrated in the pure lines. Rolloff 2.7 kHz, but a 4.7 kHz peak sticks out. It lacks chest and warmth.

differences.a: After the body, a faint, irregular, decaying chitter trail with only 3-4 onsets. It falls to -40 dB by 0.79 s and has 0.21 s of silence at the end.
differences.b: Tail has 8 evenly spaced (about 0.08-0.09 s) click blips from 0.54 to 1.15 s, mechanical like a clock tick. The gap between 0.45 and 0.55 s drops to about -60 dB, then the clicks come back at about -36 dB. A hit at 1.15 s runs close to the end, with only 0.05 s of trailing silence.

differences.a: Soft rise to a peak at 0.17 s, ragged sustain to about 0.4 s, then falls 20 dB by 0.3 s after the peak, with a gradual fade through the chitters.
differences.b: Peak at 0.18 s and a smoother, more uniform plateau to about 0.43 s. Falls almost vertically (-20 dB at 0.31 s, -40 dB at 0.35 s), so the transition to the tail is abrupt and lacks the residual growl/breath.

differences.a: Fast onset at 0.06 s into a rough vocal burst, with a low-level breath or rustle before it.
differences.b: Three or four tiny ticks at 0-0.05 s, then an onset at 0.05 s. The pre-ticks sound like clock ticks, not breath. The body has a gentler, more uniform start.

differences.a: Formant-like movement, no clear fundamental, with the centroid climbing over time as noise and clicks take over.
differences.b: A clear linear upward sweep of the two tonal lines, about 2.1->3.0 kHz over 0.4 s, which sounds like a siren or whistle and does not match A's character.

differences.a: Peak -2.3 dBFS, -15.3 LUFS, crest 16.8 dB.
differences.b: Peak -5.4 dBFS, -15.8 LUFS (close), crest 15.8 dB. Peak is about 3 dB lower. The brief asks for a peak at or below -1 dBFS, so there is headroom.

differences.a: 1.28 s with a 0.21 s silent tail.
differences.b: 1.28 s, but the tail is cut off almost at the end (0.05 s silence). Body timing (0.05-0.43 s) matches well.

change_notes: Remove or mute the two tonal sweep lines. If a pitched element is kept, make it a heavily noise-modulated formant at about -20 dB relative to the body, with at most a 10% pitch drift, not a clean sweep to 3-5 kHz. Cut the 4.7 kHz spike by at least 15 dB.

Rebuild the body (0.06-0.43 s) as a sawtooth/pulse source at about 120-250 Hz, with irregular jitter (+/-8% random pitch wobble at 20-40 Hz) and 30-40% added noise. Feed it through two moving bandpass formants (about 400-700 Hz, Q about 3, and 1.8->2.6 kHz, Q about 4). Add soft distortion/waveshaping for grit. Target spectral flatness of about 0.1-0.15.
Add low-end weight: a 150-400 Hz band at +6 dB, or a low-passed noise layer at 100-700 Hz, so bass+low_mid reaches about 10% of energy, up from about 3%. Keep the sub below 80 Hz empty.
Replace the regular AM comb pulsing with slow, random amplitude flutter (6-15 Hz, 20-30% depth) so the body feels ragged and vocal, not buzzy.

Shape the envelope: rise over about 0.11 s from 0.06 s to a peak at 0.17 s, keep it ragged to 0.40 s, then fall about 20 dB by 0.47 s. Leave a residual 100-600 Hz growl/breath tail at -25 to -30 dB until about 0.6 s, instead of dropping straight to -60 dB.

Rework the chitter tail: 3-4 soft clicks, not 8, at irregular times (about 0.50, 0.68, 0.91, 1.01 s), each 10-25 ms, bandpassed at 2-5 kHz with a short resonant decay, and falling from about -35 to -50 dB relative to the peak. Randomise the spacing and level by +/-30%.
Replace the 0-0.05 s tick pre-clicks with a quiet breath noise (highpassed at 500 Hz, -30 dB, 50 ms fade-in).
Finish with silence from about 1.07 s to 1.28 s (about 0.2 s), and make sure the last click is at or before 1.05 s.

Raise the peak to about -2 dBFS (about +3 dB overall). Keep the integrated level at about -15.3 LUFS by adding the body and low-end energy and reducing the tail ticks, rather than turning everything up.

review.summary: B is three clean, gated ~700-900 Hz beeps with silent gaps, while A is one continuous, dense, bass-heavy buzzing tone with noise bursts and a fade. They share length and loudness, but the role and feel differ greatly: A is a sustained machine drone, B is a thin sine-like beeper.

B matches length (0.86 s) and integrated loudness (-21.6 vs -21.1 LUFS), but its character differs: a sustained 0.45 s pitched downward-sweeping tone with a sub thump replaces A's sharp noisy impact and steady train of ~8 chitter clicks, followed by a sparse, weak tail of ticks.

differences.a: Sharp, loud broadband noise burst peaking at 0.02 s (clips, +2 dBFS peak) with a crest factor of 26 dB, giving a snappy impact.
differences.b: Slow, soft onset peaking at 0.12 s on a sub/low thump with a sustained tone. Peak is -4.6 dBFS and crest is 19.7 dB, so there is no sharp snap.

differences.a: Impact burst, then a rapid train of 8 bright chitter clicks at ~12 Hz (0.09-0.66 s), then a strong final snap at ~0.68 s, then a fizzy tail.
differences.b: A 0.0-0.46 s continuous tone-and-noise block with a falling harmonic stack, then a few sparse clicks. After 0.5 s there are separated blips at ~0.09 s spacing that are weaker than A's pulses.

differences.a: Almost entirely noise and formant-like texture, with no clear pitch (pitch movement: none). It reads as chitinous and gritty.
differences.b: Clear pitched tonal sweep with three harmonics: fundamental ~1 kHz falling to ~450 Hz, partials near 2.2 kHz and 3.5 kHz. This is a laser or electronic zap, not an insect. Spectral flatness is 0.51 against A's 0.002.

differences.a: No pitch movement.
differences.b: A downward sweep of ~1 kHz to ~450 Hz over 0.45 s, plus a ~100 Hz sub thump at the start.

differences.a: Centroid ~6.7 kHz. Presence band (49%) and air (34%) dominate, mid ~15%, almost no bass.
differences.b: Mid band dominates at 51%, presence only 18%, air 25%, low_mid 5%. The centroid is lower overall, and it rises to 13 kHz by the last quarter as only hiss-like clicks remain.

differences.a: Stuttering decay with the loudest stretch around 0.3-0.5 s, a final accent at 0.68 s, -20 dB at 0.22 s and -40 dB at 0.55 s.
differences.b: Flat sustain at about -22 dB until 0.5 s, then an abrupt drop at 0.46 s (-66 dB bin), then weak clicks. Its envelope is block-shaped rather than a decaying chatter.

differences.a: 0.863 s, with 8 onsets at a regular ~0.08 s spacing starting at 0.09 s and the last strong snap at ~0.68 s.
differences.b: 0.86 s, but 6 onsets only start at 0.32 s (0.41, 0.49, 0.58, 0.66, 0.74) and the early part is a single drone, so the chatter is late and sparse.

differences.a: Peak +2.1 dBFS (clipped), LUFS -21.1.
differences.b: Peak -4.6 dBFS, LUFS -21.6. Integrated loudness is on target, but the energy sits in the sustained tone rather than in transients.

differences.a: Quiet fizzy tail from 0.72 s with faint high-mid residue, 0.11 s trailing silence.
differences.b: The tail is a few isolated tiny blips with dark gaps between them, 0.05 s trailing silence. It sounds gated.

change_notes: Delete the sustained sweep tone (the ~1 kHz to 450 Hz falling partials). Replace it with a noise-based layer, or reduce it to a faint, short 15 ms formant ping at 1.5-2 kHz.
Add a 40 ms broadband noise-crack impact at 0 s with a 1 ms attack and exponential decay (~25 ms). Put the 1-8 kHz energy 8-10 dB above the body and peak at about -1 dBFS.
Remove or cut the sub thump. Make it ~120 Hz, 30 ms and at -15 dB, or drop it. A has almost no bass.

Build 8 click pulses at 0.09, 0.17, 0.26, 0.34, 0.42, 0.50, 0.58 and 0.66 s (about 12 Hz). Each pulse is 15-25 ms of noise band-passed at 4-10 kHz, Q ~2, plus a 500-1500 Hz resonant body ping. Add ±10 ms jitter and ±10% pitch variation.
Make the pulse envelope stutter and fall: start around -18 dB, peak at 0.3-0.5 s, then roughly -20 dB by 0.22 s and -40 dB by 0.55 s. Do not leave a flat plateau.
Add a stronger final snap at 0.68 s (+6 dB over neighbouring pulses, 40 ms, broadband from 300 Hz to 10 kHz).
Add a fizzy tail from 0.72 to 0.80 s: a 5-10 kHz noise fade from -45 to -65 dB, and a bit of 1-2 kHz sweep. Soften the gating and avoid a hard cut.
Raise the high-frequency balance to presence ~45% and air ~30%, mid ≤15%, targeting a centroid of ~6.5 kHz. Add a high-shelf of +4 dB above 4 kHz if needed.
Keep it mono with a length of 0.86 s. Target -21 LUFS and a peak of -1 dBFS.

review.summary: B matches A's length (0.11 s) and its 540 Hz sine pitch almost exactly, but it is a flat, steady tone with a fade-out, whereas A has a loud sub-heavy thump and a dipping-then-swelling tone that cuts off hard. B is a close role match but smoother, slightly quieter and less punchy.

differences.a: Instant, clicky broadband thump peaking at about 0.01 s (about 0 dBFS, 1 clipped sample), with energy from sub-bass to 2 kHz, plus a distinct 1-2.5 kHz bump for about 25-30 ms.
differences.b: Softer onset peaking around 0.04 s by the measurement, with a small hiss/click burst in the high end (up to ~10 kHz plus). The low thump is weaker, and there is no clear 1-2 kHz mid bump.

differences.a: The tone level sags about 10 dB (-5 to -16 dB) around 0.07 s and then swells back to about -9.5 dB at the end. This gives a wobble or beating feel.
differences.b: Perfectly flat at about -10.2 dB for 0.08 s, then a quick fade over the last ~25 ms to silence. No dip or swell.

differences.a: 0.109 s with no trailing silence; the end is a hard cut while the tone is still sounding.
differences.b: 0.11 s, but the audible content ends at ~0.09-0.10 s with ~20 ms of trailing silence (active fraction 0.85).

differences.a: Peak 0 dBFS, RMS -9.1 dB, a hot sound.
differences.b: Peak -2.9 dBFS, RMS -11.5 dB, about 2.4 dB quieter in RMS and about 3 dB lower at the peak.

differences.a: Low end below 200 Hz is a strong, wide thump that fades by ~0.04 s. Weak harmonics at ~1 kHz, 5.4 kHz and 10.4 kHz.
differences.b: Has a distinct 100-250 Hz band lasting ~35 ms, and more high-frequency click energy (4-12 kHz) in the first 40 ms. The sine is the same at 538 Hz, with a faint second peak near 581 Hz.

differences.a: No tail, hard cut.
differences.b: Short fade with no reverb. Qwen's mention of a long reverb and descending pitch is unreliable; the measurements show a steady 540 Hz tone.

differences.a: Steady ~538 Hz.
differences.b: Steady ~538-540 Hz (the centroid by quarter is constant).

Slow amplitude dip (~-10 dB at 0.07 s) and swell on the tone

change_notes: Shorten the attack to a 1-3 ms ramp so the peak lands at ~0.005-0.01 s. Add a 25-30 ms thump: sine at 60-100 Hz plus a short 1-2 kHz band-limited burst, 5-8 dB above the beep body at t=0, decaying exponentially (~10 ms time constant).
Cut the 4-12 kHz click burst by about 15 dB, or low-pass it at ~4 kHz, and shorten it to ≤10 ms.
Reduce the 100-250 Hz band to ~25 ms and move it lower (about 50-100 Hz) so it reads as a thump, not a boomy tone.
Add a slow amplitude modulation to the 540 Hz sine: ~0 dB at 0.02 s, dipping about -8 dB at 0.07 s, back to about -4 dB at 0.11 s. A 0.5 depth LFO at ~14 Hz would do it.
Remove the trailing silence and make the tone run to 0.109 s, with at most a 3-5 ms fade to avoid a click.
Raise the level by about 3 dB so the peak is around -1 dBFS and RMS around -9.5 to -10 dBFS.
Optionally add a very quiet (-50 dB) partial at 1.08 kHz and 5.4 kHz for the same faint upper content.

review.summary: B has the right length and loudness, but it reads as three evenly spaced, tonal, thumpy hits with a sustained 60-200 Hz boom instead of A's wet, noisy, crunchy bite. The timing, texture and low-end character all differ, so it needs significant reshaping.

differences.a: Wet, crunchy, noisy organic chomp. Many small broadband grains, granular and squelchy, with a flatness of 0.24.
differences.b: Smooth, synthetic percussive hits with a pingpong or button-click feel. Flatness is 0.49 and the hits are clean, with no wet or gristly grain.

differences.a: Soft pre-click at 0.05 s, then two close loud bursts at about 0.13 and 0.19 s that peak at 0.16 s. A smaller chomp lands at 0.28-0.33 s and a faint click at 0.44 s, so the hits are irregular and cluster.
differences.b: Three near-identical hard vertical-edge onsets at 0.05, 0.14 and 0.28 s. Each is a sharp full-band click that decays cleanly, and the first is already near full level. The pattern is regular, with no pre-tick and no fourth click.

differences.a: Low end is mostly 150-400 Hz body with some rumble. Bass is 11% and low-mid 14.5%. Mids and highs are spread evenly, with a centroid of about 5 kHz.
differences.b: Strong, sustained sub-bass/bass block at 20-200 Hz after each hit. The 200-500 Hz low-mid is hollowed out at 2.9%. Presence is boosted to 32.5% and the centroid is brighter at 5.5 kHz.

differences.a: Energy is concentrated in 0.12-0.25 s. It is -18 dB in the 0.2 tenth, then falls irregularly to -40 dB at 0.34 s and fades to a quiet rattle by 0.6 s.
differences.b: Each hit has a smooth exponential decay with a flat low-frequency boom lasting about 0.1-0.2 s, and the last hit's boom runs to about 0.5 s. The boom adds a sustained, tonal feel that A lacks. The -20 dB decay is slower at 0.1 s versus 0.07 s.

differences.a: Has 0.0 s of leading silence, with the first tick at 0.05 s. The main energy is at 0.12-0.25 s and the tail runs to about 0.6 s.
differences.b: Has 0.04 s of leading silence, then a loud first hit at 0.05 s. The peak is at 0.14 s and the main energy runs 0.05-0.3 s, so the bite is spread out instead of climaxing at 0.16-0.2 s. The total length of 0.78 s matches.

differences.a: Noisy crunch layer, a small mid snap near 700-1000 Hz, a low thump and a wet rattle tail.
differences.b: Mostly click plus low sine-like boom. There is no wet squelch or rattle layer and no mid snap, and the tail is nearly empty.

differences.a: No audible pitch movement, with only a vague low thump around 100-300 Hz.
differences.b: A stable low boom around 40-150 Hz has a perceptible tone, with a comb-like striping below 40 Hz that suggests a repeating LFO or pulse train.

differences.a: Peak -2.2 dBFS, -20.8 LUFS integrated, RMS -24.3 dB.
differences.b: Peak -1.9 dBFS, -21.2 LUFS, RMS -23.7 dB. Loudness is well matched.

differences.a: Dry, with a low-level wet rattle that fades by about 0.6 s and a faint click at 0.44 s.
differences.b: Dry, with a smooth fade and no rattle. It has 0.27 s of trailing silence versus A's 0.2 s.

differences.a: Mono.
differences.b: Mono.

Two tightly clustered loud crunch bursts at 0.13 and 0.19 s
Wet, granular squelch and gristle texture

change_notes: Replace the low sine boom: high-pass at about 80 Hz, move the body to 150-350 Hz, and shorten each thump to 40-60 ms with a fast exponential decay. Drop the sustained 20-200 Hz block, and remove the sub-40 Hz pulsing.

Retime the hits to A: a soft pre-click at 0.04 s (-14 dB relative to the main hit, band-passed 700-1000 Hz, 15 ms), main bite hits at 0.13 s and 0.19 s (about 40 ms apart, the second at -2 dB), a smaller chomp at 0.30 s (-8 dB), and a faint tick at 0.44 s (-20 dB). Move the loudest energy to 0.16-0.19 s.

Make the crunch wet and granular: for each hit, use 20-40 ms of noise with random amplitude grains (3-6 ms bursts) through a 1-8 kHz band-pass, plus a band-limited squelch with a 300-900 Hz resonant sweep and 5-10% random jitter in grain timing. Lower the flatness toward 0.25 by shaping the noise and not using flat white noise.

Soften the clicks: lengthen the attack to 2-5 ms and use a lowpass at about 10 kHz. Roll the presence band (2-6 kHz) down by about 3 dB and fill the low-mid band at 200-500 Hz up to about 12-15% of energy.
Add a wet rattle tail: filtered noise at 300-3000 Hz, with a few random 5 ms ticks from 0.35 to 0.55 s, decaying from -35 dB to silence by 0.6 s. Keep the end dry, with no reverb.
Vary the pitch of the thump and the hit spacing by ±10% for the variant 'a/b/c' set, and keep the peak at -2 dBFS and about -21 LUFS.

review.summary: B matches A's length (1.78 s) and integrated loudness (about -14.9 vs -14.5 LUFS), but the character is wrong. A is a bright, wet, crunchy noise death with irregular crackles. B is a dark, tonal, amplitude-modulated buzz (~450 Hz and ~2 kHz bands) for the first 0.45 s, followed by sparse tick-like clicks. It reads as an electronic toy, not an organic creature.

differences.a: Highly noisy and flat (flatness 0.75) with no tonal peaks. It is a gritty, wet, crunchy noise texture.
differences.b: Much more tonal (flatness 0.35). A pulsing buzz with banded harmonics near 450 Hz and 2 kHz and an AM warble of about 8-10 Hz over the first ~0.45 s.

differences.a: Very bright: centroid about 6.8 kHz, with 70% of energy above 2 kHz (presence 32%, air 37%) and a modest sub thump.
differences.b: Much darker overall: centroid about 3.5 kHz, with 73% of energy in low-mid and mid (28% and 45%). The first quarter is only about 1.9 kHz, then the clicks jump to 10-13 kHz. Air is 13% and presence is 9%.

differences.a: Loud noise burst with a low thump, then dense irregular crackles, squelches and crunches (onsets at 0.05, 0.26, 0.34, 0.42, 0.6, 0.95, 1.28, 1.36 s) over a hissy noise bed.
differences.b: A sustained tonal drone for 0.45 s, then 12 isolated, sparse, regularly spaced ticks (0.55-1.68 s) with silence between them and no noise bed. It sounds like a laser or beep sequence, which Qwen also heard.

differences.a: Fast 0.03 s attack, then about -20 dB by 0.2 s. A ragged, continuous crackle sustain follows and slowly decays to -40 dB at 1.37 s, with a hiss tail ending near 1.5 s.
differences.b: Holds near the peak (-10 dB) for about 0.2 s, then falls to about -20 dB by 0.65 s. After that the tick pattern is mostly gaps and drops to -40 dB by 1.14 s, with a tail that never fully fades (ticks still occur at 1.6-1.68 s and the file ends only 0.03 s later).

differences.a: Strong broadband opening crack plus a thump, with a 20.9 dB crest factor and slight clipping. The transients are sharp and irregular throughout.
differences.b: The attack is soft and tonal, with no broadband crack. The crest factor is lower (12.9 dB) and the later clicks are uniform and neat.

differences.a: No pitch movement. Sub thump at about 40-100 Hz at the start.
differences.b: No sweep, but there are clear pitched bands (about 450 Hz and 2 kHz) that give a false musical pitch. Sub is minimal (0.7%) and the low end is a diffuse 20-200 Hz hum.

differences.a: Short hissy fade, then 0.24 s of silence. Dry.
differences.b: No fade-out hiss. The sound ends on a click with almost no trailing silence (0.03 s).

differences.a: Integrated -14.5 LUFS, peak +3.8 dBFS (clipped).
differences.b: Integrated -14.9 LUFS, peak -3.6 dBFS (no clipping). The loudness matches, though B's energy is front-loaded into the drone.

differences.a: Mono.
differences.b: Mono.

change_notes: Remove or heavily reduce the 450 Hz and 2 kHz tonal drone and its 8-10 Hz AM. Replace the first 0-0.2 s with a white or pink noise burst high-passed at about 1.5 kHz, with a 3 ms attack and a 150 ms exponential decay, peaking at about -3 dBFS.
Add a body thump under the burst: a sine at 100 Hz falling to 45 Hz over 120 ms, 0.15 s long, with a fast decay. Aim for about 5% of the energy in the sub band.
Add a wet squelch layer at 0-0.25 s: a band-passed noise (1-3 kHz) with a resonant sweep from 2.5 kHz to 800 Hz and fast random amplitude modulation at 30-60 Hz. Keep it about 6 dB below the burst.

Replace the sparse ticks with dense, irregular crackle bursts from 0.2 to 1.4 s. Use 3-8 ms noise grains high-passed at 2 kHz at random intervals (10-80 ms, denser early), with random amplitudes of -12 to -30 dB. Add stronger clusters near 0.26, 0.34, 0.42, 0.6, 0.95, 1.28 and 1.36 s.

Add a continuous hissy noise bed (highpass at 3 kHz, tilted brighter) from 0.2 to 1.5 s, starting at about -28 dB and decaying to -45 dB. This lifts presence and air to about 30-35% each and the centroid to about 6-7 kHz.

Shape the global envelope to match A: -20 dB at 0.2 s, about -25 dB at 0.7 s, -40 dB at about 1.37 s and silent by 1.5 s. Add about 0.2-0.25 s of silence at the end. Trim the sparse click train to stop before 1.4 s.
Keep peaks at or below -1 dBFS (no clipping). Normalise to about -14.5 LUFS after the changes, since the added noise will raise the loudness. Create 2-3 random-seeded variants.

review.summary: B has a similar length, overall loudness and a sub-heavy opening, but it is darker, more tonal and more rhythmic. Its opening is a pulsing 450 Hz-ish tone and its tail is a regular row of ticks, so it reads less like a wet, noisy alien dissolve with irregular crackle.

differences.a: Very noisy and broadband (flatness 0.50), with no stable tonal peaks. It is a gurgling, squelchy screech.
differences.b: Much more tonal (flatness 0.20), with visible harmonic bands near 450 Hz and 1-2 kHz in the first 0.5 s. It sounds like a synth tone rather than a creature.

differences.a: Three phases: a loud noisy burst with a sub thump, a gurgling wash, then sparse irregular crackles that dissolve.
differences.b: A pulsing tonal burst, then a long regular train of 24 tick/click onsets. There is no gurgly wash in between.

differences.a: Wet, organic, chittering and crackly. Qwen heard a boing/burst followed by static or fire crackle.
differences.b: Mechanical. Qwen heard clock ticking and a creaking door, which fits the metronomic tick grid.

differences.a: Centroid about 3.8 kHz, with 54% of energy in mid and presence and 13.6% in air. The centroid rises to 6-7 kHz in the crackle phase.
differences.b: Centroid about 2.1 kHz and rolloff 3.3 kHz. Energy is concentrated in low-mid (38.7%) and mid. Presence and air total only about 12%, and the first-quarter centroid of about 1.6 kHz is far darker. The later quarters read about 10 kHz because the ticks dominate.

differences.a: The attack takes about 0.11 s to a clipped peak, with a loud sustained body until about 0.4 s.
differences.b: The peak is at 0.01 s, so it is an instant hit. The opening 0.5 s is amplitude-modulated, with a pulse about every 0.1 s, which is audible as a wobble.

differences.a: Falls about 20 dB by 0.56 s and 40 dB by 1.66 s. The tail is a low-level wash with crackle bumps, then silence from about 2.2 s.
differences.b: Falls 20 dB by 0.82 s and 40 dB by 1.97 s, so it is slightly slower. The tail is made of isolated spikes with gaps, and it runs right to the end of the file (0.03 s trailing silence versus 0.68 s).

differences.a: Sound is active for about 2.2 s, then about 0.68 s of silence. Crackle onsets are sparse and irregular, at 1.43, 1.62, 1.79 and 1.89 s.
differences.b: Ticks start at 0.56 s and run to 2.76 s at a roughly even 0.08-0.10 s spacing. That is far denser (24 onsets versus 5) and too regular.

differences.a: Peaks at +4 dBFS (clipped) with RMS -18.7 and -16.2 LUFS.
differences.b: Peaks at -4.2 dBFS with RMS -17.7 and -16.7 LUFS. This is within tolerance, is cleaner and has no clipping.

differences.a: Diffuse wash with a faint reverberant hiss tail.
differences.b: Dry isolated ticks with no diffuse wash between them.

differences.b: Mono.

Keep the sub thump (40-150 Hz, 0-0.5 s) but add a downward pitch sweep from 150 Hz to 50 Hz over 300 ms. Increase the 200-400 Hz body slightly so the bass total is near 23%, and lower the low-mid hump by about 8 dB.
Add a gurgle layer from 0.5 to 1.3 s: noise at -20 to -25 dB relative to the burst, modulated by a random 15-40 Hz LFO with bandpass sweeping 500 Hz-3 kHz, to give the wet bubbling feel.

Trim the active length to about 2.2 s and pad about 0.6 s of silence at the end, keeping the 2.85 s file length. Make the 40 dB decay reach about 1.7 s.

Add per-variant random pitch variation of ±5% and randomise the click timing.

review.summary: B is a low, boomy sub/bass thump with a slow tremolo-like pulsing and almost no crack, mids or highs, whereas A is a bright, noisy, broadband gunshot crack with a bass thump and a dark mottled tail. Length and loudness match, but the character reads as a kick or impact rather than a gunshot.

differences.a: Instant 0 s attack with a broadband crack, bright noise burst up to 10+ kHz and a strong initial drop (-9 dB by 0.1 s).
differences.b: Soft 10 ms attack with no crack. It starts at -6 dB and stays flat to about 0.1 s, so it feels like a thud, not a shot.

differences.a: Centroid ~700 Hz, rolloff 775 Hz. Sub 21%, bass 44%, low-mid 16%, mid 9%, presence+air ~4.6%.
differences.b: Centroid ~260 Hz, rolloff 108 Hz. Sub 27%, bass 66%, and only ~7.5% above 250 Hz (low-mid 2.6%, mid 3.5%, presence 0.9%, air 0.5%). Far too dark and boomy.

differences.a: Noisy and gritty (flatness 0.057), with mottled noise texture through the body.
differences.b: Almost pure tone (flatness 0.008), a smooth sine-like rumble with little noise.

differences.a: Fast front-loaded decay: -16 dB at 0.2 s, -20 dB at 0.18 s, -40 dB at 0.43 s, with a long gradual tail of low rumble.
differences.b: Sustained plateau (-6 to -9 dB until ~0.2 s), then a steep drop. -20 dB at 0.26 s but -40 dB at 0.38 s, so the tail dies abruptly and sits ~30 dB lower than A from 0.5 s.

differences.a: Irregular, mottled reflections that read as a short room tail; chaotic and metallic.
differences.b: Regular amplitude pulsing (about 30-40 Hz beating) in the waveform, which sounds like a tremolo or a sub-bass wobble. It is clean and synthetic, not a gunshot.

differences.a: Sub thump, noise crack, mid body and a dark tail.
differences.b: A single low sub/bass layer; no crack, mid body or tail layer.

differences.a: Dark, rumbly, mottled tail with highs gone after ~0.3 s, active to ~0.47 s.
differences.b: No real reverb; the tail is sub-only and ends by ~0.4 s, with trailing silence of 0.2 s versus A's 0.13 s.

differences.a: No obvious pitch movement, a thumpy low end under noise.
differences.b: Sub fundamental is held steady and slowly decays, with no pitch drop.

differences.a: Peak -0.7 dBFS, RMS -14.4, -16.3 LUFS, crest 13.7 dB.
differences.b: Peak -1.6 dBFS, RMS -13.6, -16.6 LUFS, crest 12 dB. Loudness is matched, but the energy is sustained low end rather than a peaky transient.

Set the attack to 0-1 ms and add an initial transient click with a peak near -1 dBFS. Then make the body drop ~9 dB by 0.1 s and ~16 dB by 0.2 s, instead of the flat plateau (currently -6 dB until 0.2 s).

Remove the tremolo-like pulsing: stop the sub oscillators from beating (detune or phase artefacts around 30-40 Hz). Replace them with a single sine that sweeps from ~150 Hz to ~50 Hz over 120 ms, decaying by ~0.2 s.

Reduce sub/bass dominance: cut the sustained 20-100 Hz layer by ~8-10 dB and trim its length to ~0.2 s, aiming for sub ~21% and bass ~44%. Target a centroid of ~600-800 Hz and 85% rolloff of ~700-800 Hz.
Add a mid body layer: bandpassed noise at 300-2000 Hz with a short metallic clack/resonance at ~800-1200 Hz, 80-150 ms, about -6 dB under the crack. Raise the low-mid to ~15% and the mid to ~9%.

Add a dark tail: lowpassed noise or a short reverb (~0.2-0.3 s) with a 1 kHz lowpass closing to ~400 Hz, decaying to -40 dB by ~0.43 s with irregular amplitude modulation for the mottled texture. Extend audible energy to ~0.47 s and fade to silence by ~0.6 s.
Add a little noise (about 10-15% flatness-raising grit) to the low layer so flatness rises from 0.008 to ~0.05.
Keep the peak at or below -1 dBFS (about -0.7 to -1.0) and -16.3 LUFS, rebalancing the layers after the above changes.

review.summary: B is a regular, evenly spaced train of ~20 amplitude-modulated noise pulses that cuts off at ~0.5 s, whereas A is an irregular chitter that swells to a bright peak near 0.2 s, has a few sharp low-mid clicks around 0.32-0.4 s, and fades into a soft tail. Loudness and centroid are close, but the rhythm, shape, and character are quite different.

differences.a: Irregular, organic chitter: soft rattle start, dense bright burst peaking ~0.18-0.25 s, then 2-3 distinct sharper clicks/pops at ~0.32-0.40 s with 1-3 kHz body.
differences.b: One uniform layer of ~20 near-identical noise pulses at a steady ~40 Hz rate (~25 ms spacing) with no distinct phrases, no clicks and no climax, so it sounds like a buzz or motor rather than a bug.

differences.a: Quiet start (-38 dB in first tenth), swell to peak at 0.18 s, drop ~20 dB by 0.4 s, below -40 dB by ~0.5 s, then a very faint tail to ~0.57 s.
differences.b: Sudden jump to about -11 dB in the first tenth, then a flat plateau (-11 to -13 dB) until 0.4 s, followed by a symmetrical fade to nothing by ~0.5 s. The fade is abrupt, with digital silence from 0.7 s (-200 dB) instead of a gentle residual.

differences.a: No clean attack; granular click-like pulses with sharp, irregular transients, and the clicks at 0.32-0.4 s are the sharpest events.
differences.b: Every pulse is a soft, rounded, sinusoidally shaped swell with a slow attack and no sharp transients (crest 15.8 dB vs 18.4 dB). It sounds smooth and tremolo-like rather than clicky.

differences.a: Content runs ~0.57 s with a faint tail; onsets at 0.05, 0.17 and 0.32 s; the loudest region is ~0.15-0.3 s.
differences.b: Content ends at ~0.5 s, with 0.3 s of trailing silence and 5 evenly spaced onsets (0.05-0.42 s). Peak is earlier (0.13 s) and spread across 0.1-0.4 s.

differences.a: ~79% presence (4-8 kHz), 15% air, 6% mid; centroid drifts from 7.8 kHz down to ~4.5 kHz as clicks arrive; 85% rolloff ~7.9 kHz.
differences.b: 45% presence, 29% air, 25% mid; rolloff 10.7 kHz; centroid flat at ~6.8 kHz throughout. Too much mid and air, too little concentrated 4-8 kHz, and no spectral movement over time.

differences.a: Mostly granular noise (flatness 0.15) with some tonal clustering and a faint 12 kHz peak.
differences.b: Much flatter and noisier (flatness 0.50) with banded formant-like striations in the spectrogram. It reads as broadband buzz rather than structured chitter.

differences.a: Short, faint residual rattle and hiss with a low-end smear, dying gradually through ~0.6 s.
differences.b: No tail at all; hard stop followed by digital silence.

change_notes: Replace the fixed ~25 ms pulse train with randomised micro-bursts: 8-14 noise grains of 3-12 ms each, with jittered spacing of 10-40 ms (±50%) and random amplitudes. Use fast attack (<1 ms) and exponential decay (~5 ms) so they read as clicks, not smooth lobes.

Shape the overall envelope: start at about -38 dB at 0-0.1 s, ramp up to the peak at 0.18-0.22 s, hold until ~0.3 s, drop ~20 dB by 0.4 s, and fall below -40 dB by 0.5 s. Remove the flat plateau that currently starts at ~0.05 s.

Band-pass the main chitter noise at 4-8 kHz (Q ~1), with a gentle low-pass at ~9 kHz. Cut the 1-3 kHz noise by ~10 dB and the >10 kHz air by ~8 dB so presence is ~75% and mid is ≤8%. Add a faint ~12 kHz sparkle at -30 dB.

Add 2-3 sharp click/pop layers at 0.32 s, 0.36 s and 0.39 s: each is a 10-20 ms noise burst band-passed at 1-3 kHz, plus a ~700-1000 Hz sine/resonant ping with 15 ms decay, about +3 to +6 dB over the surrounding chitter.
Add a soft low-mid thump (150-400 Hz, 30 ms decay, ~-12 dB relative to the chitter peak) under the clicks for body.
Add a tail: low-level 3-6 kHz noise at -45 to -60 dB from 0.45 to 0.6 s, fading with a ~100 ms exponential decay instead of a hard cut. Keep about 0.2 s of near-silence at the end.
Slide the filter centre from ~8 kHz at 0-0.1 s down to ~4.5 kHz around 0.3-0.4 s to reproduce A's centroid movement (7.8 kHz → 4.5 kHz).
Raise the peak to about -1 dBFS, while keeping about -13.5 LUFS, and add per-trigger randomisation of grain timing and ±10% filter frequency so repeated idles don't sound identical.

review.summary: B matches A's length (1.41 s) and loudness (-14.5 vs -14.0 LUFS) and roughly follows the burst-then-clicks layout. But it is a much cleaner, tonal, synthetic sound: two bright pitched whistle lines over a smooth AM-pulsed buzz, with a late-starting body and sparse ticks after it. A is a raw, gritty, low-mid-heavy noise screech with a dense chitter tail.

differences.a: Flatness 0.28: raspy, noise-like formant screech with no stable pitch lines.
differences.b: Flatness 0.038: very tonal. Two clear whistle lines (~2.2 kHz and ~4.6 kHz, gliding slightly upward) dominate and read as a synth or siren, not a creature.

differences.a: Gritty, organic, crumpling or ripping, with irregular amplitude flutter and broadband grit up to the top of the spectrum.
differences.b: Smooth, regular, comb-like amplitude modulation (vertical striping) with a clean buzzy sheen. Sounds mechanical and artificial.

differences.a: Fast onset at 0.05 s, peaks at 0.11 s, with a sharp click near 0.2 s. Hits hard immediately.
differences.b: Starts quietly (-30 dB in the first tenth) with a few soft pulses, then swells to a peak at 0.29 s. Attack is slower and softer, with no crack.

differences.a: Strong low-mid body at 150-400 Hz (~10% low_mid, 1.2% bass) plus 1-4 kHz grit. Centroid in the first quarter is 2.8 kHz.
differences.b: Almost no energy below 400 Hz (low_mid 1%, bass 0). Energy sits at 1-5 kHz, concentrated in the whistle lines. Thin and lacks the warm body.

differences.a: Plateau to ~0.4 s, then drops about 20 dB in 0.27 s and tails off gradually, reaching -40 dB at 0.87 s.
differences.b: Plateau to ~0.45 s, then falls off a cliff (-20 dB at 0.21 s, -40 dB at 0.26 s). The tail is then just isolated ticks with deep gaps.

differences.a: Dense chitter tail of clicky rattles every ~0.08-0.1 s from 0.4 to 1.15 s, decaying gradually and still fairly broadband.
differences.b: Tail is sparse, thin, very short bright ticks at irregular spacing with deep silence between. Stays bright (centroid 6-7 kHz) and reads as clock ticks.

differences.a: Peak +1.6 dBFS (clipped), -14.0 LUFS.
differences.b: Peak -4 dBFS, -14.5 LUFS. Loudness matches. The peak is a little below the -1 dBFS target, and crest factor is lower.

differences.b: 1.41 s with 0.04 s of trailing silence. Burst is ~0.05-0.5 s and ticks run to the very end.

differences.a: No stable pitch. Only an unclear formant-like movement.
differences.b: Whistle lines drift up slowly and are clearly pitched.

change_notes: Remove or cut the 2.2 kHz and 4.6 kHz tonal lines by at least 25 dB. If any tone stays, mix it 20 dB under the noise and make it wander randomly rather than glide steadily. Target flatness around 0.25.

Rebuild the main burst (0-0.4 s) as bandpassed noise through two moving formant filters, ~300 Hz (Q 3) and ~1.5-3 kHz (Q 2). Add a 150-400 Hz growl layer (saw or pulse at ~120-180 Hz with distortion) to bring low_mid to ~10% and bass to ~1%.
Replace the slow swell with a fast attack: 5-10 ms ramp starting at 0.04 s, peaking by ~0.11 s. Remove the soft pulses before it. Add a 2-6 kHz noise crack, ~10 ms, at ~0.2 s, +6 dB over the body.
Make the amplitude flutter irregular: 25-60 Hz random-rate AM, 40-60% depth, instead of the regular comb pattern.
Smooth the end of the burst: from 0.4 s fade over ~0.25 s to -20 dB instead of a sudden cut at ~0.45 s.

Rebuild the tail as 8-10 short clicks (3-8 ms bandpassed noise, 1-5 kHz with a little 300 Hz thud) every 80-100 ms from 0.4 to 1.15 s. Decay them from about -30 dB to -60 dB, with slight timing jitter and varied amplitudes. Add a faint noise bed at -45 dB under them so the gaps aren't dead silent.
Leave ~0.2 s of near-silence at the end. Raise the peak to about -1 dBFS and keep ~-14 LUFS.

review.summary: B is a three-hit burst of broadband noise with a sustained 60-200 Hz boom under each hit, so it reads as a gun or thud. A is a crunchy, clicky bite made of clustered bright snaps with a thin low thump. Length and loudness match well, but the character and timing do not.

differences.a: Wet, crunchy chitin bite built from many tiny discrete snaps and crackles, with an organic, irregular feel.
differences.b: Smooth, dense, white-ish noise bursts with a gun-shot or percussive-hit feel. Spectral flatness is 0.52 against A's 0.13, and Qwen heard a knife or gun.

differences.a: Presence-heavy (58% at 2-6 kHz), mid 25%, bass under 1%. Centroid is about 5.4 kHz and rolloff about 7.7 kHz.
differences.b: Bass is 14.5% from a sustained 60-200 Hz block. Presence is only 29% and air is 26%. Rolloff is about 11 kHz, so it is too airy and too boomy, and the presence band is hollow.

differences.a: Very short snaps. The loudness falls about 20 dB within 0.13 s of the peak, and the snaps are separated by gaps with little sustained energy.
differences.b: Each hit has a long exponential body, with -20 dB at 0.29 s and a sustained low-frequency block of about 0.13-0.2 s per hit. It sounds like a boom or pad, not a snap.

differences.a: Starts with a faint tick at 0-0.05 s. The main bite is at 0.07-0.14 s and the second cluster at about 0.17 s, with the peak at 0.09 s. Several sub-clicks sit inside each cluster.
differences.b: Silent for the first 0.04 s. Hits land at 0.05, 0.18 and 0.26 s, so there are three evenly spaced hits instead of two clusters. The third hit is the biggest and falls later than A's energy.

differences.a: Sharp, bright, clicky transients with a crest factor of 27.5 dB. The peaks are spiky and varied in level.
differences.b: Hard but uniform noise-burst onsets, with a crest factor of 20.9 dB and every hit built the same way. There is no fine click detail.

differences.a: Snap clusters, a short low thump, wet crackle and a decaying rustle tail.
differences.b: Only noise bursts plus a sustained low boom. There are no discrete crackles and no scattered rustle tail.

differences.a: Quiet, scattered crackles from 0.25-0.45 s, then a faint noise tail. It is -40 dB by 0.39 s.
differences.b: A smooth noise decay that is -40 dB by 0.46 s, with no crackle. It is a little longer but cleaner and less textured.

differences.a: -18.9 LUFS, with the peak clipping at +5.8 dBFS.
differences.b: -19.1 LUFS, with the peak at -1.7 dBFS. This is on target and properly limited.

differences.a: No pitch movement. Noisy, with a brief thump.
differences.b: A static low boom with a 20-40 Hz pulsing artifact visible in the spectrogram. There is no pitch movement.

Make each click a band-passed noise burst at 2-6 kHz (Q around 1.5) with a 1 ms attack and a 5-15 ms exponential decay. Add a few 1-3 ms clicks at 6-9 kHz for snap. Cut most content above 9 kHz (low-pass at 8-9 kHz) so the rolloff is about 7.5 kHz.

Shorten the low layer to a thump of 80-200 Hz, 60-80 ms, with a 3 ms attack, an exponential decay and a 160 Hz to 70 Hz drop. Set it about 12-15 dB below the click layer so bass energy falls to roughly 1-3%. Remove the sustained boom and the sub-40 Hz pulsing, and high-pass at 50 Hz.

Keep the -19 LUFS and -1 dBFS peak. The decay should reach -20 dB by about 0.15 s and -40 dB by about 0.4 s. Add a very quiet noise floor tail to 0.5 s, with silence from about 0.5 s to 0.72 s. Make 2-3 variants by shifting click timing by +/-10 ms.

review.summary: B matches A's duration (1.76 s), loudness (-23.5 LUFS) and peak level, but it plays as a sequence of noisy synthetic bursts with sustained tonal beeps and a continuous noise bed. It does not read as a dry, clicky Thompson reload with three distinct metal hits and quiet gaps, and its pacing and character differ noticeably.

differences.a: Gritty, dry metallic foley: clacks, rattles and scrapes of metal on metal, with a crunchy 1-9 kHz noise texture.
differences.b: Smooth broadband noise bursts with an electronic feel, plus pure sine-like pings. Qwen hears 'electronic beeps and blips', which suggests sci-fi rather than a mechanical weapon.

differences.a: Almost entirely noise and impact. There is no sustained pitched tone, only a very faint mid tone near 1-2 kHz in the quiet gap.
differences.b: Clear sustained tonal lines: a ~1.05 kHz ping at 0.3-0.4 s and 0.75-0.85 s, a steady ~900 Hz bar from 0.95 to 1.25 s, and a 1.05 kHz ping with harmonics at 1.33 s. Spectral flatness is 0.067 against A's 0.003.

differences.a: Three clusters of discrete clicks and scrapes (mag out ~0.13-0.35 s, mag in ~0.52-0.82 s, bolt clack ~1.3-1.5 s). Between them are only faint ticks.
differences.b: Long noise swells (0.13-0.4 s, 0.5-0.85 s), a flat sustained noise and tone block (0.95-1.25 s), a decaying clack at 1.3 s, and a noise hiss block (1.5-1.76 s). They read as sweeps and pads rather than discrete mechanical events.

differences.a: Starts with events at 0.13 s. Active fraction is 0.3, with sparse events, quiet gaps, and 0.26 s of silence at the end.
differences.b: Same total length, but active fraction is 0.66. Events are longer, and the gap at 0.85-0.95 s is short. A hiss block fills 1.5-1.76 s, and trailing silence is only 0.02 s.

differences.a: Each hit has a near-instant attack and decays to -20 dB in 0.06 s and -40 dB in 0.13 s. There is no sustain.
differences.b: The nominal -20/-40 dB decay times are similar (0.07/0.12 s), but the first two blocks have 0.2-0.3 s sustained noise with ragged envelopes. The 0.95-1.25 s block is a flat sustain with no decay.

differences.a: Dry, with a fast decay into near silence. The last 0.26 s is empty apart from faint hiss.
differences.b: Mostly dry, but the closing 1.5-1.76 s is a steady hiss at roughly -45 dB that cuts off at the file end. The ping ringing at 0.4 s and 0.85 s adds a resonant tail.

review.summary: B matches A's length (0.6 s) and loudness (-15.6 vs -15.3 LUFS) but is a dark, tonal sub-bass boom (83% bass, centroid 541 Hz) with no crack, so it does not read as a punchy SMG shot. A is a broadband noisy blast with an instant attack and a fast decay.

review.summary: B has the right overall length, loudness and bright, noisy-then-ringing idea, but it is a much simpler sound. It is a ~0.2 s noise burst, a gap, then a single wobbling 5 kHz sine, so it lacks A's double-hit, multi-partial glide, low rumble and shimmering tail.

differences.b: A noise burst followed by one pure sine at ~5 kHz and a faint line near 12 kHz. No other partials, rumble or shimmer.

differences.a: Instant peak at 0.03 s with a crunchy clipped burst, a clear gap, then a distinct second hit at ~0.1-0.15 s.
differences.b: A continuous ~0.2 s noise block with no clear gap between hits and a slightly later peak (0.12 s). Its pulsing texture reads as a buzz rather than two crisp hits.

differences.a: Decays 20 dB by 0.34 s and 40 dB by ~1.1 s, with a smooth, quiet fade.

differences.b: A single tone drifts slowly down from ~5.2 kHz to ~4.6 kHz. It is monotonic and static, with no fall-rise.

review.summary: B is three long, flat, 80–90 ms beeps that step downward (about 4.8k, 3.3k, 2.2k Hz) across the full 0.31 s. A is a single 0.07 s ascending four-step chirp (1.5k to 5k Hz) followed by near silence. B has the wrong direction, density, duration and loudness, so it does not fill A's role.

differences.a: All the audible content is in the first about 0.07 s, then a near-silent tail with about 0.12 s of trailing silence. Active fraction is about 0.23.
differences.b: Three separate beeps of about 85 ms each, at 0–0.09, 0.11–0.195 and 0.21–0.30 s, with gaps of about 15–20 ms. Active fraction is about 0.8 and it fills the whole clip.

differences.a: Peak -9.5 dBFS, RMS -21.6 dBFS, crest 12 dB. Sparse and moderate.
differences.b: Peak -2.4 dBFS, RMS -8.1 dBFS, crest 5.6 dB. About 13 dB hotter in RMS and nearly a continuous tone, so it will read as much louder and more fatiguing.

differences.a: Fast swell of about 20 ms, a short sustain, then a sharp cutoff. A -40 dB drop takes about 0.06 s, followed by a very quiet tail.
differences.b: Each beep is a flat-top block with a quick onset and a roughly 10 ms release at its end. Nothing is dynamically shaped, and the third beep has an amplitude wobble of about 150 Hz.

differences.b: Centroid about 3.1 kHz. About 69% mid and 31% presence, so it is darker and more mid-heavy. Average energy sits lower because the beeps fall in pitch.

differences.b: Smooth symmetrical spindle: slow rise to a peak at 0.5 s, broad plateau to about 0.65 s, fast drop to -20 dB by 0.52 s and -40 dB by 0.92 s. There is no dip and no second bump.

differences.b: Active only about 77%. The signal ends abruptly at about 1.0 s, followed by about 0.45 s of near silence (-80 dB), so the sound feels shorter and cut off.

differences.a: Quick swell with a faint transient at 0.06 s and a sharper snarl onset at 0.93 s. Peak at -0.5 dBFS, crest factor 16.7 dB.

review.summary: B matches A's length and loudness but not its character. It has a few pitched, ringing blips, then a 0.25 s gap, then a long low-frequency sine-like thud, where A is a dense, noisy cluster of 5+ metallic clicks and clacks that builds to a heavy clunk near 0.55 s.

differences.b: Only about 4 tonal blips (0.0, 0.09, 0.14, 0.20 s) and one big low thud at 0.55 s. It reads as an alert or beep sequence, not a mechanism.

differences.a: Mid and presence dominant (45% / 35%), air 18%, almost no bass. Centroid is about 5.4 kHz and rolloff about 8.5 kHz.
differences.b: 75% bass, centroid is 668 Hz and rolloff is 1.1 kHz. Dark and boomy, with the sub-200 Hz energy of the final hit sustained and very loud.

differences.a: Broadband noisy click bursts with ringing metallic body at 1-5 kHz and no steady tones (flatness 0.035).
differences.b: Pure sine-like partials: steady lines at about 1.1 kHz and 2.8-3.1 kHz plus harmonics, with very low flatness (0.003). Sounds like a synth tone or beep, not metal.

differences.a: Each hit decays within 30-80 ms. The overall peak is at 0.54 s and is followed by a quick fade, with the last 0.12 s silent.
differences.b: The early blips decay slowly (about 80 ms). The final hit is a long, even, 100 Hz-ish sine ring-out lasting about 0.25 s, with no silent tail at the end (trailing silence 0).

differences.b: Softer, tonal attacks. The clicks have some broadband content, but the big hit's attack is a sine burst with little crack.

review.summary: B is a close match for A's role: a continuous, bass-heavy helicopter rotor loop of the same 3.07 s length and about the same loudness. It differs in having a more regular, pronounced chop, more sub weight, less low-mid body and no 160-200 Hz tonal band, and it adds some top-end air.

differences.a: Steady level of -8 to -9.7 dB per tenth, with one broad dip to about -12 dB around 0.6-0.8 s of the clip. Chop flutter is irregular and dense.
differences.b: Per-tenth level swings are larger and more erratic (-7.1 to -12.8 dB, about 5-6 dB between neighbouring tenths). The chop reads as a distinct, regular pulse train of about 12-14 pulses per second.

differences.a: Bass is 64%, low-mid 27%, sub 2.5%, centroid about 333 Hz. Body is thick through 200-600 Hz.
differences.b: Bass is 74%, sub 6.3%, low-mid only 14%, centroid about 353 Hz. Heavier sub and thinner mids, so it sounds boomier and less full.

differences.b: No visible tonal band. Spectrum is a smooth wash of low-frequency noise and pulses with broadband grit. Flatness is 0.019 vs A's 0.029.

differences.a: Dense, irregular, gritty churn with no obvious periodicity, so it loops without a noticeable pattern.
differences.b: Cleaner, more evenly spaced vertical striations from regular blade pulses. This gives a more recognisable rotor beat, but it is more mechanical and more repetitive.

differences.a: Very dull: presence 0.7%, air 0.1%, with nothing meaningful above a few kHz in the spectrogram.
differences.b: Presence 1.0% and air 0.6%, and the spectrogram shows content up to 10 kHz and above. Brighter and hissier. The 22.05 kHz bandwidth of A is a different delivery rate, not a target.

differences.b: RMS -9.3 dBFS, peak -1.8 dBFS, -10.7 LUFS, crest 7.5 dB. Loudness is matched, but peaks are spikier.

differences.b: Starts and ends near -9.4 / -9.5 dB, which is fine. The pulse regularity and the 5 dB tenth-to-tenth swings could make the repeat audible.

review.summary: B has the same overall length (0.84 s) and integrated loudness (-25.3 LUFS), but it is four long, widely spaced 2-3.5 kHz beeps. A is a dense stutter of about 8 short pulses on a 5.9 kHz tone. The role (turret alert beep) is only loosely met, and the rhythm and pitch are wrong.

differences.a: About 8 rapid pulses at roughly 80 ms spacing (onsets 0.08, 0.16, 0.27, 0.35, 0.43, 0.51 s). The pulses shorten, then a louder final blip ends at 0.63 s, with a faint tail to 0.84 s.
differences.b: Only 4 long beeps (about 0.2 s each) at a 0.21 s spacing (onsets 0.21, 0.42, 0.63) with clear silent gaps. Each beep lasts about 3x longer than A's pulses, so it feels slow and phone-like.

differences.b: Tone at ~1.7 kHz in the first beep, then ~3.2 kHz, ~2.8 kHz and ~2.9 kHz. The pitch steps between beeps and drifts slightly within each one. Centroid is 2651 Hz, less than half of A's 5928 Hz.

differences.a: Very bright and piercing. It has a weak ~500 Hz buzz band, broadband hash and high harmonics near 11-19 kHz.
differences.b: Entirely mid band (100%), with nothing above ~5 kHz apart from a very faint line near 8-9 kHz. It sounds duller, warmer and more like a phone ring.

differences.b: A single sine-like tone per beep, with no secondary layers.

review.summary: B is a sustained, droning low-frequency buzz with a hard cut at ~0.47 s, while A is a swelling stomp that decays fast with a small secondary bump and a faint tail. Overall loudness matches, but the envelope, timing and character differ a lot, so B reads as a rumble or hum rather than a footstep.

differences.a: Swells to peak at ~0.07 s, falls 20 dB by ~0.09 s after the peak and 40 dB by ~0.27 s; clearly percussive with a fast decay.
differences.b: Starts at its peak, then decays slowly and linearly in dB (-12 to -36 dB over 0.4 s); -20 dB at 0.33 s. Reads as a sustained tone, not an impact.

differences.a: ~20 ms of near-silence, then a swelling thud of several pulses peaking at 0.07 s, with a small mid/high burst at the hit.

review.summary: B matches A's duration, average loudness and low-mid weighting, but it is a smooth, steady, harmonic tone with a symmetrical swell and a hard cutoff, not a gritty creature growl with a transient bump. It does not read as a Cyberdemon pain roar.

differences.a: Rough, gravelly, noisy vocal growl with irregular grit and broadband energy. Reads as a creature or cyborg roar.
differences.b: Clean, steady buzzy harmonic stack (sawtooth/pulse-like) with regular amplitude pulsing. Reads as a synth drone or string note, not a voice.

differences.a: Fast rise within about 0.1 s, onsets at 0.05 s and 0.14 s, and a sharp transient bump at about 0.33 s. Crest factor is 17.6 dB.
differences.b: No onsets and a slow fade-in with no transient. Crest factor is only 8.9 dB, and the peak is 8.6 dB lower at -8.7 dBFS.

differences.a: Peak at 0.33 s, then a gradual weakening through the body and a smooth fade-out. Reaches -20 dB at 0.7 s and -40 dB at 0.97 s, with a breathy tail to about 1.4 s.
differences.b: Symmetric lens-shaped swell peaking at 0.56 s. Holds near the peak, then drops off a cliff at about 1.2 s (-29 dB at 0.7 s, -47 dB at 0.8 s). The -20 dB and -40 dB times happen to match, but the shape is wrong. It has an abrupt gate-like cutoff and no breathy tail.

differences.a: Centroid about 1.1 kHz, rolloff 1.5 kHz. Noisy upper content to 6-10 kHz with presence at 4% and air at 1%. Darkens after about 1.1 s.
differences.b: Similar centroid, but the energy sits in discrete harmonics up to about 2.5 kHz with little above 4 kHz. Presence is 1.1% and air 0.1%, so it sounds dull and lacks grit. The late-quarter centroid of 3070 Hz is just codec noise in the near-silent tail.

differences.a: Noise-dominated with only vague harmonics. Dense, irregular formant-like movement in the 150-500 Hz range.
differences.b: Strongly tonal, with clearly resolved harmonic lines and a regular comb-like amplitude modulation of about 50-60 Hz.

differences.a: Unclear pitch and irregular fundamental wobble, around 150-400 Hz, with a vocal-like contour.
differences.b: Static fixed fundamental of about 90-100 Hz with no contour. It sounds mechanical and lifeless.

differences.a: Growl body, mid-range gritty roar, transient hit and breathy tail, plus possibly a mechanical cyborg element.
differences.b: A single layer, with no impact, no breath and no mechanical accent.

change_notes: Replace the static harmonic stack with a growl voice. Use a band-limited sawtooth/pulse fundamental that glides from about 180 Hz up to 260 Hz over 0-0.3 s, then down to 110 Hz by 1.1 s. Add 8-15% random jitter on pitch and 30-60 Hz amplitude modulation with random depth. Filter through 2-3 moving formants (about 500 Hz, 1.1 kHz, 2.2 kHz).

Add a gritty noise layer: bandpassed noise at 1-6 kHz, -10 dB under the body at first and following the main envelope. Add waveshaping or distortion (drive about 12 dB) on the whole voice for roughness, and push the centroid to about 1.1 kHz with presence of about 4%.

Fix the envelope with a 60-100 ms attack to full level, a peak at about 0.33 s, then a smooth exponential decay: -20 dB at 0.7 s, -40 dB at 0.97 s. Remove the symmetric swell and the hard cutoff at 1.2 s.

Add a transient: a 20-30 ms noise burst at 0.33 s (bandpass 2-5 kHz), +6 dB over the body. Also add two small 10-20 ms bumps at 0.05 s and 0.14 s. This should raise the crest factor to about 15 dB or more.
Add a breathy tail: highpassed noise (1.5-4 kHz) fading from 1.0 to 1.4 s at about -35 to -50 dB, with a lowpass sweep from 3 kHz down to 800 Hz. Follow it with silence to 1.7 s.
Add a subtle mechanical layer: a metallic ring-modulated tone at about 300-700 Hz, 150 ms long, at -18 dB, at 0.3 s for a cyborg feel.

Normalise so the peak is about -1 dBFS while keeping integrated loudness near -15 LUFS. The extra crest factor means lowering the body level so the transient carries the peak. Remove the DC offset with a 20 Hz highpass.

review.summary: B is a sequence of tonal, pitched ringing pings (~1 kHz with harmonics) ending in a big sustained sub-bass boom, whereas A is a bright, noisy, broadband flurry of metallic clicks and clacks. Length and overall loudness match, but timbre, balance, tail and character are all wrong for a turret rack.

differences.a: Centroid ~5.8 kHz, energy mostly 1-8 kHz (mid 36%, presence 38%, air 24%), almost no bass (0.1%).
differences.b: Centroid ~980 Hz, 65% of energy in bass (a 60-120 Hz boom), mid 25%, presence and air under 7%. Dark and bottom-heavy.

differences.a: Noisy, broadband metallic clicks with low flatness (0.037) from resonant clacks, with no steady pitch.
differences.b: Pure, narrow tonal pings with a very low flatness of 0.005. Clear pitched lines near 1.1 kHz with harmonics at 2-3 kHz and above, sounding like glass or bell chinks.

differences.a: Roughly 6 distinct mechanical events (click-clack, heavy clack with thump, small tick, medium clack, sharp click-clack, final heavy clack), each a short impact.
differences.b: 4 pitched pings plus a large sub-bass boom at 0.27 s that dominates. No real mechanical clack or rattle texture.

differences.a: Each hit decays in 20-50 ms, with gaps between clusters. Energy is steady to ~0.37 s, then falls fast.
differences.b: Each ping rings and decays slowly, filling the gaps. The boom sustains from 0.27 s to 0.5 s, decaying very slowly (active fraction 0.96 vs 0.73).

differences.a: Very short, dry tail that fades to silence by ~0.48 s.
differences.b: Ends with a still-audible boom and ring, with no clean cut-off. It sounds like a long resonant tail.

differences.a: Sharp, broadband, noisy transients on every hit, with a peak at 0.07 s.
differences.b: Soft, tonal onsets. The only strong transient is the 0.27 s boom, so the peak lands at 0.25 s, late in the clip.

differences.a: Hits near 0.01, 0.07, 0.15, 0.19, 0.27, 0.32 s. Irregular and busy, with the loudest hit early.
differences.b: Regular spacing at ~0.05, 0.13, 0.21, 0.27, 0.37 s. Clip is front-light and ends with the biggest event at 0.27 s.

differences.a: No pitch. Brief 100-400 Hz thumps only on heavy hits.
differences.b: Sequence of rising and falling pitched tones around 1-1.7 kHz, which sounds melodic, plus a 60-120 Hz sustained note.

differences.a: Peak -3.8 dBFS, -15.0 LUFS, crest 15 dB.

change_notes: Delete the sustained 60-120 Hz boom at 0.27 s. Replace it with a 25-40 ms thump: a sine at 180 Hz falling to 80 Hz, at about -12 dB relative to the clicks, and only on the 0.07, 0.19 and 0.32 s hits.
Replace the ringing sine pings with noise-based clicks. Use white noise through a band-pass at 3-6 kHz (Q ~2), with a 1 ms attack and 15-30 ms exponential decay, for each hit.

Add a short metallic resonance to each click: 2-3 inharmonic modal partials (e.g. 2.3, 3.7, 5.9 kHz) with 10-20 ms decay at about -10 dB relative to the noise. Keep the bandwidth wide so it reads as metal clack and not a bell.
Retime the events to about 0.01, 0.07, 0.09 (small echo clack), 0.15 (quiet tick), 0.19, 0.27, 0.32 s. Make the 0.07 s and 0.32 s hits the loudest (peak near -4 dBFS), the others 6-10 dB lower.
Pair each main hit as click plus clack: a second smaller transient 15-25 ms later, with slightly lower filter centre (about 2.5 kHz).
Cut the tail. After 0.37 s apply a 60 ms fade to -40 dB and leave only faint high noise (-45 dB) to 0.48 s, with no reverb.
Tilt the EQ: high-pass at 300 Hz except for the thumps, with a +3 dB shelf above 5 kHz so the centroid lands near 5-6 kHz. Normalise to peak about -4 dBFS and -15 LUFS.

review.summary: B is three smooth, steady, buzzy tone blocks with hard gaps, where A is a rough, bursty, vocal growl with a dynamic, organic envelope and a long fade. Overall loudness and spectral centroid match, but the character, transients and peak level do not.

differences.a: Rough, throaty, modulated creature growl with irregular, formant-like harmonic bands and vocal breath/grit.
differences.b: Smooth, evenly pulsed (roughly 100 Hz AM) harmonic buzz with regular vertical striations. It reads as synthetic, like an engine or spaceship, and not as an animal.

differences.a: Sharp onsets at 0.05 s, 0.37/0.5 s, 1.21/1.29 s, 2.06/2.19 s, with a bright bark streak near 1.25 s. Crest factor is 21.7 dB and the peak is -4.4 dBFS.
differences.b: Soft swell-in blocks with no transients. Attack is 0.41 s, crest factor 9.5 dB, peak -16.8 dBFS, and only 2 detected onsets.

differences.a: Irregular swells and drops: roar at 0.4-1.1 s, accent at 1.25 s, quieter dip, big roar at 2.05-2.8 s, then a slow, natural fade to about 3.6 s.
differences.b: Three near-identical flat-topped blocks (0-0.9 s, 1.05-1.95 s, 2.2-3.1 s) with abrupt cut-offs and dead gaps. The tail drops by about 60 dB and then goes silent.

differences.a: The sound is active across 87% of the clip, with a 0.2 s silent end and a lingering low-level tail with weak pulses at 2.83 s and 3.11 s.
differences.b: The clip is the same total length (3.89 s), but 0.86 s of the end is silent, with 72% active. The gap structure is mechanical and evenly repeated.

differences.a: Energy split: bass 16.8%, low-mid 51%, mid 30%. Strong 100-500 Hz body plus harmonic lines near 1 and 2 kHz, and a rolloff of 1.36 kHz.
differences.b: Low-mid is overweight at 70%, bass only 6.5%, mid 21%, and a tiny amount of sub. Energy is concentrated at 450-1000 Hz with a clean ladder, and the rolloff is lower at 1.18 kHz. The result is thin in the 100-300 Hz growl body.

differences.a: Tonal harmonics mixed with rough breath noise and broadband grit, and flatness of 0.001 with vocal irregularity.
differences.b: Almost purely periodic harmonic tone, with noise lacking in the body. The unnatural regularity makes it sound like a drone.

differences.a: Pitch is unclear but wanders organically as the vocal formants shift between bursts.
differences.b: Static, near-constant pitch in each block, with identical blocks repeated and only a slight drop at the end.

differences.a: Peak -4.4 dBFS, RMS -26.1, -25.0 LUFS, loudness range 3.3 LU.
differences.b: Integrated loudness is matched at -25.3 LUFS, but the peak is 12 dB lower at -16.8 dBFS. Loudness range is only 2.3 LU, so it feels flat and lacks punch.

differences.a: A long, natural, quiet rumbly tail that reaches -40 dB at 3.59 s.
differences.b: No real tail: the third block cuts off at about 3.1 s, followed by only a faint low-level smear.

change_notes: Rebuild as a formant-filtered vocal growl: sawtooth or pulse source at 60-90 Hz fundamental, with 2-3 formant bandpasses (approx. 450 Hz, 1.0 kHz, 2.1 kHz, Q 4-6) whose centres are moved by random LFO/jitter of +/-15%. Replace the regular AM with irregular jitter, 30-80 Hz rate at random depth 20-50%.
Add attack transients: a 20-40 ms noise burst bandpassed 1-4 kHz at 0.05 s, 0.37 s, 1.22 s and 2.06 s, shaped with a 5 ms attack, +8 dB over the body. Cut the 0.41 s swell-in to under 80 ms.

Restructure the envelope to match A: burst 1 at 0.05-0.35 s; sustained roar at 0.4-1.1 s; short bark at 1.22-1.4 s (30% shorter, brighter, upper formant to 3 kHz); dip at 1.6-2.0 s at -10 dB; big roar at 2.05-2.8 s, the loudest. Make the three blocks distinct in length and pitch (e.g. -3 and +2 semitones), not copies.
Remove the dead gaps: fill 0.9-1.05 s and 1.95-2.2 s with low-level growl or rumble at -20 to -30 dB relative to the roars, instead of silence.
Add a bass body layer: low-passed noise/saw at 100-300 Hz, +6 dB, so bass is about 17% and low-mid about 50%. Reduce the 450-1000 Hz dominance by about 4 dB.

Add grit: mix 10-20% broadband noise (200 Hz-3 kHz) modulated by the growl envelope, and apply soft saturation (tanh drive about 3) for roughness. Keep content above 3 kHz minimal, with a 12 dB/oct lowpass at about 3.5 kHz.

Extend and soften the tail: after 2.8 s, exponentially decay a low rumble (100-250 Hz) over about 0.8 s to -40 dB at about 3.6 s, add two small pulses at 2.83 s and 3.11 s at -15 dB, and keep only 0.2 s of silence at the end.
Raise the peak to about -4 dBFS by increasing transient and roar levels (or a limiter at -4 dBFS), keeping the integrated level at -25 LUFS; this lifts crest factor to about 18-20 dB.

review.summary: B replaces A's noisy, clattery, mechanical click sequence with a pitched, beep-like tonal sequence plus a low sub-heavy boom, so it reads like a game UI chime instead of a turret being cocked. Total length and integrated loudness match, but the character, spectrum and timing structure are very different.

differences.a: Broadband, noisy metallic clacks and rattles (flatness 0.036) with resonant but inharmonic content.
differences.b: Clean, pure sine/harmonic tones with discrete stable partials (flatness 0.003), reading as beeps.

differences.a: Energy concentrated in mid and presence (1-8 kHz), centroid about 5.6 kHz, bass about 0.2%, bright and clacky.
differences.b: 75.8% of energy in the bass band, centroid 729 Hz, and the last quarter centroid is about 135 Hz, so it is dull and boomy, with a few tonal lines near 1-3 kHz.

differences.a: Small ticks, a 3-4 clack ratchet group, an isolated tick, a louder rattle cluster, a heavy bolt-slam and a brief metal ring tail.
differences.b: Five stepped tonal beeps rising in pitch (roughly 1.1 to 1.3 kHz fundamentals), then one big sub-heavy sustained boom at 0.6 s. No clacks, rattle or latch character.

differences.a: Sharp, sparse, varied-amplitude percussive transients with little sustained body.
differences.b: Beeps have instant attacks but then sustain and decay linearly like organ or sine stabs, with uniform, repetitive amplitude. The final boom has a soft sustained body.

differences.a: Quiet ticks 0-0.1 s, cluster 0.15-0.3 s, tick at 0.39 s, louder cluster 0.44-0.62 s, tail to about 0.75 s. About 0.13 s of trailing silence, irregular rhythm.
differences.b: Five evenly spaced beeps at about 0.05-0.3 s, then a dead gap of about 0.25 s (0.35-0.6 s), then one boom at 0.6 s lasting to the end, with only 0.02 s of trailing silence. The rhythm is regular and the gap sits in the wrong place.

differences.a: Each event decays quickly (-20 dB in about 0.09 s), leaving a short, faint tail.

review.summary: B is a sustained, buzzing sub drone that starts at full level and decays slowly over 0.45 s, whereas A is a staggered build-up of low pulses that swells to a peak around 0.14 s and then drops away quickly. differences.b: Peaks instantly at t=0 (attack 0 s, no leading silence) with no build-up, so it reads as a sustained tone start rather than a footfall.

change_notes: Reshape the envelope: attack 20-40 ms to a peak at about 0.1-0.25 s (not 0.55 s), hold at -13 to -15 dB until 0.55 s, then decay exponentially: -20 dB at 0.5 s, -40 dB at 0.9 s. Remove the symmetric swell and the cliff cut; use a 0.3-0.4 s smooth release.

Replace the regular AM pulsing with irregular modulation: randomise the pulse rate between 30 and 90 Hz with 30-50% jitter, plus a slow random FM wobble of +/-15% on the fundamental at 3-8 Hz, to get a throat-rattle growl.

review.summary: B is four long, smooth sine-like beeps around 2-3 kHz, while A is a fast train of about 13 short, bright, buzzy, harmonically rich bursts. Overall length and loudness match, but rhythm, brightness and character differ a lot, so B does not fill A's role.

review.summary: B is a smooth, slow-swelling, sustained drone/growl with banded harmonics, whereas A is a harsh, abrupt, bright roar that peaks early (0.37s), then collapses quickly into a quiet tail. Length and integrated loudness are similar, but the envelope, attack, brightness and peak level are all wrong for a punchy boss death roar.

differences.a: Immediate harsh, raspy onset at full level (-20 dB at 0 s) with bright noisy burst up to ~10 kHz and a gritty surge near 0.37 s (-11 dB); crest factor 18 dB.
differences.b: Slow fade-in from -30.6 dB, no transient, no onset detected; crest factor only 9.5 dB so it feels flat and compressed.

differences.a: Peak at 0.37 s, drops 20 dB by ~0.73 s after the peak and -40 dB by 1.83 s; level falls to -28 dB by 0.4 of the file and sits at ~-40 dB over the rest, i.e. a front-loaded roar with a long quiet rumbling tail.
differences.b: Peak at 0.83 s, holds -15 to -17 dB until ~1.5 s, then drops abruptly at ~1.85 s to silence-ish. Back-loaded, plateau-like, with a cliff-like cutoff rather than a natural decay.

differences.a: Long, quiet low-mid rumble and breathy tail from ~1.1 to 2.3 s, slowly darkening (-40 to -53 dB).
differences.b: Almost no tail: hard drop at ~1.85 s then a low-level residue (-42 to -54 dB) with a thin spurious vertical spike near 2.25 s.

differences.a: Raspy, distorted, noisy vocal roar with chaotic, irregular energy (speckled spectrogram).
differences.b: Clean, regular amplitude-modulated harmonic/buzz tone (vertical stripes ~30-40 Hz pulse rate), reading as an engine/drone or alien machine, not a creature.

differences.a: Noisy, broadband in the first 0.4 s, gritty harmonics afterward.
differences.b: Almost purely tonal/harmonic (flatness 0.0), very little noise; little air/presence.

differences.b: Static pitch/formant bands with no gestural movement; centroid slides from 1500 Hz to 96 Hz only through level fade, not a pitch fall.

review.summary: B is a clean, loud 3.7 kHz sine double-beep with a silent gap, while A is a very quiet, ultra-bright (9.6-16 kHz) pulsing buzz that cuts off at 0.16 s. Same total length, but the register, texture, loudness and timing all differ, so B does not fill A's role.

review.summary: B matches A's length, overall loudness and low-mid centroid, but it is a smooth, steady, engine-like drone with a slow swell and a sudden cut near 1.55 s. A is a ragged, noisy, vocal growl with a bright breath onset, a peak near 0.5 s and a gradual rattling decay. It fills the role poorly and has the wrong feel.

differences.b: Uniform, periodic, buzzy tone with regular amplitude modulation and straight harmonic stripes. Qwen heard it as an engine or motorcycle, so it reads as mechanical.

differences.b: Low-mid 63%, bass 10%, mid 23%, sub 2.5%. Bass is lighter, the mids are more prominent and there is a constant sub hum at 20-50 Hz.

differences.a: Quiet muttering phrase 0.05-1.15 s with onsets at 0.05, 0.24 and 0.38 s, a near-silent gap at 1.15-1.23 s, then a loud roar from 1.23 s to ~1.8 s.

A is a dense, crunchy, clipped noise burst that collapses into a granular debris rumble. B has the right role but lacks A's violence, debris texture and sub-only tail.

differences.b: Instant attack at 0 s, peak at t=0 (-12.8 dB in the first tenth), no swell and no distinct onset. Reads as a sustained buzz starting at full level.

review.summary: B matches A's two-phase structure, 1.89 s length and integrated loudness, but it sounds like a smooth, periodic engine idle rather than a rough, gritty creature growl. It lacks A's chaotic mid-range rasp, its transient bumps and its dip between phases, and it has a different low-end balance.

differences.b: Very regular, comb-like pulse train of evenly spaced harmonics (~40-60 Hz modulation) that reads as a motor or engine idle (Qwen heard an engine). Smooth and mechanical.

differences.a: Energy is split between bass (48%) and low-mid (46%), with almost no sub. 85% rolloff is ~431 Hz. Centroid is ~1 kHz early and ~360 Hz late.

differences.a: Noisy, broadband and raspy, with scattered mid-range formant-like speckle at 1-5 kHz in the first half.

review.summary: B matches A's length (2.97 s) and integrated loudness (-25.6 vs -25.4 LUFS), and it has the same rough landmarks (hit at 0.58 s, impact near 1.4 s). A is a continuous low rumble with two discrete clicks, a clack and a smooth whirr.
