review.summary: B is the right kind of sound, a short noisy impact with a sub thump, and matches A's length, loudness and overall energy. It lacks A's sharp double-thud structure, the falling 600-250 Hz sweep and the sustained ~800 Hz metallic ring, and it has a muddier, longer sub block plus stray tail clicks.

differences.a: Fast onset after a quiet 0.05 s lead-in; dense broadband burst with a sharp, punchy front. Peak near 0.12 s, clipped.
differences.b: Gradual swell from about 0.05 s to a peak at 0.13 s, with a soft, rounded front and a slightly lower peak (-2.4 dBFS). Reads less like a sharp hit.

differences.a: Two distinct heavy low thuds (~0.08-0.12 s and ~0.18-0.30 s) give a clear double-hit feel.
differences.b: One continuous sub block from 0.05 to about 0.25 s, then a weaker bump to about 0.38 s. The pulses are smeared and do not read as two separate hits.

differences.a: Audible falling tonal sweep from about 600 Hz to 250 Hz inside the body, between 0.05 and 0.25 s.
differences.b: No pitch movement; the body is plain noise and sub.

differences.a: Thin steady metallic ring near 800 Hz from 0.24 s to about 0.9 s, plus soft low-mid residue. Smooth fade, ~40 dB down by 0.5 s.
differences.b: No sustained tone. Tail is a noise wash with scattered vertical clicks at about 0.4-0.8 s (onset at 0.44 s). Falls 40 dB by 0.28 s, so the tail is shorter and less metallic.

differences.a: Centroid ~1.27 kHz; noise bright up to ~6 kHz; sub 16%, bass 22%, low-mid 29%, mid 22%.
differences.b: Centroid ~1.22 kHz, similar split but a heavier sub/bass block (18%/24%). Mids are somewhat less dense and the body is more muddy.

differences.a: Flatness 0.19: noise body mixed with a tonal ping and sweep.
differences.b: Flatness 0.07: smoother, more tonal or rumbly, with less crunchy noise grain.

differences.a: 0.975 s, with active content to about 0.7 s and 0.3 s of silence.
differences.b: 0.98 s, active to about 0.64 s, then silent. Timing is comparable.

differences.a: Peak +0.4 dBFS (clipped), -19.0 LUFS.
differences.b: Peak -2.4 dBFS, -19.5 LUFS. Within tolerance.

differences.a: Mono.
differences.b: Mono.

missing_elements: Second distinct low thud at ~0.18-0.30 s
Falling 600->250 Hz tonal sweep in the body
Sustained ~800 Hz metallic ring through the tail
Sharp punchy transient crack at the front of the hit
extra_elements: Sub-heavy continuous rumble block 0.05-0.25 s
Scattered click/tick artifacts in the tail at ~0.4-0.8 s
Slow swell into the peak
change_notes: Sharpen the attack: add a 2-6 kHz noise crack, 10-20 ms with a 1-2 ms rise, at 0.05 s, about +6 dB over the body, and cut the slow swell so the peak lands by ~0.07-0.12 s.

Split the sub into two hits: a 45-80 Hz sine thump with pitch drop from 100 to 45 Hz over 80 ms at 0.08 s, and a second one at 0.19 s, 100 ms long, about -2 dB. Put a 40-60 ms gap or dip of ~8 dB between them instead of one held block.
Add a falling sine/triangle sweep from 600 to 250 Hz over 0.05-0.25 s, about -12 dB under the noise body, to give the metallic pitched drop.

Add a metallic ping: a 780-820 Hz sine with a slight 1.5 kHz partial at -20 dB, starting at 0.24 s and decaying to silence by ~0.8 s (about -50 dB at 0.5 s, slow exponential), instead of the noise wash.
Remove the isolated click events at 0.4-0.8 s, or lowpass the tail noise at 2 kHz and fade it smoothly to -60 dB by 0.65 s.
Make the body noise grainier and denser: raise the noise level 3-4 dB in 1-6 kHz for 0.05-0.25 s, and trim the sub/bass block by about 2 dB so the double thud stays punchy rather than boomy.
Keep the peak near -1 dBFS (raise ~1.4 dB) and loudness near -19 LUFS, and keep the final 0.3 s silent.

review.summary: B is the right kind of sound: a three-phase mechanical rifle reload with matching length, onset grid and slam position. It is cleaner, tonal and synthetic where A is gritty and noisy, with a lighter, less punchy slam, an extra late click and about 2.6 LU less loudness.

differences.a: Gritty, raw, rattly broadband noise with metallic scrapes. It sounds like a real recording and has a continuous noise floor between clicks.
differences.b: Cleaner and more synthetic, with discrete bursts of noise on near-silent gaps. Flatness is 0.43 against 0.31 for A, and the notes call it digital and electronic.

differences.a: Very little bass (0.9%) and low-mid 7.1%. Energy sits in mid and presence. The slam has a short thump below 500 Hz.
differences.b: Low-mid is nearly double (13.1%) and bass 2.2%. There is a bloomy 100-250 Hz thump on each click and a long, sub-heavy slam, so it sounds boomier and less clacky.

differences.a: Almost no stable tonal content, only a faint 3 kHz line after 2.5 s and a short 8-10 kHz ring at the slam.
differences.b: Distinct sine-like pings at about 1.5-2 kHz on the mag clicks (0.2 s, 1.2 s, 1.35 s, 1.5 s) and peaks at 7.8, 9.2 and 12.6 kHz. They read as electronic beeps rather than metal.

differences.a: Instant, sharp snaps with a hard crack. The slam has a strong full-spectrum transient peaking at 0 dBFS, and the snap at 1.4 s is the loudest of phase 2.
differences.b: The transients are softer and more clustered. The slam is a broad noise burst with a rounder onset and less peaky crack (crest 22.3 dB, peak -1.6 dBFS). Phase-2 clicks are thin and ping-like.

differences.a: The slam drops 20 dB in 0.1 s and 40 dB in 0.27 s, followed by a faint residual rattle to about 2.9 s.
differences.b: Similar 20 dB drop (0.11 s) but a faster 40 dB decay (0.21 s). The tail is cut off hard at about 2.55 s, with no residual rattle or 3 kHz line.

differences.a: Phase 1 has a rattly cluster of 0.21-0.52 s with a few stronger taps. Phase 2 has light clicks building to a snap at 1.4 s. The slam is at 2.05 s with a short ring.
differences.b: The same three-phase structure. Phase 1 is more spaced, with an extra isolated burst at about 0.85 s that is louder than A's faint tick. B also adds a stray click at about 1.6 s, a clean pre-slam gap with a tick at 1.87 s, and a late isolated click at about 2.5 s.

differences.a: File is 3.53 s with 0.21 s leading silence and 0.98 s trailing silence. Slam peaks at 2.1 s. Gaps are 0.9-1.05 s and 1.65-1.95 s.
differences.b: File is 3.53 s with 0.3 s leading silence and 0.99 s trailing silence. Slam peaks at 2.1 s. The gap structure is similar, but the first event starts about 0.09 s later.

differences.a: -16.4 LUFS, RMS -22.5 dB, peak +0.2 dBFS with one clipped sample.
differences.b: -19.0 LUFS, RMS -23.9 dB, peak -1.6 dBFS. About 2.6 LU quieter, though inside the brief's ±3 LU. Slightly weaker presence in phases 1-2.

differences.a: Mono.
differences.b: Mono.

differences.a: A faint residual tail with a thin 3 kHz line, otherwise dry.
differences.b: A very short decay and then an abrupt cutoff, with no lingering rattle.

change_notes: Replace the sine-like 1.5-2 kHz pings on the phase-2 clicks with filtered noise plus inharmonic metal resonators (3-6 kHz, decay 20-40 ms, Q around 3-5), and cut the tonal ping level by at least 10 dB.
Reduce the low-mid bloom: high-pass the click layers at about 250 Hz and shorten the 100-250 Hz thumps from about 80 ms to 25-40 ms at -6 dB. This brings low-mid from 13% to about 7-8%.

Tighten the slam: add a 1-3 ms full-band noise crack at 2.05 s, +4 dB over the body, with a 3-8 kHz emphasis. Keep a short 200-500 Hz body of about 60-80 ms and shorten the sub that now runs from 20 Hz up. Raise the peak to about -0.5 dBFS.

Add a gritty noise bed at -40 to -45 dB relative to the peak, bandpassed at 2-9 kHz, with randomly modulated 5-15 ms bursts (rattle) across 0.2-0.6 s and 1.1-1.5 s. This lowers flatness toward 0.3 and removes the clean-digital feel.
Make the phase-2 snap at 1.4 s stronger: +6 dB over the other clicks, with a 1-3 kHz crack of about 15 ms and a brief 150 Hz thump of 30 ms.

Remove or lower by 12 dB the stray clicks at about 1.6 s, 1.87 s and 2.5 s, and reduce the 0.85 s burst to a faint tick at -35 dB relative to the peak. Keep the gaps at 0.9-1.05 s and 1.65-1.95 s near-silent.

Add a 0.5 s residual tail after the slam: noise at -60 dB, 2-6 kHz, with a faint 3 kHz tone at -70 dB, instead of the abrupt cutoff at 2.55 s. Add a short metallic ring at 8-10 kHz, 80 ms, at the slam.
Raise overall level by 2-3 LU so integrated loudness is about -16.5 to -17 LUFS, and move the first onset from 0.3 s to about 0.21 s.

review.summary: B is the right kind of sound: a low-heavy, noisy rumble-burst of the same length, with a similar decay. It starts later and slower, has less bass-to-low-mid weight and less high-end hiss, and its tail thins out into scattered bumps instead of a smooth decay.

differences.a: Ramps up within about 0.05 s and hits the main burst right away. There is a strong, sharp transient with peaks reaching 0 dBFS or higher and some clipping.
differences.b: Starts after about 0.05 s of near-silence, then a step onset with peak at 0.11 s (attack 0.09 s). It is softer and a little late, and has no clip-level crack.

differences.a: Active from 0 s, with the body from 0.05 to 0.5 s and a second accent near 0.35 s. The tail ends around 1.08 s plus 0.06 s of silence.
differences.b: Same total length of about 1.21 s, but the first 0.05 s is empty, with 0.02 s of leading silence and a 0.09 s trailing gap. The onsets are scattered (0.05, 0.25, 0.33, 0.81, 0.99 s), so the timing feels less like one burst with one accent.

differences.a: The body is sustained and fairly steady through about 0.4 s, then a smooth decay (-20 dB at 0.65 s, -40 dB at 1.08 s).
differences.b: There is a dip in the first 0.2 s (-18.6 dB in the 0.2 s slot against -9 dB around it) and a hotter bump at 0.3 s. The decay is slightly faster (-20 dB at 0.56 s, -40 dB at 1.01 s), and the tail is a string of isolated pulses at 0.8-1.0 s.

differences.a: Centroid is about 268 Hz, rolloff about 194 Hz, with 44% sub and 40% bass, so it has solid 60-250 Hz punch.
differences.b: Centroid is about 217 Hz, rolloff about 129 Hz, with 46.5% sub and 29% bass. It is sub-heavy and lacks 60-250 Hz body. The later part of the tail falls to about 47 Hz, much lower than A.

differences.a: Very noisy and rough, with broadband hiss and rattle extending up to the highs early on. A faint 12 kHz streak is also present.
differences.b: Noise-like but cleaner and more low-passed. There is less mid/high hiss and no high streak. Spectral flatness is higher, though that is just the low-end distribution.

differences.a: Jittery, rattling and clanky, with dense irregular amplitude pulses.
differences.b: Has a slower, more regular amplitude-modulated pulsing, closer to a wobble than a rattle. It is less metallic.

differences.a: -15.7 LUFS, RMS -12.4 dBFS, peak +3.8 dBFS (clipped).
differences.b: -17.0 LUFS, RMS -14.2 dBFS, peak -1.2 dBFS, no clipping. This is about 1.3 LU quieter, which is within tolerance.

differences.a: The tail loses highs first and fades smoothly into a thin low tail.
differences.b: The tail is darker and thinner, with separated low bumps and a slightly abrupt cutoff. There is a dip near 1.1-1.2 s (-107 dB).

Mid and high hiss (steam) layer extending to several kHz and a faint 12 kHz component

60-250 Hz punch in the body

extra_elements: About 0.05 s of near-silence at the start

change_notes: Remove the empty lead-in: start the burst at 0 s with a 5-10 ms attack, and add a 10-20 ms broadband noise click (1-6 kHz) at the start at about +6 dB over the body to get the hit.
Fix the dip at 0.2 s: hold the body at about -9 to -11 dB from 0.05 to 0.4 s, and put a single accent at 0.35 s of +3 dB instead of the several onsets at 0.25/0.33.

Add 60-250 Hz body: raise a 100-200 Hz noise/rumble layer by about +4 dB, and cut the sub below 50 Hz by about 3 dB to move the bass share from 29% to about 40% and the centroid from 217 Hz to about 270 Hz.
Add a steam hiss layer: bandpass noise at 2-8 kHz, 0.4 s long, at -25 dB under the body, decaying faster than the low end (lowpass sweeping 8 kHz down to 1 kHz).

Replace the slow wobble with a rattle: modulate the body with random 30-60 Hz amplitude jitter (30-40% depth), and add a few short metallic clank resonances at 600-1500 Hz, 20-40 ms each, in the 0.05-0.4 s range.
Smooth the tail: use one exponential decay reaching -20 dB at about 0.65 s and -40 dB at about 1.08 s, and remove the isolated bumps at 0.8 and 1.0 s. End with 0.06 s of silence.
Keep the peak at -1 to -3 dBFS and the loudness near -16 LUFS (raise by about 1 dB).

review.summary: B matches A's length, three-onset timing, loudness and decay shape, but it sounds cleaner and more synthetic. A sustained 366 Hz tone with clean harmonic lines replaces A's noisy, rattly creak, and the transients are sharper and more separated.

differences.a: Noisy broadband rattle with no dominant tone; only faint lines near 800 Hz and 1.6 kHz.
differences.b: Strong sustained ~366 Hz tone from about 0.24 to 0.85 s, with clean harmonics at ~1 kHz, 2.1 kHz, 3.3 kHz and 4.6 kHz. It reads as a drone or buzzer rather than a door.

differences.a: Flatness 0.236, noisy and rattly with a mottled texture.
differences.b: Flatness 0.098, noticeably more tonal and cleaner. The sustained harmonic stack dominates the middle and tail.

differences.a: Quiet, soft latch click at 0.05 s, then clatter bursts at 0.14 s and 0.23 s that sit inside a sustained rattle.
differences.b: Sharp, isolated, bright transients at 0.06, 0.15 and 0.24 s, with a clean gap after the first. The first hit is louder and more percussive than A's quiet click, and its centroid is about 3.7 kHz in the first quarter against A's 2 kHz.

differences.a: Sustained rattle to ~0.5 s, then -20 dB at 0.4 s and -40 dB at 0.6 s, with a faint scrape tail to ~0.85 s.
differences.b: Similar overall shape, but it dips more between hits (-24 dB against -19 dB at the third tenth) and decays slightly earlier (-20 dB at 0.33 s, -40 dB at 0.53 s). The tone holds on while the noise drops away.

differences.a: Heavy low thumps (40-150 Hz) pulse through the middle, giving a boomy, irregular clunk with wobbling bursts to ~0.55 s.
differences.b: Low thump is present at 0.08-0.4 s but fades earlier and is smoother, with little pulsing rattle after 0.4 s. There is no creak or squeal with pitch movement.

differences.a: Thinning scrape and faint ~800 Hz squeal, fading naturally to near silence at 0.85 s.
differences.b: Tail is mostly the steady ~366 Hz and 1 kHz tone, ending with a fairly abrupt cutoff at ~0.87 s. Late tick-like noise bursts appear at 0.68-0.8 s.

differences.a: 0.96 s, onsets at 0.05, 0.14 and 0.23 s, peak at 0.23 s.
differences.b: 0.96 s, the same three onset times and the same peak time. Leading silence is 0.04 s against 0.01 s.

differences.a: -17.9 LUFS, peak -0.1 dBFS, RMS -20.4 dBFS.
differences.b: -18.3 LUFS, peak -1.5 dBFS, RMS -21.0 dBFS.

differences.a: Mostly unpitched; a faint hinge squeal around 800 Hz to 1.6 kHz.
differences.b: Static pitched tone around 366 Hz with fixed harmonics and no glide, which sounds synthetic.

change_notes: Cut the sustained 366 Hz tone by 15-20 dB, or replace it with a creak whose frequency glides 800 Hz to 1.6 kHz over 0.3 s, with amplitude wobble at 10-20 Hz. Fade it to nothing by 0.8 s so there is no steady drone.
Add a bandpassed noise rattle (300 Hz-3 kHz) with random 20-40 ms bursts from 0.25 to 0.6 s, using irregular amplitude modulation at 15-30 Hz. Raise flatness toward ~0.22.

Soften the first hit: lower its level by about 8-10 dB and its brightness, to a short ~15 ms click with a faint 1.7 kHz ping. Roll off above ~6 kHz on all three transients so the first-quarter centroid drops from 3.7 kHz to about 2 kHz.
Extend the 40-150 Hz thumps with pulsing bumps at about 0.14, 0.23, 0.32, 0.4 and 0.5 s, each with a 50-80 ms decay, so the low end continues to ~0.55 s instead of ending at 0.4 s.
Reshape the tail: let the scrape decay smoothly with a lowpass sweep from 2 kHz to 600 Hz over 0.58-0.85 s, and remove the ticks at 0.68-0.8 s. Drop the ~0.87 s hard cut and use a 60 ms fade.
Fill the dips between onsets by about 3-4 dB (the third tenth is -24 dB in B against -19 dB in A). Raise the peak to about -0.5 dBFS and lengthen the decay so -40 dB arrives at ~0.6 s.

review.summary: B has the right overall shape: a short noisy thud with sub weight, a similar 0.98 s length, matching loudness and a fading tail. It misses A's metallic 800 Hz ring, its double-thump structure and its gritty bright burst, and it adds a sustained sub bed and a pulsing tail that A lacks.

differences.a: Bright, gritty broadband burst reaching 8 kHz+ for 0.05-0.25 s. Centroid 1272 Hz, rolloff 2.3 kHz, flatness 0.19, with a strong low-mid and mid body (29% and 22%).
differences.b: Darker and more low-weighted. Centroid 1074 Hz, rolloff 1.8 kHz, bass 28%, sub 20%. The highs are concentrated in a narrower burst around 0.1-0.2 s and the mids are thinner.

differences.a: A thin, steady metallic ring near 800 Hz starts at about 0.25 s and persists faintly to about 0.9 s. A faint falling sweep runs from about 400 Hz to 250 Hz.
differences.b: No tonal ring and no prominent peaks. Only diffuse noisy mids around 500-1000 Hz, so the metallic ping is absent.

differences.a: Two distinct heavy thumps at about 0.08-0.12 s and 0.17-0.3 s, giving a double-hit feel. Decays to -40 dB at 0.5 s.
differences.b: One sub bed of about 40-100 Hz held flat from 0.05 to 0.35 s, with a single dip at about 0.21 s. It sounds like a sustained boom rather than two punchy hits. Decay to -40 dB at 0.41 s.

differences.a: A tiny pre-click at 0.05 s, then an abrupt full-band onset at about 0.05-0.06 s (sharp wall in the waveform). Peak reached by 0.12 s.
differences.b: A gradual swell: a quiet ramp from about 0.05 s to a peak at 0.13 s, with no sharp transient wall. This is less punchy and the onset is softer.

differences.a: A smooth, thin, quiet tail with the ring, fading to silence by about 0.9 s.
differences.b: A rhythmic series of vertical pulses and bursts at 0.3-0.7 s, plus a faint sub bump around 0.78-0.9 s. It sounds like a stuttering or ratcheting tail, not a natural decay.

differences.a: Gritty, noisy, flatness 0.19.
differences.b: Cleaner and more tonal, flatness 0.054, because the sub is tone-dominated.

differences.a: Peak +0.4 dBFS (clipped), -19.0 LUFS.
differences.b: Peak -2.3 dBFS, -19.2 LUFS. This is on target and clean.

differences.a: 0.975 s, about 0.3 s of trailing silence, active fraction 0.44.
differences.b: 0.98 s, 0.32 s of trailing silence, active fraction 0.32. Slightly shorter audible content.

differences.b: Mono.

change_notes: Replace the flat sub bed with two sine thumps: the first at 0.07 s, 100 Hz falling to 45 Hz over 80 ms, decaying in about 90 ms; the second at 0.17 s, 90 Hz falling to 40 Hz over 120 ms, decaying in about 130 ms. Keep the sub at or below the current level and remove the sustained hold and the late bump at 0.78-0.9 s.

Add a metallic ring: a sine at 800 Hz (optionally with a partial at about 1.6 kHz at -12 dB) starting at 0.24 s at about -45 dB relative to the peak. Decay it slowly over about 0.6 s so it is faintly audible to 0.85 s.

Brighten and roughen the main burst: 0.05-0.25 s of white noise high-passed at 300 Hz with energy up to 8 kHz, boosted +4 dB at 2-6 kHz. Add a bandpassed 300-1.3 kHz noise layer (about 0.2 s) to lift the low-mid and mid body to about 29% and 22%.

Remove the periodic pulses and ratchet bursts from 0.3-0.7 s. Use smooth exponential noise decay, with a -40 dB point at about 0.5 s (currently 0.41 s). Add a faint 400 Hz to 250 Hz falling sine sweep over 0.1-0.3 s at about -25 dB relative to the peak.
Keep the peak at -1 to -2 dBFS and about -19 LUFS. No clipping is needed.

review.summary: B has the right overall structure (thud, clicks, rustle, beeps, tail) and matches length and loudness. But its beeps are four long, loud, pure tones that dominate the sound, whereas A's beeps are short, noisy and buried in foley and end on one flat confirmation tone. B's opening thud and handling foley are also thinner and less crunchy.

differences.a: Beeps are three short ~4.5 kHz blips (~0.69, 0.75, 0.80 s) sitting inside noisy thumps, then one longer flat-topped beep at ~0.89-0.97 s.
differences.b: Four long, loud beeps at 4.5 kHz (plus a 9 kHz harmonic) from ~0.65 s, each swelling with a thump. The last one rings on to ~1.2 s.

differences.a: Final beep is a short (~80-100 ms), flat-topped gate that cuts off abruptly. The quiet tail then drops to about -62 dB.
differences.b: Final beep is a long (~0.3 s) decaying tone that runs to ~1.2 s. It sits at the loudest part of the file (-10 dB per tenth), so the ending feels sustained and lacks A's crisp confirmation.

differences.a: Onsets at 0.05, 0.21, 0.63 and 0.89 s. The beeps are compact and the sound is back to a quiet tail by ~1.0-1.2 s.
differences.b: Overall length matches at 1.5 s, but the beep section is stretched across 0.65-1.2 s. There is an extra onset at ~1.26 s, a faint tail event A lacks.

differences.a: Two sharp, bright click transients at ~0.21 and ~0.28 s, extending to high frequencies, with low thump bodies.
differences.b: Only a thin click at ~0.21 s, and a weaker one at ~0.27-0.3 s. Ringing low-frequency pulses at 0.1-0.3 s fill the gap, which sounds more tonal than clicky.

differences.a: Heavy, crunchy, clipped broadband impact (0-0.17 s) with noisy mids up to ~6 kHz, plus a rustly, scraping foley bed (0.37-0.6 s) with small clicks.
differences.b: Opening thud is cleaner and more low-end focused, with less mid crunch. The rustle at 0.35-0.6 s is more of a smooth noise or tonal wash than scrapey handling.

differences.a: Mid-heavy and wide: mid 29%, presence 21%, low-mid 17%, bass 20%.
differences.b: Presence-heavy (39%) from the beep tones, with low-mid 10% and mid 16%. Centroid is 622 Hz in the first quarter vs A's 3.4 kHz, so the opening is much darker.

differences.a: Faint noisy room tail from ~1.0 to 1.4 s with a quiet high-mid hiss.
differences.b: Gap with a dark, empty background after the beeps, then a faint band of hiss around 1.25-1.4 s. Falls to about -93 dB, so it is much quieter and cleaner than A.

differences.a: -16 dBFS RMS, -14.5 LUFS, clipped peak at +1.8 dBFS. Loudest at the start thud and the final beep.
differences.b: -18.4 dBFS RMS, -14.7 LUFS, peak -1.5 dBFS with no clipping. Loudness matches well, but the energy is concentrated on the beeps rather than the opening impact.

differences.a: Beeps at a steady ~4.5 kHz. Thumps around 100-200 Hz.
differences.b: Beeps at 4.5 kHz, which matches well, plus a 9 kHz overtone that adds a harder, more synthetic edge. Thumps drop in pitch under each beep.

differences.a: Mono.
differences.b: Mono.

change_notes: Rebuild the beeps. Use three short 4.5 kHz blips (~40-50 ms each) at 0.69, 0.75 and 0.80 s, with a 5 ms attack, a 10 ms release, and level at about -12 dB relative to the thump bursts. Remove the 4th beep and the 9 kHz partial, or drop it by 20 dB.
Make the final confirmation beep a single 4.5 kHz tone with a flat-topped envelope, 0.89 to 0.97 s (~80-90 ms), a 3 ms attack and a 5 ms release. Remove the ringing decay to 1.2 s.
Add noise to the beeps: mix in 1-6 kHz bandpassed noise at about -15 dB under the blips, with 100-200 Hz thumps ~60 ms long, so they sit in the foley.

review.summary: B is the right kind of sound: a long, bass-heavy, noisy explosion with the same length and a similar overall level. It lacks A's sharp blast onset and its secondary debris bumps, has a plateau-like body instead of a decay, and a slightly brighter, boxier tone.

differences.a: Near-instant blast that peaks at 0.04 s, with a bright broadband crack on top of the boom and a sharp wideband onset.
differences.b: Starts 0.02-0.05 s late with a slower 0.06 s attack and peak at 0.08 s. The onset is a soft swell into a flat noise body, with no distinct crack.

differences.a: Peaks at 0.04 s, then falls steadily: -5 to -9 dB through 0.4 s, -13 to -20 dB at 0.5-0.7 s, -20 dB at 0.96 s, -40 dB at 1.5 s. Continuous roll-off with a natural rumble fade.
differences.b: Holds a flat plateau at -7 to -10 dB until about 0.5 s, then a sustained shelf at about -14 dB. Stays high until 1.3 s, then drops abruptly (-20 dB at 1.31 s, -28 dB at 0.8 s). It reads as a gated block that cuts off rather than a natural decay.

differences.a: Irregular amplitude bursts and secondary bumps (onsets at 0.68, 0.82, 1.22 s) give a debris/crackle feel. Waveform shows clustered peaks.
differences.b: Only 2 detected onsets (0.05 and 1.51 s). Body is fairly uniform noise with a few spectral flicks near 0.85 and 1.25 s. The late stray blips at 1.5-1.6 s are mostly a tail artefact and do not read as debris.

differences.a: Very low-heavy: centroid 250 Hz, rolloff85 215 Hz, bass 70%, sub 16%, low-mid 8.6%.
differences.b: Centroid 375 Hz, rolloff85 452 Hz, bass 57%, sub 18%, low-mid 17%. Extra 250-500 Hz energy makes it boxier and less deep. Start centroid 513 Hz vs 287 Hz.

differences.a: -9.1 LUFS, peak +1.7 dBFS, heavily clipped (1661 samples), RMS -8.3 dB.
differences.b: -11.3 LUFS, peak -1.2 dBFS, no clipping, RMS -10.1 dB. About 2 LU quieter; still within the brief's tolerance and cleaner by design.

differences.a: 1.746 s, active from 0 s, trailing silence 0.13 s.
differences.b: 1.75 s, but with leading silence of 0.02 s and trailing silence of 0.17 s; the active portion is slightly shorter.

differences.a: Short natural rumble fade with no reverb wash; the quiet tail lies below 200 Hz by 1.5 s.
differences.b: Abrupt cutoff at about 1.4 s followed by a thin, separate low blip at 1.5-1.6 s. Qwen's 'reverberant' note is probably unreliable, since the measurements show no reverb.

differences.a: Noise-like (flatness 0.006), with crackly texture in the mids and highs in the first 0.4 s.
differences.b: Also noise-like (flatness 0.018) with a similar crackle texture, but slightly more mid/presence energy (5.8% mid vs 3.5%).

missing_elements: Sharp 20-50 ms broadband crack at the very start
Instant onset, with no pre-roll or soft swell
Secondary debris bumps around 0.68, 0.82 and 1.22 s
Smooth progressive decay into a low rumble through 0.5-1.5 s
Heavier saturated low end with a deeper centroid
extra_elements: Excess 250-500 Hz low-mid energy
Flat sustained plateau and mid-shelf in the body
Abrupt cutoff at about 1.4 s and a stray low blip at 1.5-1.6 s
change_notes: Fix the onset: start the sound at 0 s with no leading gap, and cut the attack to 5-10 ms (peak at 0.03-0.04 s). Add a 2-6 kHz noise crack, 20-40 ms, +6 dB over the body.

Reshape the envelope to a continuous decay: about -2 dB at 0.1 s, -8 dB at 0.4 s, -14 dB at 0.6 s, -20 dB at 0.96 s, -40 dB at 1.5 s. Replace the plateau and the abrupt gate at 1.4 s with an exponential fade (time constant about 0.45 s).
Add three debris bumps of 40-80 ms noise bursts at 0.68, 0.82 and 1.22 s, at about +4 to +6 dB over the local envelope, with a low-passed 300-1500 Hz crackle.

Move the energy lower: low-pass the body noise at 600 Hz (12 dB/oct) and sweep the cutoff from 1.5 kHz at 0 s down to 250 Hz by 1.2 s. Cut 250-500 Hz by 4-6 dB. Target a centroid of about 250 Hz and rolloff85 of about 250 Hz.
Add a sine thump falling from 100 Hz to 40 Hz over 0.5 s, about +3 dB, to deepen the bass and sub (target bass 65-70%, low-mid under 10%).
Remove the isolated tail blip at 1.5-1.6 s (it is a stray artefact). Let the rumble fade to silence by 1.6 s.
Raise loudness by about 2 LU, to about -9.5 LUFS, with soft saturation or a limiter (peak -1 dBFS). Keep it free of hard clipping.

review.summary: B matches the overall length (0.76 s) and the burst / gap / tick / hum layout, but its second half is far too loud and heavy. A has faint ticks followed by a low hum, while B has a loud mid tick and two big bursts with a dead-silent hole around 0.42-0.47 s. B is also darker overall, with its initial burst weaker in the mids and highs.

differences.a: Faint arming ticks at ~0.35, 0.44 and 0.5-0.53 s, 20-30 dB below the opening slap, then a soft low hum with its own pulses at ~0.62 s.
differences.b: A loud burst at 0.35-0.41 s (about -12 dB) and two very loud full-band bursts at 0.5-0.58 s and 0.62-0.72 s (about -6 to -7 dB), each wide and 'bursty' rather than a tick.

differences.a: One dominant event in the first 0.25 s (peak at 0.04 s, loud sustained noise to 0.2 s). The rest is quiet and builds gently, so the energy is front-loaded.
differences.b: Three loud blocks of comparable level (opening, ~0.5 s and ~0.65 s); the end is as loud as the start. Per-tenth envelope reads -7.9, -9.7 ... -6.2, -16.7, -6.9 versus A's -2.8, -4.5 ... -16.5, -28, -22.

differences.a: Continuous low-level fill between events (about -35 dB), with a faint rumble bridging the ticks.
differences.b: A hard digital silence (below -100 dB across the spectrum) around 0.42-0.47 s, which reads as an audio dropout or gate rather than a quiet gap.

differences.a: Centroid ~1 kHz, with 23% mid, 29% low-mid and 5% presence energy; the opening burst is broadband and lit up to 5-10 kHz.
differences.b: Centroid ~600 Hz, rolloff85 only 495 Hz (A 1680 Hz), mid just 4.8%, low-mid 14.8%; sub is 12.9% vs 4.5%. Heavier and boomier, with less crunch.

differences.a: Fast crunchy slap peaking at 0.04 s, clipped, hot.
differences.b: A 0.17 s peak time. The opening is a flat-topped noise block with no distinct slap transient. Quick drop at ~0.29 s.

differences.a: Dense, crunchy noise slap with bass body; the end is a low pulsing hum at about 25-30 Hz modulation, under 200 Hz.
differences.b: The final bursts are broadband noise with little sustained tone; no distinct low pulsing hum. Spectral flatness is higher (0.092 vs 0.023).
0.76 s; onsets at 0.05, 0.35, 0.45, 0.53 and 0.62 s. Onset times match, but one extra onset appears and the later ones are far more prominent.

differences.a: -10.1 LUFS, peak +2.6 dBFS (clipped, 728 samples).
differences.b: -12.5 LUFS, peak -1.2 dBFS, no clipping. Within tolerance overall, but the energy is distributed very differently.

differences.a: DC offset 0.025.
differences.b: DC offset -0.094, which is noticeable and wastes headroom.

missing_elements: Soft, small mechanical arming ticks (quiet, 1-4 kHz, 20-30 dB below the slap)
Low-level rumble bed bridging the gap between ticks
Pulsing sub-200 Hz hum as a distinct final element
Bright, crunchy broadband top end (5-10 kHz) on the opening slap
extra_elements: Loud noise burst at 0.35-0.41 s
Two loud full-band noise bursts at 0.5 s and 0.62 s that dominate the second half
Digital-silence gap at 0.42-0.47 s
Heavy sub energy (12.9%)
change_notes: Cut the late events: turn the 0.35 s burst into a 5-10 ms click (1.5-4 kHz band noise plus a 1.5 kHz tick) at about -22 dB relative to the opening slap. Make the 0.45 s tick even fainter, about -30 dB.

Rebuild the 0.5 s and 0.62 s elements. At 0.5 s use a short 15 ms click at about -20 dB. From 0.55 to 0.75 s use a 90-130 Hz sine/triangle hum with 25-30 Hz amplitude modulation (~60% depth), ramping from -30 dB to about -14 dB. Drop the broadband noise from these bursts, or low-pass it at 400 Hz at -25 dB.
Fill the 0.42-0.47 s hole with a -40 to -35 dB low-passed noise/rumble bed (under 300 Hz) running from 0.25 to 0.55 s. Remove any gate or hard mute there.

Sharpen the opening slap: a 3-5 ms click transient at 0 s, with the noise burst peaking at 0.04 s instead of 0.17 s. Use noise from 200 Hz to 8 kHz at about 0 dB, plus a 60-150 Hz thump pitched 150 to 60 Hz over 80 ms. Decay to -20 dB by 0.17 s and below -40 dB by 0.28 s.
Rebalance the spectrum: lower the sub shelf below 60 Hz by about 6 dB, and add +4-6 dB around 1-4 kHz on the opening burst so the centroid is about 1 kHz and rolloff85 reaches 1.5-2 kHz.
Remove the DC offset with a 20 Hz high-pass, and keep the peak at about -1 dBFS (soft clip is fine). Aim for about -11 to -10.5 LUFS, with most of the energy in the first 0.25 s.

review.summary: B matches the overall length, loudness and two-act structure (mag work, thunk near 1.1 s, gap, clacks into a big bolt hit near 1.85 s), but it is busier and more evenly bright, with a thin tail and a continuous handling bed where A is sparse, dry and quiet. It is the right kind of sound with moderate differences in tail, density and low-end character.

differences.a: Sparse: a few distinct clicks at 0.09-0.3 s, one isolated click at 0.38 s, a very quiet bed to 1.0 s, then a clear thunk at 1.06 s.
differences.b: Dense chatter of 9 or more small clicks and ticks between 0.05 and 0.92 s (onsets every ~0.1 s), so the quiet stretch before the thunk is lost.

differences.a: After the bolt slam at 1.87 s, a ringing tail with a sustained 2.3-3 kHz tone line and pulsing low thumps runs to ~2.65 s, then small late clicks.
differences.b: Tail after the bolt is short and clicky (-40 dB in 0.18 s vs 0.39 s), with only isolated late ticks and a brief tone near 1-2 kHz at 2.3 s. No sustained ringing.

differences.a: Almost no energy below 200 Hz in the first half; the second half has faint pulsing sub/bass under 100 Hz. Centroid ~5.9 kHz, mid 25.6%, air 27.5%.
differences.b: Has 150-400 Hz thuds on each impact, a strong 200-500 Hz body on the bolt hit, and a sub burst at 1.85 s. Presence is higher (45.7%) and mid lower (19%). Centroid 6.3 kHz.

differences.a: The bolt slam at 1.87 s is a bright, broadband impact with a quick decay (-20 dB in 0.06 s) after a cluster of 3-4 clacks.
differences.b: The bolt hit at 1.82 s is the loudest and a similar role, but heavier, with a lower thud and a longer body (-20 dB in 0.09 s). Pre-hit clacks are comparable.

differences.a: Impact-based noise with a ~1 kHz click body and a tonal ringing line at 2.3-3 kHz in the tail.
differences.b: Noisier and more uniformly bright (flatness 0.19, centroid steady ~6 kHz across all quarters). Has stray thin tonal lines at 8-12 kHz around the bolt hit, which sound synthetic.

differences.a: Clear dynamic contrast: very quiet bed, big 1.06 s thunk, near-silent gap 1.45-1.62 s, final peak. Gap is truly empty.
differences.b: Gap around 1.4-1.6 s is present but there is low-level activity and ticks (1.31 s click). The thunk near 1.1 s is weaker relative to the rest (-18.7 dB vs -13.1 dB tenth-envelope). Ends in silence at ~2.46 s (0.32 s trailing) vs ~2.65 s.

differences.a: Peak -2.8 dBFS, -21.0 LUFS, crest 23.6 dB.
differences.b: Peak -3.6 dBFS, -21.2 LUFS, crest 22.4 dB. Effectively matched.

differences.a: 2.78 s, with main events at 1.06 s and 1.87 s.
differences.b: 2.78 s, main events at 1.06 s and 1.82 s. Timing matches closely.

missing_elements: Sustained ringing 2.3-3 kHz metallic tone line in the tail after the bolt slam
Very quiet, sparse friction/rattle bed (0.4-1.0 s) as a contrast to the thunk
Low-level pulsing sub (<100 Hz) under the tail from ~1.7-2.6 s
Truly silent gap at 1.45-1.62 s
Longer decay (~0.4 s to -40 dB) on the impacts
extra_elements: Dense run of small clicks/ticks at 0.35-0.92 s
Heavy 150-400 Hz thud on every impact, plus a sub burst at the bolt hit
Thin high tonal lines at 8-12 kHz around the bolt hit
Isolated late ticks near 2.4 s and a 1.31 s click
change_notes: Thin the 0.35-0.92 s ticks: remove 5-6 of the clicks and leave a bed of filtered noise (bandpass 300-3 kHz) at about -45 dB under the thunk, so the first act is mostly quiet with only 3-4 events before 0.65 s.
Add a ringing tail after the bolt slam at 1.87 s: sine/resonant bandpass at 2.5 kHz (Q ~20), 0.7 s decay, starting about -30 dB under the hit, with slight 8-10 Hz amplitude pulsing.
Lengthen impact decays so -40 dB is reached in ~0.35 s (increase noise burst release from ~0.1 s to ~0.25 s) on the 1.06 s thunk and 1.87 s slam.
Cut the low-mid thud: high-pass the clicks at 250 Hz and lower the 200-500 Hz body of the bolt hit by ~6 dB, with the sub burst at 1.85 s reduced to under 60 Hz at -12 dB or removed.
Rebalance upward in the mids: boost 800-1.2 kHz click body by +3 dB and reduce the 6-12 kHz noise by ~3 dB to bring presence from 46% toward 39%.
Remove the 8-12 kHz tonal whines and make the 1.06 s thunk +4 dB louder so it dominates the first act.
Clear the 1.4-1.62 s gap: delete the 1.31 s tick tail overlap and gate everything to silence between 1.45 and 1.60 s.
Extend the last clicks to ~2.55 s and fade out by ~2.65 s (trailing silence ~0.15 s).

review.summary: B is the right kind of sound, a loud, low-heavy rifle blast with a similar 1.5 s length, loudness and band balance. But it has a slower attack, a pulsing low-end tail and a faster, darker decay, so it is less sharp and less natural than A.

differences.a: Near-instant 10 ms attack with a broadband crack reaching into the highs, so the shot reads as sharp and punchy.
differences.b: Peak arrives at 0.07 s, so the attack is softer and the crack is less defined, though the spectrogram does show some early broadband energy.

differences.a: Smooth exponential decay: -20 dB at 0.56 s and -40 dB at 1.0 s, with about 0.45 s of trailing silence.
differences.b: Decays faster: -20 dB at 0.4 s and -40 dB at 0.89 s, so the body is shorter. The envelope is lumpy rather than smooth.

differences.a: Dense, noisy, smeared low body and tail with no rhythmic structure.
differences.b: Visible periodic amplitude pulsing at roughly 25-30 Hz in the sub and bass (vertical striping and waveform bumps) that continues through the tail. It sounds like a flutter or motor-boat rumble rather than reverb.

differences.a: Smooth, darker reverberant tail of low rumble fading by about 1.2 s.
differences.b: Tail is rhythmic and sparse, with two flagged onsets at 0.69 s and 1.04 s that read as separate bumps or echoes. It cuts off abruptly around 1.38 s.

differences.a: Centroid about 837 Hz, rolloff 1.4 kHz. Mids and highs hold longer, and the centroid by quarter is 1012/720/849/425 Hz.
differences.b: Centroid about 801 Hz, rolloff 1.18 kHz, and it darkens much faster (720/268/198/66 Hz by quarter). The tail is almost pure sub, with less mid and upper-mid body between 0.2 and 0.8 s.

differences.a: Essentially pure broadband noise (flatness 0.0).
differences.b: Slightly more tonal or periodic (flatness 0.085) because of the sub pulsing.

differences.a: Peak -2.8 dBFS, -18.4 LUFS.
differences.b: Peak -1.8 dBFS, -18.7 LUFS. Close, with slightly less energy in the late body.

differences.a: DC offset -0.002.
differences.b: DC offset -0.018, about 8 times larger, suggesting a slow low-frequency component.

differences.a: 1.50 s file with about 0.45 s of trailing silence.
differences.b: 1.50 s file with about 0.38 s of trailing silence. Basically matched.

missing_elements: Sharp 10 ms muzzle crack at t=0 with high-frequency content out to 10 kHz or more
Smooth, dense reverberant tail with sustained low-mid and mid noise out to about 0.8 s
extra_elements: Periodic 25-30 Hz amplitude pulsing or flutter in the sub/bass
Discrete bump-like onsets at about 0.69 s and 1.04 s
Abrupt tail cutoff near 1.38 s
change_notes: Fix the attack: start the main blast at full level at 0 s with a 1-3 ms rise so the peak is at about 0.01 s, not 0.07 s. Add a 2-8 kHz noise crack of 20-40 ms at +4 to +6 dB over the body.
Remove the sub pulsing: drop the LFO or tremolo on the low layers, or any comb or feedback loop that causes the 25-30 Hz modulation. Replace it with a smooth noise-driven rumble with no periodicity.

Rebuild the tail as a smooth reverb of low-passed noise (cutoff sweeping from 3 kHz to about 400 Hz) with an exponential decay of about 0.25 s time constant, so the level is -20 dB at about 0.55 s and -40 dB at about 1.0 s.

Add mid body between 0.05 and 0.6 s: 200-1000 Hz noise at -12 to -15 dB relative to the peak, decaying over about 0.5 s, to lift the centroid to about 850 Hz in the first half and keep about 400 Hz in the last quarter.
Shape the thump: sine at 150 Hz falling to 45 Hz over about 120 ms, decaying over about 0.3 s. Don't hold sub energy beyond 0.5 s.
Remove the secondary onsets at 0.69 s and 1.04 s, and end the tail with a 50-100 ms fade, not a hard cut at 1.38 s.
High-pass at about 20 Hz to cut the DC offset to below 0.005, and keep the peak at about -2.5 dBFS.

review.summary: B matches A's length, loudness and low-end boom closely, but it lacks the fast descending zap line and the mid resonance band, and it decays faster with a pulsing, tremolo-like tail. It reads more like a generic explosion or boom than a sci-fi blaster.

differences.a: Bright diagonal zap sweeping from several kHz down to about 400 Hz over roughly 0.4 s, which gives the laser character
differences.b: No visible sweep. Broadband noise burst at the start with no distinct descending line, so it reads as an explosion or gunshot

differences.a: Slow, steady decay: -20 dB at 1.5 s and -40 dB at 2.04 s
differences.b: Faster decay: -20 dB at 0.96 s and -40 dB at 1.76 s, so the body is shorter and the tail less sustained

differences.a: Distinct mid resonance band around 450-1000 Hz sustained through about 1.5 s, plus a low wash under about 300 Hz
differences.b: Energy is a smooth wash with no sustained mid band. The low end is concentrated below about 100 Hz and stays strong into the tail, and the sub is a bit heavier (18.7% vs 16.1%)

differences.a: Gritty, distorted, granular rumble with a smooth tail
differences.b: Amplitude-modulated, pulsing low end (vertical striping, waveform bumps near 1.1-1.9 s) with onsets at 1.13, 1.8 and 1.89 s that sound like flutter or re-hits

differences.a: Fast attack at 0.03 s, no discrete onsets, with a sub thump and noise
differences.b: Same 0.03 s peak, but a sharper, higher transient. The peak is -1.7 dBFS vs -4.4 dBFS, and the first tenth is quieter (-26 dB vs -18 dB), suggesting a slightly delayed or softer start

differences.a: Dark, noisy reverb-like tail with high end dying first, fading out by about 2.07 s
differences.b: Tail ends more abruptly at about 2.53 s, with a low rumble cutoff (about 100 Hz) lingering to the end and a hard stop

differences.a: -21.5 LUFS, peak -4.4 dBFS
differences.b: -21.8 LUFS, peak -1.7 dBFS. Integrated loudness is matched, but the peak is about 2.7 dB hotter

differences.a: 2.76 s file, 0.69 s trailing silence
differences.b: 2.76 s file, 0.66 s trailing silence

differences.a: Mono
differences.b: Mono

missing_elements: Fast descending laser zap from about 5 kHz to 400 Hz over 0.3-0.4 s
Sustained 450-1000 Hz resonant mid band during the body
Slow, smooth, noisy tail lasting to about 2 s
extra_elements: Low-frequency amplitude pulsing or flutter and re-hit onsets at about 1.1 s and 1.8-1.9 s
Strong sustained sub rumble below 100 Hz through the tail
Hotter, sharper initial crack
change_notes: Add a pitch-swept zap at t=0: saw or square plus a little noise, exponential sweep from 5-6 kHz to 400 Hz over 0.35 s, with a 0.4 s decay. Level it about 6-8 dB above the noise bed in the 1-5 kHz region so it reads as a clear laser line.
Add a mid-band resonance layer: a bandpass noise or comb at 450-1000 Hz (Q about 4-6), starting at 0.2 s and fading from about -35 dB to -55 dB by 1.5 s.

Lengthen the body decay: reduce the decay rate so the envelope hits -20 dB at about 1.5 s and -40 dB at about 2.0 s, instead of 0.96 s and 1.76 s. Use a slower exponential on the noise and rumble layers.
Remove or smooth the amplitude modulation and re-hits in the 1.1-1.9 s range: cut LFO or tremolo depth on the sub and rumble layers, and drop the secondary transients at 1.13, 1.8 and 1.89 s.
Reduce the sustained sub: apply a 60-80 Hz high-pass or fade the sub from 0.4 s, and let it fall below -40 dB by about 1.2 s. Keep the sub thump to 50-150 ms. Replace it with mid-heavy grainy noise.
Lower the peak from -1.7 dBFS to about -4 dBFS with a soft clipper or saturation, keeping the integrated level near -21.5 LUFS.
Make the tail fade smoothly to silence by about 2.1 s with a dark low-pass sweep (8 kHz down to 1 kHz) instead of a cut at about 2.5 s.

review.summary: B is the right kind of sound, a 1.2 s low-end-dominated burst, but it behaves like a steady sine-like hum with a hard onset at 0.05 s. A is a gritty, fluttering steam rumble with a broadband hiss body, and B lacks that character and its mid/high content.

differences.a: Gritty, irregular rumble with vertical striations and random flutter, like steam puffs, plus broadband noise body.
differences.b: Smooth, regular amplitude-modulated hum, like a sustained low tone with a periodic beat (about 25-30 pulses per second in the waveform). Sounds synthetic and tonal, not steamy.

differences.a: Sub 56%, bass 22%, centroid about 330 Hz, rolloff85 about 215 Hz. Energy spreads continuously up through mids and highs, with hiss out to 10 kHz.
differences.b: Sub 67%, rolloff85 only 65 Hz, with a hard shelf near 100-150 Hz. Mids and highs are much weaker, and the centroid falls to about 50-90 Hz in the later quarters (A stays 190-360 Hz).

differences.a: Mostly noise (flatness 0.004 with strong low-end modulation), with a hissy mid/high layer that holds up to about 0.8 s.
differences.b: Dominated by a tonal low-frequency body. The noise layer is thin and fades by about 0.8 s, with the high band dropping out early.

differences.a: Swell from a quiet start (-21 dB in the first tenth) to peak at 0.07 s, with a brief bright flick to 10 kHz and clipping transients.
differences.b: Silent until 0.05 s (-39 dB in the first tenth), then a abrupt full-band step onset and peak at 0.11 s. The hard edge is a bit clicky and the swell is missing.

differences.a: Strong body to about 0.4 s, -20 dB at 0.63 s, -40 dB at 1.06 s.
differences.b: Similar shape, but -20 dB comes later (0.79 s vs 0.63 s) and the tail is smoother. The overall length matches.

differences.a: Integrated -16.5 LUFS, with the peak clipping at +3.8 dB. Crest 16.8 dB.
differences.b: -18.7 LUFS (2.2 LU quieter, within the brief's tolerance), peak -1.4 dBFS, crest 12.5 dB. Cleaner but less punchy.

differences.a: No clear pitch, with a noisy low rumble.
differences.b: A distinct low pitch, with a faintly audible tonal fundamental under 100 Hz and no pitch movement.

differences.a: Quiet tail that fades out irregularly over about 0.15 s.
differences.b: Smooth fade to digital silence, with no airy residue.

missing_elements: Irregular steam-puff flutter (random amplitude modulation) in the rumble
Sustained broadband hiss layer from 500 Hz to 10 kHz through 0.6-0.8 s
Bright 5-10 kHz flick at the very start
Soft swell into the onset
Low-mid energy around 200-500 Hz in the late body
extra_elements: Regular, periodic amplitude pulsing that sounds like a tonal beat
Hard step onset at 0.05 s after silence
Strong steady sub shelf below 100 Hz
change_notes: Replace the regular AM on the low layer with irregular flutter: band-limited random modulation at 20-50 Hz, 40-60% depth, with the rate jittered 20% so no steady beat remains.
Add a hiss layer: white noise band-passed at 500 Hz-6 kHz, level about 12-15 dB below the body at 0.1 s, decaying to -25 dB by 0.8 s. Also add a thin 6-10 kHz noise puff for 40 ms at the start.
Lift the 150-500 Hz region: add a low-passed noise (cutoff 400 Hz) at about -6 dB relative to the sub, so the centroid stays at 200-350 Hz in the later quarters instead of 50-90 Hz.
Start the sound at 0.0 s with a 60-70 ms swell from about -20 dB instead of silence plus a hard step. Peak at 0.07 s rather than 0.11 s.
Cut the sub sine's contribution by about 3 dB and detune or add noise to it (add ±3 Hz random drift) so it reads as rumble, not a tone.
Speed up the decay: -20 dB at about 0.63 s, -40 dB at about 1.05 s, with a short irregular tail rather than a clean fade.
Raise the overall level by about 2 dB to reach -16.5 LUFS while keeping the peak at or below -1 dBFS.

review.summary: B is the right kind of sound, a loud bass-heavy rifle shot with a similar loudness and a low-mid tail, but its blast is a flat, blunt block that cuts off abruptly at about 0.33 s. The tail is a separate, thinner section with odd high-frequency streaks, so the shot loses the sharp crack-to-thump collapse and natural decay of A.

differences.a: Near-instant, sharp noisy crack peaking at 0.04 s with near-clipping level (0 dBFS), and a ragged secondary burst at about 0.2-0.27 s.
differences.b: Peak is at 0.15 s, with the first tenth lower (-8.7 dB) than the second (-7.1 dB), so the front is a blunt, sustained block with no distinct crack. The initial snap is softened.

differences.a: Smooth, continuous decay: -20 dB at 0.29 s and -40 dB at 0.78 s, with a gradual roll-off through the body.
differences.b: Holds loud to about 0.33 s, then drops abruptly (a vertical cliff in the spectrogram and waveform), then a separate quieter section. -20 dB at 0.17 s and -40 dB at 0.66 s, so the shape is gated rather than natural.

differences.a: Continuous reverberant low-mid rumble from 0.5 to 0.88 s, with highs fading smoothly and a small bump near 0.41 s.
differences.b: A thin, detached tail with a bump around 0.4-0.6 s. Vertical broadband streaks (discrete clicks or reflections) appear at 0.65-1.3 s, and the low rumble ends sharply at about 1.47 s. It sounds like a separate echo rather than a room decay.

differences.a: Bass 42%, sub 11%, low-mid 21%; centroid 1105 Hz, rolloff 1744 Hz.
differences.b: Sub 15%, bass 34%, low-mid 23%; centroid 1154 Hz, rolloff 1550 Hz. Slightly more sub and less punchy bass, and the post-blast body is darker (centroid about 500 Hz vs 740-870 Hz).

differences.a: Noisy, distorted and ragged, with a flatness of 0.089.
differences.b: Noise-like but a bit flatter (0.123) and more uniform. It lacks the ragged distortion and doubled burst.

review.summary: B matches A's length (2.99 s), loudness (-20.4 vs -20.1 LUFS) and peak time (0.74 s), but it is a diffuse noisy texture with one big burst. It lacks A's sharp metallic clacks, the low-mid thuds and the rising whine, so it doesn't read as a reload sequence.

review.summary: B matches A's opening buzzy burst in length, spectral balance and LUFS, but the eight 0.1 s ticks are almost inaudible and badly spaced, and there is an unwanted burst near 0.9 s. As a countdown tick it misses the key rhythmic element.

differences.a: Eight evenly spaced click ticks at 0.1-0.9 s, each with two small chirp peaks near 6 and 10 kHz, at about -60 dBFS and clearly audible as a countdown.
differences.b: The ticks are tiny chirps at roughly 0.12, 0.22, 0.42, 0.62 and 0.82 s, at about -90 to -100 dB. They are effectively inaudible, irregular and fewer than eight; the measurements report no onsets.

differences.a: A steady 10 Hz pulse train (0.1 s spacing) running to 0.92 s, followed by silence.
differences.b: The rhythm is lost. The only energy after the opener is faint chirps at roughly 0.2 s spacing, plus a stray burst at 0.88-0.95 s. The 0.1 s grid is not kept.

differences.a: No extra event at the end. The last tick at 0.9 s is the same as the others, and the file is silent after 0.92 s.
differences.b: A noisy broadband puff (about 1 kHz, 5-12 kHz plus lows) at 0.85-0.95 s, at -63.7 dB in the last tenth. It is louder than every tick and sounds like a stray bang or tail, breaking the countdown.

differences.a: Peak -0.6 dBFS, with ticks about 40-50 dB below the opener (tenths at about -59 to -63 dB).
differences.b: Peak -6.5 dBFS, with ticks about 70-85 dB below the opener (tenths at about -89 to -101 dB). LUFS matches at -21.8 only because the opener dominates.

differences.a: Flat sustain at high level to about 0.08 s, then a hard gate cut. It reaches -20 dB by 0.08 s and -40 dB by 0.13 s, with a small tick at 0.1 s.
differences.b: Fast linear taper (teardrop waveform) from the peak down over about 0.1 s, with a softer fade and low-frequency bloom around 0.1-0.2 s. There is no sustained plateau or hard cut.

differences.a: Instant, punchy onset with a sustained buzz and sub thump. Subsequent ticks are crisp clicks of 20-30 ms.
differences.b: Instant attack, comparable thump. The ticks are soft chirps with a downward sweep and no crisp click transient.

differences.a: Many stacked harmonic bands (about 1.1k, 2.2k, 3.4k, 4.6k and 7-11k Hz) with a strong 4.6 kHz line. Tick centroid is about 15 kHz in later quarters.
differences.b: Fewer partials (about 1k, 2.2k, 4.6k, 8k and 10k Hz) with a thinner harmonic stack. Overall centroid and band percentages are close (62% presence, 21% air), but ticks sit lower (about 5-10 kHz) with a centroid of about 6.6 kHz throughout.

differences.a: Buzzy, dense, metallic electronic beep with a rough texture.
differences.b: Cleaner, more sine-like partials with a smoother, more tonal opener. It reads as a plain tone rather than a buzz.

differences.a: Very short decay with a faint 4.6 kHz whisker to about 0.15 s and a gated silence after the ticks.
differences.b: A short low-frequency tail to about 0.2 s plus the noisy puff near 0.9 s.

review.summary: B is the right kind of sound (a short noisy impact with sub thump) with matching length, loudness and band balance, but its shape differs. It swells in gradually instead of hitting hard, the thump is a flat block rather than pitched hits, the metallic ring is missing, and the tail is a scatter of ticks.

differences.a: Abrupt onset at ~0.05 s: the waveform jumps to full level in one step and the noisy burst starts at full energy. It also has a faint pre-tick.
differences.b: Gradual swell from ~0.03 s to a peak at 0.13 s, with one sharp spike at ~0.13 s. It feels softer and more like a whoosh-in than a bullet hit.

differences.a: Two or three distinct pitched low thumps (~0.08-0.12, 0.17-0.22, 0.27-0.33 s) with a falling swoosh from ~500 to 250 Hz.
differences.b: One continuous sub block (20-100 Hz) from ~0.05 to 0.4 s, with no discrete thumps and no pitch sweep.

differences.a: Smooth fade with a thin, steady ~800 Hz metallic ring running from 0.24 to ~0.9 s at a very low level.
differences.b: No sustained ring. The tail is made of irregular broadband clicks or ticks between ~0.4 and 0.85 s, which sound like debris or hoofbeat-like patter (Qwen heard hooves).

differences.a: Sustained loud body for ~0.2 s, then -20 dB at ~0.24 s and -40 dB at ~0.5 s, with a long thin tail.
differences.b: Peak is shorter and falls faster: -40 dB by ~0.27 s, with the 0.4-0.5 s region dipping and re-rising from the ticks. Body energy is shorter and the sustain is weaker.

differences.a: Flatness 0.19, mixing noise with tonal parts (the 800 Hz ring and a sweep).
differences.b: Flatness 0.07, with the lowest band being sub-heavy and fairly pure and no distinct tonal ring. Reads as more smooth and less crunchy.

differences.a: Noise burst bright to ~8 kHz, with a low-mid body around 300-900 Hz. Centroid 1272 Hz.
differences.b: Similar overall balance (centroid 1315 Hz), but the energy is concentrated around 2-5 kHz in the middle and a bit more present at the top. Band percentages are within ~2% of A.

differences.a: -19.0 LUFS, peak +0.4 dBFS (clipped).
differences.b: -19.3 LUFS, peak -1.5 dBFS.

review.summary: B is the right kind of sound, a short noisy crunch with a low thump, and its loudness and overall envelope are close to A. It lacks A's staggered thud pulses and the steady ~780 Hz metallic ring, and it adds an odd blip at 0.45 s plus a soft, rumbly sub bed.

differences.a: A has a thin, steady metallic ring at about 750-800 Hz that runs from 0.25 s to roughly 0.7 s and is the signature of the tail.
differences.b: B has no tonal ring. Its tail is diffuse noise residue with scattered vertical streaks and no sustained line.

differences.a: A has 2-3 distinct heavy thuds below 150 Hz at about 0.08-0.12 s, 0.17-0.24 s and 0.26-0.33 s, with gaps between them, plus a descending 300-600 Hz tonal sweep.
differences.b: B has one continuous sub/bass block from 0.05 to 0.22 s that fades gradually to about 0.4 s. It has no separate pulses and no descending sweep, so the body feels smoother and less boomy-punchy.

differences.a: A starts with a quiet tick at 0.0-0.05 s and then a sudden hard jump into the noise burst at about 0.05 s. The edge is sharp and clips.
differences.b: B ramps up more gradually from about 0.03 s to a peak at 0.12-0.15 s. It has less abrupt onset and no distinct opening tick.

differences.a: A's tail is clean, with no stray events after the main hit.
differences.b: B has an isolated click or blip near 0.45-0.47 s (a third onset) and sparse vertical streaks at 0.25-0.6 s. These read as artifacts or an unintended echo.

differences.a: A is mixed noise and tone (flatness 0.19), with a tonal ring and tonal sweep.
differences.b: B is flatter-sounding in a noisy sense but measured less flat (0.076), with low-frequency tonal content and no distinct mid peak. The mid texture is generic noise.

differences.b: B drops 20 dB in 0.09 s and 40 dB by 0.4 s. It is slightly shorter and tighter, and its tail is quieter overall (about 5 dB below A at 0.2-0.5 s).

differences.b: B has a centroid of about 1.33 kHz and a rolloff of 2.8 kHz. It is slightly brighter in its noise burst, and its sub is a bit heavier and flatter (17.8% vs 16%).

review.summary: B is a close match for A: the same heavy, bass-rich blaster blast with a noisy crack, a rumbling body and a long dark tail, and nearly identical length, envelope and loudness. The main gaps are a slightly darker, flatter overall balance and missing mid-frequency tonal smears and zap streaks.

differences.b: Centroid about 1.77 kHz, rolloff85 4.2 kHz. Bass is heavier at 35%, mid 18.6% and presence 10.4%, so it is a bit darker and boomier.

differences.b: First-quarter centroid is higher at 2.1 kHz, so the opening is brighter. Highs are broad noise with one faint diagonal sweep near 0 s and no distinct zap layer.

differences.a: Mid-frequency tonal smears around 0.5-1 kHz at 0.3-1.0 s, plus thin high streaks. These give a metallic, energy-weapon character.
differences.b: Body is mostly undifferentiated noise and low rumble with no visible tonal mid smears. Flatness is higher (0.16 vs 0.13), so it is slightly noisier and less tonal.

differences.a: Smooth decay with highs gone by about 1.4 s. Dark residue below -75 dB with a faint wash up to 1 kHz to the end.
differences.b: Low rumble holds a little longer, to about 1.2 s at the sub and bass, then cuts to near silence, with an abrupt fall to -111 dB in the last tenth. Faint broadband noise floor and vertical ticks around 1.2-1.5 s in the highs.

differences.a: Peak at 0.15 s, -20 dB at 0.59 s, -40 dB at 1.13 s, 1.02 s trailing silence.
differences.b: Peak at 0.15 s, -20 dB at 0.61 s, -40 dB at 1.18 s, 0.96 s trailing silence. Essentially identical.

differences.b: Peak -1.6 dBFS, -14.2 LUFS, true peak -1.0 dBTP. About 0.3 LU quieter, within tolerance.

review.summary: B matches A's length (2.29 s), loudness (-23.3 vs -23.0 LUFS) and general bright metallic-clack feel, but its event layout is different and it lacks A's strong second clunk at 0.64 s, the heavy rattle/slide at 1.3-1.85 s and the rising charge-up whine at the end.

differences.a: Defined sequence: eject clack at 0.04 s, handling rattle, a strong insertion clunk at 0.64 s, a quiet gap, a dense rattle/slide at 1.3-1.85 s, then a rising electronic whine from 1.9 s to 2.29 s.
differences.b: A big hit at 0.05 s, a noisy burst at 0.55-0.75 s, then many small low-level ticks and faint low thumps through to the end. The rattle/slide section is not clearly defined and there is no ending tone.

differences.a: The final 0.35 s has thin rising glide lines (about 1 to 6 kHz) as a charge-ready cue, the only pitched event.
differences.b: No rising sweep at the end. Only static narrow lines at about 7.7 and 9.2 kHz near the first hit, and a faint tail of noise.

differences.a: Two distinct sharp, loud transients (0.04 s and 0.64 s, both near full scale) with metallic ring. The second is the strongest.
differences.b: Only the first hit is a sharp transient. The 0.55-0.75 s event is a diffuse noise burst with no hard clunk, so the insert impact is weak.

differences.a: Clear dynamic contour: peak, quiet gap at 0.8-1.3 s, a swell from 1.3 s, then a tonal fade. Tenth-by-tenth envelope is about -17 to -47 dB.
differences.b: After 0.8 s it is a flat low-level scatter of ticks with no swell. The -40 dB decay is 0.39 s vs A's 0.77 s, and the last 0.3 s is noise rather than a tone.

differences.a: Heavy low-mid and bass body (100-500 Hz) in the rattle section, with the spectrum extending above 10 kHz (rolloff 11 kHz, air 25%).
differences.b: Low-end sits in a few isolated decaying thumps at 100-300 Hz. The big first-hit sub burst (20-80 Hz) is not in A. Rolloff is 9.2 kHz and air is 20%, so it is slightly darker.

differences.a: Real mechanical foley: gritty metallic clacks, rattles and slide.
differences.b: Synthetic-sounding ticks and noise bursts with a thin hiss-like bed. Less physical, with pitched thumps that read as low drums.

differences.a: Onsets at 0.05, 0.18, 0.45, 0.64, 0.86, 1.1, 1.3, 1.69 and 1.82 s, with deliberate spacing.
differences.b: 14 onsets, many small ones (0.3, 0.53, 0.71, 0.83, 1.0, 1.09, 1.2, 1.28 s), which makes the middle busier and less structured. The overall duration matches.

review.summary: B is a 5 s multi-event reload with matching loudness and overall spectral balance, but its event structure is misplaced. It has dense, loud clutter from 0 to 2.5 s, only one big hit at about 2.9 s, a weak final cluster near 4.5 s, and a dead zone from 3.3 to 4.2 s. A has a different layout, with a quiet intro, a clack at 1.2-1.6 s, a thump at 2.9-3.1 s and two big slams at 4.2 and 4.6 s.

differences.a: Quiet rustles and small clicks from 0 to 1 s, then distinct big events: a clack at 1.2-1.6 s, a thump at 2.9-3.1 s, and two loud slams at 4.2 and 4.6 s. Quiet gaps separate them.
differences.b: Dense, continuous run of similar clicks and thumps from 0.2 to 2.5 s, with a mid-sized hit around 2.2-2.4 s. Only one major hit at 2.9-3.0 s, and a smaller cluster at 4.4-4.7 s.

differences.a: Loudest events fall at 1.3 s, 2.9 s and 4.2/4.6 s (peak at 4.47 s). The gap from 3.4 to 4.1 s is near silent, so the sequence builds toward the end.
differences.b: Peak at 2.93 s. The first half is busy and the last second is weaker. The 1.2-1.6 s clack is missing as a distinct event, and the 4.2 s slam is replaced by a smaller cluster that starts about 4.3 s.

differences.a: Final slams are the loudest and heaviest, with envelope at tenths around -12 dB and a -40 dB decay of about 0.48 s.
differences.b: Decays are shorter and tighter (-20 dB at 0.15 s, -40 dB at 0.31 s). The final event is lower than the 2.9 s event, so the loudness arc is inverted.

differences.a: Big events have a broadband noisy crack on top of a thick sub-bass thump. The hits are heavy, metallic and slam-like.
differences.b: Many similar sharp clicks with a 100-250 Hz thump. They sound like the same repeated hit, with less distinction between latch, insertion and slam.

differences.a: Strong sub-bass thump below 100 Hz under the main hits, with broad mid noise. Spectrogram shows low-end columns at about 0.3-0.9 s, 1.3-1.5 s, 2.9-3.1 s and 4.2-4.7 s.
differences.b: Thumps are punchy and short, centred about 40-200 Hz, and occur on nearly every click. This is too busy in the low end early on, though the overall band percentages are close to A's.

differences.a: Mostly noisy and metallic, with only faint tonal rings near 1 kHz at 3.0-3.3 s and 4.7 s.
differences.b: Several clear sine-like ringing pings at about 1-2 kHz with harmonics near 5 kHz. Qwen heard them as electronic beeps, which gives a sci-fi or notification character. The pings recur throughout instead of appearing as a faint ring in two places.

differences.a: Dry, with short tails and a clean silence at 3.4-4.1 s, apart from a faint ring that fades by about 3.4 s.
differences.b: Also fairly dry, but the noise decays unevenly and the file ends after 0.18 s of trailing silence. The wideband noise bed between events fills the gaps that should be silent.

differences.b: Peak -1.6 dBFS, -19.7 LUFS, loudness range 2.5 LU. The level matches, but dynamics are flatter and the peak is slightly hotter.

differences.a: Dense, churning noise wash with a thick sub region, rumbling and unified.
differences.b: Similar noisy wash with slightly more visible mid-high grain and a bit more bass-band separation. Overall character is comparable.

differences.a: Peak -1.7 dBFS, RMS -12.8, -13.0 LUFS.
differences.b: Peak -1.2 dBFS, RMS -13.3, -13.2 LUFS. Essentially the same.

differences.a: 2.0 s, 0.2 s trailing silence, active about 81%.
differences.b: 2.0 s, 0.21 s trailing silence, active about 79%. Matches.

change_notes: Remove the broadband click at about 1.0 s: find the stray impulse or retrigger at 0.98-1.02 s and delete it, or limit its level to below the surrounding noise (-20 dB or more). Check the filter or envelope reset that causes it.
Smooth the 1.0-1.5 s decay: replace the step at about 1.2 s with a continuous exponential fall from about -20 dB at 1.0 s to -40 dB at 1.5 s, with no gating.
Remove or shrink the re-swell bump at 1.25-1.5 s (about -20 dB), or replace it with a soft swell near 0.9-1.0 s at about -3 dB relative to the surrounding level, as in A.

Rebuild the rumble tail from 1.0 to 1.8 s as 60-300 Hz low-passed noise with a slow 1 s exponential decay (time constant about 0.35 s). Fade it to zero with a 150 ms fade between 1.7 and 1.85 s so there is no hard edge.
Sharpen the attack by adding a 2-8 kHz noise crack of about 20-40 ms at 0.05 s, +3 dB over the body, to lift the first-tenth level from -32 to about -27 dB.
Keep the low-pass sweep on the noise body closing from about 8 kHz to 500 Hz over about 1 s, so the third-quarter centroid falls to about 160 Hz rather than holding near 310 Hz.
Keep the peak near -1.5 dBFS and -13 LUFS, and keep it mono.

review.summary: B matches A on length, overall loudness, band balance and the decay-to-silence, but it is a different sound in shape: a swelling noisy burst with a transient peak and a gradual taper, rather than a steady loud motor rev that steps down about 9 dB at 0.48 s into a rattly chug.

differences.a: Loud plateau of about -16 dB from 0.05 to 0.48 s, then an abrupt 8-10 dB step down into a quieter sustain that fades out by about 1.2 s.
differences.b: Peaks around 0.15-0.2 s and then tapers smoothly with no step. It is already about 6 dB down by 0.4 s and keeps falling. The motor-rev-then-drop shape is missing, and the decay to -20 dB comes earlier (0.63 s vs 0.8 s).

differences.a: Single clean onset at 0.05 s into a dense, steady buzz with no sharp spike. Crest factor 16.7 dB.
differences.b: Two onsets (0.07 and 0.15 s) and a spiky, transient-heavy burst around 0.15-0.2 s. Peak is -2.4 dBFS and crest factor 18.3 dB. It reads as an impact or whoosh rather than a motor spinning up.

differences.a: Harmonic motor buzz with visible tonal bands near 450-700 Hz and about 2 kHz, plus a rattly pulsing texture.
differences.b: Mostly broadband noise, with no distinct harmonic lines or engine periodicity. It sounds like rumble or an explosion (Qwen heard an explosion). The spectrogram shows only vague low-frequency striations.

differences.a: Mechanical, buzzy and rattly, with a fast engine chug in the second half, so it clearly reads as a chainsaw.
differences.b: Smeared, rumbly noise burst with an irregular low-frequency flutter. The chainsaw identity is weak.

differences.a: Strong 50-200 Hz block that is bright and steady through the first half, then drops. Hard lowpass near 10 kHz. Centroid rises from about 1.06 to 2.1 kHz and then falls.
differences.b: Overall band percentages match (bass 38%, low-mid 31%), but the centroid is flat at about 1.27 kHz. The high-mid energy is concentrated in the first 0.3 s as a bright burst. There is no hard 10 kHz cutoff, and a slow roll-off is visible instead.

differences.a: 1.278 s, with onset at 0.05 s, loud section to 0.48 s and silence by about 1.23 s.
differences.b: 1.28 s, with onset at about 0.07 s and a late-starting, shorter active portion (active fraction 0.79 vs 0.88). Trailing silence is 0.1 s.

differences.a: Peak -4.4 dBFS, RMS -21.1, -19.5 LUFS.
differences.b: Peak -2.4 dBFS, RMS -20.7, -19.7 LUFS. Integrated loudness matches, but the peak is higher.

differences.a: Dry, short tail with no reverb.
differences.b: Dry tail that fades to silence, though the long thin taper may feel slightly smeared.

missing_elements: Sustained loud motor rev plateau from 0.05 to 0.48 s
Abrupt 8-10 dB step down at about 0.48 s
Harmonic buzz bands at 450-700 Hz and about 2 kHz
Rattly engine chug pulsing in the second half
Hard lowpass near 10 kHz
extra_elements: Spiky noise burst or transient peak at 0.15-0.2 s
Explosion- or rumble-like broadband swell
Second onset at 0.15 s
change_notes: Rebuild the envelope: hold a flat level from 0.05 to 0.48 s (attack about 30-50 ms), then drop 8-10 dB within about 20 ms. Sustain at that lower level, fade to -20 dB by about 0.8 s and to silence by 1.2 s.

Make the motor tonal. Use a sawtooth or pulse oscillator at about 80-110 Hz with harmonics up to 2 kHz and a slight upward pitch drift of 5-10% over 0.4 s. Add a 2-stroke-style amplitude modulation at 40-60 Hz (30-50% depth) on the rev layer, and keep it periodic rather than random.
Add formant or bandpass emphasis at about 450-700 Hz (+6 dB, Q about 3) and about 2 kHz (+4 dB) during the loud half so the harmonic bands appear. Keep the 50-200 Hz body.
Remove the explosive transient and second onset. Cut the burst at 0.15 s, lower the peak to about -4 dBFS, and use a gentle 30-50 ms attack with no click.

In the second half (0.48-1.1 s) use a quieter rattly chug: noise bandpassed at 1-3 kHz, gated or modulated at about 25-35 Hz, about 8-10 dB below the rev. Keep the 100-300 Hz body at -10 dB so the low end drops with the step.
Lowpass the whole sound at about 10 kHz (steep, 24 dB/oct) and keep the sound dry. Keep it mono, with the onset near 0.05 s and RMS about -21 dBFS.

review.summary: B matches A's length, swell-and-decay envelope, loudness and band balance closely, but it is far less tonal and its brightness holds constant instead of darkening, so it reads as a noisier, flatter rumble than A's harmonic, falling engine.

differences.a: Centroid falls from ~1350 Hz to ~435 Hz across the clip, so the engine darkens as it winds down; rolloff85 about 2.1 kHz.
differences.b: Centroid stays flat at ~1000-1070 Hz in every quarter; rolloff85 about 1.8 kHz. No darkening, so no sense of winding down.

differences.a: Very tonal (flatness 0.003), with a clear harmonic comb from 200 Hz to 4 kHz and distinct striations.
differences.b: Much noisier (flatness 0.052), with a smeared, diffuse spectrogram and weak harmonic lines. Reads as noise or static rather than an engine.

differences.a: Falling engine pitch and harmonics as it decays, like a rev winding down.
differences.b: No clear pitch movement. The harmonic structure is static or unclear.

differences.a: Gradual swell, from -28 dB in the first tenth to a peak at 0.41 s, with the level holding to ~0.5 s.
differences.b: Jumps to about -12 dB in the second tenth, then dips to -16 dB, then rises again to a peak at 0.47 s. The waveform shows a bump and a louder burst at ~0.45 s, so the swell is less smooth.

differences.a: -20 dB about 0.54 s after the peak, -40 dB at ~1.04 s, tapering to silence by ~1.5 s.
differences.b: -40 dB at ~0.95 s, with the tail dropping to silence a bit earlier. Very similar overall, with a slightly shorter tail.

differences.a: Gritty, buzzy two-stroke chainsaw with fast amplitude-modulation chugging at 100-200 Hz.
differences.b: Similar low pulsing, but the mid and high texture is hissy and static-like. Qwen heard static plus a chirp, which is not engine-like (partly unreliable).

differences.a: 1.89 s with 0.39 s of trailing silence.
differences.b: 1.89 s with 0.47 s of trailing silence, so the active part is slightly shorter. Peak at 0.47 s versus 0.41 s.

differences.a: Peak -2.5 dBFS, -14.0 LUFS.
differences.b: Peak -1.4 dBFS, -14.3 LUFS. Essentially matched.

missing_elements: Clear harmonic comb (200 Hz-4 kHz) with a stacked buzzy engine tone
Progressive darkening/pitch fall during the wind-down
Light metallic chain rattle in the mids
extra_elements: Static-like broadband hiss in the mids and highs
Possible tonal chirp or whistle artifact (per Qwen, low confidence)
Louder mid-clip burst at ~0.45 s
change_notes: Rebuild the core as a sawtooth or pulse engine tone at 110-140 Hz with 30-60 Hz amplitude modulation at 60-80% depth, and add harmonics up to ~4 kHz. Aim for spectral flatness below 0.01.

Add a falling pitch and filter sweep: lower the fundamental by ~15-25% (e.g. 130 to 100 Hz) from 0.5 s to 1.4 s. Sweep a lowpass from ~4 kHz to ~800 Hz over the same span so the centroid goes from ~1300 Hz to ~450 Hz.
Reduce broadband noise by ~10 dB and bandpass it at 1-4 kHz, making it a two-stroke buzz layer rather than static. Remove any sine chirp.
Smooth the swell: ramp from -28 dB at 0 s to the peak at 0.41 s with no dip, and remove the 0.45 s burst (or reduce it by ~4 dB).
Extend the tail slightly so -40 dB lands at ~1.05 s and the sound fades to silence by ~1.5 s. Keep the total at 1.89 s.
Add a faint metallic chain rattle at 1.5-3 kHz, -18 dB under the body, with 15-25 Hz modulation.
Keep the peak at or below -2 dBFS and integrated loudness at ~-14 LUFS.

review.summary: B follows A's overall timeline, loudness and big-hit placement (peak at 2.03 s, final cluster at 2.5-2.9 s), but sounds cleaner and more synthetic. It is brighter and more tonal in the early clicks, with a spurious long mid-section rattle and a very prominent low-end boom under the 2.0 s hit. A is a gritty, dense foley-style rattle with strong 0.5-1.0 kHz body.

differences.a: Centroid about 6.8 kHz, rolloff 11.2 kHz. Bursts are dense from 500 Hz to 10 kHz, with the body centred around 1-3 kHz and a gritty low-mid warmth.
differences.b: Centroid about 8.3 kHz, rolloff 15.3 kHz. Noise is bright and hissy right up to the top of the spectrum, and the 1-2 kHz body is thinner. It sounds more like air and static than metal.

differences.a: Broadband noisy metallic clacks with no clear pitched components.
differences.b: Contains pitched tonal blips with harmonics at about 2 kHz (0.1 s), 1.1 kHz (0.26 s) and about 1.4 kHz (0.6-0.7 s, 1.55 s, 2.7 s). The first two onsets read as electronic beeps, and Qwen heard beeps. Other hits are hissy noise bursts.

differences.a: Distinct foley events: faint clicks, a mag-release clack cluster at 0.54-0.71 s, single taps, a loud seating clack at 2.03 s, and a final bolt cluster at 2.59-2.84 s.
differences.b: 23 onsets versus 16. A band of dense small ticks runs 0.8-1.7 s and fills the gaps that are quiet in A, and extra hits sit at 2.16 and 2.25 s. The pattern is busier and less sparse.

differences.a: Very sharp, short metallic clacks with fast decay (-20 dB in 0.04 s, -40 dB in 0.14 s).
differences.b: Attacks are sharp, but decays are slower (-20 dB in 0.1 s, -40 dB in 0.24 s), so hits ring or smear more.

differences.a: The loudest clack at 2.03 s is a tight, sharp hit with a short ring. The envelope is peaky at 1.7-2.1 s and 2.6-2.9 s.
differences.b: The 2.03 s hit is a broad noise burst about 0.2 s long, with a heavy low boom at 80-250 Hz. The last cluster at 2.6-2.9 s is quieter and less defined than A's, and the envelope is about 5-7 dB lower in some tenths.

differences.a: Near-silent tail with a faint noise floor and a few quiet ticks. Trailing silence 0.67 s.
differences.b: Clean digital silence after 3.0 s (trailing silence 0.94 s, envelope -103 dB). It is slightly shorter in activity and has no room noise, but the difference is small.

differences.a: No pitch movement.
differences.b: No pitch movement, but the static tonal blips add pitched content.

differences.a: -21.9 LUFS, peak -3.6 dBFS, crest 24.9 dB.
differences.b: -21.9 LUFS, peak -3.5 dBFS, crest 25.6 dB. True peak is -1.9 dBTP.

differences.a: 4.03 s, one-shot, first onset at 0.09 s, big hit at 2.03 s.
Mono.
differences.b: Mono.

Sparse quiet gaps between 0.8 and 1.7 s
