change_notes: Remove or replace the pitched sine/FM blips at 0.1 s (about 2 kHz), 0.26 s (about 1.1 kHz) and 0.6-0.7 s, 1.55 s, 2.7 s (about 1.1-1.4 kHz). Use damped noise-plus-inharmonic-resonator clicks instead, with 3-4 modes between 1.5 and 6 kHz, Q of 8-15 and a 15-30 ms decay.
Lowpass the broadband noise at about 11 kHz (12 dB/oct) and boost 1-3 kHz by 4-6 dB to bring the centroid from about 8.3 kHz to about 6.5-7 kHz.
Shorten the decays of every click: -20 dB by 0.04-0.05 s and -40 dB by 0.14 s. Use exponential envelopes of 20-40 ms for ticks and about 60 ms for the main clacks.

Thin out the 0.8-1.7 s region: drop the ticks at 0.8, 0.88, 1.04, 1.33 and 1.84 s. Keep only 1.17 s (one tap), a quiet cluster at 1.42/1.50/1.58 s (-12 dB relative to the main hits) and one click at 1.75 s.

Rebuild the 2.03 s seating hit as a sharp 60-80 ms metallic clack with a 2-4 kHz noise crack and a short resonant ring. Reduce the 200-300 Hz boom to about -15 dB and cut the length of the low thump from about 200 ms to 60-80 ms, pitched 120 Hz to 60 Hz.
Strengthen the final cluster at 2.59, 2.67, 2.76 and 2.84 s by about +4-6 dB, using 70-100 ms rattly clacks with a dense 500 Hz-8 kHz body. Remove the extra onsets at 2.16, 2.25 and 2.52 s.

Add a very quiet pink-noise floor at about -70 dBFS in the tail from 3.0 to 4.0 s, with 2-3 faint ticks. Keep the final level at about -22 LUFS and the peak at or below -3 dBFS to give true-peak headroom.

review.summary: B is a very close match to A: same length, same attack and decay times, similar spectral balance and loudness, with only small differences in tail texture and high-frequency behavior. It would pass as the same bolt-action rifle shot in game.

differences.a: Tail is a smooth, darkening rumble that thins out gradually. It fades to -50 dB by about 0.9 of the file and to near-silence by about 1.7 s.
differences.b: Tail has similar decay times (-20 dB at 0.86 s, -40 dB at 1.59 s). The spectrogram shows faint vertical streaks in the highs from 0.9-1.8 s, and the tail ends in a slightly sharper cutoff near 1.85 s.

differences.a: Centroid 1510 Hz and rolloff85 3338 Hz, so slightly brighter and more open in the upper-mids. The centroid falls to about 330 Hz by the end.
differences.b: Centroid 1424 Hz and rolloff85 2972 Hz, slightly less top end. The tail stays a bit warmer and heavier in the low-mids (centroid 461 Hz in the third quarter against 324 Hz in A).

differences.a: Decay is smooth: -9.5, -8.3, then -16.7, -18.9, -20.8, -28 dB in the middle tenths.
differences.b: The first 0.2 s hold more level before the drop (-8.9, -9.2, then -14.8). Mid-body is somewhat louder around 0.4-0.6 s (-24.8 against -28.3 dB), so it is slightly sustained.

differences.a: Attack time 0.03 s, with a peak at -0.5 dBFS and a noisy broadband crack.
differences.b: Attack time 0.02 s, with a peak at -1.0 dBFS and a similar broadband crack. Slightly crisper, with a marginally lower peak.

differences.a: -13.0 LUFS, RMS -14.9 dBFS.
differences.b: -14.1 LUFS, RMS -15.3 dBFS, about 1 LU quieter and within tolerance.

differences.a: Dense, noisy, slightly distorted body with a bumpy, flickering texture. Band-limited codec peaks at 16-17 kHz.
differences.b: Similarly dense noisy body with a strong sub/bass column. A bit more spectral flatness (0.097) and a noticeably higher bitrate. DC offset is larger (-0.013 against 0.002).

differences.a: 1.98 s with 0.25 s of trailing silence.
differences.b: 1.98 s with 0.20 s of trailing silence, essentially identical.

extra_elements: Faint vertical high-frequency streaks or flutter in the late tail (0.9-1.8 s), which A does not have
Slightly stronger sub energy (7.4% against 6.3%)
change_notes: Smooth the late tail: lowpass the reverb tail's noise at about 6 kHz after 0.9 s, or reduce the HF flutter and grain modulation above 8 kHz after 0.9 s by about 6-10 dB.
End the tail with a longer fade-out, about 80-100 ms, starting at 1.75 s, so the cutoff near 1.85 s does not sound abrupt.
Add about 1-2 dB more upper-mid energy at 2-4 kHz in the first 0.3 s, so rolloff85 rises from about 2.97 kHz to about 3.3 kHz.
Drop the body level at 0.4-0.6 s by about 2-3 dB, so the mid-body is closer to A at -28 dB.
Raise the output level by about 1 dB, to about -13 LUFS, and keep the peak at or below -1 dBFS.
Remove the DC offset with a high-pass filter at about 15-20 Hz.

review.summary: B is a close match for A's chainsaw rev-up swell: same 0.86 s length, fade-in/peak/fade-out shape, mono, bass-heavy balance and loudness. The main gaps are a slightly earlier peak, a steeper tail, a blurrier pulse texture, and a bit more broadband noise.

differences.a: Peaks at 0.42 s. Falls gradually to about -42 dB by the end, with a long fade from 0.55 s onward (-12 to -23 dB per tenth).
differences.b: Peaks slightly earlier at 0.38 s. The final tenth drops to -50.7 dB, a little steeper and quieter than A, with a slightly shorter active fraction (0.91 vs 0.97).

differences.a: Clearly pulsing, cylinder-like firing, with distinct vertical striations. Also a faint click-like onset as the motor catches.
differences.b: Also pulsing, but the striations are denser and more uniform, so it sounds smoother and more like noise-modulated rumble. Flatness is higher (0.039 vs 0.005), so it is less tonal. Qwen heard it as vacuum-like whoosh and static.

differences.a: Centroid is 720 Hz at the start and then moves around (847, 539, 1085, 1076 by quarter). Settles into a steady harmonic hum near 200 Hz in the second half. Rolloff is 1172 Hz.
differences.b: Overall centroid and band percentages match closely. Centroid drifts steadily downward (761 to 625 Hz), so the tail does not brighten or settle onto a distinct hum. Rolloff is slightly lower at 1098 Hz.

differences.a: Rise-fall with a slight pitch drop near the end, settling toward a loop-pitch hum around 200 Hz.
differences.b: Little distinct pitch movement. Dense low-frequency energy with no clear settling tone.

differences.a: Very tonal and harmonic (flatness 0.005), with a faint high haze.
differences.b: More noise-like (flatness 0.039). A broadband mid/high noise bloom around the peak, visible at 2-5 kHz.

differences.a: Peak -2.5 dBFS, RMS -14.2, -13.0 LUFS, crest 11.7 dB.
differences.b: Peak -1.2 dBFS, RMS -14.5, -13.2 LUFS, crest 13.3 dB. Essentially matched, with slightly spikier peaks.

differences.a: 0.864 s, no leading silence, one onset at 0.05 s.
differences.b: 0.86 s with 0.03 s leading silence and 0.01 s trailing silence. Same onset at 0.05 s.

missing_elements: Distinct starter-pull click or catch transient at the very start
Clear settled ~200 Hz harmonic hum in the second half that leads into the loop
extra_elements: Broadband 2-5 kHz noise bloom around the peak
Smoother, denser amplitude modulation that reads closer to a vacuum motor
change_notes: Add a ~10-15 ms starter-catch click at 0.04-0.05 s: band-passed noise at 1-3 kHz, about -12 dB relative to the body.
Make the pulse more distinct: amplitude modulation at 25-35 Hz with 50-60% depth on the 60-120 Hz sawtooth engine layer. Reduce or soften any random noise modulation.
Reduce noise flatness: lower the 2-5 kHz noise bloom by 3-4 dB and keep rolloff near 1.2 kHz. Shift the balance toward a harmonic stack (6-10 harmonics of a ~90 Hz fundamental).

Add a gentle pitch arc: rise the fundamental about 10-15% from 0 to 0.42 s, then settle down to about 100 Hz. Add a steadier ~200 Hz harmonic component in the 0.55-0.8 s section for a better loop handoff.
Lengthen the tail slightly: move the peak to about 0.42 s and keep the final fade near -42 dB rather than -50 dB, so the last tenth lands about 6-8 dB louder.
Pull the peak down about 1 dB to roughly -2.5 dBFS and reduce crest to about 12 dB with light limiting.

review.summary: B has the right overall frame (1.03 s, same peak and LUFS, leading silence, burst–gap–burst–click layout), but its content is more tonal and sparse: one low thud, then ringing pitched tones and a sharp spike, instead of A's dense noisy metallic rattles.

differences.a: Dense, speckled, noise-like metallic clacking and scraping across 500 Hz-4 kHz (flatness 0.005), reading as real foley of a bolt cycle.
differences.b: Much more synthetic. Narrow sustained tonal lines near 1.2-1.5 kHz and 4-5 kHz (a ringing 'ping'), plus a few stray high tones at 8-12 kHz. Flatness 0.267 is far more tonal.

differences.a: Roughly six onsets: soft scrapes at 0.42 s, sharp clicks, a loud clack at 0.52-0.56 s, a quiet rattle at 0.64-0.72 s, a long loud rattle burst at 0.78-0.9 s, and a final click at 0.94 s.
differences.b: Only four onsets: one loud first hit at 0.5 s, a quiet mid section, a rising swell into a big spike at 0.83 s, and a small tick at 0.91-0.95 s. The intro scrapes and clicks are missing, and the 0.64 s rattle is nearly empty.

differences.a: Almost nothing below 200 Hz; energy is mid-heavy and bright (centroid 5.7 kHz).
differences.b: Strong 200-300 Hz bloom and 30-90 Hz thump at the first hit (about 0.51-0.56 s), which A lacks. The first hit reads like a thud, not a metal clack. The overall centroid is similar, but it is distributed differently over time.

differences.a: Attack is gradual and clicky (0.1 s), with several small transients before the main burst.
differences.b: A single very fast attack (0.03 s) at 0.5 s. The second burst has one large isolated spike at 0.83 s that is more prominent than A's.

differences.a: Starts at 0.42 s, with a second burst at 0.78-0.9 s and the last click at 0.94 s. Duration 1.03 s.
differences.b: Starts at 0.5 s with a faint low rumble from about 0.17 s. Second burst at about 0.74 s. Same total length and nearly the same final click time.

differences.a: Bursts swell and decay quickly (0.05 s to -20 dB). The second burst is a roughly 0.12 s sustained rattle at a level equal to the first.
differences.b: Decays are similarly short (0.03 s). The second burst is a long, flat, low-level rattle ending in a spike, so its energy is weighted differently. The first burst is much louder than the second (envelope -13 dB vs about -29 dB), whereas A's two bursts are balanced.

differences.a: No sub-bass rumble or pre-roll. Silent before 0.42 s.
differences.b: A faint low-frequency rumble begins at 0.17 s, about -100 dB. Inaudible in practice, but it is a stray artefact.

differences.a: Peak -2.9 dBFS, -20.6 LUFS, RMS -24.4.
differences.b: Peak -2.9 dBFS, -20.7 LUFS, RMS -25.7.

missing_elements: Soft scrape and tick intro at 0.42-0.5 s
Several sharp small clicks before the main clack
Equal-weight, dense metallic rattle in the 0.78-0.9 s burst
Rattle/scrape in the 0.64-0.72 s lull
Noisy, broadband metal-on-metal grit
extra_elements: Low thud with 200-300 Hz and 30-90 Hz energy on the first hit
Ringing tonal pings at about 1.2-1.5 kHz and 4-5 kHz
Narrow high tonal lines at 8-12 kHz

change_notes: Replace the first hit's 30-90 Hz thump and 200-300 Hz bloom with a metallic clack: high-pass at about 200 Hz and cut the sub/bass layer by 20 dB or more. Use 1-4 kHz bandpassed noise with a 5-10 ms envelope plus a few 4-10 kHz resonators.
Add an intro at 0.42-0.5 s: 3-4 quiet scrape/tick transients of 5-15 ms each, 2-6 kHz noise at about -25 to -30 dB relative to the main clack, to match A's bolt-lift start.

Rebuild the 0.78-0.9 s burst as a dense rattle: bandpassed noise (500 Hz-6 kHz) amplitude-modulated by 8-12 random micro-hits per 100 ms, about 0.12 s long, peaking at about -6 dB, similar in level to the first burst (within 3 dB). Reduce the 0.83 s spike by about 8 dB.

Cut the sustained tonal pings: shorten the 1.2-1.5 kHz and 4-5 kHz resonances from about 100+ ms to under 25 ms, lower their level by 10-15 dB, and remove the 8-12 kHz tonal lines. Target spectral flatness above 0.1 to make it noisier.
Fill the 0.64-0.72 s lull with a quiet metallic rattle at about -30 dB (a 40-60 ms noise scrape, 1-4 kHz) so the gap reads as A's lull, not empty.

Shift the first clack to about 0.52 s, with the preceding scrape from 0.42 s. Keep the final click at 0.93-0.95 s (3-4 kHz, 20-30 ms). Remove the sub-rumble before 0.45 s. Keep peak at -3 dBFS and -20.6 LUFS.

review.summary: B matches A's length, loudness and broad band balance, but it is a smoother, noisier drone with one big swell at 0.6 s and no rhythmic surges, so it loses the pulsing, buzzy chainsaw engine feel.

differences.a: Four distinct rev surges (about 0.05-0.3, 0.38-0.5, 0.56-0.8, 0.85-1.2 s) with 3-6 dB dips between them, then a gradual fade from about 1.2 s.
differences.b: Rises from 0.1 s into one big swell peaking at about 0.6 s, drops abruptly at about 0.63 s, then holds a flatter, lower plateau to the end. It has no regular surge pattern.

differences.a: Soft fade-in over about 0.05 s. The peak sits inside the surges and no single event stands out.
differences.b: Has a prominent loud burst at about 0.55-0.63 s, about 4-6 dB over the rest, ending in a hard cut. It sounds like an isolated event and the peak is 1.6 dB hotter (-2.7 vs -4.3 dBFS).

differences.a: Very tonal and harmonic (flatness about 0), with a clear 600-800 Hz band and striations up to 2-3 kHz. Rough but pitched buzz.

review.summary: B is a close match to A in role and overall shape: a ~1.34 s low chainsaw-grind swell peaking near 0.25 s, then decaying, with matching loudness. It is smoother and more static in tone, lacks A's bright early grit, and has a bumpy mid-tail with a sudden drop at about 0.95 s.

differences.a: Bright, evolving spectrum: centroid rises from ~830 Hz to ~1.3 kHz at the peak, then falls to ~500 Hz. Gritty 200-1000 Hz and upper-mid grain reach up to ~10 kHz in the first half.
differences.b: Centroid is flat at ~650 Hz through the whole sound. Energy is a bass-heavy band (40% bass vs 33%) with a weaker 1-4 kHz grain and a rolloff of 1.05 kHz vs 1.18 kHz.

differences.a: Smooth, monotonic decay with a gentle tail-off: -20 dB at 0.72 s, -40 dB at 1.04 s, then a quick cut near 1.25 s.
differences.b: Decay is similar on paper (-20 dB at 0.69 s, -40 dB at 0.98 s) but has audible bumps around 0.55-0.9 s, then an abrupt step-down at ~0.95 s, which is most visible in the spectrogram. It also ends in a longer near-silent tail.

differences.a: Single onset at 0.05 s, with a fast but organic swell to the peak at 0.23 s from a near-instant start (0.01 s leading silence).
differences.b: Two onsets (0.07 s and 0.15 s). It starts ~40 ms later (0.05 s leading silence) and has a slightly steeper rise to -7.4 dB in the 0.2 s bin, with a peak 1.5 dB hotter.

differences.a: Rough, streaky amplitude-modulated motor/chain buzz with random grit and rasp, like a saw biting material.
differences.b: Smoother, more regular low-end pulsing with vertical stripes in the sub, reading more like a synthetic rumble. It has less rasp and less random grit, and the mid-tail has a fluttering, pulsed quality.

differences.a: Tail thins out with brightness dropping steadily and a dry, quick finish.
differences.b: Tail stays at constant brightness (centroid ~650 Hz) and fades out more darkly, with a clearer secondary bump near 0.55-0.9 s.

differences.a: -15.6 LUFS, peak -2.7 dBFS, RMS -16.1 dB.
differences.b: -16.0 LUFS, peak -1.2 dBFS, RMS -15.6 dB. Very close, with slightly higher crest.

differences.a: Almost entirely noise and grind, with no distinct tone.
differences.b: Similar noisy character with somewhat more low-frequency tonal pulsing in the sub band (flatness 0.032).

Lower the peak by ~1.5 dB (to about -2.7 dBFS) and keep integrated loudness near -15.6 LUFS.

review.summary: B is the right kind of sound (heavy low-end AS50 shot with a long rumbling tail) and matches overall length, loudness and band balance, but its attack is softer, its tail is built from distinct reflection bursts, and it cuts off abruptly around 2.9 s, so the tail feels different.

differences.a: Fast attack peaking at 0.06 s; a sharp broadband crack at the start with bright content in the first ~0.3 s.
differences.b: Peak at 0.12 s, so the onset is slower and less snappy. Its high content is broad and stays bright for ~1 s, so it reads less like a single crack.

differences.a: Smooth, continuous dark rumble that fades gradually to ~4.5 s, with only faint flutter in the tail.
differences.b: Tail is a plateau of low-mid energy with distinct vertical bursts (~1.4 s, ~2.1 s) that read as separate echoes or clicks, then an abrupt drop at ~2.95 s, followed by a weak low-level decay with periodic bright ticks to ~4.4 s.

differences.a: Steady decay: -20 dB at 1.12 s, -40 dB at 2.93 s, with a smooth slope.
differences.b: Similar -20 dB (0.96 s) and -40 dB (2.84 s) times, but the shape is stepped, with a hold from ~1.0 to 2.9 s and then a cliff drop.

differences.a: Muzzle crack, sub boom, blast body, and a dark echo tail without distinct events.
differences.b: Same basic layers, plus discrete echo/crackle events at ~0.82, 1.23, 1.33, 1.52, 2.13 and 2.62 s that make the tail busier.

differences.a: Peak -3.9 dBFS, -19.1 LUFS, crest 16.4 dB.

review.summary: B has the same overall length (3.42 s), a similar onset grid and matching integrated loudness, but it is a thin, hissy, noise-dominated sequence rather than A's distinct mechanical reload with a loud squelch body at 0.55 s and a heavy clack/thunk cluster around 1.1-1.6 s. The events are weaker and less defined, and the tail is cut off much earlier.

differences.a: Distinct staged events: soft latch clicks, a loud noisy 200-2000 Hz slide/squelch at 0.53 s, a clack cluster at 0.89-1.17 s, a heavy low-mid thunk and rattle, then sparse ticks.
differences.b: A near-continuous bed of broadband noise with 20 small ticks. Only one real event at about 1.1 s. The 0.53 s event is a faint tone blip near 1.5 kHz with weak low-mid bloom, and there is no squelch body.

differences.a: Peak around 1.09 s, with the 0.55 s burst also strong. Active fraction 0.54, with energy sustained to about 2.9 s (-40 dB at 1.63 s). Envelope by tenth runs -25 to -56 dB through 1.8 s.
differences.b: Active fraction 0.33. The 1.09 s event decays fast (-40 dB at 0.54 s) and the rest sits 30-40 dB under the peak. The envelope drops to digital silence by about 2.7 s. The sequence has little dynamic shape beyond one bang.

differences.a: Sharp, bright clacks and clicks with strong transient presence (0.05, 0.15, 0.24, 0.89, 1.01, 1.09, 1.17 s). Crest 26 dB, so the clicks are well above the bed.
differences.b: Many small, similar ticks (0.05-2.49 s) with low level and little differentiation. There are 20 onsets against A's 13, and the extra ones read as noise flutter rather than mechanical steps. Peak is 4 dB lower at -8.1 dBFS.

differences.a: Mechanical, metallic, wet or organic squelch, clicky, with a biogun feel.
differences.b: Electronic hiss and static, flatness 0.536 against A's 0.003. It sounds like white-noise crackle or a device malfunction rather than a gun mechanism. A tonal blip near 1.5 kHz and a narrow line near 8 kHz at 1.1 s sound synthetic.

differences.a: Centroid about 5.9 kHz, brightening from 3 kHz to 9 kHz over the sound. The 0.55 s and 1.4-1.7 s events carry 100-500 Hz body.
differences.b: Centroid about 7.1 kHz and flat across the sound (6.9-7.6 kHz). It is hissier overall, with almost no low-mid body except one thump at 1.1 s (sub 20-250 Hz) that A does not have at that point. The broad band percentages match, but they are distributed differently over time.

differences.a: 3.415 s, with sound active to about 2.9 s and 0.63 s of trailing silence. Heavy rattle and thunk sustained 1.2-1.8 s.
differences.b: 3.42 s, with sound to about 2.7 s and 0.7 s of trailing silence. The 1.2-1.8 s region is weak and sparse. Onset timing at 0.05, 0.24, 0.53, 0.9, 1.08 and 1.81 s roughly matches.

Make the 0.89-1.17 s cluster four distinct clacks at 0.89, 1.01, 1.09 and 1.17 s: each a 5-15 ms noise burst high-passed at 1 kHz plus a damped 2-4 kHz metallic ping with 40-80 ms decay. Make the 1.09 s clack the loudest at -4 dBFS peak, which raises the peak by about 4 dB.

review.summary: B keeps the three-burst layout, the 1.94 s length and the loudness, but each burst is a different kind of sound: a single short click, then a big low thump, then a thin ticking noise wash. A is a continuous run of noisy metallic scrapes and clacks. B reads as a different, more percussive and tonal sequence.

differences.a: Burst 1 (0.4-0.8 s) is a long swelling scrape plus clack with broadband noise from 20 Hz to 15 kHz. It is the first of three similar mechanical gestures, and the 0.4 s and 0.48 s onsets are a double hit.
differences.b: Burst 1 is a single tiny click or ping at about 0.57-0.62 s, only about 60 ms long, with a narrow resonance near 1 kHz. It is much shorter and sparser than A and has no scrape.

differences.a: Active bursts run about 0.4-0.8 s, 1.08-1.46 s and 1.69-1.94 s, about 35% active, with 0.3 s and 0.2 s gaps.
differences.b: Active time is only about 22%. Burst 1 is about 0.1 s long and starts late, at about 0.57 s. Burst 2 is about 0.2 s of body plus a ticking tail. Burst 3 starts at about 1.73 s.

differences.a: Each burst has a swelling, rounded body over 0.1-0.2 s, then a quick decay. The waveform is spindle-shaped and has no sharp spikes.
differences.b: Bursts have an instant spike followed by an exponential decay. Burst 2 is a sharp hit with a long decaying tail and later ticks. Burst 3 is a spike followed by a flat noise bed.

differences.a: Energy is centred on mid and presence, with a body around 1 kHz and the second burst darker, centroid about 2.5 kHz. There is a bass wash up to about 200 Hz in the spectrogram, but sub and bass are only 0.4% of the energy.
differences.b: Burst 2 has a strong sub and bass thump at 30-100 Hz and 200-300 Hz, a boomy impact that A lacks. Centroid is higher, 6.3 kHz vs 5.4 kHz, and presence is higher at 43% vs 38%.

differences.a: Almost entirely gritty noise, flatness about 0.003, with no clear tonal lines.
differences.b: Flatness is 0.164 and there are distinct tonal lines: a ping near 1 kHz and horizontal streaks around 8-12 kHz in burst 2. It sounds synthetic and ringy.

differences.a: Scrapey, gritty, metallic foley with a granular, continuous texture.
differences.b: Clean, synthetic click and thump with a thin ticking noise bed. It sounds more like a heavy impact or shell drop than a bolt slide.

differences.a: Clicks are fast, but the bodies swell in. The peak is -2.7 dBFS and the final burst is loud and abrupt.
differences.b: Very sharp isolated spikes, such as the one at about 1.73 s. The first burst is much quieter, at about -17 dB on the envelope grid vs A's -20, with weak onsets. Decay to -40 dB is 0.18 s vs 0.07 s.

differences.a: -20.6 LUFS, peak -2.7 dBFS, RMS -23.8.
differences.b: -20.7 LUFS, peak -3.1 dBFS, RMS -24.7. Overall level matches, but it is distributed differently: burst 1 is quiet and burst 2 dominates.

differences.a: Dry, with short tails under 0.3 s and a cut-off ending.
differences.b: Burst 2 has a subsonic rumble tail and tick echoes. There is also a faint low-frequency rumble from 0.4 to 1.6 s that spans the gaps.

Rebuild burst 2 as a click at 1.08 s (5 ms, 2-6 kHz), then a 0.15 s round-insertion slide with a swelling noise body at 1.16 s (centroid about 2.5 kHz, darker), peaking around -3 dBFS, and a faint tick at 1.33 s. Decay to -40 dB within about 0.1 s.

Rework burst 3 into three clacks at 1.69, 1.77 and 1.90 s, each a 30-60 ms gritty metallic hit with a swelling body, with the last one running to the file end without a tail. Replace the flat noise bed with these hits.

review.summary: B is very close to A in role, length, loudness and decay timing: a heavy sub/bass rumble that swells to about 0.42 s and fades by ~1.3 s. It differs in a smoother, tonal-sounding body with a slow ramp-up, a weaker gritty top end, and a single swell instead of A's two-hit rumble.

differences.a: Fast onset at 0.05 s at about -26 dB, then straight into a dense, loud body; the second onset at 0.44 s adds a swell or hit.
differences.b: Starts near silence (-33 dB in the first tenth) and ramps up slowly over about 0.15 s. The only transient is a distinct spike cluster near 0.42-0.5 s.

differences.a: Sub 38% and bass 40%, with broadband grit rising to 10 kHz+ early. The low end is full across 20-400 Hz and the centroid stays at 500-800 Hz per quarter.
differences.b: Sub 42% and bass 38%, with a concentrated sub blob at 40-100 Hz in the first 0.4 s. The first-quarter centroid is only 225 Hz and the rolloff is 352 Hz against A's 539 Hz. The top end is thinner and the 2-10 kHz haze is weaker, especially early on.

differences.a: Gritty, fluttering, granular noise with vertical striations. Reads as a chaotic, metallic rumble.
differences.b: Smoother, more tonal and pulsed body, with distinct amplitude-modulated bands and a cleaner low-mid. Less hissy and granular.

differences.a: Two onsets (0.05 s and 0.44 s). The level stays high and fluctuating from 0.1 to 0.5 s, with several irregular bursts in the waveform.
differences.b: One onset detected. The waveform shows a swell, a spike cluster near 0.45 s, a dip, then a second hump at 0.7-0.9 s. The shape is more sculpted and less continuously dense.

differences.a: -20 dB at 0.58 s and -40 dB at 1.03 s after the peak, with a gradual, grainy tail. The last tenths fall to about -61 dB.

change_notes: Shorten the intro ramp. Reach about -12 dB by 0.05 s (currently -33 dB in the first 0.1 s) with a 10-20 ms rise. This makes the sound start with A's immediate punch.

Add a gritty noise layer: bandpass 800 Hz-8 kHz, with 150-300 Hz amplitude flutter. Run it 0.03-0.8 s at about -18 dB relative to the body, fading out by 1.0 s. This raises the presence and mid energy early on.

Lift the low-mid. Add a 150-500 Hz filtered noise rumble at +3 dB, and raise the lowpass cutoff from about 350 Hz to about 600 Hz. This should move the rolloff85 from 352 Hz toward about 540 Hz and the early centroid from 225 Hz to about 500-700 Hz.
Reduce the pure-sub weight. Lower the 40-100 Hz layer by about 3 dB in the first 0.4 s and add irregular random modulation (depth about 30%, 20-40 Hz) to break up the smooth pulsing.
Soften the 0.42 s spike cluster by about 4 dB and fold it into the body as a swell. Smooth or remove the dip at 0.55-0.65 s so the level stays within about 6 dB of the peak until 0.5 s.
Extend the tail. Keep -40 dB at about 1.03 s, then add a faint low-mid residue at about -55 dB to 1.45 s with a gentle fade, so the end does not drop to -88 dB.

review.summary: B is a very close match to A in length, loudness, envelope shape and overall boomy-rifle-with-long-tail character. The remaining differences are a slightly softer attack, a brighter and airier spectrum, and a tail that cuts off more abruptly.

differences.a: Peak at 0.03 s with a sharp crack. The first tenth sits at -12.9 dB, so the crack hits at full level straight away.
differences.b: Peak at 0.05 s. The first tenth is -16.2 dB and the second tenth is -12.3 dB, so the attack is slightly softer or delayed and the crack is less immediate.

differences.a: Highs roll off steeply above about 10 kHz, and the energy is darker and more concentrated in the low end. Centroid is 1840 Hz and rolloff85 is 4005 Hz.
differences.b: The spectrogram shows more energy up to 15-20 kHz and a brighter, airier top, though centroid (1786 Hz) and band percentages are nearly identical. Sub is slightly higher (8.4% vs 7.4%) and bass slightly lower (17.5% vs 19.7%).

differences.a: Smooth, dark tail that fades to silence by about 1.65 s. The mid-tail centroid drops to about 585 Hz in the third quarter.
differences.b: The tail is a little brighter, with centroid 952 Hz in the second quarter and 720 Hz in the third. Faint high-frequency flutter streaks appear around 1.2-1.6 s, and the tail ends in a sharper cutoff around 1.6-1.85 s.

differences.a: -20 dB at 0.86 s and -40 dB at 1.55 s. The envelope falls smoothly, with a step down around the 0.6 s mark.
differences.b: -20 dB at 0.79 s and -40 dB at 1.53 s. It is slightly faster early on, then has a flatter plateau from 0.6 to 0.8 s (about -41 to -42 dB vs A's -37 to -44 dB).

differences.a: Peak -2.8 dBFS, -16.3 LUFS, crest 15.7 dB.
differences.b: Peak -1.2 dBFS, -16.6 LUFS, crest 17.0 dB. Loudness is matched, but the peak is a bit hotter.

differences.a: Very noise-like (flatness reported as 0.0) with a rumbling low-end thump.
differences.b: Also noise-based, with a similar dense texture. Its low end looks slightly more tonal and sustained in the sub range.

review.summary: B is a very close match to A: same 1.98 s length, loudness within about 0.6 LU, and nearly identical decay times, centroid and band balance. The remaining differences are a slightly softer attack, a missing secondary bump, and a brighter, more spiky top end in the tail.

differences.a: Peak at 0.04 s with a sharp crack. The first tenth sits at -10 dB and the peak tenth at -7.9 dB.

review.summary: B matches A's length, envelope shape and loudness well and has the right heavy sustained-rumble role, but it is much darker and smoother. It lacks A's gritty broadband noise, sharp attack and the pulsed swells and sputtering tail.

differences.a: Sustained, amplitude-modulated pulses, with dips of 10-15 dB, that hold near the peak all the way to the abrupt cut at 0.30 s. Active fraction is 0.97.
differences.b: Pulse levels fall off and wander: the second half drops to about -18 to -20 dB tenths with a ragged, low-level section near 0.18-0.23 s. Active fraction is 0.87, so it reads as decaying rather than a steady spin.

differences.a: Pulse groups at roughly 0.05, 0.14 and 0.23 s, about 0.09 s apart (~11 Hz). Each is wide and similar in level.

differences.b: Peak -2.6 dBFS, RMS -12.2 dBFS, crest 9.6 dB. About 2.6 dB quieter in RMS and more peaky.

differences.a: Sharp broadband noise crack peaking at 0.04 s, bright energy to the top of the spectrum, very punchy (-5 dB in first tenth).
differences.b: Softer, rounder attack with less top-end burst; first-tenth level is about 4 dB lower (-9.3 dB) and the crack is less defined.

change_notes: Replace the flat sub slab with a pitch-dropping thump: sine sweep 120 Hz to 50 Hz over about 200 ms, exponential decay with a 0.15-0.2 s time constant, reaching -30 dB by 0.35 s. Remove the hold up to 0.63 s and the abrupt cutoff.
Cut sub (20-60 Hz) level by about 4-5 dB so sub falls from 23.7% to about 14% of energy, and raise the 100-250 Hz bass body to keep weight.

Add a 20-40 ms white-noise crack, highpassed at 2 kHz and shaped with a 1 ms attack, at 0 s, about +6 dB over the current top end, with a 5-12 kHz sizzle fading over 100 ms. Target centroid about 1.4 kHz and rolloff about 2.6 kHz.
Boost the 500 Hz-3 kHz noise body by about 3-4 dB for the first 0.3 s, decaying about 20 dB by 0.32 s, to restore the gritty mid texture.
Remove the amplitude ripple/pulsing in the low layer (modulation or comb-like stepping), and use a smooth exponential envelope instead.

Remove the vertical click artifacts at 0.7-1.2 s (a reverb or echo reflection stage) and replace them with a smooth, lowpassed (about 1.5 kHz) noise tail that fades by about 1.0-1.1 s, with no hard cutoff.
Raise the final gain by about 2.5 dB to reach a peak of about -1 dBFS and -16 LUFS; use a soft limiter to keep the crest factor at about 16 dB.

review.summary: B is the right kind of heavy boomy shotgun with similar sub/bass weight, but it stays flat and loud for about 0.7 s, then has a long lumpy decay with a stray burst near 1.4 s and a cliff-like drop. A is a sharp blast that decays smoothly into a reverb tail.

differences.a: Level falls steadily: -20 dB at 0.5 s, -40 dB at about 1.0 s, so the blast is short and the tail is smooth.
differences.b: Held near -8 to -12 dB for about 0.3 s, then still around -18 to -28 dB through 0.6 s, with -20 dB only at 1.08 s. The body is much longer and more sustained, then it drops quickly to -40 dB at 1.27 s.

differences.a: A single blast plus a smooth reverb tail, with only tiny ticks near 1.29 s and 1.37 s.
differences.b: Waveform and spectrogram show distinct bursts or bumps at about 0.75-1.0 s and a broadband vertical stripe at about 1.4 s, which sound like extra shots, debris or glitches. Onsets are detected at 1.01, 1.36 and 1.58 s.

differences.a: Instant, bright broadband crack with highs extending past 10 kHz in the first 0.2 s, followed by a quick fall in brightness.
differences.b: Peak at 0.03 s, but the highs persist as grainy noise for about 0.7 s, so the crack does not stand out from the body. Its attack is less punchy relative to the sustained level.

differences.a: Smooth, dense, low-passed reverb tail that fades through about 1.5-1.6 s, with a spectrum getting darker and darker.
differences.b: Little real tail. Energy cuts off at about 1.2 s, and only a thin low-frequency residue remains afterward, plus the stray bump near 1.4 s. It sounds gated rather than reverberant.

change_notes: Shorten the main body: apply an exponential decay so the level is -20 dB at 0.5 s and -40 dB at 1.0 s, instead of -20 dB at 1.08 s. Cut the held mid/high noise to about 0.25 s.

review.summary: B matches A's length (6.24 s), loudness (-24.0 vs -23.7 LUFS) and loudest-hit time (3.8 s), but it is a dense, noisy, high-centred stream of rattles with many ringing tonal pings. A is a sparse sequence of discrete, dry, mid-heavy mechanical clunks separated by quiet gaps.

differences.a: Sparse sequence of discrete events (clicks at 0.13/0.63 s, latch at 1.16 s, clack at 1.6 s, thud at 3.3 s, slam at 3.8 s, ratchet rattles 4.1-5.3 s) with clear quiet gaps between them.
differences.b: Near-continuous stream of about 47 onsets, roughly every 0.08-0.1 s from 0.1 s onward, so the discrete reload steps are not distinguishable. The result reads as a rattling or ratcheting texture throughout.

differences.a: Active fraction 0.41, with silent or very quiet gaps (for example 1.8-2.3 s and 2.6-3.2 s). Events are spaced to tell a story: handle, latch, insert, slam, rattle.
differences.b: Active fraction 0.72, with constant activity and no real gaps. The overall length is right, but the event pacing and rhythm are wrong.

differences.a: Broadband, dry, noisy metallic clacks with no stable tonal peaks (flatness 0.057).
differences.b: Spectral flatness is 0.252, with prominent tonal peaks at 323 Hz, 7.8 kHz and 9.2 kHz. The spectrogram shows ringing pings around 1 kHz and curved descending 200-400 Hz blips. Qwen heard beeping and electronic static, which reads as digital rather than foley.

differences.a: Each hit decays very fast: -20 dB in 0.12 s and -40 dB in 0.41 s.
differences.b: Decay is much slower and smeared: -20 dB in 0.37 s and -40 dB in 1.71 s. Hits sustain into noise bursts, such as the swell around 2.2-2.7 s, instead of staying short and dry.

differences.a: Sharp near-instant transients on each clack; the 3.7-3.8 s slam is a sharp hit with a short ring.
differences.b: The 3.8 s hit is present and is the peak, but it is followed by a long rattling sustain. Most other events are soft and low in level, with no clear punchy clacks at 1.6 s and 3.3 s.

differences.a: Centroid 2.7 kHz, rolloff 5.6 kHz. Energy is mid-heavy at 300-1500 Hz, and the spectrogram shows little above 8 kHz.
differences.b: Centroid 3.1 kHz, rolloff 6.4 kHz, more presence and air, with hiss extending to 10 kHz and above. The sound is brighter and hissier. Band percentages are otherwise close (mid 48% vs 51%).

differences.a: Low-frequency body below 200 Hz at the start (0-1 s) and a heavier low-mid thump at 5.0-5.3 s that closes the sequence.
differences.b: Low body is concentrated in a single sub burst around 3.8-4.0 s. There are only small 200-400 Hz blips elsewhere, and the closing thump at about 5.2 s is missing.

differences.a: -23.7 LUFS, peak -3.4 dBFS, crest 24 dB, LRA 3.7 LU.

review.summary: B is a close match to A: a 1.1 s low rumbling flame roar with nearly identical band balance, loudness and a mid-clip peak. It differs mainly in a silent-ish start (A is audible from 0 s), a more abrupt fall at the end, and a more clustered, crackly burst around 0.4 s.

differences.a: Smooth turbulent rumble with only one brief sharp spike near 0.45 s and mild crackle.
differences.b: Several clustered crackle/pop bursts around 0.35-0.5 s and again near 0.6-0.7 s (4 onsets vs 2), so it is a bit more crackly.

review.summary: B matches A's length (4.32 s), integrated loudness (-28.8 vs -28.6 LUFS) and the overall layout of click clusters with a big clunk at about 3.2 s. However, it is much noisier and hissier, its individual hits are weak, and it lacks A's bright metallic clack character. The final clunk is a low thud with a long decay rather than A's sharp, dry hit.

differences.a: About 26 sharp, instant-attack metallic clicks and clacks that clearly stand out from near-silent gaps, with vertical strokes extending above 10 kHz and clear peaks at 0.7 s, 1.2 s, 2.0 s and 2.6 s.
differences.b: Individual clicks are very quiet and smeared into a continuous hissy noise bed. Only the 3.2 s hit stands out, so the multi-step click rhythm is barely audible.

differences.a: Each hit decays to -40 dB in about 60 ms, so the sound is dry and staccato, with clean gaps between clusters and active fraction 0.48.
differences.b: The -40 dB decay is 0.78 s, driven by the big hit's smeared body, and the noise floor is continuous between hits. Active fraction is 0.27 and loudness range is 12.1 LU versus 2.4 LU, so dynamics are very uneven.

differences.a: Distinct heavy clack at about 0.7 s (latch/breech open), three clusters of 3-4 clicks, a loud breech-lock clunk at 3.2 s, and a gritty rattle tail from 3.35 to 4.15 s.
differences.b: Click clusters are present at roughly the right times but are low-level and indistinct. There is no prominent 0.7 s clack, and the 3.2 s event is a boomy thump with tonal ringing instead of a metallic clunk. The tail is only sparse low-level bits.

differences.a: Resonant metallic body at about 700-1000 Hz in each click, with a foley-like texture.
differences.b: Dominated by broadband white-ish noise (flatness 0.169) that is bright across 1-12 kHz, with a few tonal whines near 1 kHz and 8-12 kHz (visible in the spectrogram). It sounds electronic/static, and Qwen heard beeps and static.

differences.a: Heavy low-mid body (200-1000 Hz) with bass and low-frequency smear under the hits. The centroid is about 3.5 kHz in the first quarter and 1.6-1.8 kHz afterwards.
differences.b: Centroid is about 4.3-4.5 kHz for the first three quarters (too bright and hissy), with almost nothing below 200 Hz except in the big hit. The low-mid share looks similar only because of the one large thump.

differences.a: Peak -4.1 dBFS, RMS -30.1 dBFS, with consistent hit levels across the sequence.
differences.b: Peak -8.2 dBFS, RMS -34.3 dBFS. Integrated loudness matches, but it is concentrated in the single 3.2 s hit while the other hits are 15-25 dB below it.

differences.a: Dry, short gritty rattle tail from 3.35 to 4.15 s with 0.17 s trailing silence.
differences.b: Hit at 3.2 s has a longer smeared decay and some resonant boom, with a sparse noisy tail and 0.31 s trailing silence.

differences.a: 4.315 s with 26 onsets, and cluster timings at 0.9-1.4 s, 1.6-2.1 s, 2.3-2.9 s and a main hit at 3.22 s.
differences.b: 4.32 s with 30 onsets, and cluster timings and the main hit at 3.23 s match closely. There are a few extra onsets, such as at 0.21 s and 2.56 s.

change_notes: Remove or gate the continuous noise bed: cut the broadband noise by about 20 dB between hits and use hard gates or noise bursts of 20-60 ms only, so the gaps fall to near silence (below -70 dB).

Rebuild each click as a 30-60 ms metallic hit: a 1-2 ms noise transient (2-8 kHz), plus 2-3 inharmonic damped resonators at roughly 700, 950 and 1800 Hz with a 25-40 ms decay, to give a clean -40 dB decay in about 60 ms.
Raise the click levels so the clusters at 0.9-1.4 s, 1.6-2.1 s and 2.3-2.9 s sit within 6-10 dB of the main hit, rather than 20 dB below it. Aim for a peak near -4 dBFS and RMS near -30 dBFS.
Add a heavy latch clack at 0.68-0.72 s: a 60 ms metal hit with a 400-900 Hz body and bright 3-8 kHz noise, level 3-6 dB above the average click.

Redesign the 3.2 s clunk as a dry metallic slam: a 5 ms noise crack at 2-6 kHz, a 120 ms 300-900 Hz damped metal body, and a short 80-150 Hz thump decaying within 100 ms. Shorten the current boom, whose decay to -40 dB takes about 0.78 s, to under 0.15 s, and remove the tonal ringing.
Add a low-mid foley body (200-500 Hz, band-limited noise, 30-50 ms) under each hit, and a faint 60-120 Hz thud under the larger hits for weight.
Write the tail from 3.35 to 4.15 s as 6-10 small rattle/scrape grains (10-30 ms each, 500-4000 Hz noise with resonant ringing), decaying from -35 dB to -55 dB, ending with about 0.15 s silence.
Remove the tonal whines at 8-12 kHz and the 1 kHz beep-like partials by randomizing resonator frequencies per hit (±10%) and low-passing noise above about 9 kHz at -12 dB/oct.
Trim the extra onsets at about 0.21 s and 2.56 s to match A's 26-onset count, and keep the 0.68, 0.93, 1.62, 2.3 and 2.87 s hits.

review.summary: B is the right kind of sound, a heavy boomy shotgun blast with the same sub/bass weight and similar band balance, but it hits instantly and sustains longer and louder, so its timing and punch differ from A. It is also mono, 2.3 LU quieter, and has a different tail.

differences.a: Peak at 0.14 s with a softer, bloomier onset and a noisy broadband crack in the first 0.3 s.
differences.b: Peak at 0.01 s, a hard instant transient with a sharper, more percussive start.

differences.a: Fast decay: -20 dB by 0.63 s, -40 dB by 1.26 s. Envelope falls from -11.6 to -23.8 dB by 0.2 s.
differences.b: Longer, fatter sustain: -20 dB by 1.03 s, -40 dB by 1.47 s. Body stays about 5 dB hotter through 0.5 s, and the sub stays strong until about 1.25 s before cutting off.

differences.a: Smooth, wide, reverberant low rumble tail fading gradually to about 1.6 s, with a slow high-frequency darkening.
differences.b: Tail is noisier and drier. Sub drops off abruptly near 1.25 s, then a thin noise floor remains. Sparse HF blips near 0.8-1.6 s. Envelope falls to -121 dB at the end, an abrupt cut.

differences.a: -13.7 LUFS, RMS -19.5 dBFS, crest 18.5 dB, peak -1.0 dBFS.
differences.b: -16.0 LUFS, RMS -17.7 dBFS, crest 16.4 dB. Higher RMS but lower integrated loudness, because the energy is spread differently. Peak -1.3 dBFS.

differences.a: Stereo with L/R correlation 0.46 and side-to-mid -4.3 dB, giving a spacious blast and tail.
differences.b: Mono, so no width in the tail. The brief explicitly asks for mono delivery, so this is expected.

differences.a: Centroid 712 Hz, falling 449 to 193 Hz. Rolloff85 891 Hz. More mid/high noise crack up to 5-10 kHz in the first 0.5 s.
differences.b: Centroid 619 Hz, with a brighter start (789 Hz) that falls to 303 Hz. Rolloff85 727 Hz. Band balance is close (sub 27 vs 25%, bass 42.7 vs 42.9%, low-mid 18 vs 14.5%). Slightly more low-mid and a bit less air.

differences.a: Very noise-dominated and dense (flatness 0.003), with a gritty, grating crack.
differences.b: Somewhat more tonal or smooth (flatness 0.037), less grit in the crack.

differences.b: 3.14 s file with active content to about 1.75 s and 1.39 s of trailing silence. A minor onset is detected at 1.61 s, probably an artifact.

review.summary: B is a very close match to A in length, loudness, spectral balance and overall roar-and-fade shape. Its main differences are a pronounced 3 to 6 dB pulsing in the sustain and a quieter start, where A holds a steadier level.

differences.a: Sustain is fairly steady, fluctuating about 3-4 dB with fast, fine flutter, and holds to about 0.8 s. Per-tenth levels run -15 to -19 dB.
differences.b: Sustain pulses in slow, distinct swells and dips of 5-6 dB (-16, -22.6, -16, -22, -16.7, -14.6). It reads as chuffing or bursts rather than a continuous roar.

differences.a: First tenth is already at -21.5 dB, with a swell into the roar peaking at 0.22 s and no discrete onsets.
differences.b: First tenth is much quieter at -40.8 dB, then it jumps to full level by about 0.1 s. Onsets are detected at 0.05 s and 0.21 s, with a louder blob near 0.15-0.25 s that makes a thump-like event.

differences.a: Dense, fine-grained turbulent roar with a vertical streaky look from rapid amplitude modulation.
differences.b: Similar streaky turbulence, but the modulation is coarser and slower with visible gaps, so it sounds less like a continuous gas jet.

differences.a: Centroid is 453 Hz and rolloff is 345 Hz. Bass is 63% and low-mid is 21%. The centroid drifts from 385 to 693 Hz across the quarters.
differences.b: Centroid is 425 Hz and rolloff is 388 Hz. Bass is 64.6% and low-mid is 20.9%. The centroid is flat across time at 410-450 Hz.

differences.a: Falls to -26 dB at 0.8 s, -40 dB at 0.9 s and -50 dB at 1.0 s, leaving a short dark tail.
differences.b: Very similar fade: -28.6, -43.7 and -53.6 dB, with 0.03 s of trailing silence.

Raise the final peak to about -0.5 dBFS (+1 dB) and make the noise layer more broadband and rough (less pitched resonance) to bring flatness toward 0.01 or lower.

review.summary: B matches A's length, overall loudness and sparse multi-hit reload layout, but the texture is wrong: noisy, crumply and bright with a fake-sounding bell, and the key events are missing or misplaced. The main slam at 1.08 s is present, but the 1.9 s bolt-release slam is not, and the low-mid body is missing.

differences.a: Distinct reload events: mag release click at ~0.13 s, mag-out clack at ~0.4 s, small ticks, big mag-insert slam at 1.08 s, rack/slide burst at 1.64-1.8 s, bolt-release clack with ring at ~1.93 s, then quiet settling ticks.
differences.b: Many similar small noise bursts spread across the clip (21 onsets vs 15). The 1.08 s slam is present, but the second half is a diffuse run of crumple-like bursts with no clear rack and release pair. Ends in a few tonal pings.

differences.a: Metallic, clicky Foley with hard transients. Spectral flatness is 0.005 (peaky, transient-dominated).
differences.b: Reads as crumpling or ripping plastic. Flatness is 0.256, which means a diffuse noise wash instead of crisp clicks. Qwen heard a package opening and a bell, not a weapon.

differences.a: Mid and presence-heavy with real low-mid body (6.9%). Vertical streaks reach down to ~200 Hz at the slams. Centroid ~5.3 kHz.
differences.b: Brighter, centroid ~6.5 kHz. Almost nothing between 100 and 400 Hz except at 1.08 s. Low-mid is thinner (5.0%) and there is a sub rumble under 100 Hz that A lacks. The slams lack weight.

differences.a: Sharp, isolated clicks and clacks with fast individual decays of about 0.1-0.2 s. Strong peaks, especially at 1.08 s and ~1.93 s.
differences.b: Softer noise-burst onsets with smeared envelopes. The only strong transient is the 1.08 s event. Hits at 1.9-2.0 s are weaker than A's.

differences.a: Loudness builds to the 1.08 s peak (-26 dB tenth) and then a second big cluster at 1.6-2.1 s. Gaps between events are quiet and the clip goes silent at the end.
differences.b: Overall contour is similar, but 1.08 s is dominant (-16 dB tenth, against -26 dB for A). The second cluster is relatively quieter and more spread out. Between-event noise floor is higher, and the final tenth is much quieter (-97 dB vs -72 dB).

differences.a: Gaps between events are quiet. 1.2-1.6 s is mostly empty, with long dead space before the rack.
differences.b: Dense continuous micro-activity from 1.18 to 1.82 s fills the gap where A has quiet space, so the rack at 1.64 s is not set up.

differences.a: No pitch. Only incidental ringing at the bolt release.
differences.b: Adds several clear sine-like tonal pings (~1.1 kHz at 0.45 s, ~1.8 kHz at 2.2 s, ~1 kHz at 2.45 s, plus 3-4 kHz). These read as bell or notification tones.

differences.a: 2.57 s with 0.1 s lead-in and 0.07 s tail silence.
differences.b: 2.57 s with 0.13 s lead-in and 0.12 s tail silence. Onsets at 0.13, 0.23, 0.73, 1.64, 2.21, 2.33 and 2.41 s line up nicely.

differences.a: Peak -1.3 dBFS, RMS -21.1 dBFS, -17.0 LUFS.
differences.b: Peak -1.6 dBFS, RMS -21.4 dBFS, -17.3 LUFS. Essentially matched.

differences.a: Mono.
differences.b: Mono.

change_notes: Rebuild the clicks as short metallic hits: a 5-10 ms white-noise burst through a 3-6 kHz band-pass, plus 2-3 inharmonic resonant partials (1.5, 2.7 and 4.1 kHz, Q ~15) that decay in 30-80 ms. This replaces the crumpled-noise bursts. Keep flatness well under 0.1.
Remove or mute the sustained tonal pings at ~0.45, 1.8-2.2 and 2.45 s, or turn them into very short (<30 ms), low-level resonances inside clacks.
Delete the dense micro-bursts at 1.18-1.82 s. Leave ~1.2-1.6 s near silent (<-50 dB) apart from 1-2 quiet ticks at about 1.4 s.

Make the 1.08 s mag-insert slam punchier: add a 250-400 Hz body thump of 60-80 ms (+6 dB over the clack), plus a 2 kHz-centred noise crack of 15 ms at 0 s and a second click ~80 ms later (~1.15 s). Lower its level by ~6-8 dB, so the 1.08 s peak sits near -1 dBFS with the others ~10 dB below.
Add a rack at 1.64-1.8 s: 150 ms band-passed noise (1-5 kHz) with a rising rasp, ~-8 dB relative to the slam.

Add the bolt-release at 1.93 s: a 10 ms sharp click, then a 250 Hz + 3 kHz clack with ~150-200 ms metallic ring (2.5 kHz partial, decays over 0.2 s). Make it nearly as loud as the 1.08 s slam (about -3 dBFS).
High-pass at ~60-80 Hz to remove sub rumble. Lift 200-500 Hz by ~4 dB on the slams. Roll off above 12 kHz by ~3 dB to bring the centroid from 6.5 kHz down to ~5.3 kHz.
Keep the settling ticks at 2.21, 2.33 and 2.41 s but make them 3-5 ms dry clicks at about -25 dB, and give the tail a quiet noise floor so the last 0.1 s is not near-absent.

review.summary: B is very close to A in role, length, loudness and spectral weight: a boomy, bass-heavy shot with a dark reverberant tail. It differs in a slower attack, a bright burst near 0.9 s, a cleaner and shorter tail, and fewer early reflections.

differences.a: Sharp noisy crack peaking at 0.04 s, with transient spikes in the waveform during the first 0.15 s.
differences.b: Peak at 0.08 s with a broader, denser blob of energy over 0.0-0.3 s, so the transient is softer and less snappy.

differences.a: Three small, low-mid reflection bumps at 0.54, 0.86 and 0.94 s, with a dark character that stays under a few kHz.
differences.b: One main secondary event at about 0.69 s plus a broadband bright burst at 0.88-1.05 s that reaches above 10 kHz in the spectrogram. It sounds like a separate hit or a glitch rather than a room reflection.

differences.a: -20 dB at 0.63 s and -40 dB at 1.38 s, with a smooth, gradual decay and a long rumbling tail.
differences.b: -20 dB at 0.48 s, with a dip around 0.4-0.5 s (-26 dB) then a rebound (-21 dB), and a steeper fall to -41 dB at 0.6 s. The final tenth is -84.8 dB versus A's -52.5 dB, so B ends in true silence while A keeps a faint tail.

differences.a: Continuous low-frequency rumble tail with a faint dark hiss, still audible up to about 1.5 s.
differences.b: Tail is similar in the low end but has scattered faint high-frequency streaks after 1.1 s that look like pulses or artifacts, and it gets quieter sooner.

differences.a: Sub 32%, bass 47%, centroid 373 Hz; the early part is brighter (centroid 490 Hz in the first quarter).
differences.b: Sub 36%, bass 44%, centroid 383 Hz. Slightly more sub, but the quarter centroids jump (1941 Hz in the third quarter) because of the bright burst.

differences.a: Peak -2.8 dBFS, -18.0 LUFS, crest 14.2 dB.
differences.b: Peak -1.0 dBFS, -18.3 LUFS, crest 15.4 dB. Effectively matched.

differences.a: Noisy, broadband crack with fluttery mid noise decaying through 1 kHz.
differences.b: Similar noise-dominated texture, slightly more tonal (flatness 0.019). It has a smoother body with less flutter.

change_notes: Sharpen the attack: add a 2-8 kHz noise crack, 5-15 ms long, at 0 s, +6 dB over the body, and move the peak from 0.08 s to about 0.03-0.04 s with a 1-2 ms attack.

Remove or tame the 0.88-1.05 s bright burst: low-pass that event at about 1.5 kHz, drop it by 10-12 dB, or turn it into two or three short dark thuds at 0.54, 0.86 and 0.94 s (30-60 ms each, 150-500 Hz, -20 to -25 dB re peak).
Smooth the body decay: stop the dip at 0.4-0.5 s. Use a single exponential so the level is about -20 dB at 0.6 s and -40 dB at 1.35-1.4 s.
Lengthen the tail: keep a dark reverb or rumble (below 200 Hz, with hiss under 3 kHz at about -50 dB) through 1.5 s, and fade out only in the last 0.15 s, ending near -50 dB rather than -85 dB.
Clean up the high-frequency pulses after 1.1 s: low-pass the reverb send at about 3-4 kHz, or set the high shelf above 4 kHz to -12 dB.
Trim the sub slightly (sub 36% to about 32%) with a gentle -2 dB shelf below 60 Hz, and lower the peak to about -3 dBFS to match A.

review.summary: B has the right overall length, brightness and loudness range, but its two-snap structure is muddled: a smeared noise burst with a swelling 'wash' replaces the crisp first click, and two stray ticks appear at 0.25 s and 0.33 s that A lacks. It reads as a noisier, less defined handling sound.

differences.a: Two distinct sharp snaps at ~0.05 s and ~0.11 s, each a crisp broadband click with a fast onset; second is slightly louder (peak ~0.10 s).
differences.b: Quiet noise bed from 0.03 s, then a swelling, blurred burst peaking ~0.09-0.13 s; the waveform shows a gradual ramp into a fat cluster with a second spike right after, so the two hits are poorly separated and the first lacks a sharp click.

differences.a: Only the two clicks and a small rattle; nothing after ~0.4 s apart from a faint 3 kHz artifact line.
differences.b: Extra isolated ticks at ~0.25 s and ~0.33 s (onsets detected) with a dark gap before them, reading as stray clicks or a second action not present in A.

differences.a: Metallic with tonal peaks near 7.8, 9.2 and 12.6 kHz (flatness 0.19), giving a clicky ping.
differences.b: More noise-like (flatness 0.29), no prominent tonal peaks; sounds like filtered hiss rather than metal, with a wideband wash from 20 Hz to 16 kHz.

differences.a: Little below 500 Hz; the low thumps are brief and sit under each hit; centroid ~6.3 kHz, presence 58%.
differences.b: Similar centroid (6.1 kHz) and bands, but a single strong sub/low thump at ~0.12 s (20-200 Hz) is stronger than A's, and rolloff is lower (8.7 vs 9.3 kHz), so there is less sparkle.

differences.a: Fast decay (-20 dB in 0.04 s, -40 dB in 0.13 s) with a faint tail to ~0.4 s then silence.
differences.b: Similar decay figures (0.05/0.14 s) but the tail has a mid-high hiss wash up to ~0.7 s and a pre-noise at the start, so it is less clean.

differences.a: Hits at ~0.05 and ~0.11 s (~60-80 ms apart), content mostly done by ~0.4 s, 0.77 s file with 0.54 s trailing silence.
differences.b: Same total length and leading silence, but the main event is a merged burst around 0.08-0.14 s, with extra activity to 0.35 s; trailing silence only 0.26 s.

differences.a: Peak -0.9 dBFS, -16.6 LUFS, RMS -21.8.
differences.b: Peak -2.1 dBFS, -18.7 LUFS, RMS -23.9; about 2 LU quieter, still within tolerance.

differences.a: Mono.
differences.b: Mono.

change_notes: Rebuild as two separate clicks: click 1 at 0.05 s, click 2 at 0.12 s (+2 dB over click 1). Each is a 3-6 ms noise burst highpassed at 3 kHz plus a 15-25 ms exponential decay; use a sharp attack under 1 ms, no ramp or swell.
Remove the noise bed/pre-swell before 0.05 s and the swelling envelope on the main burst; the gain before click 1 should be below -80 dB.
Delete the extra ticks at 0.25 s and 0.33 s, or fold them into a very quiet (-35 dB relative to the peak) rattle of 2-3 tiny ticks within 0.15-0.30 s.
Add metallic ping partials to each click: damped sines at ~7.8, 9.2 and 12.6 kHz (with slight random detune), 20-40 ms decay, at about -10 dB relative to the noise burst; cut flatness toward 0.19.
Reduce the low thump: use a 120-150 Hz sine of 30 ms per hit, -12 dB below the click peak, with the second slightly stronger than the first, instead of the big 20-200 Hz boom.
Lowpass the tail wash: apply a steep decay to hiss, -40 dB by 0.25 s and silence by 0.40 s, leaving about 0.37 s of trailing silence in the 0.77 s file.
Raise the overall level about 2 dB so the peak is ~-1 dBFS and integrated loudness ~-17 LUFS.

review.summary: B is a bright metallic click sound of the same length and similar spectral balance, but its structure is wrong. It opens with a ~70 ms noise swell, then has one big click at ~0.11 s and a few late ticks, instead of A's crisp double-click with a rattle tail.

differences.a: First click is a sharp, near-instant snap at ~0.05 s with a sub-click right after, and it is clearly separate from the second.
differences.b: No sharp first click. A soft, rising noise bed runs from ~0.03 to 0.10 s, then one hard hit lands at ~0.11 s. The pin-snap is missing, so the first half reads as a hiss swell.

differences.a: Two distinct metallic clicks ~80 ms apart, the second heavier. This double-click is the identity of the sound.
differences.b: One main click preceded by noise, so it reads as a single hit rather than a double-click. The late events are three isolated ticks at ~0.25, 0.32 and 0.36 s.

differences.a: Rapid decay after the second click (~0.05 s to -20 dB, 0.16 s to -40 dB) into a short rattle tail ending ~0.35 s.
differences.b: Decay is similarly fast (0.04 s to -20 dB), but there is a hard gap of silence/gating at ~0.24-0.26 s, followed by sparse ticks. This feels gated and chopped, not like a rattling tail.

differences.a: Both clicks fall within 0.04-0.18 s. The tail fades by ~0.4 s, with a faint tick at 0.55 s.
differences.b: Energy is spread more widely, with onsets at 0.05, 0.25 and 0.34 s and an active fraction of 0.25 versus 0.21. The timing is scattered where A is tight. Total length matches at 0.77 s.

differences.a: Centroid ~6.0 kHz, with a thin steady tone line near 3 kHz and faint high lines at 9-16 kHz. Little content below 150 Hz.
differences.b: Centroid ~6.2 kHz and band percentages are close. However, B has a visible sub/bass bloom (20-100 Hz) under the main click and lacks the 3 kHz ring line. Its high-frequency lines are weaker and sit near 7.6 kHz.

differences.a: Metallic and clicky with some tonal ring (flatness 0.19).
differences.b: Noisier and more hissy (flatness 0.28). Reads less like metal and more like filtered noise bursts.

differences.a: Peak -1.1 dBFS, -17.7 LUFS.
differences.b: Peak -2.3 dBFS, -19.0 LUFS. About 1.3 LU quieter, which is within tolerance.

differences.a: Short rattle/ring tail, then ~0.45 s of near-silence.
differences.b: Sparse ticks and a faint noise floor out to ~0.7 s, with 0.2 s of trailing silence. Not a ring or rattle tail.

Clear separation into two clicks ~80 ms apart

change_notes: Remove the 70 ms noise swell before the main hit. Replace it with a sharp pin-snap at 0.05 s: a 3-5 ms noise click through a 3-10 kHz band-pass plus a 6-8 kHz metallic ping, 20-30 ms decay, peaking about -4 dBFS.

Keep the heavy click at ~0.13 s, so the gap from the first is ~80 ms. Build it from a 5 ms broadband burst, a 150-300 Hz low thump of ~30 ms at about -12 dB under the click, and a metallic resonance of ~40 ms. Keep its peak at -1 to -2 dBFS and make it ~4-6 dB louder than the first click.

Add a rattle/ring tail from 0.18 to 0.35 s: 3-4 tiny ticks with a 2-4 kHz band-pass, 5-10 ms each and spaced 30-60 ms apart, plus a 3 kHz sine ring decaying over ~150 ms at about -35 dB. Fade it out, with no hard gate or gap at 0.25 s.
Delete the isolated ticks at 0.32 and 0.36 s. If any remain, keep them below -50 dB.
Cut sub energy below 100 Hz with a high-pass at ~120 Hz on the main click, so the thump sits at 150-300 Hz rather than 20-100 Hz.
Raise tonality: lower noise share in the click layers, add 2-3 inharmonic partials around 3, 7 and 9 kHz, and target a flatness of ~0.2.
Raise overall level ~1.5 dB, to a peak of ~-1 dBFS and ~-18 LUFS. Keep the file length at 0.77 s, or trim the trailing silence.

review.summary: B has the right overall envelope: loud broadband crack and boom in the first ~0.25 s, similar length, band balance and peak time. But its tail is gappy and discontinuous, with a dead hole around 0.4-0.5 s, a re-triggered burst near 0.8 s, and fast-decaying highs. It reads as a stuttering double hit, not A's smooth, continuous reverberant decay.

differences.a: Smooth, continuous decay with a long low-level tail: -20 dB at 0.32 s, -40 dB at 1.32 s. Energy is gradually ragged but never drops out.
differences.b: Decay is discontinuous. Envelope drops to about -51 dB in the 0.4 s tenth, rebounds to -27 dB, then falls off. -40 dB is reached at 0.7 s, far earlier than A's 1.32 s.

differences.a: Single blast with a continuous body. Two tiny onsets at 0.7 s and 0.81 s are just reflection debris.
differences.b: Reads as separate segments: the main blast to ~0.25 s, a secondary burst at ~0.38 s, a gap, then a distinct re-trigger near 0.81 s with a sub thump. These sound like extra hits or a second shot, not tail debris.

differences.a: Smooth, dark reverberant rumble that lingers to ~1.5 s with highs fading gradually.
differences.b: Tail is chopped, with vertical broadband clicks or stripes between 0.9 s and 1.5 s and a gated, truncated feel. Low-mid rumble persists but is not continuous. Little real reverb impression.

differences.a: Very low flatness (0.002): dominated by low-frequency energy, noisy texture, gritty and organic.
differences.b: Flatness is much higher (0.158), suggesting a more noise-like or synthetic, less low-end-dominated texture. Spectrogram shows more mid and high noise in the early part.

differences.a: Centroid 1158 Hz, rolloff 2.5 kHz. Highs decay quickly, centroid falls to ~215 Hz by the third quarter.
differences.b: Centroid 1342 Hz, rolloff 2.9 kHz, a bit brighter. Centroid jumps to 1665 Hz in the third quarter because of the late bursts, so the tail is brighter and less consistently dark.

differences.a: -17.4 LUFS, peak +0.3 dBFS (slight clipping).
differences.b: -19.3 LUFS, peak -1.5 dBFS. About 2 LU quieter, within tolerance and cleaner.

differences.a: Peak at 0.03 s, with a noisy crack and heavy thump.
differences.b: Peak at 0.02 s, equally punchy, with a fast attack and similar crest factor (17.3 vs 17.6 dB).

differences.a: DC offset negligible (-0.0009).
differences.b: DC offset 0.013, small but present; 126 kbps encode.

missing_elements: Continuous smooth reverberant tail that holds -40 dB until ~1.3 s
Gradual darkening of the tail with no dropouts or gating
extra_elements: Secondary noise burst around 0.38-0.5 s
Re-triggered sub thump and mid burst around 0.8-1.2 s that sounds like a second hit
Vertical click-like broadband stripes in the 0.9-1.5 s tail
Small DC offset
change_notes: Replace the segmented tail with a single continuous decaying layer: lowpassed noise at ~400-800 Hz plus 40-100 Hz rumble, exponential decay with -20 dB at ~0.3 s and -40 dB at ~1.2-1.3 s, with no gaps.
Remove or merge the secondary burst at 0.38 s and the re-trigger at 0.81 s. If any reflections are kept, make them tiny (-35 dB or lower relative to the peak, 20-30 ms) near 0.7 s and 0.81 s.
Fill the 0.3-0.6 s hole: keep the body at roughly -25 to -30 dB with a smoothly falling sub/bass thump (50-150 Hz) instead of dropping to -50 dB.
Sweep a lowpass on the tail noise from ~6 kHz at 0.2 s down to ~1.5 kHz by 1.0 s, and remove the high-frequency clicks above 4 kHz after 0.9 s.
Add a dark reverb or room tail, about 1 s RT with high damping, or comb/allpass feedback on the body, to reproduce A's reverberant rumble.
Raise overall level about 1.5-2 dB toward -17.5 LUFS while keeping the peak at -1 dBFS, and high-pass at 20 Hz to remove the DC offset.
Optionally lower the 2-8 kHz noise in the first 0.15 s by ~2 dB so the centroid sits nearer 1.1-1.2 kHz.

review.summary: B has the same total length (3.41 s) and a similar mid/presence balance, but it compresses A's four clack clusters into three, with a big low-frequency thud in the middle and much sparser activity. It reads as a different, thuddier reload and not as a clicky akimbo mag-swap sequence.

differences.a: Four distinct clack/rattle clusters (0.1-0.9 s, 1.4-2.3 s, 2.54-2.85 s, 2.9-3.4 s) with 21 onsets, showing two guns' mag out, mag in and bolt actions.
differences.b: Three clusters (0.1-0.75 s, 1.7-2.3 s, 2.6-3.2 s) with only 13 onsets. The first cluster is sparse and weak, and the structure is less clearly akimbo.

differences.a: Thin low end, with almost no sub or bass. Energy sits at 1-6 kHz and the clacks are bright and metallic.
differences.b: A strong 30-100 Hz boom and a 200-350 Hz blob around 1.8-2.2 s, so the middle event sounds like a heavy thud or dropped object (Qwen heard footsteps and a thud). This is a very different weight from A's light clacks.

differences.a: Active fraction 0.53. Gaps are about 0.5 s (0.9-1.4 s) and 0.25 s (2.3-2.55 s), and the final cluster runs to 3.36 s.
differences.b: Active fraction 0.23. The gap runs from 0.75 s to 1.7 s, almost a full second, and the next one is 2.3-2.7 s. The ending is cut off earlier, with 0.3 s of trailing silence versus A's 0.05 s.

differences.a: Many sharp, repeated metallic transients, with ticks between the main hits and crest around 22 dB.
differences.b: The first cluster has a few weak ticks (the 0.13 s tick stands out, then low-level rattle). The loud events are clumped into single swells with fewer discrete clicks. Impacts are less crisp and less frequent.

differences.a: Gritty, tonal-metallic clack and rattle (flatness 0.14). Handling rustle and plastic/metal clacks.
differences.b: Noisier, more hissy broadband texture (flatness 0.25) with isolated sine-like tones (about 1 kHz and 2 kHz blips, plus high horizontal lines near 7-9 kHz) that sound like synthetic beeps, not mechanical parts.

differences.a: Peak -1.0 dBFS, RMS -23 dB, -19.0 LUFS.
differences.b: Peak -2.6 dBFS, RMS -25.5 dB, -19.2 LUFS. Integrated loudness matches, but the energy is concentrated in the middle event, with the first and last clusters much quieter than A's.

differences.a: Each cluster is 0.2-0.3 s with a quick decay (0.14 s to -20 dB).
differences.b: Decays are similarly quick (0.11 s to -20 dB), but the middle event has a longer boomy sustain of about 0.4 s from the low content.

differences.a: Dry with a short tail.
differences.b: Dry, but the low thump gives a body-like tail that A lacks.

differences.a: Mono.
differences.b: Mono.

missing_elements: The fourth clack cluster; A has distinct clusters at about 0.3-0.8 s, 1.5-2.2 s, 2.5-2.85 s and 2.9-3.4 s.
Dense inter-hit ticks and rattles (A has 21 onsets, B has 13).
Handling rustle and scrape texture before the mag-in hits (about 1.4-1.65 s).
Clear paired, near-identical clack groups that suggest two guns (0.32/0.4 s and 0.69/0.77 s).

200-350 Hz thud body at about 1.8-2.2 s.
Narrow tonal blips at about 1 kHz and 2 kHz, and thin high horizontal lines near 7-9 kHz, that sound like beeps.

change_notes: Remove or heavily cut the sub boom and the low thud: high-pass the middle event at about 150-200 Hz (12 dB/oct), or reduce the 30-100 Hz layer by at least 25 dB, so the sub and bass bands are near 0%.

Rebuild the structure as four clusters. Cluster 1 spans 0.13-0.85 s with two clacks at about 0.32 s and 0.40 s and a second pair at 0.69 s and 0.77 s, at -8 to -12 dB re the loudest hit. Cluster 2 spans 1.45-2.27 s with ticks at 1.51 s and 1.59 s, hard mag-slam clacks at 1.71 s and 2.05 s, and extra ticks between. Cluster 3 spans 2.54-2.85 s (bolt clacks plus a tick at 2.73 s). Cluster 4 spans 2.9-3.36 s.

Shorten the silent gap to 0.5 s (0.9-1.4 s) instead of about 1 s, and make the second gap about 0.25 s (2.3-2.55 s). Fill the active region to about 50% of the duration, and cut trailing silence to about 0.05 s.

Make each clack a 3-8 ms noise click (band 1.5-6 kHz) layered with a 10-25 ms damped metallic resonance at 1-3 kHz (Q around 8-12, decay about 60-120 ms). Use 2-3 slightly detuned resonances for each hit, not a single pure sine.
Add 3-5 small ticks and rattles per cluster (2-5 ms clicks at -15 to -20 dB, 2-6 kHz) between main hits, and a 100-200 ms filtered-noise rustle (1-4 kHz, -25 dB) at 0.13-0.3 s and 1.4-1.65 s.
Remove the isolated pure tones at 1 kHz/2 kHz and the 7-9 kHz lines; lower the noise floor and hiss so flatness is about 0.15.

review.summary: B follows the A reload layout (1.81 s, matching LUFS, similar event times), but its sounds are weaker and less metallic. The first event is a tiny tick, the magazine thunk is a long tonal sub boom, and the closing snap is nearly absent. It reads as a sparse, synthetic imitation, not a punchy foley reload.

differences.b: The first event is a tiny tick of about 0.05 s that is barely visible in the waveform, with a faint high-frequency smear and no body.

differences.b: The closing event at about 1.62-1.7 s is a very faint tick, tens of dB below the main events. The slide-release snap is essentially missing.

differences.b: The 0.38-0.55 s event has a gradually swelling or sustained sub boom of about 150 ms with a hard end, followed by a click at 0.5 s. Narrow whistle-like tonal lines at about 8-12 kHz sit on top. It feels synthetic and less like impact metal.

differences.b: Low end is confined to the mag thunk (40-120 Hz) and is nearly absent on the other events. Highs extend up to 16 kHz+, and the midrange 200-800 Hz is hollow.

differences.b: Contains tonal whistles at about 8-12 kHz and a 1 kHz line at about 1.0-1.15 s, which makes the sound partly pitched and synthetic.

review.summary: B is a close match for A's loud, boomy, bass-heavy revolver blast, with nearly identical loudness, centroid and decay times. Its tail cuts off abruptly at about 2.0 s, and its low-mid body is a bit stronger and less dark than A's, so the ending is the main audible difference.

review.summary: B has the right overall length, loudness and onset grid for a multi-stage LMG reload, with a loud mid-sequence slam near 1.5 s. But it drops the final lock-in clack pair at 4.7-5.5 s, fills the 3.5-4.2 s section with continuous rattle instead of punchy clacks, and its sub-bass pulses and noisy hiss make it sound unlike A's crisp clacks.

differences.a: Final stage at 4.7-5.5 s is a heavy, loud clack pair (bolt slam or lock-in) with a rattle tail. It is one of the loudest events in the file.
differences.b: Nothing is audible there except a very faint, tiny blip near 5.1-5.3 s, about -50 dB. The 0.9-1.0 tenth envelope reads -200 dB.

differences.a: Active until about 5.5 s with 0.2 s trailing silence. The gap at 4.3-4.7 s is short and the sequence resumes afterwards, so active fraction is 0.54.
differences.b: Content stops at about 4.1 s, leaving 0.52 s trailing silence and a long dead gap of roughly 1.1 s. Active fraction is 0.43. The reload feels like it ends early and the finishing action is missing.

differences.a: Sharp, crisp clacks a few ms long, with fast decay and dry, tight transients, each separated by quiet gaps. Decay to -40 dB is 0.43 s.
differences.b: Onsets line up closely with A, but they are softer and smeared by sustained noise, and decay to -40 dB is 0.63 s. The 3.3-4.1 s section reads as continuous rattle or hiss, not 2-3 distinct punchy clacks.

differences.a: Dense broadband clicks with very low flatness of 0.004 and a thin tonal pair near 1.5-2 kHz around 1 s. It sounds like real metallic foley.
differences.b: Flatness is 0.301, so it is noisier and more diffuse. A visible 323 Hz tonal blob near 1.5 s and short tonal blips at about 1-2 kHz sound synthetic and pitched, not like clacks.

differences.a: Centroid is about 3.5 kHz, varying by section: 3.0, 2.5, 4.9, then 4.1 kHz. Low end is a few muffled thumps at the start, and the 1.4-2.0 s slam has strong low-mid body.
differences.b: Centroid is flat at about 4.3-4.6 kHz in every quarter, so it is brighter and more uniform. Rolloff is 7.8 kHz versus 7.1 kHz. Repeated 20-60 Hz sub pulses recur through the file, where A has them only at the start.

differences.a: Loudest event at 1.56 s. Quiet ticks between 0.9 and 1.2 s. Alternating loud and quiet stages give a loudness range of 1.2 LU.
differences.b: The 1.5 s peak is also the loudest, but the middle and late sections are more uniform, with a loudness range of 7.3 LU. Dynamics between stages are less clear, and the 3.3-4.1 s section is a sustained mid-level wash.

review.summary: B is the right kind of sound, a heavy bass-rich shotgun blast of the same 2.1 s length with similar sub/bass balance. It differs in attack shape, body sustain, tail and loudness, and it is mono where A is stereo.

review.summary: B is the right kind of sound, a boomy low-end launcher thump with a noisy burst, and it matches A in loudness, band balance and overall length. But it has a softer, slower start with a pre-onset, a clear second hit near 0.26 s, and a tail that ends abruptly around 0.8 s with no room tone or mid body.

differences.a: Near-instant attack peaking at 0.04 s, with a loud broadband noisy crack and a single onset at 0.05 s. The first tenth sits at -18 dB, so it hits right away.
differences.b: The first tenth is very quiet at -38.5 dB. A faint lead-in is followed by a ramp to the peak at 0.08 s, which is twice as slow. Onsets are detected at 0.05 s and 0.26 s.

differences.a: A slow, smooth decay: -20 dB at 0.31 s, -40 dB at 0.72 s, and a long low-level rumble out to about 0.8 s. The low block stays bright to 0.55 s.
differences.b: A faster early drop: -20 dB at 0.16 s, -40 dB at 0.59 s. Then the level falls off a cliff (-126 dB by 0.5-0.6 s per the tenth-second envelope) and the spectrogram cuts hard at about 0.8 s.

differences.a: One blast with a small secondary bump near 0.25 s, within the same low-frequency body. It reads as a single shot.
differences.b: A distinct second onset at 0.26 s, with a visible re-strike in the waveform. It could read as a double hit or a separate 'thoomp' layer.

differences.a: A natural, room-like tail with dense mid and high noise fading gradually to about 0.8 s. A faint steady resonance sits near 1 kHz.
differences.b: A drier, shorter tail that terminates abruptly around 0.8 s with a visible vertical cutoff. There is no 1 kHz resonance, and the mid and high noise fade out earlier.

differences.a: Centroid 554 Hz, 85% rolloff 431 Hz. The first quarter is brighter (805 Hz), and a mid-high noise crack reaches about 5 kHz and above in the first 0.3 s.
differences.b: Centroid 566 Hz, but rolloff 689 Hz. The first quarter is darker (590 Hz), the later quarters are flat at about 290 Hz, and the bright crack is weaker. The band percentages match closely.

differences.a: Very noise-like (flatness about 0), with a light tonal line near 1 kHz.
differences.b: Slightly more tonal and pitched (flatness 0.032). The low-end body looks more periodic and pulsing in the spectrogram.

differences.a: 1.68 s file with about 0.9 s of trailing silence. Active content is about 0.8 s.
differences.b: 1.68 s file with 1.01 s of trailing silence. Active content is about 0.7 s, slightly shorter.

differences.a: Peak -3.0 dBFS, RMS -21.4, -20.5 LUFS.
differences.b: Peak -3.1 dBFS, RMS -22.0, -20.8 LUFS. This is within tolerance.

change_notes: Make the attack immediate: remove the quiet lead-in (-38 dB in the first 0.1 s) and bring the peak to 0.03-0.04 s. Use a 1-2 ms attack on both the crack and the thump, with the first 100 ms at about -18 dB like A.

Add or strengthen a broadband noise crack: 1-5 kHz, 40-60 ms, at t=0, about +6 dB over the body, with a lowpass sweeping from 8 kHz down to 2 kHz over 300 ms. This gives the bright first quarter, about 800 Hz centroid.
Fold the second onset at 0.26 s into the main decay: reduce it by about 8-10 dB, or turn it into a soft low-passed rumble swell, so it reads as one shot with a small bump, not two hits.
Lengthen the main body decay: the 40-300 Hz thump should hold bright to about 0.55 s, reaching -20 dB at about 0.3 s instead of 0.16 s. Use a decay time constant of about 0.18-0.2 s on the low layer.

Replace the hard cutoff with a smooth 0.2-0.3 s fade-out ending at about 0.8 s. Add a low-level filtered noise tail (300 Hz-3 kHz, -45 to -60 dB) with a gentle lowpass, and optionally a very faint 1 kHz resonant band at -55 dB.

Reduce the tonal pulsing in the sub: use less periodic modulation and more noise in the low layer, bringing flatness toward 0 and rolloff down toward 450 Hz. Lowpass the body at about 300 Hz with a gentle slope.

review.summary: B is a close match in length (2.29 s), loudness (-20.7 vs -20.2 LUFS), band balance and the late 1.35-1.54 s clatter. It has a softer, darker, more rounded onset and a sustained sub plateau, so it reads as a boomier, less cracky shot than A.

differences.a: Sharp broadband crack at t=0 with bright energy up to ~10 kHz and the loudest point in the first 0.05 s; hard onset.
differences.b: The first 0.05 s is quiet (about -24 dB in the first tenth) and the hit starts around 0.05 s. The transient is softer and builds over about 60 ms to a rounded plateau, with less click.

differences.a: Centroid ~413 Hz, with a bright noisy upper-mid body (1-10 kHz) in the first 0.4 s and a centroid of 657 Hz in the first quarter.
differences.b: Centroid ~353 Hz, and the first-quarter centroid is only 175 Hz. It is much darker and more sub-dominant early on, with fewer highs after the first ~0.2 s.

differences.a: Steady decay from the peak: -15 dB to -22 dB by 0.3 s, with a dip near 0.5 s, then a gradual fall to -40 dB at 2.0 s.
differences.b: Holds a flat, loud bass plateau from 0.05 to ~0.7 s, then drops abruptly at ~0.75 s. Overall -20 dB at 0.65 s and -40 dB at 2.0 s are similar, but the shape is blockier.

differences.a: Casing/clatter bump around 1.36 and 1.44 s, soft, with a sustained low rumble from ~1.3 to 1.7 s.
differences.b: Three distinct vertical broadband clicks at 1.35, 1.44 and 1.54 s, spiking noticeably at 1.4 s (-19 dB tenth) and brighter than A's. Reads as a more distinct clatter.

differences.a: Long smooth low rumble tail with highs gone by ~1.7 s; trailing energy reaches the end.
differences.b: Similar low rumble tail, but highs persist faintly to ~2.1 s with a more gated end. The tail is cleaner and less diffuse.

differences.a: Noisy, gritty, recorded-sounding broadband blast.
differences.b: More tonal and synthetic (flatness 0.018 vs 0), with a smoother bass pulse and a more 'boom' feel than a crack.

differences.a: Peak -2.4 dBFS, RMS -18.4, -20.2 LUFS.
differences.b: Peak -1.2 dBFS, RMS -17.0, -20.7 LUFS. About 0.5 LU quieter integrated, with a slightly higher peak.

Shorten the attack to 1-3 ms and lift the early 0.2-1 kHz noise body so the first-quarter centroid rises from ~175 Hz to ~600 Hz. Fade the highs by 0.4 s with a lowpass sweeping from 10 kHz down to ~1.5 kHz.
