Trim the overall level by about +0.5 LU and peak to about -2 dBFS to match A's integrated loudness.

review.summary: B is a close match to A: a ~1.1 s mono low-passed turbulent roar with the same bass-heavy balance, loudness and fast cut-off tail. The differences are mostly in envelope shape and fine texture, so it would pass in game with small adjustments.

differences.a: Fairly steady sustain at -14 to -22 dB with fluttery dips near 0.4 s and 0.9 s. Peak at 0.59 s. Level builds quickly from -22 dB to about -17 dB in the first 0.2 s.
differences.b: Wider swells and dips: -26.7 dB at the start, a trough of -22.9 dB near 0.4 s, then a pronounced hump to -12.4 dB at 0.6 s. The overall dynamic contour is a little more uneven.

differences.a: Soft onset with no distinct click; the level builds over about 0.1 s.
differences.b: Starts slightly quieter (-26.7 dB) with two detected soft onsets at 0.06 s and 0.23 s, so the opening is a little more pulsed and slower to fill in.

differences.a: Fast fade over the last ~0.1 s, from about -19 dB to -49 dB in the final tenth, with no reverb.
differences.b: Equally fast cut, but it falls to -60 dB with about 0.03 s of trailing silence, so it is a touch cleaner and more abrupt. No real reverb, though Qwen's notes claim some.

differences.a: Bass 70.5%, low-mid 21.5%, centroid 390 Hz, rolloff85 323 Hz. The spectrogram shows a steady falloff above 1 kHz and a dark top end above ~10 kHz.
differences.b: Bass 68%, low-mid 24.2%, centroid 383 Hz, rolloff85 388 Hz. Slightly more energy at 300-600 Hz and more visible mid and high-mid grain, up to 10 kHz and beyond.

differences.a: Dense, fast vertical flutter in the low band with fine crackle in the mids.
differences.b: Similar streaky flutter, with slightly broader, slower-looking modulation and more mid-frequency speckle around 0.5-0.9 s.

differences.a: Peak -4.8 dBFS, RMS -16.4 dBFS, -16.6 LUFS.
differences.b: Peak -3.8 dBFS, RMS -16.3 dBFS, -16.8 LUFS. Essentially equal, with a peak about 1 dB hotter.

A hint of mid-frequency crackle that stays consistent across the whole body

A bigger loudness hump around 0.6 s
A little more 300-600 Hz body and high-mid grain
change_notes: Reduce the slow amplitude swell depth on the noise body: limit the 0.5-0.7 s hump to about -14 dB (currently -12.4 dB) and fill the trough near 0.4 s up to about -19 dB, so the sustain stays within roughly ±3 dB of -17 dB.
Raise the opening level from -26.7 dB to about -22 dB, with a 0.1 s fade-in, and smooth out the 0.06 s and 0.23 s pulses.
Lower the low-pass cutoff on the main noise from roughly 600-800 Hz to about 500-600 Hz, or cut 300-600 Hz by 1-2 dB, to bring rolloff85 from 388 Hz toward 330 Hz.
Keep the 20-40 Hz flutter modulation, but shorten its smoothing a bit so it reads as fast crackle rather than slow swell.
Lower the final peak by about 1 dB to bring it near -4.8 dBFS, and keep the fade-out at 0.1 s, ending at about -50 dB instead of -60 dB.

review.summary: B is a very close match to A: a 1.3 s low-passed turbulent noise roar with nearly identical band energy, loudness and fade-out. Remaining differences are a slightly softer start, two louder rumble swells and a darker top end, none of which change the role.

differences.a: Swells in from about -23 dB to -14 dB within the first 0.2 s with no distinct onsets, so it reads as a steady roar.
differences.b: Starts lower, at about -29 dB in the first tenth, and the swell is slightly slower. It also has two detected onsets at 0.23 s and 0.79 s, visible as bursts in the waveform.

differences.a: Fairly even sustain with fluttery ripple of about ±3 dB, then a fade starting near 1.05 s (-35 dB at 0.9 of the duration, -57 dB at the end).
differences.b: Sustain is less even, with a dip near 0.55-0.65 s and louder swells around 0.3 s and 0.85 s. The fade is similar, but the final tenth falls to -88 dB, so the cut is cleaner and the tail is quieter.

differences.a: Centroid is about 376 Hz, with a darker last quarter of about 276 Hz as the flame dies. Highs are dense up to about 5-8 kHz.
differences.b: Centroid is about 346 Hz and band percentages are almost identical. The centroid rises in the last quarter (436 Hz) instead of darkening. The spectrogram shows a slightly smoother, thinner mid and high texture.

differences.a: Gritty, crackling turbulence with fine fluttery modulation across the mids.
differences.b: A similar turbulent noise, but the amplitude modulation is slower and blotchier, with large irregular bursts instead of fine flutter.

differences.a: Peak -4.5 dBFS, RMS -16.5 dB, -16.9 LUFS, crest factor 12.0 dB.
differences.b: Peak -3.2 dBFS, RMS -16.7 dB, -17.1 LUFS, crest factor 13.5 dB. This is effectively the same perceived loudness, with slightly spikier peaks.

missing_elements: Fine 10-30 Hz flutter and crackle texture in the body
Darkening of the spectrum during the final fade
extra_elements: Two louder rumble bursts at about 0.25 s and 0.8 s that read as pulses
Quiet sub-noise floor in the last tenth (-88 dB), giving a cleaner cut-off
change_notes: Add faster turbulence modulation to the noise body: 10-30 Hz random amplitude flutter at about ±3 dB, and reduce the slow bursts at 0.23 s and 0.79 s by about 3 dB so the peak sits near -4.5 dBFS.
Speed up the opening swell so it reaches -15 dB by about 0.1 s. Start from about -23 dB instead of -29 dB.
Make the last 0.25 s darker by sweeping the lowpass from about 2 kHz down to about 800 Hz, so the centroid falls to about 280 Hz.
Add a gritty 1-4 kHz crackle layer at roughly -6 dB relative to the body, using random 2-5 ms grains at 40-80 per second, to match A's mid texture.
Lengthen the end of the fade slightly so the last tenth sits near -57 dB instead of -88 dB, with no hard cutoff.

review.summary: B is the right kind of sound: a 0.3 s bass-heavy minigun burst with a 1 s tail, at near-identical loudness and band balance. Its burst end is softer, its tail is shorter and darker, and it has less upper-mid and high bite than A, so it feels slightly less hard and gritty.

differences.a: The burst holds a near-constant level to 0.3 s, then drops abruptly (~12-15 dB) in a hard step. The step is visible in the spectrogram and waveform.
differences.b: The burst ramps down over roughly 0.22-0.35 s with a softer, rounded cutoff. The envelope falls from -7 dB to -25 dB, but the transition is smoother and the cut reads less sharp.

differences.a: The tail is long and wide: -20 dB at 0.45 s, -40 dB at 0.84 s. It holds a broadband noisy wash with mids and highs that fades gradually to ~0.85 s.
differences.b: The tail decays faster: -20 dB at 0.29 s, -40 dB at 0.66 s. It is darker and thinner, with a very low level near the end (-99.7 dB in the last tenth versus -72 dB in A).

differences.a: Rolloff85 is ~1.9 kHz and the centroid ~1.23 kHz. The noise is brighter and holds energy longer, with high-frequency content above 4 kHz sustained through the burst and into the early tail.
differences.b: Rolloff85 is only ~1.2 kHz, with the centroid falling from 1.3 kHz to 0.59 kHz across quarters. The tail is much darker, and the highs vanish after ~0.37 s, where A keeps them to ~0.6 s.

differences.a: Instant attack at 0 s with a dense, gritty chatter and strong shot transients from fast overlapping shots.
differences.b: The measured peak is at 0.15 s (the burst is slightly lower in level at the start: -8.3 versus -5.8 dB in the first tenth). It has a similar chatter, but the individual shots are slightly softer and more blended.

differences.a: Distorted, gritty and mechanical, with dense high-mid speckle and a stable, hard-edged amplitude ripple.
differences.b: A similar rapid-fire modulation with a slightly cleaner, smoother body. Spectral flatness is 0.129 versus 0.0, and the shot modulation looks more irregular and swelling.

differences.a: -12.8 LUFS integrated, peak -1.5 dBFS, RMS -13.5 dBFS.
differences.b: -13.9 LUFS, peak -1.9 dBFS, RMS -14.8 dBFS. This is ~1 LU quieter, well within tolerance.

differences.a: Bass is ~72% with sub 2.8%. Energy is strongest at 50-250 Hz.
differences.b: Bass is 75.5% and sub 3.0%. This is very close, with a slightly heavier low end.

Fully instant, full-level attack at 0 s

Slightly heavier sustained low end in the tail
change_notes: Sharpen the burst end: hold the burst gain flat to 0.30 s, then cut to about -14 dB within ~10 ms instead of the current ~100 ms ramp. Keep the shot ripple constant until the cut.
Lengthen the tail: raise the decay time constant so it reaches -20 dB at ~0.45 s and -40 dB at ~0.84 s (currently 0.29 s and 0.66 s). Keep ~0.15 s of trailing silence.

Brighten the tail: add a band-passed noise wash (1-5 kHz) at about -25 dB relative to burst peak, starting at 0.3 s and decaying over ~0.5 s. Raise the overall rolloff85 from ~1.2 kHz to ~1.9 kHz, and slow the centroid decline so the last quarter stays above ~1 kHz.
Make the attack immediate: start each burst at full level at 0 s, with a ~1 ms rise and a first shot transient at about -6 dB, instead of letting the level build to 0.15 s.
Add 3-6 kHz noise crack to each shot, ~5-10 ms, about +3 dB over the current level, to restore the gritty bite and lower spectral flatness toward 0.
Trim the low end slightly: reduce bass (60-200 Hz) by ~1 dB, and raise overall gain ~1 dB to reach ~-12.8 LUFS with a peak near -1.5 dBFS.

review.summary: B is a similar heavy, bass-laden noisy shot with the same length, loudness and overall envelope, but it lacks A's defining bright fast downward chirp and diagonal sweeps. It also reads as a more explosive, gunshot-like burst with a rougher texture and a mid-body energy swell.

differences.a: Bright, fast downward chirp from about 10 kHz in the first ~50 ms, plus faint falling diagonal sweeps in the 1-6 kHz range and a weak sweep to ~500 Hz near 0.5-0.65 s. This gives the laser identity.
differences.b: No clear chirp or sweeps; only a very faint diagonal at the top-left. Reads as noise burst or explosion, as Qwen's 'explosion or gunshot' note suggests.

differences.a: Sharp bright transient at 0 s, then a steady dense body whose level stays around -14 to -16 dB through ~0.2 s.
differences.b: No distinct top-end transient. The start is softer (-15 dB), then there is a visible peak burst at ~0.2 s (waveform spike). Energy swells mid-body instead of striking at the onset.

differences.a: Distorted, buzzy, grainy tone and noise blend, with low-frequency flutter and a laser-synth feel.
differences.b: Noisier and more broadband, with a vertical-striated boomy character like a rumbling blast. Spectral flatness 0.117 vs 0.007 indicates more noise and less tonal buzz.

differences.a: Sustained body to ~0.45 s, -20 dB at 0.37 s, -40 dB at 0.61 s.
differences.b: Similar shape but slightly faster: -20 dB at 0.26 s, -40 dB at 0.54 s. Dips and re-bumps around 0.5-0.7 s (-57 to -51 dB).

differences.a: Sub 25.6%, bass 36.3%, centroid 1.09 kHz, rolloff 2.2 kHz. Centroid falls from 1.3 kHz to ~200 Hz.
differences.b: Sub 25.4%, bass 31.2%, centroid 1.2 kHz, rolloff 2.5 kHz. Brighter in the first quarter (1.9 kHz) and the last quarter (1.19 kHz, with stray clicks at 0.75 s and 1.2-1.4 s), so it gets less dark and boomy as it fades.

differences.a: Quiet rumble and hiss tail that fades smoothly to ~0.9 s, with trailing silence ~0.66 s.
differences.b: Similar length and trailing silence (0.67 s), but the tail has small tick artifacts around 0.75 s and 1.2-1.4 s, and an abrupt cutoff near 1.43 s.

differences.a: Stereo, correlation 0.77, side-to-mid -8.9 dB, with a wide upper layer.
differences.b: Mono, as the brief requires for positional sounds.

differences.a: Peak -3.3 dBFS, RMS -20.4, -15.0 LUFS.
differences.b: Peak -1.1 dBFS, RMS -18.7, -15.5 LUFS. Slightly hotter in peak and RMS but within tolerance.

missing_elements: Bright fast downward chirp from ~10 kHz at 0-50 ms
Falling diagonal sweeps in the 1-6 kHz range, plus the weak sweep to ~500 Hz around 0.5-0.65 s
Buzzy tonal distorted laser-synth layer
Wide stereo upper layer

Tick or click artifacts in the tail at ~0.75 s and 1.2-1.4 s
Brighter, more broadband noise in the first 0.3 s
change_notes: Add a laser zap layer at 0 s: a sine or saw sweep from 10 kHz down to 500 Hz over 150-250 ms (exponential), 40 ms attack-free hit, about +6 dB over the surrounding noise in the 2-8 kHz band.
Add 2-3 fainter falling sweeps, e.g. 6 kHz to 1.5 kHz over 400 ms and 3 kHz to 500 Hz over 600 ms, at -15 to -20 dB relative to the main chirp.
Add a transient at 0 s: 5-10 ms bright click/noise burst (2-10 kHz), so the hit is at the start. Reduce the mid-body swell at 0.2 s by ~4 dB, or soften its attack with a 20 ms smoothing.

Replace part of the white-noise body with a distorted saw or square buzz (50-150 Hz fundamental plus harmonics, soft-clipped), aiming for flatness well below 0.05. Lowpass the noise at ~3 kHz after 0.3 s.
Lengthen the body decay slightly: -20 dB at ~0.37 s and -40 dB at ~0.6 s, and smooth the 0.5-0.7 s dip so it decays monotonically.
Remove the tick artifacts after 0.7 s; keep the tail as a smooth lowpassed (<500 Hz) rumble fading by ~0.9 s, with a fade-out rather than a hard cut at 1.43 s.
Pull the peak down to about -3 dBFS (-2 dB gain) and keep it mono as specified.

review.summary: B follows A's overall structure (quiet clicks, a mid cluster, a dead gap, and a loud closing snap near 1.38 s) with matching length and loudness. It is sparser and tonally different: the clicks are thinner, a sub-100 Hz rumble sits under each event, and the final snap has a different body.

differences.a: Almost no energy below about 150 Hz in the measurements; the clicks are broadband mechanical strokes with a dry, mid-focused body at 1-2 kHz.
differences.b: Adds a sustained 20-100 Hz rumble under every event (and a 323 Hz peak), giving a boomy, thumpy character not present in A's clicks.

differences.a: About 8 discrete events: a tick at 0 s, clicks at 0.19, 0.33 and 0.43 (the loudest early clack with a ringing tail), a tick at 0.66, a rattle cluster 0.84-1.15 with a strong transient near 0.95, and the final snap at 1.33.
differences.b: About 7 onsets. It lacks the 0-0.08 s tick, and the 0.43 s event is weak. The 0.9-1.1 s cluster is a noisy, granular hiss-like burst rather than discrete rattles or clicks, and the 0.31 and 0.65 events are thin.

differences.a: Metallic, clicky and clacky, with ringing tails on the sharper events, so it reads as a real mechanism and shells.
differences.b: Includes narrow tonal whistles (about 1 kHz, 2-3.5 kHz) at onsets, which read as synthetic beeps or pings. The final snap is a buzzy, pulsed noise burst (a double-lobed waveform) rather than one decisive latch slam.

differences.a: Final snap has a near-instant, dense broadband attack peaking around 1.38 s at -3.7 dBFS, then decays over about 0.15 s.
differences.b: Final snap peaks at 1.40 s at -4.9 dBFS with a lumpier amplitude shape and a lower-frequency (200-300 Hz) body. Early clicks have softer transients.

differences.a: Starts at about 0.01 s with a tick; first main click at 0.19 s; dead gap 1.17-1.33 s; snap at 1.33 s; 1.538 s total.
differences.b: Leading silence of 0.19 s with no initial tick; the gap and snap placement (1.15-1.35 s) match well; 1.54 s total.

differences.a: Clicks decay in tens of ms, with a ringing tail on the 0.43 s clack and a cut-off tail at the end.
differences.b: Decay to -20 dB in 0.03 s and to -40 dB in 0.1 s. The sub rumble lingers longer than the clicks, smearing the transients. The cluster around 0.85-1.1 s is more sustained than A's.

differences.a: -24.8 LUFS, peak -3.7 dBFS, RMS -26.6.
differences.b: -25.0 LUFS, peak -4.9 dBFS, RMS -28.6. The mid events are about 5-7 dB quieter than A's (for example 0.6 s and 0.9 s tenths).

differences.a: Almost entirely noise and transient content; no stable tones apart from faint high-frequency peaks.
differences.b: Noise plus several steady narrow tones and the sub rumble; spectral flatness 0.38 versus A's 0.003 (an unreliable metric, but consistent with the added tonal content).

missing_elements: Quiet tick at 0-0.08 s
Strong, sharp metallic clack with ringing tail at about 0.43-0.5 s
Discrete shell-insert rattles and clicks (with a transient near 0.95 s) in the 0.84-1.15 s cluster
Mid-high ringing metallic character on the clicks
extra_elements: Sub/bass rumble at 20-100 Hz under each event
Narrow tonal pings at about 1 kHz and 2-3.5 kHz at onsets
Granular noise burst replacing the rattle cluster
Pulsed or double-lobed buzzy body on the final snap
change_notes: Remove or high-pass the sub rumble: HPF at about 150 Hz (12 dB/oct) on all layers, or cut the 20-100 Hz thump by at least 20 dB. Keep only a small 80-120 Hz thump, 30 ms, at -12 dB under the final snap.

Rebuild the 0.84-1.15 s cluster as 4-6 discrete clicks and rattles, each a 3-10 ms noise burst bandpassed at 2-6 kHz plus a damped 1.5-3 kHz metal resonance (decay 40-80 ms). Add a stronger insert transient at 0.95 s, 6 dB above its neighbours. Replace the granular noise texture.

Strengthen the 0.43 s event into the clearest early clack: a 2 ms click plus a 2-4 kHz noise crack (15 ms) and a ringing resonance around 1.2 kHz (decay about 120 ms), peaking about -18 dBFS. Raise the 0.31 and 0.65 clicks by 4-6 dB to about -30 dBFS.
Add a very quiet tick (about -40 dBFS, 5 ms, 3-6 kHz noise) at 0.01-0.05 s.

Remake the final snap at 1.33 s as one decisive latch slam: a 1-2 ms click, then 1-8 kHz noise (60-100 ms, fast exponential decay) with a 1-2 kHz body, and a 100 ms tail with no amplitude pulsing. Peak at about -3.7 dBFS, and cut the buzzy modulation and the 200-300 Hz hump.

Cut or detune the steady narrow tones at 1 kHz, 2-3.5 kHz and above 10 kHz. If a ping is wanted, make it a short damped resonance (under 50 ms) with randomised frequency, at least 15 dB below the transient.

review.summary: B is the right kind of sound: a sub-heavy rocket launch blast with the same length, attack time and overall decay. It is darker and smoother than A, with less mid and high turbulence and no bright burst around 0.5 s. It is also mono and about 2 LU quieter.

differences.a: Noisy, turbulent mids and highs are strong in the first 0.6 s. The centroid jumps to about 3.3 kHz in the second quarter, with broadband energy up to about 10 kHz, so the blast crackles.
differences.b: The bright noise is concentrated in the first 0.3 s and then collapses. The centroid falls from 547 Hz to 224, 157 and 135 Hz by quarter, so the sound is dark and rumbly after the first moments.

differences.a: A brighter burst or debris crackle appears around 0.5-0.6 s (vertical streaks), along with a faint bump near 1.15 s. This gives a pulsing, evolving whoosh.
differences.b: No distinct secondary burst. The body decays smoothly, and a faint onset at 1.59 s is only a tail artifact.

differences.a: -20 dB at 0.71 s and -40 dB at 1.48 s. The tail is long and rumbly, with a slow drop from about 0.7 to 1.4 s.

Replace the flat 0.46 s hold with a continuous exponential decay: -10 dB at 0.1 s, -20 dB at 0.45 s, -40 dB at 0.9 s. Remove the gate and step at 0.46 s, and crossfade the tail from the body.
Cut sub energy: high-pass at about 40 Hz and lower the 20-100 Hz layer by roughly 10-12 dB so sub is about 10% and the centroid rises to about 1.4-1.5 kHz. Target presence+air at about 10%.

Rebuild the body as dense noise band-passed at 100-1500 Hz with fast random amplitude flutter (30-60 Hz), a low-pass that sweeps from 5 kHz at 0 s down to 800 Hz at 0.6 s, so the centroid falls from about 1.4 kHz to 550 Hz across the quarters.

Make the tail a short room-style reverb or filtered noise, 0.4-0.9 s, low-passed progressively from 2 kHz to 500 Hz, ending in a short fade near 0.95 s followed by 0.2 s of silence. Aim for about -12.6 LUFS and a peak of about -1 dBFS with a crest factor of about 15 dB.

review.summary: B is a very close match to A as a heavy, boomy, noisy pulse-rifle blast with the same length, loudness, band balance and long rumbling tail. The main differences are an earlier peak, a slightly shorter tail, and a more tonal, less dense noise texture.

differences.b: Peak lands at about 0.1 s and the level drops sooner, so the front reads as slightly snappier.

differences.b: Falls slightly slower to -20 dB (0.75 s) and -40 dB (1.57 s) but has a stepped, uneven profile (-27.8, -26.3, then -42.7 dB), and it cuts off abruptly near 2.5 s.

differences.a: Smooth, continuous reverb-like rumble with highs fading gradually into silence.
differences.b: Tail has some vertical banding and a dark gap in the highs around 1.7-1.9 s, with a hard stop near 2.5 s. This reads as slightly gated or artificial.

review.summary: B is the right kind of sound, a heavy revolver shot with a sub-heavy boom, a noisy crack and a dark tail. Length, loudness and band balance are very close to A. It differs in a few audible ways: a stronger low-end bloom, a dip at 0.4 s, and broadband tick or burst artifacts at 0.74 s and 0.85-0.95 s that stand out against A's smooth decay.

differences.a: Smooth, continuous dark reverb tail that darkens steadily. Only faint, quiet echo ticks around 0.64-0.87 s. Sub-bass rumble persists to about 1.2 s.
differences.b: Tail is mostly similar, but there are loud broadband vertical bursts at about 0.74 s and 0.85-0.95 s that reach up to 16 kHz. They read as distinct clicks or splashes, not subtle room reflections. Qwen also heard a 'splash'. The tail stops abruptly near 1.63 s.

differences.b: Reaches -20 dB at 0.35 s but -40 dB at 0.58 s. The envelope has a dip to -43 dB at 0.4 s followed by a rebound to -36 dB, so the decay is lumpier and the body drops faster than A.

differences.a: Peak at 0.11 s with a broadband noisy crack at the start. The first tenth is about -15 dB and the second about -12.5 dB. The crack is sustained and dense.
differences.b: Peak at 0.09 s with a similar noisy burst, but the first tenth is quieter (-17.9 dB), so the onset is a little softer. The peak is 1 dB hotter (-1.1 dBFS vs -2.1).

differences.b: Centroid about 629 Hz, rolloff 1.0 kHz. The upper-mid noise burst fades faster and the top end is slightly less bright. The sub bloom is a bit stronger and longer, at 0-0.3 s. Band percentages are within about 2 points of A.

differences.a: One shot plus faint echo flutter ticks, with no discrete splash-like events.
differences.b: One shot plus several discrete tick or burst events (onsets at 0.73, 0.87 and 1.07 s). The loud burst at 0.74 s and the wide burst at about 0.85-0.95 s add unwanted splashy elements.

review.summary: B is a close match for A in length, loudness, band balance and the heavy noisy-blast-with-rumble-tail character. It has a slightly slower, flatter body and a visible step at about 0.85 s, a gated-looking tail, and a stray late event near 2.0 s.

differences.a: Peaks at 0.14 s, then falls smoothly: -20 dB at 0.75 s, -40 dB at 1.56 s. No visible step in the spectrogram.
differences.b: Holds a flat, dense plateau to about 0.85 s, then drops abruptly (a visible step in both the waveform and the spectrogram) into a quieter tail. Overall -20 dB at 0.81 s and -40 dB at 1.62 s, but the shape is stepped rather than smooth.

differences.a: Continuous dark rumble tail that fades smoothly below 500 Hz, with a natural lowpass roll-off through about 2.5 s.
differences.b: Tail looks chopped or gated: vertical streaks and spikes in the highs at 1.6-2.4 s, then a hard cutoff near 2.5 s. A late onset is detected at 2.03 s, and the centroid rises to 878 Hz in the last quarter against 298 Hz in A.

review.summary: B is the right kind of sound: a heavy, boomy low-end gun blast of near-identical length and loudness. Its envelope is more stuttered, with a dip after the peak, and the sub energy drops out at about 1.1 s. The tail is also cleaner and lacks A's smooth rumble.

review.summary: B copies A's overall timeline (3.43 s, quiet handling, small clunk near 0.8 s, big slam at 1.8 s, long rattle after 2.3 s) and matches its loudness, but it sounds thin and synthetic. It lacks A's low-mid body and bass thump, and it replaces the heavy second bolt impact and ratchet tail with a soft tonal-sounding burst of ticks.

differences.a: Dense, full-range spectrum with strong energy in 40-1000 Hz in every event, so the hits feel heavy and metallic. The spectrogram shows warm red/orange across the low end, and the centroid rises from about 1.1 kHz to 7.6 kHz.
differences.b: Low end below about 500 Hz is almost empty (dark) except at the 1.8 s slam. Most energy sits at 1-8 kHz, with a flat centroid of about 5-6 kHz in every quarter. It sounds thin and hissy.

differences.a: The second big event at 2.3 s is the loudest and heaviest: a broadband impact with a bass thump (60-200 Hz) and bright metallic noise that rolls into a long ratcheting rattle.
differences.b: At 2.3 s there is no distinct heavy impact. The section is a mid-range cluster of soft ticks and swells (about 2.1-3.2 s) with no bass thump and no sharp slam onset.

differences.a: The 1.8 s and 2.3 s hits have sharp, noisy, broadband cracks with a decay of 0.15 s to -20 dB and 0.4 s to -40 dB.
differences.b: The 1.8 s slam is a rounded, sine-like swell with a soft attack. Decay is shorter and cleaner (0.12 s to -20 dB, 0.25 s to -40 dB). Small clicks elsewhere are quiet and gentle.

differences.a: Almost entirely noisy and metallic (flatness 0.004, a dense broadband texture).
differences.b: Noticeably tonal. There is a 300 Hz bump at the slam, fixed narrow tone lines near 1 kHz and 2 kHz, and three horizontal lines at about 10-14 kHz at 1.8 s. These read as synth pings or beeps rather than metal (Qwen heard clock ticks and a glass clink).

differences.a: Natural-sounding rustles and a ratcheting rattle with an irregular, organic rhythm.
differences.b: Regular, evenly spaced ticks (about 0.08 s intervals, 25 onsets) that sound mechanical and grid-like. The rattle sounds like pulsing amplitude-modulated bursts, not sliding or ratcheting metal.

differences.a: The last event rattles on and fades gradually until about 3.4 s, with continuous broadband air and noise.
differences.b: The tail is gated and drops out around 3.2 s, leaving obvious gaps between sparse events. Active fraction is 0.55 vs 0.74 for A, and the sound feels more fragmented.

differences.a: Total 3.43 s. Events at 0.09, 0.36, 0.76, 1.14/1.28, 1.8 and 2.3 s, with silent gaps at about 1.0 s and 2.25 s.
differences.b: Total 3.43 s. The main anchors line up (0.76, 1.14, 1.8). The 0.1-0.6 s handling section is a train of small ticks, and the structure after 2.3 s is different.

differences.a: -24.0 LUFS, peak -4.6 dBFS, RMS -27.5.
differences.b: -24.3 LUFS, peak -4.8 dBFS, RMS -28.5. This is essentially matched, but the energy is concentrated in the mid and high mids and is less weighty.

differences.b: Mono.

change_notes: Rebuild the 2.3 s event as a heavy bolt slam: a 15 ms broadband noise crack (1-8 kHz, +6 dB over the body), a 60-150 Hz thump pitched from 150 to 60 Hz over 120 ms, then a 0.4 s metallic body at 400-2000 Hz. Make it as loud as or louder than the 1.8 s hit (peak about -4.5 dBFS).

Replace the 1.8 s sine-like swell with a sharp slam. Use a 2 ms attack noise burst (2-6 kHz) over a 60-100 Hz thump with a fast pitch drop (110 to 55 Hz over 100 ms). Keep the 300 Hz body to under 20% of its level and give the layer a 0.15 s decay to -20 dB and about 0.4 s to -40 dB.

Fill in the low-mid range: add 200-900 Hz filtered noise or a damped resonant metal layer (Q about 3) under all clicks, handling rustles and the latch at 0.76 s, so the centroid starts near 1.1-1.4 kHz in the first half and rises to 6-7 kHz at the end.

Replace the regular tick train with 4-6 irregular ratchet clicks in 2.4-3.3 s, jittered by +/-30 ms and with random level varying by 6 dB. Add a continuous bright metallic noise bed (3-10 kHz, about -30 dB) decaying from 2.4 s to 3.4 s, and remove the gating at about 3.2 s.

Remove the fixed narrow tone lines at about 1 kHz, 2 kHz and 10-14 kHz. Use inharmonic, randomized metallic resonances with short 20-60 ms decays and rely more on noise (target spectral flatness well below 0.1).

Strengthen the 0.1-0.6 s handling rustle as soft cloth and metal noise, mostly 300-1000 Hz, at about -35 to -40 dB, with two light clicks at 0.09 s and 0.36 s. Add a sharper bright burst at 0.76 s (0.25 s long, 1-8 kHz) for the latch, and keep the 1.0 s and 2.25 s gaps near silent.
Keep the total length at 3.43 s, the integrated loudness at about -24 LUFS and the peak at -4 to -5 dBFS.

review.summary: B matches A's length, overall loudness and rough layout (two opening bursts, sparse ticks, gap near 2.5s, two closing clusters), but it sounds synthetic: noisy static-like bursts, tonal beep-like pings and one big thump at 0.92s instead of A's dense metallic clicks and two thumps.

differences.a: Two similar handling bursts (0-0.45s and 0.45-0.95s), each with a low thump, dense metallic clicks and a ratchet rattle. The loudest transient falls at 0.92s.
differences.b: One continuous noisy burst from 0 to 0.88s with no clear split into two gun actions. It ends in a single large low-mid boom with a downward sweep at 0.92s, around 200-300 Hz and below.

differences.a: Mostly clicky and noisy with a few narrow metallic ring lines at 8-10 kHz. The measured flatness of 0.009 is a measurement quirk.
differences.b: Hissy broadband noise wash plus sustained tonal pings at about 1-2 kHz and 9-10 kHz. These read as beeps (Qwen heard static and beeps). Flatness is 0.51.

differences.a: Real-feeling Foley with discrete, sharp, varied metallic clicks and a dry mechanical rattle.
differences.b: Synthetic, smeared noise grains with electronic-sounding sine pings. Less impactful and less like a revolver.

differences.a: Sparse ticks in the middle, with clear individual clicks that have small tails. Background stays at around -45 to -49 dB until the 0.7-0.8s tenth, then dips to -73 dB.
differences.b: The middle is much emptier. The active fraction is 0.54 against 0.85, and the envelope drops to -57, -71 and -74 dB from 0.5-0.7s. Decay to -40 dB takes 0.41s against A's 1.0s. Individual ticks are faint and the floor is very quiet.

differences.a: Centroid is 6.2 kHz, rolloff 10 kHz. Plenty of low-mid and bass energy in the thumps (0-0.2s and 0.5-0.6s) and broad energy through the low mids.
differences.b: Centroid is 7.1 kHz, rolloff 12.6 kHz. It is brighter and thinner below 500 Hz except for the one boom, and the 0-0.9s thumps are weak.

differences.a: Sharp, loud, repeated click transients. The closing clusters have crisp bursts of 4-6 clicks.
differences.b: Transients are softer and grainier. The closing clusters look like noise bursts with weak tonal blips, and the 3.1s cluster ends in a tonal ping.

differences.a: 3.51s with the quietest gap at 2.4-2.65s. Final clusters at about 2.7-2.9s and 3.1-3.3s.
differences.b: 3.51s with a similar gap at 2.4-2.6s and similar cluster placement. The onsets between 1.2 and 2.35s match A closely.

differences.b: Peak -5.1 dBFS, -24.9 LUFS, LRA 1.3. Loudness is well matched, but the single 0.92s boom stands out more.

differences.a: Dry, with short rattling tails and no reverb.
differences.b: Dry too, but it has a longer low-mid bloom after the 0.92s boom.

change_notes: Split the 0-0.92s burst into two similar-but-not-identical actions: gun 1 at 0-0.45s, gun 2 at 0.5-0.92s. Each gets a 60-120 Hz thump (40 ms decay) at its start, then 6-8 metallic clicks and a 0.15s ratchet rattle.

Reduce the 0.92s boom: cut it by about 10 dB, shorten the 200-300 Hz body to under 120 ms and remove the sweep tail. Make it a final click-plus-thump, like A's loudest transient, not a dominant drum hit.

Build clicks from 2-4 kHz bandpassed noise bursts of 3-8 ms with a sharp exponential decay, plus a short damped resonator at 3-6 kHz (Q around 8, decay under 30 ms). Don't use sustained sine partials.
Shorten or remove the tonal pings at 1-2 kHz and 9-10 kHz: limit decay to 40 ms and drop the level 10 dB. Stagger the frequencies per hit so they don't read as beeps.
Cut the broad hiss wash in 0-0.9s by about 6-8 dB and replace it with discrete clicks. Low-pass the noise at 10 kHz so the rolloff falls from 12.6 kHz to about 10 kHz.

review.summary: B is the right kind of sound (a boomy, noisy, roughly 1.1 s pistol shot) but its body is a flat sub-heavy slab with a slow ramp and a gap-and-rebound tail, so it lacks A's instant crack and smooth, bright-to-dark decay.

differences.a: Instant broadband crack at t=0 with peak at about 0.06 s. Highs up to about 10 kHz are strong in the first 0.2 s, giving a sharp punch.
differences.b: Starts after about 0.05 s of near-silence. The 0.17-0.19 s attack/peak time is measured, but the waveform and spectrogram show a hard step onset at 0.05 s followed by a flat plateau rather than a distinct crack, so it reads as a pad or burst rather than a snap.

differences.a: Centroid about 1270 Hz and rolloff85 about 2.3 kHz. Energy is spread: 10% sub, 24% bass, 32% low-mid, 24% mid, with 5.7% presence.
differences.b: Centroid about 757 Hz and rolloff85 about 1.2 kHz. 37% of energy is sub, with mid and presence reduced, so it is darker and more rumbly and less punchy.

differences.a: Body decays smoothly, -20 dB by 0.38 s and -40 dB by 0.89 s, with a continuous tail.
differences.b: Held, nearly constant sub plateau to about 0.35 s, then a sudden drop. The tail then rebounds at about 0.45 s (a second onset) and is cut off abruptly near 0.83 s in the lows. -20 dB is reached at 0.57 s and -40 dB at 0.74 s, so the decay shape is stepped and unnatural.

differences.a: Diffuse, reverberant noisy tail that darkens gradually, with highs dying first and low rumble lingering, fading out by about 0.95 s.
differences.b: Tail is a separate re-swell of mid noise with sub chopped off at about 0.83 s. It sounds like a second burst, not a room decay, and it has sporadic high-frequency blips at 0.7-1.0 s.

differences.a: 1.14 s, with a tail to about 0.95 s and 0.19 s of trailing silence. The sound starts immediately.
differences.b: 1.14 s, with a 0.02-0.05 s lead-in and 0.11 s trailing silence. Duration matches, but there is a small onset delay and a double-onset structure.

differences.a: -12.2 LUFS, peak -2 dBFS, crest 14.3 dB, so it is transient-driven.
differences.b: -14.5 LUFS by the measurement, though RMS is higher (-13.2 vs -16.3 dBFS) and crest is only 11.9 dB. The sound is sustained and flat rather than punchy, so perceived weight differs from A.

differences.a: Gritty broadband noise with no tonal lines, plus a boom.
differences.b: Noise with a tonal sub bed (flatness 0.048 vs 0.007). The sub pad reads as a sustained drone and the notes describe it as electronic and metallic.

differences.a: Stereo but narrow (correlation 0.93), with slight width in the tail.
differences.b: Mono, as required by the brief for positional sounds.

review.summary: B is a close match for A: a dense, bass-heavy noise blast of the same length, loudness and spectral balance, with a slightly sharper first transient, a bit more highs and a faster-drop tail. The remaining differences are minor.

differences.b: Peak at 0 s, with the first tenth at -5.9 dB, about 1.5 dB hotter and a bit more abrupt and crack-forward.

differences.a: Held around -7 to -11 dB until about 0.5 s, then falls smoothly to -18.6 dB at 0.6 s, -24.6 at 0.7 s and -35 at 0.9 s. -20 dB at 0.88 s, -40 dB at 1.15 s.
differences.b: Similar hold but with a slightly bumpier mid-section (-13.7 at 0.5 s, -16.1 at 0.6 s, then -26 at 0.7 s). -20 dB at 0.9 s, -40 dB at 1.2 s. The tail ends with a sharper cutoff at the end.

differences.b: Centroid 703 Hz, falling 1023 to 571 to 370 and then rising to 434 Hz in the last quarter. It has more broadband top end (energy to 20 kHz) and a brighter start. The band percentages are nearly identical.

differences.a: Granular, fluttering noise texture with smooth, dense low-end rumble.
differences.b: Amplitude modulation is a bit more pulsed or choppy in the waveform (0.2-0.6 s), with slightly more distinct low-frequency striations. It reads slightly more synthetic.

differences.a: Rumbling low-passed tail that darkens gradually, with 0.05 s of trailing silence.
differences.b: Tail is similar but a little brighter in the 0.8-1.2 s range, with 0.1 s of trailing silence.

differences.b: Peak -2.0 dBFS, RMS -11.8, -11.2 LUFS. Within about 0.7 dB.

review.summary: B is the right kind of sound (a short, bass-heavy suppressed rifle shot) with matching loudness and similar early decay, but it is a hard-cut 0.4 s event with a steady ~100 Hz tone and no tail, while A is a noisier, thumpier shot with a faint tail running to ~0.7 s.

differences.a: Faint dark tail of rumble and sparse noise decays gradually from 0.3 to ~0.7 s (-60 to -90 dB). The envelope shows -65 to -88 dB across 0.4-0.9 s.
differences.b: Hard cut to digital silence at ~0.38 s; the envelope is -200 dB from 0.4 s on. There is no tail, so the end sounds abrupt.

differences.b: A distinct sustained band at ~80-130 Hz lasts the whole 0.38 s with pulsing amplitude. It reads as a held sine or buzz, not a thump, and the waveform shows a regular beating pattern.

differences.a: Audible energy runs to ~0.7 s, with -40 dB at 0.33 s.
differences.b: Audible energy ends at ~0.38 s, with -40 dB at 0.28 s. It is about half as long and feels a bit clipped.

differences.a: Steep decay: -7.6 dB in the first tenth, then -18.5 and -34.8, then a long smooth fade. Low end decays with irregular, noisy modulation.
differences.b: The first tenth is slightly lower (-10 dB) with a similar slope to -20 dB at 0.16 s. After that it drops faster, and the low band is regularly pulsed.

differences.a: Noise-dominated (flatness 0.001) with a crackly mid and high layer, plus a bright burst up to ~10 kHz and above at the start.
differences.b: The noise burst is present but the tonal low band is more distinct (flatness 0.162). The highs are fewer, with rolloff at 5 kHz vs 6.3 kHz, and fade out by 0.35 s.

differences.a: Bass 56%, sub 7.6%, air 10.6%, centroid 2.06 kHz. Mid and high energy lingers into the tail.
differences.b: Bass 61%, sub 6.7%, air 9.2%, centroid 1.9 kHz. The balance is very close overall, but a bit less top end and a more concentrated bass.

differences.a: Peak at 0.01 s, a sharp broadband crack with a heavy thump.
differences.b: Instant peak at 0 s with a bright noise burst. Similar punch, but the peak is 1.7 dB lower (-2.0 vs -0.3 dBFS).

differences.a: -18.5 LUFS, peak -0.3 dBFS.
differences.b: -18.9 LUFS, peak -2.0 dBFS. This is well within tolerance.

review.summary: B matches A in length, loudness and sub-heavy character, but it is a pulsing, multi-burst rumble instead of A's single blast with a smooth sustained sub tail. It is the right kind of sound with a few moderate envelope and structure differences.

differences.a: One main hit with a second peak at 0.42 s. The level holds near -11 dB until about 0.6 s, then decays smoothly. Reaches -20 dB at about 1.4 s and -40 dB at about 1.63 s.
differences.b: The level is lumpy and peaks at about 0.35-0.5 s. It is already at -20 dB by about 0.95 s, but the tail then stays ragged and reaches -40 dB at about 1.65 s.

differences.a: Only two onsets (0.05 s and 0.42 s). A crisp crack is followed by a continuous, steady sub-bass body.
differences.b: Nine onsets from 0.1 s to 1.91 s, seen as repeated amplitude bursts throughout the sound. It reads like a stuttering or chattering rumble, not one blast.

differences.a: A smooth, sustained sub rumble below about 100 Hz holds from 0.6 s to about 1.9 s. Mids and highs die away by about 0.8 s.
differences.b: The tail is modulated and gated-sounding, with mid-band energy up to about 1-2 kHz persisting through 1.6 s. The centroid stays higher in the middle quarters (230 Hz, 113 Hz) than A's (75 Hz, 2 Hz).

differences.a: A sharp, bright broadband crack at 0.05 s, with energy up to about 10 kHz, then a heavier second hit at 0.42 s.
differences.b: The onset at 0.1 s is softer and swells more gradually, with less distinct crack definition. It builds to the peak at about 0.35 s.

differences.b: Sub-dominant (30.6% sub) with similar bass weight. The upper-mid noise is more evenly spread across the whole duration, and a high-frequency flicker is visible around 1.1-1.7 s.

differences.b: Similar noisy character, slightly more tonal or modulated (flatness 0.044).

differences.b: Peak -1.3 dBFS, RMS -12.9 dBFS, -17.9 LUFS. Essentially matched.

review.summary: B matches A's length, loudness and rough three-beat layout, but its final beat is almost missing, the middle burst is dominated by a loud low-frequency thump/noise burst, and the clicks are thinner and softer than A's dense metallic clacks.

differences.a: Three bursts of dense metallic clicks and rattles. The last burst is a bright two-part clack (about 1.78 s and 1.93 s) lasting about 0.3 s.
differences.b: The third beat is a single short, faint noisy blip at about 1.96 s, roughly 0.1 s long and far weaker. It reads as a tick, not a charging double-clack.

differences.a: The second burst (1.08-1.5 s) is a series of 5 sharp clicks of fairly even strength, with a slightly higher peak at 1.39 s.
differences.b: The second burst is mostly quiet clicks followed by one large, dense noise burst of about 0.12 s at 1.36 s. It has a strong 150-300 Hz body and sub energy, so it sounds like a thud or whoosh rather than a mag seat click.

differences.a: Almost nothing below 200 Hz in energy terms, with warm 1-2 kHz patches. Centroid is about 5.2 kHz.
differences.b: The 1.36 s event adds a bright, loud low-mid and bass bloom at 100-350 Hz that A lacks. Centroid is about 6 kHz and rolloff about 9.2 kHz, so it is brighter and hissier overall.

differences.a: Very noisy and metallic clacks with a rattly, complex texture; flatness measured 0.003.
differences.b: Flatness is 0.253, so it is more noise-like and diffuse. It has a few thin tonal chirps at about 1.1-2 kHz and 4.6 kHz that give a sci-fi ping, not a click.

differences.a: Active 67% of the time. Onsets at 0.33, 0.45, 0.56, 0.64, 0.72, 0.8 s and 1.08-1.46 s; gap at about 1.0-1.05 s; second gap at 1.55-1.8 s.
differences.b: Same total length and similar early onsets, but active only 41%. It lacks onsets at 0.33, 0.45, 0.56 and 1.46 s. The gap runs from about 0.9 s to 1.3 s, with the middle burst nearly empty before 1.3 s.

differences.a: Each click is a hard, near-instant transient with a short 0.04-0.16 s decay.
differences.b: The early clicks are softer and more diffuse, and the 0.6 s burst is washy. The peak decay is similar, but the transients are weaker relative to the noise bed.

differences.a: Peak -3.1 dBFS, -21.6 LUFS, evenly distributed over bursts.
differences.b: Peak -3.9 dBFS, -21.8 LUFS, but energy is concentrated in the single 1.36 s event, so the rest feels quieter than A.

differences.a: Tight, short tails.
differences.b: Dry with short tails, and trailing silence of 0.19 s vs 0.11 s. The 1.36 s burst has a slightly longer low-mid ring.

Rebuild the third beat as a two-part clack: bright noise bursts (1-8 kHz, 60-80 ms) at 1.78 s and 1.93 s, with a 0.1 s tail to about 2.1 s. Level should be within 3 dB of the 1.39 s peak, and the first clack should be the louder.

Cut the sparse tonal chirps by 6 dB, or replace them with brief inharmonic metal resonances (about 12 ms) so they read as metal hits, not sci-fi beeps.
Raise active time from 41% to about 65% by lengthening click bodies to 40-100 ms with quick decays, keeping peak at about -3 dBFS and loudness near -21.6 LUFS.

review.summary: B is the right kind of sound: a heavy low-end rocket launch blast with matching length, decay times, band balance and loudness. It is smoother and more purely sub-weighted than A, and it lacks the second debris accent and the crackly mid/high texture, so it reads cleaner and less violent.

differences.a: Has a distinct second onset at ~0.57 s (a bright debris/crackle stroke up to ~5 kHz). Faint sparse crackle accents continue in the tail.
differences.b: Single onset at 0.05 s. There is only a faint vertical streak near 0.6 s and some weak ticks around 1.6-1.8 s, so the blast reads as one clean event.

differences.a: Dense, gritty broadband noise with strong mid and high content in the first 0.7 s. Spectral flatness is ~0.001 and the centroid spikes to ~2.6 kHz in the second quarter. Reads as a violent, crackling blast.

differences.a: Peak at 0.02 s, with a crackly broadband transient and a sharp initial drop (-14 dB by 0.1-0.2 s).
differences.b: Attack of 0.04 s and peak at 0.05 s. The first 0.1 s is ~-50 dB, so there is a slightly later start, and the onset is a softer sub swell without a hard crack.

differences.a: -20 dB at 0.77 s, -40 dB at 1.6 s. The decay is lumpy, with a secondary bump near 0.57 s.

review.summary: B matches A's length (2.6 s), onset grid, peak time (~1.0 s), loudness and band balance, but it is a noisy, hissy, less defined sequence. Its clicks are soft and smeared, the two silent gaps are filled, and the main impacts lack A's sharp metallic snap.

differences.b: Events are softer and smeared, with swelling noise bursts (e.g. 0.1-0.3 s, 0.95 s, 2.1 s). Few events have a hard crack, and the waveform is mostly low-level clutter.

differences.a: Discrete, mostly dry clicks. Flatness is very low (0.002) because events are impulsive and the gaps are empty.
differences.b: Continuous noise bed with a hissy, distorted, static-like texture (flatness 0.38). It reads as electronic fuzz rather than handled metal.

differences.b: Overall length and onset times line up (0.46, 0.66, 1.10, 1.32, 1.52, 1.70, 2.07). But the gaps are filled with low-level noise and ticks, so the phrase separation is weaker. Some extra onsets at 1.83-1.99 s.

differences.a: Layered foley: mag slide, snap-in, rack, rattles, with a thump under the main impacts.
differences.b: Contains some tonal artefacts: a ~1.1 kHz ringing line with harmonics at ~1.5 s and ~1.75 s, and a 300 Hz tone at 1.0 s. These sound like electronic beeps rather than metal.

differences.a: Peak -2.5 dBFS, -20.7 LUFS.

review.summary: B is a close match for A: a 1.3 s bass-heavy shotgun blast with a long rumbling tail, nearly identical loudness, band balance, centroid and decay times. It differs mainly in a harder instant attack and a pulsing, amplitude-modulated body, plus brighter top-end content.

review.summary: B is the right kind of sound, a heavy low-frequency noise whoosh-swing of the same length and loudness as A. It has a weaker opening, a less fluttery body, a lower-pitched tail with a fixed bass step, and a shorter, cleaner end.

differences.a: Strong opening: -22.8 dB in the first tenth rising to -11.8 dB by 0.1-0.2 s. Gritty bursts at 0.05, 0.4 and 0.53 s, with a bright 10 kHz top.

review.summary: B is the right kind of sound: a long, loud, noisy tesla blast with a heavy low end and a sputtering tail, and its length, loudness and band balance are close to A. The tail is the weak spot. B has fewer, larger, clanky discrete pulses with silent gaps, where A has a continuous rumble with small crackles, and B's high end stays bright through the tail.

differences.a: The tail from 1.4 s to about 2.9 s is a continuous, smoothly decaying rumble with small, low-level crackle pulses. The centroid collapses to about 50 Hz by the last quarter.

The centroid stays at 4-6 kHz in the later quarters, so the tail remains bright and never settles into a low rumble.

differences.b: The -20 dB point is at 1.25 s and the -40 dB point at 1.88 s. There is a steeper drop near 0.3 s (-11 to -21 dB), then a stepped, bumpy tail with sudden cutoff-like gaps.

review.summary: B is the right kind of sound, a heavy low-end swing whoosh at nearly the same length and loudness as A. Its energy distribution differs: it swells in more slowly, holds a loud body longer, and has a mid-bass hump at 0.55-0.7 s and a fuller tail where A fades away.

differences.b: Starts much quieter, at about -41 dB in the first tenth, then swells to a distinct bright burst at about 0.1 s. This reads as a whoosh swell with a clean initial hit rather than A's chaotic grit.

differences.a: Steady loud body at -16 to -17 dB until about 0.5 s, then a step down of about 9 dB and a gradual fade. Reaches -20 dB at 0.94 s and -40 dB at 1.15 s.

differences.a: Gritty broadband burst, then a pulsing rumble with onsets near 0.55 s and 0.68 s, then a fading sub tail. The sub is continuous and low.
differences.b: A distinct 100-250 Hz tonal or band-limited thump block appears at 0.55-0.7 s, visible as a bright patch in the spectrogram. It is more a hit than a pulse. It reads as a 'bang' after the whoosh, and Qwen heard whoosh plus bang.

differences.a: Mostly noise and distortion in the opening, with a pulsing low rumble later. Gritty, mechanical character.
differences.b: Noise plus a more tonal low-mid thump. Qwen called it metallic and electronic. It is cleaner and less distorted than A's crackle.

review.summary: B matches A's length, peak timing (~1.0 s clunk) and overall loudness, but the spectrogram shows a different structure. B is a regular series of discrete clicks with pitched whistle tones, while A is a continuous low rumble with one big clunk and a final thump section.

differences.a: Continuous rustle and handling bed with sub/low bumps (20-150 Hz) from 0 to 1.5 s, one big broadband clunk at 1.03 s, a quiet middle, and rumbly low thumps at 2.7-3.5 s.
differences.b: Isolated, evenly spaced click/knock events (each with a ~300 Hz pitched drop) and a clunk at ~1.0 s. There is little continuous bed, and the end is a handful of thin ticks.

differences.a: Noisy and atmospheric, with no stable tonal lines apart from codec artifacts at 16 kHz (flatness 0.001).
differences.b: Visible stable horizontal tonal lines at ~1.1 kHz, 2.3 kHz, 3.4 kHz and 4.6 kHz (ringing/whistle partials) that Qwen heard as a sustained high-pitched note. They sound like synth beeps and feel eerie rather than like foley.

differences.a: Strong sustained sub/low energy (20-150 Hz) during 0-1.4 s and 2.7-3.5 s, giving weight and rumble.
differences.b: Low end is mostly short ~250-350 Hz knock thumps with decaying pitch, plus a sub burst only at the main clunk. Little sustained rumble in the first and last sections.

differences.a: Clunk decays to -40 dB in ~0.47 s, with a slower tail and a deep dropout at 1.5-1.65 s. Activity is 73% of the file.
differences.b: Clunk decays to -40 dB in ~0.28 s and the sound is much sparser (active fraction 0.33). Events are shorter and drier, the end is nearly empty, and the tail trails off in silence (0.14 s trailing silence).

differences.a: 3.53 s with the peak at 1.03 s. The final thump section runs 2.7-3.5 s and the gap sits at 1.5-1.65 s.
differences.b: 3.53 s with the peak at 0.97 s. The gap is not clearly defined, and the click grid is dense and regular (0.05-0.9 s) rather than rustly. The final section has weak thumps.

differences.a: Soft, diffuse transients that blend into a rustle. The main clunk is broadband and noisy.
differences.b: Sharper, more distinct vertical clicks with obvious pitched knocks. The main clunk has a similar broadband burst with sub energy.

review.summary: B is the right kind of sound: a 3.44 s tesla blast with the same low-end weight, loudness and length as A. It differs in tail and texture: A's highs fall away fast into a dull rumble, while B keeps bright, gated crackle through the tail and ends with a distinct thump near 1.9 s.

differences.a: After about 1 s the highs drop away and the tail becomes a dull, smooth low rumble (centroid about 490 Hz, then about 190 Hz) that fades gradually to about 3.2 s.
differences.b: The tail keeps bright 2-10 kHz content (centroid about 3.8-5 kHz in quarters 2-3) and has a sharp low-end cutoff near 1.5 s. It sounds more like a lit-up sizzle than a rumble.

differences.a: Brightness is front-loaded: centroid is 2.7 kHz in the first quarter and collapses to about 190-490 Hz afterwards. It reads as a bright burst, then a dark rumble.
differences.b: Centroid is only 1.8 kHz in the first quarter and rises to 3.8-5 kHz in the middle, the opposite contour. The opening is less sizzly and the middle is too bright.

differences.a: Dense, continuous broadband noise with a few curved zap streaks at 2-5 kHz early on and a slightly stuttering low rumble. Very noisy, with no obvious gating.
differences.b: Visible vertical gaps and dark stripes from about 0.8 s to 2.4 s suggest a gated, pulsed or stuttering crackle. Spectral flatness is 0.192 against A's 0.001, so B is more tonal or clean and less smooth.

review.summary: B matches A's length, loudness and overall click-sequence structure, but the finale is wrong: A ends with a flurry of sharp clicks and a noisy tail after a silent gap, while B puts a single big low-end thump with a tonal bloom at 2.33 s. B also loses the heavy opening, the real silent gap near 2.2 s, and the broadband bright click character, and adds tonal pings and pitched low sweeps.

differences.a: Final element (2.33-2.72 s) is a rapid flurry of sharp bright clicks (2.33, 2.41, 2.49 s) with a noisy decaying tail; energy is mid/high, with little bass.
differences.b: Final element is a single large thump/bloom at ~2.33 s with strong 20-120 Hz energy and a 200-400 Hz body, then a quick fade. It reads as one heavy slam, not a click flurry.

differences.a: Opening 0-0.35 s is a loud cluster of low thuds and metal clacks, the heaviest bass of the first half, with a clear ring. Peak is near -19 dB in the first tenth.

differences.a: Sub/bass energy is ~0.4% overall but concentrated in the opening thuds. Centroid is 6.2 kHz and varies by section (8.8k, 3.7k, 3.8k, 7.2k).
differences.b: Centroid is 7.3 kHz and flat across the clip (~7.1-7.8 kHz). The spectrogram shows low-frequency energy mostly at the end plus pitched 150-400 Hz swoops mid-clip. Bright and uniform, without A's darker, mid-heavy middle.

differences.a: Noisy broadband clicks with natural metallic ringing; spectral flatness is 0.009 in this measurement.
differences.b: Spectral flatness is 0.567, so it is much noisier and more diffuse. There are also artificial narrow tonal lines at ~1.1 kHz, 3 kHz and 4.5 kHz, plus pitched sweeps at ~200-300 Hz. These read as synthetic beeps/pings, not foley.

differences.a: A true silent gap at ~2.2-2.3 s, with near-zero energy, then the closing flurry. Distinct strong clicks at 0.91, 1.03-1.17, 1.38 and 1.73-1.84 s, with the loudest middle hit around 1.8 s.

differences.a: Middle sections sit around -40 to -60 dB per tenth. The final tenth is -41.5 dB after a -18.4 peak, so the closing burst is brief with a tail.

Add a 0.3 s band-passed noise tail (1-8 kHz) fading about 25 dB.

Rebuild the opening 0-0.35 s as a heavy clunk: a 60-120 Hz sine thud with a 15-25 ms decay at 0.0 s and 0.10-0.19 s, plus metallic clacks (2-5 kHz noise bursts of 10 ms) at 0.08 and 0.19 s. Raise the first-tenth level by about 4 dB, to roughly -19 dB.

review.summary: B is broadly the right kind of heavy low-end ground slam, with matching length, loudness, band balance and body/decay shape. It has a slower attack, a more tonal sustained sub body, a hum-like secondary tail and a stray click near 1.0 s, so it needs some tweaks.

differences.b: The first tenth sits at about -49 dB and the peak lands at 0.16 s (attack 0.15 s), so the slam swells in instead of hitting. Early peaks are tall, but there is no crisp initial crack at t=0.

review.summary: B is very close to A in role, length, loudness and spectral weight: a sub-heavy noisy rocket launch with a long dark tail. The main differences are B's flatter early envelope with a late 0.84 s secondary burst, its hotter peak, its mono image and its less bright, less crackly mid-highs after the first 0.5 s.

differences.a: Smooth, continuous decay: -13.5 dB at 0.1 s, -21 dB at 0.2 s, then falling steadily to about -45 dB by 0.7 s. No visible step.
differences.b: Sustained plateau of full-band energy to about 0.6 s, then an abrupt drop of roughly 10-15 dB at about 0.63 s. A second onset follows at 0.84 s, so it reads as a two-stage blast with a seam.

differences.a: Peak at 0.14 s with a punchy burst, about 10 dB above the next tenth-second (-13.5 vs -21 dB). Little initial snap.
differences.b: Peak at 0.17 s, starting from -32 dB in the first tenth, then a swelling burst. The onset is softer or delayed at the very front and the body is more even, with less punch relative to the sustained level.

differences.a: Highs and mids stay present and crackly through roughly 1.2 s. Centroid by quarter is 521, 2180, 1111 and 298 Hz, so the brightness peaks in the second quarter and fades slowly.
differences.b: Brightness is concentrated in the first 0.5 s and then drops sharply. Centroid by quarter is 485, 240, 213 and 307 Hz, so the body and tail are very dark and lack the mid flutter and crackle of A.

review.summary: B is very close to A in role, length, loudness and spectral balance: a heavy, boomy, noisy shotgun blast with a long rumble tail. It differs in a harder instant attack, a brighter and wider high-frequency wash, a slightly longer tail, and a late centroid rise in the final quarter.

differences.a: Sustained, dense body with no clear transient; the measured peak at 0.22 s and the -7.6 dB first tenth suggest a soft or blended onset, with the crack only in the first ~50 ms.
differences.b: Peak at 0.0 s with the loudest first tenth (-5.0 dB), so there is a more distinct initial punch and slight front-loading.

differences.b: Similar noise texture, with slightly more tonal or structured low-mid energy (flatness 0.043) and visible striations around 1-5 kHz.

review.summary: B is the right kind of sound, a bass-heavy noisy blast of the same length (1.59 s vs 1.59 s) with matching loudness and spectral balance. Its swell is about 0.28 s slower, its decay is faster and it has a second burst near 1.09 s that A lacks, so the timing and envelope feel differs.

differences.a: Swells to the peak by about 0.21 s, with the first tenth-second at -15 dB, so the onset is already strong and blurred by sub and bass.
differences.b: Starts much quieter (-20.9 dB in the first tenth) and builds to the peak at 0.49 s, so the blast hits later and feels softer at the start.

differences.a: Peak at 0.2-0.4 s, drops about 8 dB, then sustains a flutter to 0.9 s. It reaches -20 dB at 1.15 s and -40 dB at 1.35 s, then ends in a smooth fade.

differences.a: One continuous rumble with a faint bump near 0.79 s.
differences.b: Two distinct secondary bursts at 0.86 s and 1.09 s, visible in the waveform as a second noise block after a dip near 0.55 s. It reads like a re-trigger or a stuttered tail.

differences.b: Sub 19%, bass 52%, low-mid 13%. Centroid falls 475 to 145 Hz, with a 85% rolloff near 345 Hz. Slightly brighter and boxier early, a little less bass weight.

differences.a: Speckled noise up to about 10 kHz in the first half, fading to nothing, with the top end rolled off by about 10 kHz.
differences.b: Broadband noise reaches the top of the spectrum (up to 20 kHz) and is sustained longer, with vertical streaks around 1.0-1.2 s. Sounds airier and more hissy.

differences.a: Smooth, dry, low-frequency fade with no reverb.

differences.a: Peak -2.1 dBFS, RMS -12.0 dBFS, -13.5 LUFS.

review.summary: B matches A's length, loudness and the main clack timing near 1.8 s, but it lacks A's dominant low-frequency hum/swell from 2.3-3.4 s and replaces A's rustling handling with sparse, thin clicks. The result is a bright, noisy clack-only reload that ends abruptly instead of finishing on a charging rumble.

review.summary: B is very close to A in role, length, loudness, band balance and decay slope: a heavy broadband noise-burst shot with sub/bass body and a rumbling tail. review.summary: B is the right kind of sound, a heavy low-end revolver boom with a noisy body, and its loudness and spectral balance are close to A. Its attack is softer, its tail is shorter and cuts off abruptly, and the low end is more pulsing.

differences.a: Near-instant 10 ms attack with a sharp broadband crack reaching the peak immediately, then a fast drop.

review.summary: B has the same overall length, loudness and sub-heavy rumble, but it is built as a sequence of separate hits and swells with a clear 2 s cutoff. A is one big blast at the start with a smoothly decaying, crackling tail, so B changes the role and feel.

differences.a: Instant blast with peak at about 0.1 s. A broadband noise crack reaches the top of the spectrum and sits on a heavy sub thump.
differences.b: Starts near silence (-50 dB in the first tenth). Measured attack is 0.62 s with the peak at 0.63 s, so the loudest moment comes later. The first hit is softer and lacks a clear crack, and a later swell is the loudest part.

differences.a: Smooth, continuous decay: -20 dB at 0.82 s, -40 dB at 1.85 s. The body holds with churning bursts to about 0.85 s, then thins gradually.
differences.b: Uneven envelope with discrete bursts and swells at about 0.05, 0.23-0.42, 0.83-0.91, 1.19, 1.47-1.69 s. Level dips and rebounds between them. The decay to -20 dB is measured at 0.14 s, then it falls to -40 dB at 1.32 s, which is faster overall. It reads as a multi-shot or stuttering sequence, not one explosion.

differences.a: One blast plus a rolling, crackling rumble and faint debris ticks in the tail.
differences.b: Several distinct events: repeated bursts, a rounded low swell near 0.9-1.0 s, and a sharp hit near 1.45 s. Qwen heard gunshots and a thud, which fits the discrete hits. The sound has no single hero blast.

differences.a: Long, gradual low-frequency tail with scattered crackle that fades into silence from about 2.4 s.
differences.b: Hard cutoff at about 2.0 s, followed by a quiet, patchy low residue with isolated blips up to 2.9 s. It does not read as a natural tail.

differences.a: Centroid 776 Hz. The first 0.8 s is broadband to above 10 kHz and falls to under 100 Hz in the tail. Sub is 35%, bass 12%, presence/air 7%.
differences.b: Centroid 553 Hz, with 85% rolloff at 234 Hz versus 1219 Hz in A. Sub is similar at 34%, but bass is lower (7.6% vs 12.1%) and highs are weaker. Brightness is uneven: the centroid jumps to about 4.3 kHz in the third quarter.

differences.a: Dense, gritty noise in the body, flatness near 0.
differences.b: Similar noisy character but with more pulsing, tonal-looking low swells (flatness 0.07). The grit is cleaner and less churning.

differences.a: Peak -0.6 dBFS, -20.1 LUFS, RMS -19.3 dB.
differences.b: Peak -1.2 dBFS, -20.6 LUFS, RMS -18.5 dB. Loudness is well matched.

differences.a: 3.19 s with active content to about 2.4 s and 0.81 s trailing silence.
differences.b: 3.19 s with 0.9 s trailing silence and active content to about 2.0 s. Overall length matches.

differences.a: Mono.
differences.b: Mono.

missing_elements: Immediate full-level blast at t=0 with a punchy broadband noise crack
Continuous churning rumble body from 0.1 to 0.85 s
Smooth, long low-frequency decay tail to about 2.4 s with sparse crackle
Bass-band weight in the 60-250 Hz range
extra_elements: Repeated discrete bursts at about 0.23-0.42, 0.83-0.91, 1.19 and 1.47-1.69 s that read as extra gunshots
Rounded low swell near 0.9-1.0 s and a sharp hit near 1.45 s, which sound like a thud or jump
Hard cutoff at about 2.0 s followed by isolated residue blips to 2.9 s
change_notes: Move the loudest event to the start. Make a 60-100 ms noise crack (1-10 kHz, a 2 ms attack, exponential decay of about 40 ms) at 0 s, peaking at -1 dBFS. Delete or drop by 10 dB or more the later hits at 0.83, 1.19 and 1.47-1.69 s.
Put a sub thump at 0 s: sine, 130 Hz sweeping down to 45 Hz over 200 ms, plus a 40-60 Hz body held at full level to 0.3 s. Decay to -20 dB at about 0.8 s and to -40 dB at about 1.85 s.

Replace the discrete bursts with a continuous rumble layer: low-passed noise (cutoff 1.5 kHz falling to 150 Hz over 2 s) with 30-60 ms random amplitude flutter at about -6 dB depth. Place the flutter peaks at 0.34, 0.57, 0.71 and 0.85 s, with each one smaller than the last.

Add bass-band weight: boost 80-250 Hz by about +4 dB, or add a band-passed noise body at 100-250 Hz from 0.1 to 1.0 s. This raises bass from 7.6% to about 12% and the 85% rolloff from 234 Hz toward about 1 kHz.

Extend and smooth the tail: apply a gentle exponential fade on the low rumble from 0.85 s to 2.4 s, with a few quiet 2-5 ms ticks (-45 dB, 500 Hz-3 kHz) scattered through it. Remove the hard cutoff at 2.0 s and the isolated blips after it.
Keep loudness near -20 LUFS with a peak of -1 dBFS, which is already matched. Keep it mono.

review.summary: B is the right kind of sound: a heavy, boomy mono impact of nearly identical length (1.14 s vs 1.141 s), loudness (-17.5 vs -17.2 LUFS) and band balance. Differences in attack, tail rumble, secondary-bump timing and a bell-like ring are small enough to tweak rather than rework.

differences.a: Instant hit, peak at 0.04 s, with a crunchy broadband burst reaching a few kHz. The envelope starts at about -13.8 dB and rises slightly to -11.3 dB in the second tenth.
differences.b: Peak at 0.08 s, with the loudest energy in the first 0.1 s (-8.7 dB) and a more sustained, longer-lasting low-end plateau. The initial punch is less snappy and the top is a bit louder.

differences.a: Secondary bump or rattle onset at 0.32 s, small and riding on the decaying body, like debris.
differences.b: Detected onset at 0.75 s, with a distinct low-frequency bloom around 80-150 Hz at about 0.8 s. The envelope shows a -28.8 dB bump at the 0.7 s tenth versus -46.6 dB around it, so it is much more prominent and later than A's. It reads as a delayed thump or ring rather than a rattle.

differences.a: Gritty, crunchy, noisy broadband texture with metallic debris, lower tonality (flatness 0.008), and a churning pulsing low end.
differences.b: Smoother and more tonal/resonant (flatness 0.055). Qwen hears a bell-like ring, with a more electronic/mechanical feel and less crunch.

differences.a: Centroid about 802 Hz, with grit up to about 8 kHz in the first quarter. Centroid rises to 2.3 kHz in the third quarter from mid-frequency rattle, and the highs darken quickly.
differences.b: Centroid about 768 Hz with similar band percentages. Brightness is concentrated in the first 0.3 s (up to about 5-10 kHz), then falls steadily with no mid rattle (469 Hz in the third quarter), so the middle is duller.

differences.a: -20 dB at 0.35 s and -40 dB at 0.66 s, with a fairly steady fade of the rumble to about 0.9 s.
differences.b: -20 dB at 0.30 s and -40 dB at 0.60 s, so slightly faster. The tail drops to silence abruptly at about 1.03 s (-200 dB in the last tenth), versus A's smooth fade.

differences.a: 1.141 s total, with 0.28 s trailing silence.
differences.b: 1.14 s total, with 0.27 s trailing silence.

differences.a: Peak -1.8 dBFS, RMS -17.0, -17.2 LUFS.
differences.b: Peak -1.2 dBFS, RMS -16.8, -17.5 LUFS. Within tolerance.

differences.a: Dry, short rumble tail with no obvious reverb.
differences.b: Slightly more resonant, ringing tail, with a bell-like echo suggested by Qwen and the low bloom at 0.8 s.

missing_elements: Crunchy debris/metallic rattle in the 0.1-0.5 s body with mid-frequency grit (centroid rising to about 2 kHz)
Snappy instant transient peaking at 0.04 s
Small secondary rattle bump at about 0.32 s
extra_elements: Pronounced low-frequency bloom or ring at about 0.7-0.85 s (80-150 Hz)
Bell-like or tonal resonance suggested by Qwen
