change_notes: Move the secondary event: remove or drop by 20 dB the bloom at 0.75 s, and add a short rattle/debris burst (band-passed noise 800-3000 Hz, 60-80 ms, about -20 dB relative to peak) at 0.32 s.

Sharpen the attack: add a 1-4 kHz noise crack of 10-15 ms at 0 s, +4 dB over the body, and shorten the sub/bass rise so the peak lands at about 0.04 s instead of 0.08 s. Reduce the first 0.1 s plateau by about 2-3 dB so that early energy is closer to A (-13 dB).

Increase noise grit: raise the noise-to-tone ratio of the body by roughly 6 dB, with crushed or bit-reduced noise at 200-2000 Hz amplitude-modulated at 20-30 Hz for the churn. This should lower tonality (flatness toward 0.01-0.02).
Remove any ringing or bell-like tonal partials (resonant peaks above 500 Hz) and any resonant low sine sustain; keep the sub as a pitch-dropped sine 80 -> 45 Hz over 150 ms, decaying by 0.3 s.

Lengthen the decay slightly: use a rumble tail with a smooth exponential fade to -40 dB at about 0.66 s and -60 dB at about 0.9 s, with a 100 ms fade-out so it ends at about 0.9-1.0 s, not an abrupt cut.
Keep the 1.14 s length, mono output, peak at or below -1.5 dBFS and -17.2 LUFS.

review.summary: B is the right kind of sound: a boomy thump with a noisy crack, matching A's length, peak time, decay times and loudness. Its main shortfalls are a hard cut to digital silence at about 0.96 s instead of A's long quiet tail, a hotter and more continuous low end, and no tonal ring.

differences.a: Decays into a very quiet reverb-like tail that reaches about -76 dB at 0.8-0.9 s, with a faint 700 Hz tone lingering to about 1.5 s, then fades to near silence.
differences.b: Energy ends abruptly at about 0.96 s with a hard cut. The envelope reads -200 dB from 0.6 s onward, and the spectrogram shows a clean vertical edge at 0.96 s with no tail or room.

differences.a: Smooth fall: -10, -16, -25, -31, -32, -45, -49, -53, -76 dB per tenth, with -20 dB at 0.37 s and -40 dB at 0.71 s.
differences.b: -20 dB at 0.36 s and -40 dB at 0.69 s, nearly identical. It holds a plateau of about -28 dB through 0.4-0.5 s, then drops. It stays dense and sustained until about 0.7 s, then falls off a cliff.

differences.a: Has a faint metallic tonal line near 1.6 kHz up to about 0.4 s and a weak 700 Hz tone late. Also has a few lower-frequency bursts around 0.6-0.7 s.
differences.b: No distinct tonal ring. The body is a noisy, dense mush with pulse-like vertical striations through the body, with no metallic hammer ring.

differences.a: Boomy, with irregular, organic low-frequency pulsing that is uneven and has lumpy modulation.
differences.b: Regular, comb-like vertical striping in the low end, suggesting a periodic amplitude modulation or buzz. Flatness is 0.086 against A's 0.014, so it is noisier and less tonal.

differences.a: Sub 12%, bass 46%, low-mid 19%. Centroid is 939 Hz, and brightness sweeps up per quarter (970 to 4557 Hz) as the low end dies and noise dominates the tail.
differences.b: Sub 16%, bass 43%, low-mid 22%, so slightly more sub and low-mid. Centroid is 1027 Hz, with a non-monotonic quarter profile (1235, 921, 772, 1511) and a bright, noisy top end during the first 0.1 s.

differences.a: Near-instant attack peaking at 0.02 s with a loud broadband crack over a sub thump.
differences.b: Same 0.02 s peak, with a similarly sharp attack. It is about 4 dB hotter in the first tenth (-6.4 vs -10.4 dB).

differences.a: Peak -1.8 dBFS, RMS -18.7, -17.2 LUFS.
differences.b: Peak -1.1 dBFS, RMS -18.5, -17.6 LUFS. This is within tolerance, but the energy is more front-loaded in the body.

differences.a: File is 1.65 s, with about 0.74 s of near-silent tail.
differences.b: File is 1.65 s with about 0.77 s of digital silence, so audible content ends sooner. The active fraction is the same, about 0.4.

missing_elements: Quiet reverb-like tail between about 0.75 s and 1.5 s
Metallic tonal ring near 1.6 kHz in the first 0.4 s
Weak 700-800 Hz tone in the late tail
Irregular low-frequency bursts around 0.6-0.7 s
extra_elements: Regular comb-like low-frequency pulsing or buzz through the body
Slightly stronger sub and low-mid weight
Hard cut to digital silence at about 0.96 s
change_notes: Add a dark reverb or noise tail: 0.7-1.5 s, low-passed at about 800 Hz, starting near -60 dB and fading to -90 dB. Replace the hard cut at 0.96 s with a 150-300 ms exponential fade-out so there is no vertical edge.

Add a metallic ring: a sine or narrow-band resonance at about 1.6 kHz, 0.02-0.4 s, decaying about -30 dB, at about -35 dB below the body peak. Optionally add a faint 700 Hz tone at -75 dB from 0.8 to 1.5 s.

Reduce the regular low-frequency amplitude modulation or buzz. Either randomize the pulse rate (jitter of +/-30%) or lower the modulation depth to under 3 dB so the body is lumpy and organic, not combed.

Lower the sub layer (about 50-100 Hz) by about 2-3 dB and trim the body (200-500 Hz) by about 2 dB to bring sub to about 12% and low-mid to about 19%. Reduce the 0-0.1 s peak by about 3 dB so the first tenth sits near -10 dB.
Shape the body so the plateau at 0.4-0.5 s is lower (about -32 dB at 0.4 s, -45 dB by 0.5 s), then add 1-2 small low-frequency bursts (60-120 Hz, 40 ms) near 0.6 and 0.7 s at about -50 dB.
Let the high-frequency noise decay more steadily so the centroid rises over time, like A's 970 Hz rising to 4.5 kHz in the tail, rather than staying bright only in the first 0.1 s.

review.summary: B is the right kind of sound: a short, punchy suppressed rifle shot with a similar attack, loudness, bass-heavy balance and 0.14 s decay to -20 dB. It cuts off to digital silence at about 0.4 s and so lacks A's quiet low-level tail, and it has a slightly different low-end structure.

differences.a: Quiet rumbling tail with faint room-like noise lasting to about 0.75 s; envelope -59 to -88 dB across 0.4-0.9 s with low-frequency residue, no abrupt end.
differences.b: Tail ends abruptly at about 0.4 s; envelope drops to digital silence (-200 dB) from 0.4 s on. The spectrogram shows a hard cutoff, so the sound ends too early and unnaturally.

differences.a: Audible content about 0.75 s, with decay to -40 dB at 0.33 s and a trailing silence of 0.72 s.
differences.b: Audible content only about 0.4 s, with decay to -40 dB at 0.29 s and a trailing silence of 0.77 s. The shot feels shorter and drier.

differences.a: Smooth, continuous decay: -7, -18, -34, -43, -59 dB per tenth, then a slow fade to the end.
differences.b: Similar initial decay (-9, -20, -37), but it falls to -53 at 0.3 s and then vanishes. The decay is slightly steeper and lacks the long low-level shoulder.

differences.a: Dense bass and sub up to about 200 Hz that sustains for roughly 0.3 s, with bright broadband noise to above 10 kHz in the first 0.15 s. Centroid 1981 Hz.
differences.b: Bass is similar (48% vs 51%) and the centroid is close (2082 Hz). The low end is slightly more band-limited and drops sharply after 0.18 s, with the later centroid falling to about 238 Hz and then 10 Hz, so there is little mid/high content in the late body.

differences.a: Noisy, broadband texture with very little tonal content; flatness near 0.
differences.b: Mostly noise-like in the spectrogram, but the measured flatness of 0.2 and an onset at 0.21 s suggest a tonal or bumpy low-frequency component and a secondary event. Qwen heard a tinny 'ding', which is unreliable but hints at some ringing.

differences.a: Peak at 0.02 s, a muffled crack plus heavy thump, and no secondary onsets.
differences.b: Peak at 0.01 s, a slightly faster and brighter-sounding attack, and a detected onset at 0.21 s, probably a low-frequency modulation or bump in the body.

differences.a: Peak -1.1 dBFS, -18.6 LUFS, RMS -20.3.
differences.b: Peak -2.4 dBFS, -19.1 LUFS, RMS -23.2. Slightly quieter, but within tolerance.

missing_elements: Quiet low-frequency rumble tail and faint room-like noise from 0.4 to about 0.75 s
Smooth natural fade-out instead of a hard cutoff
Sustained low-level mid/high noise residue in the late body
extra_elements: Hard digital cutoff at about 0.4 s
Possible secondary bump at about 0.21 s in the low-frequency body
change_notes: Extend the tail: add a low-passed noise/rumble layer (cutoff about 300-800 Hz) starting at 0.1 s, at -45 dB falling to -80 dB, lasting to about 0.75 s, with an exponential fade (time constant about 0.2 s) so it never cuts off.
Remove the abrupt end: apply a 100-150 ms fade-out to every layer and make sure no layer is gated at 0.4 s.
Lengthen the body: slow the sub/bass thump decay so it holds about -45 dB at 0.3 s (A: -43 dB) instead of -53 dB; use a 60-150 Hz pitch-dropped sine with a decay of about 200 ms.
Add a faint muffled 1-4 kHz noise puff, 100-300 ms long, at -50 to -60 dB, for the late-body mid content, and a soft, short reverb (RT60 about 0.3 s, 10% wet) to supply a room-like tail.
Check the 0.21 s bump: smooth any amplitude modulation or tonal ringing in the low layer so the decay is monotonic and noise-like.
Raise the overall gain by about 1.3 dB so the peak is about -1.1 dBFS and loudness is about -18.6 LUFS.

review.summary: B is the right kind of sound: a sub-heavy ground-impact rumble of nearly the same length, loudness and spectral balance as A. Its envelope falls away earlier and more steeply, it has a stronger mid/high crunch up front, and its onset pattern is a bit different, so the body feels shorter and less sustained.

differences.a: Dense churning rumble holds near full level to about 0.7 s. It reaches -20 dB at 0.86 s and -40 dB at 1.21 s, so the body is sustained.
differences.b: Level drops sharply after about 0.5 s (envelope -33.9 dB at the 0.5 tenth). It reaches -20 dB at 0.53 s and -40 dB at 0.97 s, so the body is roughly 0.3 s shorter and the fall is more abrupt.

differences.a: Peak at 0.15 s. The initial 0.2 s is a bright crunchy burst over a low thump, and the level stays high afterwards.
differences.b: Measured peak at 0.32 s, with the loudest content early and a spiky waveform in the first 0.3 s. The transient is more broadband and hissy (mid/high noise up to 10 kHz in the first 0.5 s), so it reads as a brighter, longer crack than A's.

differences.a: Rough amplitude flutter of rolling debris at 20-250 Hz, with very low spectral flatness (0.005) and a dense, continuous rumble.
differences.b: Rumble is more broken up, with a visible mid-frequency noisy haze (flatness 0.029). Hiss-like mid/high noise is audible during the body, and the rumble is less cohesive.

differences.a: Weaker pulses at 0.93, 1.03 and 1.2 s are dark and low in level, and the sound fades smoothly into a sub-bass tail to about 1.43 s.
differences.b: Broadband vertical bursts at about 0.86, 1.03 and 1.2 s extend up to the top of the spectrum. They look like clicks or debris hits and stand out from the dark decay. The tail then cuts off more abruptly, with trailing silence of 0.39 s versus A's 0.29 s.

differences.a: Sub 35%, bass 48%, centroid 344 Hz. After the strike, energy settles to a centroid of about 90 Hz.
differences.b: Sub 36%, bass 41%, centroid 342 Hz, but the centroid stays higher through the body (489, 273, 169 Hz by quarter vs A's 371, 97, 84). The low-mid and mid content is greater and decays more slowly than A's.

differences.a: Peak -1.9 dBFS, RMS -15.5, -17.0 LUFS.
differences.b: Peak -1.3 dBFS, RMS -15.8, -17.3 LUFS. Matches within tolerance.

differences.a: 1.72 s, active fraction 0.71.
differences.b: 1.72 s, active fraction 0.65, so the sound is slightly shorter in perceived duration.

differences.a: Mono.
differences.b: Mono.

missing_elements: Sustained churning sub rumble holding strength through about 0.7-0.85 s
Smooth dark sub-bass decay tail through about 1.4 s
extra_elements: Hissy mid/high noise haze across the body
Broadband click-like bursts at 0.86, 1.03 and 1.2 s extending to the top of the spectrum
Slightly higher DC offset (0.009)
change_notes: Extend the sub/bass rumble body: hold the 20-250 Hz layer near full level until about 0.8 s, then decay to -20 dB by about 0.85 s and -40 dB by about 1.2 s (A's values), instead of falling at 0.5 s.

Shorten and darken the strike crack: use a 2-6 kHz noise burst of about 100-150 ms that decays quickly, with a lowpass at about 5 kHz after 0.2 s, and move the peak to about 0.15 s with a fast 5-10 ms attack.

Reduce the mid/high haze during 0.2-0.9 s by about 10 dB (lowpass the debris noise at about 800 Hz), and add 15-25 Hz amplitude flutter to the 20-250 Hz rumble to bring flatness down toward about 0.005.
Lowpass the late pulses at 0.86/1.03/1.2 s at about 400 Hz and drop them to roughly -45 to -55 dB so they sound like weak dark thuds, not broadband clicks.
Lengthen the dark sub-bass fade-out to about 1.4 s with a smooth exponential curve, and reduce trailing silence from 0.39 s to about 0.29 s.
Remove the DC offset with a high-pass at 15-20 Hz, and keep peak at about -1.5 dBFS and loudness at -17 LUFS.

review.summary: B is the right kind of sound (heavy, boomy, noisy pulse-rifle blast with sub thump and rumbling tail) with matching length, loudness and band balance, but its envelope is stepped rather than smoothly decaying: a full-level body that cuts abruptly at about 0.8 s, then a second rumble bump.

differences.a: Smooth continuous decay: slight dip after ~0.2 s, -20 dB at 0.62 s, -40 dB at 1.47 s, fading into a gradual rumble.
differences.b: Body holds high level to ~0.8 s then drops almost vertically by ~25-30 dB, followed by a separate quieter rumble bump around 1.0-1.6 s and a second drop near 1.65 s. It sounds like three blocks rather than one decaying blast.

differences.a: Dark, smooth low rumble tail with gradual HF roll-off, highs fading over ~1.5 s, no gating.
differences.b: Tail is patchy: vertical striations in the highs between 0.85 and 1.8 s suggest gated or stuttering noise, and the lows have a distinct secondary swell. The tail ends abruptly at ~2.5 s.

differences.a: Near-instant onset with dense broadband burst; the first ~0.2 s is sustained at a high level and the peak is at 0.22 s.
differences.b: Also instant, but the peak is at 0.29 s and the body stays flat and loud longer with some spiky peaks. It is slightly less punchy and more sustained, with no distinct crack.

differences.a: Centroid ~985 Hz, rolloff 1.57 kHz, sub 17.5%, bass 45%, with more mid/high energy in the first 0.5 s.
differences.b: Centroid ~903 Hz, rolloff 1.16 kHz, sub 19.7%, bass 40.8%. Slightly darker and more sub-heavy, with less upper-mid energy in the decay.

differences.a: Noise-like wash with a fluttery low-end texture, spectral flatness ~0.01.
differences.b: Noise-dominated with a more gritty, buzzy texture and higher flatness (0.095); Qwen hears it as metallic/electronic and white-noisy.

differences.a: -11.2 LUFS, peak -1.9 dBFS, RMS -16.3.
differences.b: -12.8 LUFS, peak -1.5 dBFS, RMS -15.1. About 1.6 LU quieter in integrated terms, within tolerance.

differences.a: Dual-mono stereo file (correlation 1.0).
differences.b: True mono file. Equivalent in practice and consistent with the positional-sound requirement.

differences.a: 2.75 s with 0.66 s trailing silence; audible to ~2.1 s.
differences.b: 2.75 s with 0.57 s trailing silence; audible to ~2.5 s.

missing_elements: Smooth, continuous exponential decay of the body into the tail
Gradual progressive high-frequency roll-off through the tail
Fluttery, natural low-end rumble texture
extra_elements: Abrupt cut at ~0.8 s ending the main body
Secondary rumble swell at ~1.0-1.6 s
Gated or striated high-frequency noise bursts at 0.85-1.8 s

change_notes: Replace the hard cut at 0.8 s with one continuous decay: apply a single exponential envelope on the noise body reaching -8 dB at 0.3 s, -20 dB at 0.6 s and -40 dB at 1.45 s, with no gate or step.
Remove or fold in the secondary rumble swell at 1.0-1.6 s: crossfade the sub/bass layer smoothly, with a decaying level of about -25 dB at 1.0 s and -40 dB at 1.5 s.
Make the tail HF noise continuous rather than gated: sweep a lowpass from ~8 kHz at 0.3 s down to ~1.5 kHz at 1.0 s and ~400 Hz at 1.8 s, and remove any amplitude modulation or stutter above 2 kHz.
Shorten the full-level plateau: peak at 0.2 s (attack ~5 ms, then hold 0.15 s) and reach -7 dB by 0.3 s instead of holding to 0.8 s.
Add a 2-4 kHz noise crack of 15-20 ms at t=0, about +4 dB over the body, for punch and a little more upper-mid energy in the first 0.5 s.
Lift the bass/low-mid slightly: reduce the sub (40-60 Hz) by ~1.5 dB and raise 100-300 Hz by ~2 dB so bass is ~45% and the centroid is near 1 kHz.
Fade the tail to silence by ~2.1 s with a smooth 0.3 s fade rather than an abrupt end near 2.5 s, and raise the overall level ~1.5 dB to land near -11.5 LUFS.

review.summary: B follows the two-part layout and total length (2.35 s) of A, but the loud second half is a sparse, pulsing set of impacts that dies at about 2.1 s instead of a continuous, dense, held surge to 2.2 s. The first half is also much more clicky and tonal than A's rattly handling.

differences.a: Second half is a continuous, dense electrical or motor surge from 1.2 s to 2.2 s, held at -14 to -22 dB per tenth, with strong 100-300 Hz body and a crackling top.
differences.b: Second half is a series of discrete bursts and thumps (onsets at 1.41, 1.63, 1.8, 1.96, 2.05 s) with gaps between them, so it reads as banging or clanking rather than a charge-up. There is one big spike at about 1.63 s.

differences.a: Surge starts abruptly at 1.2 s, swells to about 1.4 s, holds loud to about 2.1 s, then fades over about 0.15 s. Active fraction is 0.84.
differences.b: Energy is uneven and spiky, ending with a hard final hit at about 2.05 s and then a cutoff, with 0.21 s of trailing silence. Active fraction is 0.67 and the decay is much shorter (-20 dB in 0.3 s vs 0.8 s). There is no sustained swell and no taper.

differences.a: Very noisy and buzzy, with a dense broadband texture (flatness about 0.004 in the measurement) and no clear tonal lines.
differences.b: Has isolated tonal pings (about 1 kHz at 0.07 s and 0.45 s, about 1.5 kHz at 1.1 s, about 1 kHz at 2.1 s) over a more impulsive, sparse texture. It sounds more like beeps and chirps, which Qwen also noted.

differences.a: First half (0-0.6 s) is quiet, continuous mechanical rattle and scrape with a latch clunk at 0.66 s. Its level is about 10 dB below the surge.
differences.b: First half is 16 onsets total, mostly distinct clicks and thumps at 0.05, 0.16, 0.24, 0.37, 0.45, 0.59 and 0.67 s, each with a 200 Hz thump and a tonal ping. It is louder and more staccato, with no continuous rattle bed. Tenths at -14 to -20 dB are only about 6 dB below the surge.

differences.a: Gap at about 0.75-1.05 s, small clicks at 1.08 and 1.22 s, then the surge from 1.22 s.
differences.b: Gap at about 0.8-1.05 s and clicks at 1.06-1.27 s are similar, but the main body only really builds from 1.4 s. It is largely finished by about 2.1 s, so there is a late start and early end.

differences.a: Centroid about 3.5 kHz, with 31% bass and 8% sub energy. The surge is a broad low mass at 100-300 Hz plus a bright noisy top to above 10 kHz.
differences.b: Heavier bass and sub (42.5% and 10.2%) with weaker highs (rolloff 7.8 kHz vs 9.0 kHz). The upper noise is patchy and only present in bursts from about 1.4 s.

differences.a: Peak -2.5 dBFS, -17.1 LUFS, crest 16.9 dB.
differences.b: Peak -1.3 dBFS, -17.6 LUFS, crest 19.3 dB. Integrated loudness is matched, but the higher crest factor from the single spike makes it feel more transient and less sustained.

differences.a: Mono.
differences.b: Mono.

change_notes: Replace the second-half bursts with one continuous surge from 1.2 s to 2.1 s: 100-300 Hz saw or pulse hum with 60-120 Hz AM at about 40-60 Hz, plus dense 1-10 kHz noise with crackle. Level it steadily at about -14 to -18 dB per tenth with no gaps longer than 20 ms.

review.summary: B is a pistol-shot-like sound with matching total length and a similar -20/-40 dB decay time, but it is a blocky, sustained, sub-heavy slab with a hard cutoff at ~0.47 s, a delayed start, and a second low-frequency block, rather than A's instant crack and smoothly decaying reverberant boom.

differences.a: Instant onset at 0 s with a sharp broadband crack that peaks at 0.07 s, bright to 10 kHz+.
differences.b: Starts after ~0.05 s of near-silence (-45 dB in the first tenth), then a gated, flat-topped onset with no distinct crack. Peak at 0.09 s.

differences.a: Smooth, continuous exponential-like decay: -10.6 dB at 0.1 s, -20 dB by 0.39 s, -40 dB by 0.88 s.
differences.b: Block-shaped: holds nearly flat from 0.05 to 0.2 s, steps down at ~0.47 s by ~15-20 dB, then a second hump around 0.5-0.8 s before cutting off at ~0.85 s. The -20/-40 dB times match only by coincidence.

differences.a: Natural reverberant tail from 0.4 to 0.95 s that darkens gradually, with highs rolling off and a modulated low-mid wash.
differences.b: The tail looks like a quieter repeat of the body, with the 20-120 Hz band holding flat until a hard stop at ~0.85 s and sparse mid fragments. This sounds like a gated, stuttering second event rather than room decay.

differences.a: Centroid ~1.3 kHz; sub 12%, bass 18%, low-mid 32%, mid 25%. Low-mid body with a broadband crack.
differences.b: Centroid ~1.0 kHz; sub 29.5%, bass 22%, low-mid 24.5%, mid 18%. Rolloff 1.8 kHz vs 2.3 kHz. Over twice the sub energy, which makes it a boomy rumble, and the tail centroid collapses to ~270-330 Hz.

differences.a: Dense broadband noise burst with a low thump; flatness 0.014.
differences.b: Flatness 0.068 and a flat, static sub band at 20-120 Hz that reads as a held tonal or drone layer under the noise. It has no pitch drop.

differences.a: Punchy, crisp, gunshot-like, with a natural reverberant fade.
differences.b: Heavy, buzzy and sustained, like a synthetic burst or rumble. Has a mechanical gated quality, and the two-block structure suggests a double event.

differences.a: -13.3 LUFS, RMS -16.5, peak -2.3 dBFS, crest 14.2 dB.
differences.b: -15.5 LUFS, RMS -14.9 dBFS, peak -1.6 dBFS, crest 13.2 dB. The integrated figure is lower by 2.2 LU but the RMS is higher. The body is sustained, so it feels heavier but less snappy.

differences.a: 1.14 s total, with 0.19 s trailing silence and an immediate start.
differences.b: 1.14 s total with 0.11 s trailing silence. The ~50 ms leading gap delays the hit and the sound effectively ends at ~0.85-0.95 s.

review.summary: B is the right kind of sound: a heavy, bass-dominant rumbling slam with a similar length, sustain, drop-off and loudness. Its attack is slower and its debris texture is brighter and flatter. It also lacks A's secondary bursts and has a shorter, cleaner tail.

differences.a: Sharp broadband crack in the first 0.1 s, peaking at 0.07 s at -1.9 dBFS, with a clear initial hit.
differences.b: Peak at 0.13 s, and the first tenth is slightly louder (-7.5 dB vs -11.4 dB). The hit is a bit more sustained and less crack-defined, but still immediate.

differences.a: Two discrete secondary bursts at about 0.67 s and 0.78 s (onset detection), plus pulsing granular fluctuations that read as debris falling.
differences.b: No detected onsets. The sustain is a more uniform noisy wash, with a faint broadband burst near 0.8 s at the end of the body.

differences.a: Crunchy, granular, gritty low-mid debris crackle, mostly in the first 0.3 s.
differences.b: Denser, more continuous noise with brighter content in the highs (up to 10 kHz+) during the body. Flatness is higher (0.035 vs 0.006), so it sounds slightly hissier and less like pure rumble.

differences.a: Centroid 405 Hz, rolloff 203 Hz, with the middle of the sound at about 83-118 Hz. The top end falls off steeply after 0.9 s.
differences.b: Centroid 446 Hz, rolloff 215 Hz, so it is very close overall. The first quarter is brighter (589 Hz vs 446 Hz), and sub/bass shares match well (36.8% and 49.6% vs 33.3% and 50.4%).

differences.a: Level holds at -10 to -19 dB until about 0.8 s, then falls to -20 dB at 0.77 s and -40 dB at 1.01 s.
differences.b: Nearly the same shape, but a bit faster: -20 dB at 0.68 s, -40 dB at 0.94 s, and a sharper cutoff at about 0.8 s and 1.05 s.

differences.a: Rumble murmur fades gradually through about 1.25 s, ending in 0.3 s of silence.
differences.b: Abrupt drop after 1.05 s, then a very faint low-frequency hum at about -85 dB, and 0.48 s of trailing silence. The tail is shorter and less natural.

differences.a: -16.9 LUFS, peak -1.9 dBFS, RMS -15.4 dB.
differences.b: -17.1 LUFS, peak -1.3 dBFS, RMS -15.9 dB. Practically equal.

review.summary: B has the same length and a similar impact onset near 0.26 s, but it sounds like a sustained noisy whoosh/hiss bed with a soft attack and no sharp clank. A has a hard, clipped metallic crunch that drops about 20 dB in 0.35 s, then a quiet rumble and small clunks, while B stays loud and bright for the whole length.

differences.a: Abrupt, clipped broadband crunch at 0.26 s (peak +3.7 dBFS) with a sharp metallic clank and a vertical onset edge.
differences.b: Soft ramp-up starting around 0.2 s. Peak is -1.1 dBFS, with no clipped samples and no sharp clank, so it feels like a swell rather than a stamp.

differences.a: Drops about 20 dB within 0.35 s of the impact, then holds a low bed of about -20 to -25 dB, with a final fade after 1.8 s.
differences.b: Stays at about -15 to -23 dB with only a small dip after the hit, and -20 dB isn't reached until 1.48 s. It reads as a plateau rather than impact then decay.

differences.a: Has a clank/impact, a rumble bed, rattles, and discrete clunks at 1.49, 1.71, 1.84 and 1.93 s (one clunk is prominent near 1.5 s).
differences.b: Has one continuous noise bed plus a static 323 Hz tonal band in the first 0.3 s. There are no discrete clunks in the tail, and the single detected onset is at 0.21 s.

differences.a: Bass-heavy and sustained: sub+bass is 25%, the centroid falls from 1.9 kHz to 575, 499 and 73 Hz across the quarters, and there is little above 8 kHz.

differences.a: Gritty noise with faint resonant metallic bands near 1 and 2 kHz, plus bright ringing after the hit.

differences.a: Quiet rumble from 0 to 0.25 s, impact at 0.26 s, fade complete near 2.03 s.
differences.b: Near-silent lead-in (about -40 dB) until 0.2 s, then sound until about 1.95 s. Total length matches (2.06 s).

differences.b: -14.4 LUFS, crest 15.3 dB. Peak is lower and the bed is louder relative to the hit, so the dynamics are flatter.

differences.a: Tail is a dying rumble with small clunks, reaching -40 dB at about 1.66 s.
differences.b: Tail is sustained noise that cuts off quickly after 1.8 s (-40 dB at 1.7 s) with no clunks.

review.summary: B is the right kind of sound (a long noise-and-sub explosion of the same 6.8 s length), but it sustains a flat, bright body for about 2.5 s and then breaks into rhythmic, gated burst pulses. A is a hard blast that falls fast into a dark, low rumble. The tail character and tonal balance are clearly off.

differences.a: Loud from 0 s, falls about 10 dB per tenth. Reaches -20 dB at about 1.1 s and -40 dB at about 3.6 s. It is front-loaded and decays steadily.
differences.b: Held plateau at -5 to -9 dB for about 0.5 of the file (about 3.4 s). Envelope drops only in the second half, with a bump back up at tenth 9. Reads as a sustained roar, not a decaying blast.

differences.a: Crackling debris tail of small irregular onsets (about 0.1-0.3 s apart) that blends into the continuous rumble and darkens steadily.
differences.b: Tail is made of distinct gated bursts, like a stuttering or machine-gun pattern, with silent gaps between them in the waveform. Qwen heard it as 'clicking' and 'static', which fits.

differences.a: Dark. Centroid 755 Hz overall, falling to 57 Hz by the last quarter. About 60% of energy is in sub and bass. Rolloff85 is 1.1 kHz.
differences.b: Much brighter. Centroid 1490 Hz overall and rising to about 4 kHz in the later quarters, so the tail gets brighter instead of darker. Rolloff85 is 3.1 kHz. Presence and air are about 12.5% versus 5.5% in A.

differences.a: Instant blast with a broadband burst and sub impact, then a small dip before the body swells. Hits hard from the first sample.
differences.b: Starts at about -9 dB with no distinct crack or impact. Peak is measured at 2.79 s, so there is no defined blast moment.

differences.a: Long dark low-frequency rumble tail to about 5.8 s. It stays low-end heavy and fades smoothly, with the last 0.95 s near silent.
differences.b: Tail has no low-end rumble sustain. It is bursts, then a brief noisy hiss at 5.3-6.2 s with an abrupt cut. Trailing silence is 0.59 s.

differences.a: -4.7 LUFS, heavily clipped (+9.6 dBTP), loudness range 23.4 LU, so the dynamics are strong.
differences.b: -8.9 LUFS, peak -1.3 dB, loudness range 5.1 LU. It is cleaner and safer, but flatter in dynamics, so it feels less explosive.

differences.a: Noisy but low-flatness because of the strong sub. Saturated, with a boom body.
differences.b: Flatness 0.178 against 0.033, so it is noisier and less boom-centric.

differences.a: 6.79 s with 0.95 s trailing silence. Onsets are densest at 2.1-5.2 s.
differences.b: 6.79 s with 0.59 s trailing silence. Onsets are only from 3.4 s onward, so the debris phase starts about 1.3 s later than A.

change_notes: Rebuild the envelope. Put the peak at 0-0.1 s, then use an exponential decay so the level is -20 dB at about 1.1 s and -40 dB at about 3.6 s. Remove the 3 s plateau.
Add a blast layer. Use broadband noise with a 5 ms attack and a lowpass sweep from 12 kHz to 500 Hz over 1.2 s. Add a 2-4 kHz noise crack, 20 ms, at 0 s, +6 dB over the body.
Add a sub boom. Use a sine sweeping from 80 Hz down to 35 Hz over 400 ms, with an exponential decay of about 1.5 s and soft saturation. Target sub plus bass at about 55-60% of energy.

Make the tail darker with time. Sweep the lowpass from about 3 kHz at 2 s down to 200 Hz at 5.5 s so the centroid goes from about 300 Hz to under 100 Hz. Cut the 4 kHz brightness in the later quarters.

Replace the gated pulses with irregular crackle. Use 5-20 ms noise grains at random 80-300 ms spacing between 2.1 and 5.2 s, with random amplitudes (-12 to -30 dB) and a decay that falls with time. Mask them under a continuous low rumble (brown noise lowpassed at 150-250 Hz) so there are no silent gaps.
Add a continuous rumble bed (30-120 Hz) fading from -20 dB at 2 s to -45 dB at 5.8 s, ending in about 0.9 s of near-silent tail. Remove the hiss patch at 5.3-6.2 s and fade out smoothly.
Raise the loudness. Add soft-clip saturation before a limiter at -1 dBFS and aim for about -6 to -5 LUFS with a loudness range above 15 LU. Keep peaks at or below -1 dBFS.

review.summary: B is a close match for A's role: a 4 s low rumble loop at nearly the same loudness, band balance and swell-to-1.5 s shape. It differs in having a visible vertical-striped crackle/click layer up to 15+ kHz and slightly softer, longer fades.

differences.a: Smooth grainy low rumble. Highs above 2 kHz are negligible and appear only as faint wisps, with no distinct clicks.
differences.b: Dense, regular vertical striping across the spectrogram from about 1 kHz to 15+ kHz, which is a train of broadband clicks or crackles (about 10-15 per second) over the rumble. Qwen heard it as crackling flame and rain.

differences.a: Dry, mechanical, granular machine hum with a flickering mid-frequency flutter.
differences.b: Reads as a fire or rain crackle on top of the rumble, so it feels more like a flame than a heating machine.

differences.a: Centroid 151 Hz, rolloff 172 Hz. Faint reddish mid wisps to about 2 kHz and almost nothing above.
differences.b: Centroid 176 Hz, rolloff 194 Hz, and drifting from 207 Hz down to 155 Hz across the quarters. Band percentages are nearly identical, but the click layer adds high-frequency content that A lacks, and it also has a stronger 1-3 kHz patch around 1.3-1.6 s.

differences.a: The rumble is at full level within about 0.1 s and stays active for 98% of the file, with a very short fade at the end.
differences.b: Quieter at the start (-23 dB in the first tenth) and fades in and out over about 0.25 s each side. Active fraction is 91%, with leading silence 0.08 s and trailing 0.06 s.

differences.a: Gentle swell to a peak at 1.55 s (about -13 dB), then sits at -15 to -18 dB and tapers. Small bumps at 2.44-2.93 s.
differences.b: Peak at 1.47 s, so timing is well matched, but the swell is more pronounced, with a loud burst around 1.4-1.6 s, and the level is more uneven (-12.0 at 0.6 s against -18.9 at 0.8 s). Onsets are spread evenly rather than clustered after 2.4 s.

differences.a: -17.2 LUFS, peak -2.3 dBFS, RMS -15.2.
differences.b: -17.4 LUFS, peak -1.5 dBFS, RMS -15.5. Well within tolerance, and a slightly higher crest factor of 14 dB.

differences.a: Fades to silence at both ends, which leaves an audible seam.
differences.b: The same fade-in and fade-out structure, but with longer silent edges, so the seam is slightly more noticeable.

Replace the clicks with a faint 500-2000 Hz band-passed noise flutter at about -35 to -40 dB relative to the rumble, amplitude-modulated at 20-40 Hz, to match A's mechanical, grainy texture.

Add 3-4 small level bumps of about +2 dB at 2.44, 2.62, 2.77 and 2.93 s (30-50 ms) in the second half. Smooth out the 0.6-0.8 s level dip, which is currently about 7 dB.

review.summary: B has the right length, brightness and a rough rasp-then-clicks layout, but its energy collapses after 0.4 s and its sub-bass thump and isolated tonal blips make it read as a different sound from A's dense chittering screech.

differences.a: Dense rasp holds loud through about 0.3 s, falls 20 dB by 0.29 s and 40 dB by 0.64 s, with clicks riding on a continuous decay.
differences.b: Loud only to about 0.4 s, then drops to -40 and -58 dB in the 0.4-0.6 s tenths. Reaches -20 dB by 0.09 s and -40 dB by 0.25 s, so the decay is much faster and gappy.

differences.a: Continuous noisy rasp followed by a train of clicks with 500-1000 Hz wet bodies, a strong accent click near 0.58 s and a small formant-like burst at 0.67-0.76 s.
differences.b: Rasp for 0.0-0.25 s, then sparse isolated blips with long silent gaps. The listening notes call them beeps, so they likely have a tonal or electronic character, and the 0.5-0.6 s dead zone breaks the chitter continuity.

differences.a: Essentially no energy below 200 Hz. Mids hold a wet 450-1000 Hz body and the top is a 15-17 kHz sizzle.
differences.b: Strong sub and bass thumps at 20-150 Hz during 0-0.2 s. They are absent in A and add a bass pulse that makes it sound heavy rather than insectoid. The 450-1000 Hz body is weak.

differences.a: Dense speckled noise with a wet organic crackle.
differences.b: Spectral flatness 0.67 and Qwen hears beeps and static, so it is cleaner and more synthetic, with narrow tonal blips instead of noise clicks.

differences.a: 0.82 s, active fraction 0.84, onsets near 0.33, 0.41, 0.55 and 0.64 s, ending in a late burst.
differences.b: 0.82 s, but active fraction only 0.58 and a 0.08 s tail of silence. Onsets at 0.2, 0.29, 0.41, 0.49, 0.62 and 0.72 s are more regular and evenly spaced.

differences.a: Sharp click at 0 s, with the peak near 0.13 s inside a dense rasp.
differences.b: Starts softer at -22 dB and builds to a peak near 0.13 s with a thumpy low-frequency pulse. Each later blip has a clean click-and-decay shape.

differences.a: -17.1 LUFS, peak +0.7 dBFS, slight clipping.
differences.b: -19.2 LUFS, peak -1.5 dBFS. About 2 LU quieter, within tolerance, and the peak is cleaner.

differences.a: Dry, with a small late burst and a short near-silent end.
differences.b: Short ringing decays on each blip, which is slightly reverberant, and no late burst in the same role.

change_notes: Remove everything below 150 Hz: high-pass at 180 Hz, 24 dB/oct, to delete the 0-0.2 s sub thumps.

Rebuild the opening rasp as bandpassed noise at 2-12 kHz with amplitude modulation at 60-120 Hz for a chitter texture. Start at full level with a 1-2 ms click, hold near peak to 0.2 s, then decay to -20 dB by 0.3 s.

Fill the 0.3-0.65 s region with 5-6 noise-burst clicks, each 15-40 ms with a 3 ms attack and 25 ms decay. Use noise with a 500-1000 Hz bandpass body plus a 4-8 kHz layer, at -20 to -28 dB re peak, never dropping below -45 dB between them, so the tail is continuous (-40 dB at about 0.6 s).
Replace tonal beeps with noise clicks: set flatness near 0.01-0.05 by using no sine oscillators, and use band-limited noise with Q below 3.
Add a stronger accent click at 0.58 s: 30 ms, 400-900 Hz body plus noise crack, about +6 dB over neighbouring clicks.
Add a small late burst at 0.67-0.76 s: 80 ms of noise with formant-like bandpasses at 500 Hz and 6-10 kHz, about -25 dB re peak, then fade to silence by 0.80 s.
Add a faint 14-17 kHz noise sizzle (-35 dB) under the first 0.3 s.
Raise overall level about 2 dB to reach -17 LUFS, keeping the peak at -1 dBFS.

review.summary: B is the right kind of sound, a short noisy 4-8 kHz chitter with a main burst near 0.2 s, but it is built from discrete gated bursts with silent gaps instead of A's continuous rattling swell. It also has an unrelated sub-bass thump, and its tail is a sparse series of ticks.

differences.a: Continuous rough rattle from 0 to 0.3 s that swells smoothly to the peak at 0.18-0.25 s, with only -14 to -11 dB between tenths.
differences.b: Separate gated bursts: a hit at 0.07 s, a dip, then two blocks at 0.18-0.27 s, with deep gaps between them (-22 to -34 dB tenths). It feels stuttery, not like a swell.

differences.a: Little bass energy (0.0% sub and bass). Low content is only a faint smear, and the clicks have a thumpy body around 1-3 kHz.
differences.b: Strong sub-bass blocks at 20-100 Hz under the 0.07 s hit and the 0.18-0.25 s bursts. This adds a boomy weight the original lacks, while the 1-3 kHz click body is weak.

differences.a: Two or three sharp clicks/pops at 0.32-0.40 s with 1-3 kHz energy (about 1 kHz peak), loud enough to read as clear events.
differences.b: Clicks at 0.32-0.5 s are narrow, quiet ticks of mostly high-frequency energy. There is no mid-range pop, and the 0.3-0.4 s section is far weaker than A's.

differences.a: Decays gradually: -40 dB reached around 0.34 s, then a faint hissy residual to about 0.57 s.
differences.b: Cuts hard after 0.27 s (-40 dB at about 0.09 s), then sparse isolated ticks through 0.7 s with silence between them. This reads as detached clicks, not a fading rattle.

differences.a: Dense, granular noise (flatness 0.148) with clustered texture and a 12 kHz peak, which sounds like organic chittering.
differences.b: Noisier and more broadband (flatness 0.277) with more distinct bursts and no 12 kHz peak. The texture is cleaner and more synthetic, less organic.

differences.a: There is no clean attack. The onsets at 0.05, 0.17 and 0.32 s emerge from the rattle.
differences.b: A sharp, isolated hit at 0.07 s with a prominent low-frequency thump, plus hard-edged burst starts at 0.18 s, so it is more percussive.

differences.a: -13.5 LUFS, peak -0.4 dBFS, RMS -18.8 dB.
differences.b: -15.9 LUFS, peak -2.1 dBFS, RMS -20.9 dB. About 2.4 LU quieter, partly because of the longer gaps.

differences.a: 0.8 s with 0.23 s trailing silence and 47% active.
differences.b: 0.8 s with 0.22 s trailing silence but only 38% active. The overall timing and peak position (0.17-0.18 s) match.

missing_elements: Continuous low-level rattle bed filling 0-0.15 s and linking the bursts
Mid-range (1-3 kHz) thumpy click/pop body at 0.32-0.40 s
Gradual hissy decay tail from 0.4 to 0.57 s
Narrow 12 kHz air peak
extra_elements: Sub-bass thump (20-100 Hz) at 0.07 s and under the 0.18-0.25 s bursts
Isolated high-frequency ticks scattered from 0.45 to 0.7 s
Hard-edged percussive hit at 0.07 s
change_notes: Remove or high-pass the sub-bass: put a 150-200 Hz high-pass at 12 dB/oct on all layers so the 20-100 Hz blocks drop below -60 dB and the thump no longer dominates.

Add a continuous 3-8 kHz noise bed from 0 to 0.3 s, amplitude-modulated at 40-70 Hz (random jitter), swelling from -38 dB at 0 s to the peak at 0.18-0.2 s. Keep gaps between bursts shallower than 10 dB.
Smooth the 0.18-0.27 s burst: instead of two hard gated blocks, use one swell with a 120 ms rise and 60 ms fall, keeping the 4-10 kHz band dense.

Add 3 mandible pops at 0.32, 0.36 and 0.40 s: 15-25 ms each, bandpassed at 0.9-2.5 kHz with a short sine body around 900-1000 Hz, -8 to -12 dB relative to the main burst peak, and a quick exponential decay of about 30 ms.
Replace the isolated ticks at 0.45-0.7 s with a continuous hiss tail: 4-8 kHz noise decaying from -40 dB at 0.4 s to -65 dB at 0.57 s, then nothing. Remove the ticks after 0.57 s.
Soften the 0.07 s hit: lower it to -28 dB relative to the peak, use a 10 ms attack, and make it a noise click at 2-6 kHz with no low-frequency body.
Add a faint 11-12 kHz narrow band at about -30 dB relative to the 4-8 kHz level from 0.05 to 0.3 s for the air sheen.
Raise the overall level by about 2.5 dB so integrated loudness reaches -13.5 to -14 LUFS, with the peak at -1 dBFS.

review.summary: B has the right length, a similar spectral balance and a comparable click-based chitinous idea, but it is made of isolated, clean clicks with silent gaps instead of A's continuous scrabbly crackle bed. It also lacks A's crunchy mid-clip burst and its slow tail, so it reads as sparser and more electronic.

differences.a: Sustained, bursty energy through ~0.65 s. Decay to -20 dB takes 0.18 s and to -40 dB takes 0.78 s, with a fading sparse tail to ~0.84 s.
differences.b: Each event decays quickly (-20 dB at 0.05 s, -40 dB at 0.14 s). Long near-silent gaps sit between clicks and the tail dies away early (-93 dB in the last tenth).

differences.a: Continuous layer of small scratchy ticks and crackles between the major hits, plus a big crunchy burst at ~0.32-0.4 s with a 2-6 kHz cluster and a low thump.
differences.b: Discrete separated clicks, with no crackle bed. The ~0.31-0.4 s region is nearly empty (-56 dB tenth), and the biggest events sit at 0.44 s and 0.6-0.7 s, so the main crunch is missing or displaced.

differences.a: Gritty noise with no stable tones (flatness 0.25). Texture is crumpled shell or paper.
differences.b: Flatness 0.50 (noisier in the statistical sense), but the spectrogram shows steady tonal lines near 1.8 kHz and 4.9 kHz around 0.07-0.14 s and a ~200 Hz hum patch. Qwen reported a humming, electronic, controller-like quality.

differences.a: Very loud clipped snap at 0 s (peak +5 dBFS) with a low thump, followed by sharp cracks at ~0.15-0.18 s and 0.32 s.
differences.b: A strong opening burst of ~40 ms that is broader and more like a noise puff, then softer clicks. It lacks the sharp isolated crack transients.

differences.a: Organic, chitinous, crunchy and scratchy.
differences.b: Cleaner and more synthetic; clicks sound metallic or electronic, closer to a controller click than a bug leg.

differences.a: -19.6 LUFS, peak +5 dBFS (clipped), RMS -23 dB.
differences.b: -21.8 LUFS, peak -1.7 dBFS, RMS -24.4 dB. This is within the brief's tolerance and cleaner, but the average energy is concentrated in the opening.

differences.a: Centroid 5.7 kHz with a 4 kHz-ish dip in the early quarter (centroid by quarter: 7.5, 3.8, 5.5, 6.0 kHz). Low thumps accompany big hits.
differences.b: Overall balance is nearly identical (mid 39%, presence 34%, air 22%). Centroid is lower in the first quarter (4.0 kHz) and there is slightly less low thump under the later hits.
0.87 s with matching onset times, but active fraction is only 0.53 and the activity is concentrated early and in the mid-late region.

Crunchy shell-crush burst with 2-6 kHz cluster at ~0.32-0.4 s

change_notes: Add a continuous crackle bed: band-passed noise at 2-8 kHz, amplitude-modulated with random 5-15 ms grains at 150-300 grains/s, level about -30 to -26 dB re the opening, running 0.03-0.65 s. This fills B's gaps, which currently sit at -50 dB or lower.

Rebuild the 0.31-0.45 s event as a crunch: a 2 ms click, then 80-120 ms of noise at 2-6 kHz with a 5-10 ms stuttered grain envelope, plus a 60-120 Hz sine thump with a 40 ms decay, peaking about -8 dB (the loudest after the opening).
Remove or heavily reduce the tonal artifacts: delete the 1.8 kHz and 4.9 kHz sustained lines and the ~200 Hz hum around 0.07-0.14 s. Use noise-only bursts or filter noise with Q below 3.
Lengthen the per-click decays from ~50 ms to 20 dB down to ~100-150 ms, with a 2-3 ms attack, and fill the 0.07-0.30 s span with 4-6 ticks at about -20 to -25 dB.
Add a sparse fading tail: 4-5 faint ticks between 0.65 and 0.84 s at -40 to -50 dB, so the tail is at about -40 dB at 0.78 s instead of dropping to -93 dB.
Sharpen the opening: replace the noise puff with a 1-3 ms broadband click (up to 12 kHz) plus a 100 Hz thump of 30 ms, peak about -1.5 dBFS. Keep the 0 s event 6-8 dB above the body.
Raise the overall level by about 2 dB, to about -19.6 LUFS, by adding the crackle bed, not by raising the peak. Keep the peak at or below -1 dBFS.

review.summary: B is the right kind of sound, a loud noisy bass-heavy tesla blast with a rumbling pulsed tail, and it matches A closely in length, loudness and sub/bass weight. Its tail is more discrete and rhythmic, with a faster 20 dB decay and a brighter mid-section, so it feels slightly different.

differences.a: Tail is a smooth, continuous low rumble with irregular small pulses (onsets at about 1.56, 1.79, 1.99, 2.23, 2.46, 2.63 s). It fades gradually as a dark sub/bass wash until about 3.0 s.
differences.b: Tail is made of clearly separated bursts or thumps about every 80-100 ms (14 onsets from 1.16 to 2.63 s) with deep gaps between them. It reads as stuttering or sputtering and not as a rumble.

differences.a: Stays strong to about 0.8 s, falls 20 dB at 0.87 s and 40 dB at 1.88 s, then trails off slowly.
differences.b: Falls 20 dB at 0.61 s and 40 dB at 1.48 s, so it decays faster. The envelope is uneven, with dips to about -54 dB between the bursts.

differences.a: Centroid drops from about 2.9 kHz in the first quarter to about 60-80 Hz by the end, so it darkens steadily. The tail is mostly below 500 Hz.
differences.b: Centroid is 1.4 kHz in the first quarter, then rises to 3.7-4.4 kHz in the middle quarters. The bursts carry hiss and high-frequency content, so the tail stays bright and does not darken.

differences.a: Dense broadband noise and crackle with extremely low flatness, mainly from the strong low end.
differences.b: Higher measured flatness (0.195) and a noisier, hissier texture in the tail. The cleaner broadband gaps between the bursts make it feel more gated.

differences.a: Instant, dense bright burst of crackle in the first 0.9 s, with the loudest transient near 0.68 s.
differences.b: Similar dense burst in the first 0.9 s with the peak at 0.72 s. The opening is slightly less bright in the first quarter (centroid 1.4 kHz vs 2.9 kHz).

differences.a: 3.44 s file, active to about 3.0 s, with 0.47 s of trailing silence.
differences.b: 3.44 s file, active to about 3.1 s, with 0.35 s of trailing silence and a hard cutoff near 3.1 s.

differences.a: Peak -1.5 dBFS, -14.1 LUFS, LRA 4.0.
differences.b: Peak -1.5 dBFS, -14.5 LUFS, LRA 2.1. The loudness is essentially matched, but the dynamics are a bit flatter in the main body.

missing_elements: Smooth continuous low-frequency rumble bed under the tail
Progressive darkening of the spectrum over time (highs gone by about 1.5 s)
Long gradual decay between 1 and 2.5 s
extra_elements: Regular, repeated high-frequency burst or sputter pulses every 80-100 ms from 1.1 to 2.6 s
Deep gaps between bursts, so the tail sounds gated
Bright hiss in the tail
change_notes: Add a continuous rumble bed under the tail: brown or low-passed noise at 40-250 Hz, with a 1.5 s fade starting at about 1.0 s and a slow decay to -50 dB by 3.0 s. It should fill the gaps between the bursts.
Cut the number of tail pulses from 14 to about 6-7 and space them irregularly at about 1.25, 1.56, 1.79, 1.99, 2.23, 2.46 and 2.63 s, with 100-250 ms between them. Randomize their amplitude by ±4 dB.
Low-pass each tail burst at about 500-800 Hz, and sweep the cutoff from 2 kHz at 1.2 s down to 300 Hz at 2.6 s. This gets the quarter centroids to about 600 Hz and 80 Hz instead of 3.7-4.4 kHz.

Slow the main-body decay: hold the burst near full level until about 0.8 s, then reach -20 dB at about 0.85 s and -40 dB at about 1.9 s (currently 0.61 s and 1.48 s). Use an exponential tail with a time constant of about 0.45 s.
Brighten the first 0.3 s: add a 3-10 kHz crackle or noise burst of about 0.3-0.5 s at +3 dB so the first-quarter centroid reaches about 2.5-3 kHz.
Raise the gap floor between bursts to no lower than -40 dB, and fade the end smoothly to silence by about 3.0 s with a 150 ms fade-out instead of a cutoff. Leave 0.4 s of trailing silence.

review.summary: B matches A's length, loudness and overall three-cluster reload layout well, with the loudest hit at the end. But it adds pitched tonal ringing, a low resonant 'boing' tone, and a heavy final thump, which make it sound more synthetic and less like dry metallic foley.

differences.a: Almost entirely broadband noise-like metallic clacks. The only tonal content is a faint mid-band tone near 1 kHz.
differences.b: Pure sine-like ringing partials at about 1.2 kHz, 1.7 kHz, 5 kHz and 8-12 kHz, visible as thin horizontal lines. Spectral flatness is 0.40 versus A's 0.003. Qwen describes a 'boing' and a ping-pong ball.

differences.a: Low-frequency content is only a vertical thump on the big hits, with almost no sustained bass. It is dry and the first two clusters are scrapy and dense.
differences.b: Sustained resonant low tone at about 250-350 Hz, with a downward pitch glide at 0.94 s and a 0.3 s ring at 1.33 s. It sounds like a boing or a drum. There is also a ~200 Hz thud under the first cluster.

differences.a: Decays are fast, about 0.06 s to -20 dB and 0.13 s to -40 dB. The events are dry with no sustain.
differences.b: Click transients decay faster (0.03 s and 0.06 s), but the added tonal and low resonances ring 0.2-0.3 s. The ringing partials and the 0.94 s low tone make the envelope feel boingy rather than clacky.

differences.a: The 0.94-1.25 s gap holds only faint ticks and handling noise. The 0.94 s event is barely there.
differences.b: A distinct low-mid tonal blip at 0.94 s with a falling pitch (about 400 to 200 Hz, 0.15 s), plus a separate tonal click at 1.17 s with 1.9 kHz ringing. These are more prominent than A's gap content.

differences.a: Centroid is 5.7 kHz. Presence is 47%, mid 30% and air 20%. Scrapy dense energy sits at 1-5 kHz.
differences.b: Centroid is 6.1 kHz. Presence is 40%, mid 34% and air 23%. It is a bit brighter, with a thinner 2-5 kHz body and more air hiss.

differences.a: Last clack at 1.31-1.33 s is a heavy metallic slam with a thump extending down to 20 Hz. Peak is -4.6 dBFS and crest 23 dB.
differences.b: Final hit is a bright crack with a stronger, longer low thump (sub energy and a ~300 Hz ring). Peak is -3.7 dBFS, true peak -2.5 dBTP, a bit hotter, and the crest is slightly spikier.

differences.a: 1.76 s with clusters at 0.13-0.35, 0.52-0.82 and a final at 1.3-1.5 s, and 0.26 s trailing silence.
differences.b: 1.76 s with matching cluster timing. The first onset is slightly earlier at 0.06 s and the trailing silence is 0.37 s, so the final hit ends a bit sooner. Overall timing is very close.

differences.a: -23.5 LUFS, RMS -27.9 dBFS.
differences.b: -23.6 LUFS, RMS -28.1 dBFS. Essentially identical.

missing_elements: Dense scrapy, rattly metallic texture in the 1-5 kHz range during the first two clusters
Sparse, quiet handling ticks in the 0.94-1.25 s gap
Dry, purely noise-based metal-on-metal character with no pitched ringing
extra_elements: Sine-like ringing partials at ~1.2 kHz, ~1.7 kHz, ~5 kHz and 8-12 kHz
Resonant 250-350 Hz tonal body at 0.94 s and 1.33 s that sounds like a boing

change_notes: Remove or heavily reduce the tonal partial oscillators (about 1.2 kHz, 1.7 kHz, 5 kHz, 8-12 kHz). Replace them with bandpassed noise bursts (Q 2-4) at 2-6 kHz, or keep at most one partial at about -30 dB relative to the clack, with decay under 40 ms.

Delete the 300 Hz ring after the 1.33 s hit. Replace it with a short thump: sine from 150 Hz down to 50 Hz over 80 ms, decay about 100 ms, level -12 dB under the crack. It should not last past 1.45 s.
Remove the 0.94 s pitched falling tone (400 to 200 Hz). Replace it with a faint 3-5 ms tick at -35 dB, or just quiet handling noise at 1-3 kHz.
Make the first two clusters denser: add 4-6 noise micro-clicks per cluster, 3-10 ms each, bandpassed at 1.5-5 kHz, with random spacing of 10-30 ms. Raise the 1-5 kHz body by about 3 dB.
Reduce the 1.17 s click's tonal ring (1.9 kHz) to a noise-dominant metallic tick. Keep the click about 10 dB under the final hit.
Lower the air band above 10 kHz by about 2-3 dB with a gentle shelf to bring the centroid from 6.1 kHz to about 5.7 kHz.
Trim the final hit by about 1-2 dB so true peak is about -4 dBTP. Keep the 0.3 s trailing silence.

review.summary: B is the right kind of sound (a noisy, crackly alien death with the same 1.78 s length and similar brightness), but its energy is distributed differently. It has a soft, sustained sub-bass pulsing bed instead of a single sharp thump, and the loud crackle section runs much longer than in A. It is also about 2.6 LU quieter.

differences.a: Loud, hard opening burst peaking at 0.03 s with a strong clipped low thump, then a 20 dB drop by 0.2 s. It is punchy and impactful.
differences.b: Slower, softer onset peaking at 0.05 s. The first tenth is about 5 dB quieter (-23 vs -18 dB), and there is no distinct impact followed by a drop.

differences.a: Quick fall of 20 dB by 0.2 s, then a ragged, irregular sustain of crackles that thins gradually, reaching -40 dB at about 1.37 s.
differences.b: Stays near the same level for much longer: -20 dB is reached at 0.85 s versus 0.2 s in A. It is a flatter, more sustained plateau until about 1.3 s, then falls off, with -40 dB at 1.34 s.

differences.a: Sub energy is about 5%, concentrated in a single 40-100 Hz thump at 0-0.15 s. Everything after that is bright noise with little low end.
differences.b: Sub is about 11%, with pulsing 20-100 Hz bursts repeating through the whole sound until about 1.5 s. The result is a rumbly, boomy bed that A does not have, and the centroid dips to 4.7 kHz in the second quarter.

differences.a: Distinct sequence: thump plus noise burst, then sharp irregular crackle and squelch clicks (0.26, 0.34, 0.42, 0.6 s), then a sparse crinkly bed and a few clicks near 1.28 and 1.36 s.
differences.b: Onsets are spaced differently (0.34, 0.67, 0.92, 1.05, 1.13, 1.36, 1.44, 1.52 s), and the sound is more of a rhythmic burst pattern. Its trailing bursts at 1.36-1.52 s are well after A's last events, so they sound like a stuttering coda.

differences.a: Gritty, wet, crunchy, chitinous noise that is organic and irregular, with dense random clicks.
differences.b: Noisy and bright, but it reads as more pulsed and amplitude-modulated, with some electronic/metallic quality per the listening notes. The crackle is less wet and less dense.

differences.a: -14.5 LUFS, peak +3.8 dBFS with clipping (82 samples), crest 20.9 dB. It is hot and punchy.
differences.b: -17.1 LUFS, peak -1.6 dBFS, no clipping, crest 17.4 dB. It is about 2.6 LU quieter, within tolerance but at the low end, and less peaky.

differences.a: Hissy tail fades out by about 1.5 s, followed by 0.24 s of silence.
differences.b: Ends with sparse small bursts until about 1.6 s, then 0.18 s of silence. There is a hard cut-off at the end (-47 dB in the 10th tenth, then digital silence).

differences.a: 1.78 s, active fraction 0.75.
differences.b: 1.78 s, active fraction 0.85, so it feels denser and longer in the body.

Gradual thinning of the crackles into a quiet bed

Remove the stuttering bursts at 1.44 and 1.52 s. Replace them with a quiet hiss tail (6-10 kHz noise, around -40 dB) fading to silence by 1.55 s, using a smooth 100 ms fade to avoid the hard cut.
Raise the overall level about 2-3 dB to reach about -14.5 to -15 LUFS with peak at or below -1 dBFS, using soft limiting on the opening burst for punch without clipping.
Reduce periodic amplitude modulation and any metallic tone by randomizing click spacing, and keep the noise unpitched with flatness around 0.75.

review.summary: B is the right kind of sound, a bass-heavy distorted whoosh burst with a low rumble tail, and its length and decay times match A well. It is quieter, lacks A's upper-mid swoosh sweep and thin 2.2 kHz air tail, and cuts off hard around 1.2 s.

differences.a: Very loud and hot: -11.9 LUFS, peak +5.5 dBFS with 835 clipped samples, which gives a saturated, punchy feel.
differences.b: -14.1 LUFS, peak -1.4 dBFS, no clipping. About 2 LU quieter and less aggressive, though within the brief's tolerance.

differences.a: Gritty, clipped and distorted impact with broadband noise extending up the spectrum.
differences.b: Cleaner and smoother, with less visible grit and saturation.

differences.a: A curved upper-mid noise sweep (about 3-10 kHz) rises and falls between 0.15 and 0.9 s, giving the whoosh quality.
differences.b: Only a diffuse mid-high noise bloom around 1-5 kHz, peaking near 0.3-0.4 s, with no clear rising and falling sweep.

differences.a: Rumbling, fluttering low decay fading smoothly to about 1.2-1.7 s, plus a faint thin band near 2.2 kHz that lingers.
differences.b: Low rumble stays strong until about 1.1 s, then drops abruptly at about 1.2 s (the envelope falls to silence). No 2.2 kHz air band. A few gated-looking high-frequency blips around 1.0-1.15 s.

differences.a: Onset at 0.05 s, peak at 0.23 s, with a hard impact-like start and clipped bursts through 0.3 s.
differences.b: Peak at 0.19 s with a soft initial swell (first tenth is -17.7 dB vs A's -8.8 dB). Less of an immediate hit.

differences.a: -20 dB at 0.29 s after the peak, -40 dB at 0.94 s, with a long smooth decay.
differences.b: -20 dB at 0.3 s, -40 dB at 0.9 s. Closely matches until the early cutoff.

differences.a: Centroid 251 Hz, sub 21% and bass 61%. Brighter mid energy at 0.3-0.6 s.
differences.b: Centroid 300 Hz, sub 25%, bass 55%, low-mid 14%. Slightly more sub and low-mid, similar overall weight.

differences.a: 1.81 s file, about 1.17 s active, 0.64 s trailing silence.
differences.b: 1.81 s file, about 1.2 s active, 0.72 s trailing silence. Essentially the same.

Clipped, saturated grit on the initial impact

Trim sub slightly (-1.5 dB below 60 Hz) so the centroid moves from 300 Hz toward 250 Hz.

review.summary: B is a sub-heavy, tonal thump with a slow amplitude flutter that sounds like a droning pulse, not A's sharp, noisy, broadband gunshot crack with a fast decay. Length and overall loudness are close, but attack, brightness and character miss the role.

differences.a: Instant 0 s peak at -0.7 dBFS with a sharp broadband crack in the first ~90 ms, dropping about 9 dB by 0.1 s.
differences.b: Attack is softer, peaking at 0.02 s, with a flat -7 dB plateau through the first 0.2 s. There is no distinct crack.

review.summary: B is the right kind of sound with matching length, loudness and overall spectral balance: a dense noisy screech followed by a sparse clicky tail. Its structure differs, though: the burst starts later and is more tonal and bass-heavy, and it has a gap before a sparser, shorter chitter.

differences.a: The burst hits at once with a fast-rising, dense noise onset, peaking at 0.11 s, with a click near 0.2 s and a clipped spike (peak +1.6 dBFS).
differences.b: A tiny blip at 0 s, then a hard step onset at about 0.05-0.06 s. The burst has a clear gap in front of it and a cleaner, smoother-looking start (peak -1.3 dBFS).

differences.a: Sustained plateau to about 0.4 s, then a sharp drop and a long, continuous, gradually decaying chitter. -40 dB at 0.87 s, with energy still present to about 1.17 s.
differences.b: The main burst is a modulated two-lobe body (about 0.06-0.35 s) that drops quickly, then a thin tail. -40 dB is reached at 0.59 s, and the tail is mostly silent after about 1.0 s apart from isolated ticks.

differences.a: About 8-10 small pulses spaced roughly 80-100 ms apart from 0.4 to 1.15 s, steadily weakening. They read as a continuous rattle with a body underneath.
differences.b: A few isolated, widely spaced, bright clicks (0.55, 0.69, 0.77, 0.87, then a gap, 1.07, 1.15), and the last ones are louder than the middle ones. There is a hole around 0.9-1.05 s, and the gap and late loud ticks sound like random pops, not a decaying chitter.

differences.b: Strong energy extends down to 20-100 Hz during the burst, with vertical banding that sounds like a thump or growl. This is heavier and less raspy. The 2-5 kHz energy is similar.

differences.b: Flatness 0.16: more tonal and harmonic, with pulsed amplitude lobes (about 8 per second) that sound like a growl or buzz instead of a ragged screech.

differences.b: Smoother and more synthetic. The tail ticks are narrow, steady bright bars with some tonal whistle lines near 1.1-1.2 s at about 5-6 kHz.

review.summary: B is the right kind of sound, a 9.4 s stereo broadband wind-rush loop at matching loudness and band balance. It is a flat, static bed with none of A's slow swell, darker edges or buffeting flutter, so it feels less like gliding airflow.

review.summary: B has the same overall duration and a similar opening burst, but its body is a sparse series of separate clicks and ticks rather than A's continuous rasping noise with two swells. The result reads as crumpling paper or a click sequence, not a sustained creature screech.

differences.a: Body stays dense and fairly steady from 0.1 to 0.6 s at about -20 to -26 dB per tenth, with two swells at 0.4-0.5 s and 0.6-0.7 s. It reaches -20 dB at 0.43 s and -40 dB at 0.7 s.

differences.a: Continuous dense rasping noise with a formant-like band at 450-1000 Hz, which gives it a vocal, creature quality.
differences.b: Discrete impulsive clicks with dark gaps between them. The vocal band is faint and only appears in the first 0.3 s. The sound is more like crumpled paper or debris than a creature.

Shorten the body decay: reach -20 dB at about 1.7 s instead of 3.0 s, with an exponential fade (time constant about 0.6 s), then a long thin tail of -25 to -35 dB to about 5.1 s. Remove the swell near 2.1 s.

Make the three pulses buzzier: use sawtooth or pulse waves (0.15-0.2 s each at 0.1, 0.5 and 0.9 s, fundamental about 550-600 Hz) with 15+ harmonics up to 6 kHz, and add 30-60 Hz AM or flutter. Keep their pitch constant or only slightly dropping, 3% across the three.

Brighten and roughen the tail: add a bandpassed (1-2.5 kHz) noise layer with 8-14 Hz amplitude flutter and a slow 1.2 kHz band wobble of ±100 Hz from 1 to 4.5 s, at about -25 dB. Raise the tail centroid toward 1.5-2 kHz.
Make the whistle wander: sweep the 6 kHz line by ±150 Hz with a slow LFO (0.5 Hz), fade it out over 0.5-3 s instead of cutting it, and reduce the level 3 dB.

Replace the hard 5.4 s cutoff with a lowpass sweep from 8 kHz to 1 kHz over 4.5-5.6 s, plus a gradual amplitude fade. Reduce the digital streaks by smoothing the noise generator or adding a 5 ms crossfade.

review.summary: B has the right overall shape: a gritty noisy rasp, then sparse clicks fading out over about 1.1 s, with matching length, loudness and band balance. It differs in structure, though. The rasp is split into two bursts with a dip between them, the transition clicks are weaker, and the tail clicks are cleaner and die out earlier.

differences.a: One continuous dense rasp from 0 to about 0.3 s, then a fast drop into clicks. It reads as a single screech.
differences.b: Two separate swells: a build to about 0.15-0.2 s, a dip near 0.27 s, then a second louder burst peaking near 0.38-0.4 s that ends abruptly at about 0.43 s. It reads as two pulses or a stutter.

differences.a: Instant, full-level rasp at 0 s. Sharp high-peak click spikes at 0.28 s and 0.39 s, with clipping, form the transition to the chitter.
differences.b: Starts soft and ramps up, with an onset at 0.05 s and the peak at 0.39 s. Its loudest point is a broad noisy swell rather than a sharp spike, so the transition lacks a crisp crack.

differences.a: Dense rasp occupies 0-0.3 s, transition clicks 0.28-0.45 s, then chitter onsets at 0.53, 0.61, 0.73, 0.81, 0.89 and 0.99 s. Active fraction is 0.79.
differences.b: Dense rasp runs to 0.43 s, about 0.1 s longer, so the clicks begin later (0.48, 0.56, 0.65...). Active fraction is 0.66, with a near-silent final 0.12 s versus 0.05 s.

differences.a: Gritty, mottled, fluttering vocal-like rasp with fast amplitude modulation, plus crackly foley-like clicks. The spectral flatness of 0.073 shows semi-tonal grit.
differences.b: Smoother, noisier body (flatness 0.159) with a more metallic or static feel, which Qwen described as a malfunctioning device. It sounds less organic and less like a creature vocalisation.

differences.a: Clicks fade gradually and the tail is faint and crackly to about 1.07 s. Envelope is -40 dB at 0.55 s but with residual crackle.
differences.b: Clicks are cleaner and sparser, with big gaps and some thin tonal ticks near 4.6 kHz. The tail drops to -94 dB in the last tenth, so it ends abruptly and drier than A.

differences.a: Centroid 3.55 kHz, rising from 3.4 to 6.9 kHz as clicks get brighter. Strong 2-5 kHz and 200-500 Hz body in the rasp.
differences.b: Centroid 3.28 kHz, starting lower at 2.85 kHz. More low-end weight (below 100 Hz) in the burst peaks and slightly less top-end shimmer. Band percentages are very close.

differences.a: Peak +1 dBFS with clipping, -15.1 LUFS, crest 18.7 dB.
differences.b: Peak -1.9 dBFS with no clipping, -15.5 LUFS, crest 16.9 dB. This is within spec and cleaner.

differences.a: Mono.
differences.b: Mono.

change_notes: Merge the two bursts into one rasp from 0 to 0.30 s: start at full level with a 3 ms attack and remove the dip at 0.27 s. Keep the level within about 3 dB across the burst.
Cut the second swell (0.35-0.43 s). Replace it with two sharp clicks, 2-8 kHz noise, 5-10 ms, at 0.28 s and 0.39 s, +8 to +10 dB over the rasp body, to match A's spike transients.

Move the chitter clicks earlier to about 0.53, 0.61, 0.73, 0.81, 0.89 and 0.99 s. Make each a 10-20 ms band-passed noise burst at 3-6 kHz, each 3-5 dB quieter than the last, and raise the centre frequency from 3 kHz to 6 kHz across the series.

Add 30-60 Hz amplitude modulation (50-70% depth) and a 300-500 Hz formant-like band to the rasp for an organic, vocal grit. Lower the noise-to-tone flatness from 0.16 to about 0.08, using a 2-5 kHz band-passed noise with some comb or ring modulation.

Remove the 4.6 kHz tonal ticks. Add low-level crackle (about -50 dB, sparse 1-3 ms ticks) filling the gaps from 0.45 to 1.07 s, and extend the tail so it stays above -70 dB until about 1.05 s instead of ending near 0.93 s.
Keep the peak around -1 dBFS and loudness near -15 LUFS. Lift the rasp's centroid to about 3.4 kHz by trimming sub-100 Hz energy in the burst.

review.summary: B has the right overall length, peak time and loudness, but it is a single concentrated hit at about 0.15-0.25s with sparse isolated ticks after it. A is a multi-chomp, wet, crunchy bite with sustained broadband body through about 0.4s, so B reads as a thinner, more staccato bite.

differences.a: Main bite is two close bursts at about 0.13s and 0.19s, then a secondary chomp at about 0.3s. Reaches -40 dB at about 0.34s with a gradual, lumpy decay and a low-level rattle to about 0.58s.
differences.b: One dominant burst peaking around 0.17s that falls to -40 dB within about 0.08s. After that only isolated tiny ticks remain, with deep gaps between them. Active fraction is 0.22 against 0.47 for A.

differences.a: Dense cluster of chomps: a soft pre-click at 0.05s, a double main hit, a secondary chomp at 0.3s and a faint click at 0.44s. They are joined by continuous wet rattle.
differences.b: Isolated ticks at 0.0, 0.05, 0.13, 0.25, 0.33, 0.44, 0.52 and 0.65s are sparse and sit 15-30 dB below the main hit. They read as separate clicks rather than chewing. The second chomp at 0.28-0.3s is a narrow mid blip.

differences.a: Wet, crunchy, organic. Broadband noise is modulated into gristly crunch, with spectral flatness 0.24.
differences.b: Noisier and more diffuse in the main hit, with flatness 0.345. It sounds more like a clean noise burst or thud than a squelchy crunch. The fixed horizontal line near 1.1-1.5 kHz in the main hit adds a tonal, synthetic whistle.

differences.a: Strong 150-400 Hz body in both main hits, with energy spread evenly up to 10 kHz. The centroid stays steady at about 3-3.8 kHz per quarter.
differences.b: Overall band balance is close (centroid 4.9 kHz vs 5.0 kHz). The low body is concentrated into one 80-300 Hz burst, and the centroid swings between 4.2 and 7.1 kHz because the tail is only bright ticks. Late elements are overly hissy and thin.

differences.a: Short dry tail with low-level rattle fading to near silence by about 0.6s.
differences.b: Dead silence between ticks, with an abrupt cutoff and trailing silence of 0.24s. Tail content is below -58 dB per tenth, so it feels empty rather than fading.

differences.a: First sizeable transient at about 0.13s is followed by a second at about 0.19s, so the bite has a double snap.
differences.b: Single sharp onset at about 0.15s with a quick fall. The pre-click at 0.05s is softer and sits well below the main hit.

differences.a: Peak -2.2 dBFS, -20.8 LUFS.
differences.b: Peak -3.0 dBFS, -21.1 LUFS. Close, but the energy is more concentrated in one hit.

change_notes: Split the main hit into two bursts: a first at 0.13s and a second at 0.19s that is -2 dB quieter. Each is 40-60 ms of band-passed noise (300 Hz-8 kHz) with a 2 ms attack and about 40 ms exponential decay.

Add a wet crunch bed from 0.12 to 0.40s. Use noise amplitude-modulated at 40-70 Hz with random depth, band-passed at 1-6 kHz, at -18 to -24 dB relative to the main burst. Fade it to -40 dB by about 0.4s so the gaps between chomps fill in.
Raise the second chomp at 0.28-0.32s to roughly -12 dB relative to the main hit. Give it a 150-300 Hz thump of 50 ms and a 2-5 kHz crunch, instead of the narrow mid blip.
Remove or notch the steady 1.1-1.5 kHz tone in the main hit. If a tonal component is needed, pitch it down from 700 to 300 Hz over 80 ms, mixed low.

Lower the noise purity: add a 120-250 Hz thump with a short pitch drop (250 to 120 Hz over 60 ms) under each main burst. Reduce high-frequency hiss above 8 kHz by about 3 dB so the late ticks are less brittle.
Replace the scattered late ticks (0.45-0.65s) with a faint low rattle at -45 to -50 dB, and keep one soft click at 0.44s. Fade smoothly to silence by about 0.6s rather than leaving isolated blips.
Keep the total length at about 0.78s and the peak at about -2 dBFS, aiming for -20.8 LUFS. This is variant a, so vary chomp timing by ±10 ms in the other variants.

review.summary: B is the right kind of sound: a 1.35 s mechanical press one-shot with matching band balance, loudness (-20.8 vs -20.6 LUFS) and decay times. Its build-up is weaker, its attack is sharper and more sudden, and the brightness and body are distributed differently over time.

differences.a: Gradual swell from a rumble start (-48 dB at first tenth, -20 dB at 0.1-0.2 s) to a peak at 0.23 s; the impact is blended into the churn with no hard edge.
differences.b: Near-silent lead-in (-69 dB, about 0.04 s leading silence), then a sudden sharp hit at 0.18 s with a broadband vertical click up to the top of the spectrum. It reads as a distinct stamp or crack rather than a swell.

differences.a: Continuous motor or servo rumble from 0 s with a warm 400-450 Hz band at 0.02-0.17 s, which builds into the main crunch.
differences.b: The pre-impact motor layer is very faint (about 10-15 dB lower, almost silent). The 300-330 Hz tone sits after the hit (0.18-0.35 s) instead of before it, so the order of events is reversed.

differences.a: Centroid by quarter is 374 / 442 / 313 / 72 Hz: the tail goes very dull and low, with almost nothing above 500 Hz after 0.7 s.
differences.b: Centroid by quarter is 498 / 867 / 921 / 776 Hz: the tail stays brighter, with hiss-like mid and high noise lingering to about 1.2 s. The overall centroid (539 Hz) is similar, but the tail is not as dull.

differences.a: Rough, fluttery low-frequency striation (pulsing rumble) below 300 Hz with gritty crunch up to 2-4 kHz at 0.2-0.35 s.
differences.b: Smoother, more sustained sub/bass block (40-150 Hz) from 0.18 to 0.55 s, with less fluttering. Noisier flatness (0.01 vs 0.002) and a more synthetic feel.

differences.a: Peak at 0.23 s; -20 dB by about 0.35 s after the peak and -40 dB by 0.69 s; quiet low tail to about 1.2 s.
differences.b: Peak at 0.18 s; decay times (0.37 s and 0.68 s) are nearly identical; the tail ends slightly sooner and drops to digital silence after 1.25 s. Trailing silence is 0.37 s vs 0.3 s.

differences.a: Duration 1.35 s; onsets at 0.05 s and 0.2 s; peak at 0.23 s.
differences.b: Duration 1.35 s; onsets at 0.05 s and 0.18 s; peak at 0.18 s, about 50 ms earlier with a shorter build.

differences.a: -20.6 LUFS, peak -4.6 dBFS, crest 18.2 dB.
differences.b: -20.8 LUFS, peak -4.1 dBFS, crest 19.0 dB. Effectively matched.

Soften the main hit: lengthen the attack ramp to about 0.15-0.2 s, delay the peak to about 0.22-0.24 s, and cut the HF click above 6 kHz by about 12 dB (low-pass at about 4 kHz) so it blends into the swell.
Darken the tail: low-pass the 0.5-1.2 s section at about 400-500 Hz (12-24 dB/oct), reducing mid/high noise by about 10 dB so the quarter centroids land near 300 / 70 Hz.
Add amplitude flutter of about 15-30 Hz (30-50% depth) to the sub/bass body (40-250 Hz) from 0.1 to 0.7 s to match A's striated rumble, and reduce the sustained sub block by about 3 dB after 0.35 s.
Keep the gritty noise burst at 1-3 kHz, about 150 ms around 0.2-0.3 s, and make sure it peaks with the thump rather than ahead of it.
Extend the tail so it fades out by about 1.2 s with a gentle exponential rather than a sudden drop; keep total length 1.35 s and loudness at -20.6 LUFS.

review.summary: B matches A's length, loudness (-16.8 vs -16.5 LUFS), centroid and overall shape of a noisy rasp, a peak near 0.4 s and then sparse clicks. It lacks A's low growl and has a tighter, cleaner, drier tail, so it reads more like a hiss-burst than a gritty creature vocalisation.

differences.a: Strong warm growl at 100-350 Hz with modulated blotchy texture, plus faint tonal bands near 650 Hz and 1.3 kHz in the first 0.4 s. Low end is a defining part of the opening.
differences.b: Low body is weak and appears only as vertical streaks around 0.1-0.4 s. Energy is concentrated at 2-8 kHz, with a sizzly mid/presence band and a stray 9.4 kHz peak.

differences.a: Rasp is partly pitched and organic, with flatness 0.305 and a vocal formant-like structure.
differences.b: More tonal-hiss, with flatness 0.103 and a speckled granular texture. It sounds synthetic and less like a throat rasp.

differences.a: Loud sustained rasp from 0-0.35 s, a peak click at 0.4 s, then a stepped decay. The -40 dB point is at about 0.55 s, with ticks continuing at moderate level to about 1.0 s. Active fraction 0.79.
differences.b: Similar rise to a peak at 0.39 s, but the 0.4-0.5 s region drops away abruptly. Clicks after 0.5 s are much quieter and sparser (envelope -69 dB at 0.7 s) and the tail is dead by about 0.99 s. Active fraction 0.61.

differences.a: Peak is a sharp, isolated crack at 0.4 s on top of the rasp, with 9 onsets. It clips slightly and has crest 21 dB.
differences.b: Peak at 0.39 s is a broad swell of dense noise about 80 ms wide rather than a single crack. Onsets are fewer and more evenly spaced.

differences.a: Growl, screech hiss and click/crackle layers are all present. The late clicks are broadband and have a clear body.
differences.b: Late clicks are thin, high and narrow-band, and are separated by near silence. There is no vertical-streak harshness in the 0.2-0.4 s zone.

differences.a: Short, dry tail with ticks fading by about 1.08 s.
differences.b: Dry as well, but longer trailing silence (0.13 s vs 0.04 s). The last clicks are almost inaudible.

differences.a: -16.5 LUFS, peak +0.8 dBFS (clipped).
differences.b: -16.8 LUFS, peak -2.3 dBFS. Cleaner and on target.
1.12 s, with onsets at 0.05, 0.36, 0.52, 0.60, 0.72, 0.80, 0.89 and 0.98 s. The click timing is close, but the 0.24 s accent is missing.

change_notes: Add a growl layer: sawtooth or pulse at 110-160 Hz, formant-filtered at 250-350 Hz, amplitude-modulated at 25-40 Hz, from 0 to 0.38 s, level about -6 dB relative to the noise layer.
Add faint resonant bands at 650 Hz and 1.3 kHz (Q about 8, -20 dB) during 0-0.2 s for a vocal tone.
Make the 0.4 s peak a sharp crack: 5-10 ms, 2-6 kHz noise burst at +4 dB over the rasp, with the rasp dropping 6 dB just before it. Cut the 80 ms noise swell to about 40 ms.
Add an accent burst at 0.24 s, 40 ms, -3 dB relative to the main rasp.
