Keep the peak at -1 to -2 dBFS and hold -16.5 LUFS. Trim trailing silence to about 0.05 s.

review.summary: B has the right overall shape: a noisy double-hit onset, a ringing tone and a fading tail, at nearly the same length and decay times. It differs in character: a loud, sustained 1.2 kHz tone replaces A's thin, gliding high partials, it is darker, it lacks the deep rumble, and it has a gated tail.

differences.a: Thin inharmonic partials at about 2.2 kHz and 4.5 kHz glide down then slowly up over 1.5 s. Further partials sit at 1-3 kHz and curve downward after the second hit.
differences.b: One strong, steady, slightly tremolo-modulated tone at about 1.1-1.25 kHz runs from 0.07 to 0.65 s with almost no glide. It then drops about 15 dB and continues faintly to about 0.95 s. Fixed fine partials at 2.2, 3.3 and 5.6 kHz sit above it.

differences.a: Very bright, centroid about 7.1 kHz, air about 34%, presence 16%, mid 44%, with energy up to 15-18 kHz.
differences.b: Darker and mid-heavy, centroid about 5 kHz, mid about 60%, air 24%, presence 10%. The 1.2 kHz tone dominates, and the centroid jumps to 12.6 kHz in the third quarter only because of a noise burst.

differences.a: Two loud, crunchy broadband bursts (0-0.09 s and about 0.1-0.15 s) that clip and reach down to the low end. Very faint thin partials follow, with a low rumble under the whole sound.
differences.b: The first burst is similar but shorter and cleaner, and the second hit is a small click at about 0.13 s. The sustained tone then sits well above everything else, and a vertical gate-like re-entry of noise appears at about 1.0 s.

differences.a: Peak at 0.03 s, -20 dB at 0.34 s, -40 dB at 1.11 s. A smooth, quiet ringing decay into a shimmering tail.
differences.b: Peak at 0.05 s, -20 dB at 0.32 s, -40 dB at 1.13 s, so the timing matches. The envelope is bumpier: the tone pulses, the level is higher between 0.2 and 0.6 s, and there is a step at about 1.0 s.

differences.a: Smooth, continuous shimmer of high partials at 8-12 kHz that fades into silence, with 0.46 s of trailing silence.
differences.b: Tail is dark noise around 0.5-2 kHz, with a visible cut at 0.7 s and a re-entry at 1.0 s. It lacks the high shimmer. Trailing silence is 0.32 s.

differences.a: Instant, clipped, crunchy onset at 0.03 s with very high crest.
differences.b: Peak at 0.05 s with a slightly softer, cleaner onset. There is a thump at about 20-100 Hz in the first 0.05 s and little bass after that.

differences.a: -17.9 LUFS, peak +0.8 dBFS, clipped.
differences.b: -20.1 LUFS, peak -1.9 dBFS. This is about 2 LU quieter, which is within tolerance and safer for clipping.

differences.a: Noise-dominated opening, then pure thin ringing with a fine noise haze.
differences.b: Tone is more prominent and noise is spread evenly over the highs through to about 1.0 s, so it reads as a beeping tone with hiss.

differences.a: Mono.
differences.b: Mono file. Qwen's left/right description is probably invented.

change_notes: Reduce the 1.2 kHz tone by 15-20 dB and shorten it to 0.3 s. Alternatively, replace it with 2-3 thin sine/FM partials near 2.2 kHz and 4.5 kHz. Start each about 3% higher and glide down about 5% over 0.3 s, then drift back up about 3% by 1.5 s. Keep them at -35 to -45 dB relative to the burst, ringing about 1.3 s.

Remove the tremolo on the main tone, or reduce its depth to below 1 dB. Remove the step at 0.65 s and the noise re-entry at 1.0 s so the decay is smooth. Fade the noise bed continuously: -30 dB at 0.3 s, -50 dB at 0.8 s.

Add a high shimmer. Use 3-4 quiet partials between 8 and 12 kHz plus a 15-18 kHz sparkle from 0.3 to 1.2 s, fading about 40 dB. Raise the high-shelf above 6 kHz by about +4 dB so the centroid is near 7 kHz.
Make the second burst at 0.10-0.15 s louder (about -6 dB relative to the first) and more crunchy, with broadband noise 1-12 kHz, 40 ms long, instead of the small click at 0.13 s.
Lengthen the first burst to 80-90 ms and move its onset to 0.03 s, with a slight soft clip. Add a low rumble at 40-120 Hz at -40 dB, decaying over about 1.2 s.
Raise the overall level by about 2 dB toward -18 LUFS, keeping the peak at or below -1 dBFS. Keep the file mono at 1.6 s with trailing silence of about 0.4 s.

review.summary: B is a sparse series of discrete, isolated clicks with a loud mid-band crack at 0.28 s, where A is a dense, continuous crackly rustle with a sharp snap at 0.31 s. The lengths match, but B's texture, density and continuity are quite different from A's.

differences.a: Continuous, dense scratchy rustle with many small clicks overlapping, like chitin scrabbling or crumpled plastic.
differences.b: Isolated, clean, discrete clicks and pings separated by near-silence; reads as ticking or clock-like, not scrabbling.

differences.a: Sustained busy bed from 0 to about 0.6 s, with levels around -21 dB per tenth. The decay to -40 dB takes about 0.42 s and the tail thins out gradually.
differences.b: Each click decays almost instantly (-40 dB in 0.05 s). Tenth-second levels fall to -45 to -55 dB between events, giving a gappy, stop-start envelope with active fraction 0.39 vs 0.78.

differences.a: Rustle bed, small clicks, a sharp broadband snap at about 0.31 s, secondary crunches at 0.36, 0.39 and 0.51 s, and low thumps underneath.
differences.b: Only isolated clicks and one big burst at 0.28-0.33 s; no continuous rustle bed, and the secondary crunches are weak and sparse.

differences.a: Onsets are irregular (0.05, 0.2, 0.28, 0.36, 0.45, 0.59, 0.76 s), organic and clustered. Total length is 0.83 s.
differences.b: Onsets are on a near-regular 0.08 s grid (0.05, 0.13, 0.21, 0.29, ...), which sounds mechanical like a ticking clock. The length is correct at 0.83 s, but the tail dies by about 0.73 s.

differences.a: Main snap at 0.31 s is a very sharp, broadband crack from the low end to the highs, peaking above 0 dBFS, with an extremely short transient.
differences.b: The main event at 0.28-0.33 s is a roughly 50 ms wide, thick burst rather than a single crack, with a sustained tonal ping near 1.5 kHz and a weaker line near 4.3 kHz.

differences.a: Almost purely noise and clicks (flatness 0.33), with no sustained tones.
differences.b: Visible stationary tonal lines at about 1.57 kHz (lasting to about 0.44 s) and about 4.3 kHz that sound like beeps or pings; this is out of character for a bug step.

differences.a: Centroid about 6 kHz, rolloff 11 kHz, 25% air, with faint low thumps from 40-200 Hz under the clicks.
differences.b: Centroid about 4.8 kHz, rolloff 8.6 kHz, 19% air, and the mid band is heavier (50% vs 38%). The low end is largely empty except for the big burst, so there are no steady thumps for weight.

differences.a: -18 LUFS, peak +5 dBFS with clipping, and a steady level through the first half.
differences.b: -20.3 LUFS, peak -2.1 dBFS and a lower RMS; perceived loudness is lower because the gaps are quiet.

differences.a: Sparse crackles at 0.59 and 0.76 s, with a fade to silence by about 0.78 s.
differences.b: A few faint ticks at 0.6-0.73 s and then silence; the same general shape but even sparser.

differences.a: Continuous noise bed that swells from 0.06 s to a peak at 0.11 s, then decays smoothly (-20 dB at 0.22 s, -40 dB at 0.37 s) with active fraction 0.72.

differences.a: Dense, wet, rasping chitter, with vertical striations from fast amplitude modulation and a continuous organic noise texture.
differences.b: Reads as discrete clicks, ticks or knocks with short ringing tails, closer to a mechanical tapping or dripping than a creature rasp. Flatness is 0.63 against A's 0.32, so the noise is whiter and less structured.

differences.a: Soft swell into the peak, with only small flutter pulses at about 0.20 s and 0.25 s and one onset detected.
differences.b: Five hard onsets (0.06, 0.14, 0.22, 0.30, 0.39 s) with high crest. The two big peaks near 0.11 and 0.13 s are far louder than anything else, and the waveform spikes are much sharper than A's.

differences.a: Mid formant-like bands around 1-3 kHz at the peak, plus the noise bed. No low-frequency content.
differences.b: Broadband clicks extending down to 20-100 Hz with a strong low-frequency thump at 0.10-0.13 s. No sustained noise bed or clear formant region, only a weak band near 2 kHz.

differences.a: Centroid 10.6 kHz, rolloff 14.5 kHz, with sub and bass at 0%.
differences.b: Centroid 11.7 kHz, rolloff 16.6 kHz and brighter. Sub and bass are 0.4% each, which is small in percentage but visible in the spectrogram as a bright low column at 0.1-0.13 s.

differences.a: 0.59 s, with energy running to about 0.5 s and a gradual fade.
differences.b: 0.59 s, but energy is gone by roughly 0.45 s. Late events (0.39 s, 0.42 s) are faint isolated ticks and the tail is -87 dB at the end.

differences.a: Peak -3.2 dBFS, -20.8 LUFS, RMS -25.6 dB.
differences.b: Peak -2.9 dBFS, -21.2 LUFS, RMS -25.5 dB. True peak is -1.6 dBTP. Overall loudness is well matched, but the energy is concentrated in a few spikes.

differences.a: Faint hissy tail fading smoothly into silence.
differences.b: No continuous hiss tail. Each click has its own short decay, and there is a faint isolated sustain near 0.28-0.35 s.

change_notes: Add a continuous noise layer, high-passed at 3 kHz, with a swell from -35 dB at 0.06 s to the peak at 0.11 s, a decay to -20 dB by 0.22 s and -40 dB by 0.37 s, and a fade to silence by 0.5 s. This should be the main body so active fraction rises from 0.45 to about 0.7.
Apply 30-60 Hz tremolo or granular amplitude modulation with 50-80% depth to the noise bed so it chitters. Randomise the rate by +/-20% over time.
Remove the sub and low content: high-pass everything at 400-500 Hz and delete the thump at 0.10-0.13 s, so sub and bass are 0%.

Soften the clicks: cut the number of hard onsets from 5 to 2-3, with each about 3-5 ms attack and 20-40 ms decay, and lower them to 6-10 dB below the noise-bed peak. Place them at about 0.20 s and 0.25 s to match A's flutter pulses.
Shape the noise with a bandpass formant at 1-3 kHz (Q about 2-3), +6 dB at 0.10-0.14 s, to add the wet rasp. Use a mix of about 25% filtered noise or pitched buzz at 1-3 kHz with 75% broadband hiss.
Lower the spectral flatness toward 0.3-0.4 by low-passing the noise at about 14 kHz, which also moves the centroid to about 10.5 kHz and the rolloff to about 14.5 kHz.
Keep the overall level at about -21 LUFS and cap the peak at -3 dBFS.

review.summary: B is a creature-bite-like burst of about the same length and spectral balance as A, but it has two bursts instead of three tightly clustered chomps, a much shorter body, a stray tonal whistle, a thin low end, and a sparser tail with isolated ticks. Role is recognisable but weight and feel differ.

differences.a: Three clustered chomp bursts at about 0.02, 0.07 and 0.13 s, each with noisy crunch and thick body, forming a dense 0.02-0.18 s mass.
differences.b: Two bursts, a main one at about 0.02-0.08 s and a smaller second hit at about 0.10 s. The third chomp is missing and the gap before the tail is clean.

differences.a: Sustained energy: -20 dB at 0.14 s, -40 dB at 0.43 s. The low rumble and crunchy residue continue to about 0.45 s.
differences.b: Drops faster: -20 dB at 0.07 s, -40 dB at 0.3 s. Active fraction 0.32 vs 0.43. Body dies after about 0.2 s.

differences.a: Strong low thump at 80-300 Hz extending down to about 40 Hz through all bursts, with the lows persisting to about 0.5 s.
differences.b: Low energy is a compact blob at about 150-300 Hz during the first 0.15 s and little below 100 Hz. The lows are thinner and shorter overall, though the band percentages are similar.

differences.a: Mostly noisy and crunchy, flatness 0.20, with a wet organic texture.
differences.b: Flatness 0.32, with an audible narrow tonal line at about 1 kHz (0.06-0.2 s) and a faint line near 3.5 kHz, giving a synthetic beep or whistle character instead of wet chitin.

differences.a: Smooth decaying low rumble with faint scattered clicks, trailing silence 0.17 s.
differences.b: Sparse isolated ticks or bursts at about 0.31, 0.4 and 0.49 s, with dark gaps between them. They read as stray clicks, not a rumble, and trailing silence is 0.22 s.

differences.a: Sharp attack of 0.02 s, with a bright broadband crack on a peak that clips.
differences.b: Similar fast attack of 0.01 s with a bright broadband onset, but about 3 dB lower peak and no clipping. Peak at 0.02 s matches.

differences.a: Integrated -20.3 LUFS, peak +1.3 dBFS with clipping.
differences.b: Integrated -21.6 LUFS, peak -1.9 dBFS, about 1.3 LU quieter. This is within tolerance, and the lack of clipping is an improvement.

differences.a: Centroid starts around 3.5 kHz and varies at 3-5 kHz across the sound.
differences.b: Centroid rises from 4.5 kHz to 6.3 kHz as the lows die, so the tail is brighter and hissier than A's low-weighted tail.

differences.a: 0.725 s, mono, one-shot.
differences.b: 0.73 s, mono, one-shot. Matches.

change_notes: Add a third chomp burst at 0.13 s: 60-80 ms of bandpassed noise (1-6 kHz), -4 dB vs the first burst, with a 5 ms attack. Keep the second at about 0.07 s instead of 0.10 s so the three bursts cluster over 0.02-0.18 s.
Remove or cut the 1 kHz sine line by at least 20 dB, or replace it with a filtered noise formant at 800-1200 Hz. Delete the 3.5 kHz tone.

Lengthen the body: slow the amplitude decay so the level is -20 dB at about 0.14 s and -40 dB at about 0.43 s. Use an exponential tail with a time constant of about 90 ms, instead of the current 0.07 s drop.
Add a low thump layer: a sine sweeping 180 Hz to 60 Hz over 120 ms at each burst, with a -3 dB step per burst, plus lowpassed noise at 40-200 Hz decaying out to 0.45 s at -12 dB under the body.

Replace the isolated tail clicks at 0.31-0.49 s with a continuous low-level crunchy residue: lowpass noise at 1.5 kHz, falling from -30 dB at 0.18 s to -50 dB at 0.45 s. Keep at most 1-2 faint ticks, at least 15 dB below the bursts.
Add wet crunch: 2-3 ms granular noise crackle at 2-8 kHz inside each burst, with random micro-gating at about 200 Hz. Lowering the noise filter tilt should bring flatness toward 0.2.
Raise overall gain about 1.5 dB to land near -20.3 LUFS, keeping the peak at or below -1 dBFS. Limit the highs in the tail so the centroid stays at 3-5 kHz.

review.summary: B is a similar-length bright noisy chitter, but it is built from discrete, sharply separated impact bursts with a clear low-end thump and a quieter overall level, whereas A is a continuous swelling rasp with sustained texture and almost no bass.

differences.a: One continuous noisy rasp that swells from about 0.03 s to a sustained plateau (-11 to -13 dB) through about 0.2 s, then drops about 20 dB by 0.23 s.
differences.b: Separate staccato bursts at roughly 0, 0.06, 0.11, 0.13, 0.19 and 0.22 s, each decaying quickly with gaps between them. The envelope is spiky rather than a swell, and the -40 dB decay time is 0.15 s.

differences.a: Almost no energy below 500 Hz (sub, bass and low_mid all about 0%). The spectrum is all presence and air, with formant blobs at 1-4 kHz.
differences.b: Strong low-frequency blobs at 40-150 Hz at about 0.06, 0.12 and 0.21 s, which give thumpy percussive hits. These are not visible in the band percentages but are clear in the spectrogram.

differences.a: Gritty semi-tonal rasp (flatness 0.13) with formant-like 2-4 kHz blobs and a faint downward streak near 0.18 s. It sounds like a chitinous, vocal insect.
differences.b: Very flat, white-ish noise (flatness 0.58) with a thin steady whistle line near 4.6 kHz. It reads as percussive impacts or a digital beep, not a creature voice.

differences.a: Opening click, rasp body with several small click pulses, and a distinct isolated tick at about 0.27 s.
differences.b: It does have a tick near 0.27 s and a later blip near 0.41 s, but it lacks the tonal 2-4 kHz formant layer, and its hits are large and thumpy rather than small mandible ticks.

differences.a: -13.3 LUFS, RMS -17.4 dB, peak 0 dBFS with one clipped sample, dense sustained energy.
differences.b: -15.7 LUFS, RMS -19.8 dB, peak -1.5 dBFS. The sound is quieter and spikier because there are gaps between hits.

differences.a: Centroid 7.6 kHz, rolloff 10.9 kHz.
differences.b: Centroid 8.4 kHz, rolloff 13.4 kHz, so it is brighter and hissier at the top.

differences.a: Soft opening click at 0 s, then a gradual swell to a peak at 0.11 s, with small ticks along the way.
differences.b: Loud transient at 0 s (-16 dB in the first tenth versus A's -22 dB) and several equally sharp transients after it.

differences.a: The tail after 0.29 s is faint and hissy, with 0.15 s of trailing silence.
differences.b: The tail is darker and sparser, with isolated blips near 0.41 s and 0.46 s and 0.12 s of trailing silence. Both are essentially dry, so this is a small difference.

Remove all content below 400 Hz with a high-pass at about 500 Hz (12-24 dB/oct). This removes the 40-150 Hz thumps.

Reduce noise flatness to about 0.15-0.2: use band-limited, amplitude-modulated noise (60-120 Hz AM, 50-70% depth) instead of white noise, and cut the top above about 11 kHz with a low-pass to bring the rolloff near 11 kHz and the centroid near 7.6 kHz.
Add a formant layer: two band-passed resonances at about 2.0 kHz and 3.2 kHz (Q about 6-8), with a slow downward glide of about 600 Hz around 0.15-0.2 s, at about -10 dB relative to the rasp.
Make the clicks small: 4-5 mandible ticks of 3-5 ms at 0.0, 0.04, 0.08, 0.12 and 0.17 s, band-passed at 2-5 kHz, only +3 to +4 dB above the rasp rather than as large hits.

Keep the isolated snap at 0.26-0.28 s (8-10 ms, 2-10 kHz, about -12 dB relative to the rasp peak). Delete the whistle at 4.6 kHz and the stray tail blips at 0.41 s and 0.46 s; leave only a very faint hiss tail below -60 dB.
Raise the overall level to about -13.3 LUFS (about +2.4 dB) with a limiter ceiling at -1 dBFS. The denser sustained rasp will do most of this work.

review.summary: B is the right kind of sound, a short bright crunchy bite with similar length and spectral balance. Its envelope is clustered differently, with a dip between hits and a weaker low thump, and it is a bit quieter, flatter and more hissy.

differences.a: Dense cluster of 2-3 chomps at ~0.03-0.14 s with continuous energy between them, then a smooth decay (-20 dB at 0.15 s, -40 dB at 0.31 s) with a lingering low thud around 0.24-0.29 s.
differences.b: Strong first hit at 0.03-0.07 s, then a near-gap (~-38 dB in the 0.1 s bucket) before a second burst at ~0.17-0.2 s. The hits read as two separate events rather than a continuous chomp cluster. Reaches -20 dB at 0.02 s.

differences.a: Low body thump (80-300 Hz) is sustained and strong across 0.05-0.3 s, with several pulses and a distinct lower thud at ~0.25 s.
differences.b: Low body is a short, strong pulse under the first hit (20-150 Hz, 0.04-0.07 s) and a weaker one at ~0.19 s. There is no thud at 0.25 s and little weight after 0.2 s.

differences.a: Three or more sharp snaps at about 0.03, 0.07 and 0.12 s, with the highest peaks at ~0.07 and ~0.12 s. Hot, clipped, crunchy.
differences.b: Two main transient groups (0.05 and 0.18 s). Individual snaps are less dense, and the second group is separated by a quiet gap.

differences.a: Flatness 0.14, gritty noise with some resonant content.
differences.b: Flatness 0.46 with a stray tonal line at ~1.4 kHz lasting 0.05-0.17 s. This sounds like an artificial whistle or resonance. The rest is more hissy.

differences.a: Centroid 6.2 kHz, rolloff 8.4 kHz. The centroid falls from 6.4 kHz to 1.3 kHz as the sound decays, so the tail gets darker.
differences.b: Centroid 6.7 kHz, rolloff 10.3 kHz. The centroid stays at 6.4-7.3 kHz, so the tail stays bright and hissy rather than darkening.

differences.a: -19.7 LUFS, peak +4.9 dBFS (clipped).
differences.b: -22.0 LUFS, peak -3.2 dBFS. About 2.3 LU quieter, but within the +/-3 LU target. The peak is safe.

differences.a: Quiet noisy tail with faint clicks to ~0.65 s.
differences.b: Noise tail to ~0.6 s with a 0.19 s gap at the end, a bit more audible and flat. It cuts off sharply at ~0.61 s.

differences.a: 0.725 s, active energy through ~0.3 s.
differences.b: 0.73 s, active energy through ~0.37 s.

Add a low thud at 0.22-0.29 s: a sine at ~120 Hz falling to 70 Hz over 80 ms, with a 10 ms attack and 60 ms decay, about 6 dB below the main body. Extend the 100-250 Hz body layer under 0.05-0.2 s with a 150 ms decay so it rises with each chomp.

Reduce noise flatness: swap some white noise in the chomps for bandpassed crunch or short resonant clicks at 3-6 kHz, targeting flatness ~0.2.

Raise the level by ~2 dB to reach about -20 LUFS while keeping the peak at about -1 to -2 dBFS. Keep the first hit slightly stronger than the later ones, as in A, whose strongest peaks are the second and third chomps.
Shape the tail so the noise fades smoothly to silence by ~0.6 s with a 100 ms fade-out, avoiding the abrupt cutoff.

review.summary: B has the right length and overall loudness, but it is a sustained, sub-heavy boom with a pulsing body instead of A's instant-crack, fast-decaying punchy shot. It sounds darker, longer and more like a rumble or explosion than a submachine-gun round.

differences.a: Instant full-scale onset at 0 s with a broadband crack reaching 10 kHz+. The first tenth sits at -2.7 dB and the peak is at 0 s.
differences.b: Attack takes about 10 ms and the first tenth is at -6.8 dB. There is no sharp crack, and the waveform starts as a blunt, rounded body.

differences.a: Monotonic fast decay: -8, -12.5, -21.7 dB over the first 0.3 s, then -20 dB at 0.2 s.
differences.b: Energy is held and re-swells: -11, -8.2 (louder than the previous tenth), then about -20 dB through 0.3 s. It reaches -20 dB only at 0.31 s, so the body is sustained and bumpy. Waveform shows pulsing bursts.

differences.a: Centroid about 1.1 kHz, rolloff 1.55 kHz. Energy is 10% sub, 27% bass, 37% low-mid, 15% mid.
differences.b: Centroid about 700 Hz, rolloff 991 Hz. Energy is 29% sub, 35% bass, 21% low-mid and 11% mid, so it is much heavier and darker, with weak mids and highs.

differences.a: Noisy mid crack over a thump (flatness 0.076) with ragged noise texture.
differences.b: More tonal, sustained sub drone (flatness 0.047). The noise is thin and brief. It reads as a boom rather than a gun.

differences.a: Short, dark, ragged room tail fading by about 0.48 s, with irregular low-frequency texture.
differences.b: Low-frequency sustain is held to about 0.42 s, then drops abruptly. The tail has rhythmic amplitude modulation (pulsing about every 30-40 ms) that sounds artificial. Cleaner fade at 0.55 s.

differences.a: 0.60 s file with 0.12 s trailing silence, -40 dB at 0.48 s.
differences.b: 0.60 s file with 0.08 s trailing silence, -40 dB at 0.50 s. Active fraction is 0.68 vs 0.53, so it feels longer.

differences.a: Peak -0.8 dBFS, RMS -14.3, -15.3 LUFS.
differences.b: Peak -1.2 dBFS, RMS -14.6, -16.3 LUFS. Close, but the loudness is carried by sub energy rather than the crack.

differences.a: Crack burst + thump + dark room tail.
differences.b: Mostly a single sub-heavy rumble layer with a weak noise layer. No distinct crack layer, and the rhythmic modulation is an unneeded layer.

missing_elements: Sharp 5-10 ms broadband crack with energy up to 10 kHz+
Strong 1-2 kHz mid noise body
Fast monotonic decay of the body
Ragged, irregular room tail texture

Periodic amplitude pulsing (about 25-35 Hz) in the body and tail

change_notes: Add a crack layer: white noise, high-passed at 1.5 kHz and extended to 10 kHz+, 8 ms with an exponential decay and a 0-1 ms attack, at 0 s, about +6 dB over the body. Make the peak -0.8 dBFS at t=0.
Shorten the sub: pitch the thump from about 110 Hz down to 45 Hz over 100 ms, with an amplitude decay time constant of about 60 ms. Cut sub energy from 29% to about 10% (roughly -8 dB).
Add a mid noise body: bandpass 300-1500 Hz, 0-0.2 s, decaying to -20 dB by 0.2 s. This lifts the centroid to about 1.1 kHz and low-mid to about 37%.
Remove the periodic amplitude modulation and the re-swell. Use a monotonic envelope: -8 dB at 0.1 s, -12 dB at 0.2 s, -22 dB at 0.3 s, -40 dB at 0.48 s.
Make the tail a dark noise tail: lowpass about 800 Hz, 0.2-0.48 s, with irregular, non-periodic reflections (2-3 random echoes at 20-60 ms, -18 dB) rather than regular pulses.
Fade to silence by about 0.48 s, leaving 0.12 s of trailing silence. Keep the file at 0.6 s, mono, peak about -1 dBFS, and target -15.3 LUFS.

review.summary: B is the right kind of sound (a low-mid mechanical press thud with a gritty rumbling decay) and matches A closely in length, loudness and band balance. It differs in that it hits earlier and harder as a single sharp slam, lacks A's early 450 Hz tonal hum, and has a brighter, less darkening tail.

differences.a: Gradual build: a soft rumble with a faint 450 Hz band from 0 s rises over ~0.2 s to a peak at 0.2 s, with a small clank near 0.2 s and another bump around 0.4 s. Few hard transients.
differences.b: Near-silent start (~0.03 s leading silence, -56 dB in the first tenth) then an abrupt, sharp full-band slam at ~0.16-0.17 s with a vertical click reaching the top of the spectrum. It reads as a single hard hit.

differences.a: Sustained tonal band near 450 Hz from 0 to ~0.3 s under a continuous grind, plus a precursor at 0.05 s and a mid clank at 0.2 s.
differences.b: Only a weak ~300 Hz band appears after the hit. The pre-hit section is faint, with little pre-roll energy. A bass thump dominates the impact with a bright click on top.

differences.a: Centroid ~867 Hz, darkening strongly across the sound (425, 568, 468, 232 Hz by quarter). The late tail is mostly low rumble.
differences.b: Overall centroid is similar (807 Hz), but it stays bright through the tail (879, 1129, 1218, 933 Hz). The tail keeps mid and upper-mid noise, with peaks at 2.4 and 3.6 kHz, instead of falling to bass.

differences.a: Peak at 0.2 s, -20 dB at 0.34 s, -40 dB at 0.62 s, tail gone by ~0.85 s, 0.23 s trailing silence.
differences.b: Peak at 0.16 s (~40 ms earlier), -20 dB at 0.28 s, -40 dB at 0.61 s, tail gone by ~0.77 s, 0.29 s trailing silence. The decay shape is close, but the hit is earlier and the end slightly shorter.

differences.a: Pre-peak ramp is substantial (-41 dB at tenth 0, -22 dB at 0.1 s), and the sustain is rattly, with strong pulsing striations down to ~0.8 s.
differences.b: Ramp-up is much lower (-56, -24 dB), and the sustain is rougher and more random than pulsed. The tail drops faster after 0.7 s (-71.6 dB vs -62 dB at tenth 9) and then goes fully silent.

differences.a: Gritty noise bed with a distinct tonal mechanical component near 450 Hz. Very low spectral flatness (0.005).
differences.b: Noisier and less tonal (flatness 0.011), with a granular mid texture.

differences.a: Peak -3.0 dBFS, RMS -21.5, -19.8 LUFS.
differences.b: Peak -2.0 dBFS, RMS -21.4, -20.1 LUFS. This is within tolerance, though the crest factor is slightly higher (19.4 vs 18.5 dB).

missing_elements: Sustained ~450 Hz tonal mechanical hum/band during the first 0.3 s
Slow 0.2 s build-up and rumble before the main clunk
Distinct pulsing/rattling low-frequency striations in the 0.4-0.8 s tail
Darkening of the tail toward ~230 Hz centroid
Secondary clank/bump around 0.4 s
extra_elements: Sharp broadband click at ~0.16 s reaching the top of the spectrum
Strong sub/bass thump (20-100 Hz) at the moment of impact

change_notes: Add a pre-roll: a 450 Hz band-passed tone (Q ~6, plus a 900 Hz harmonic at -12 dB) with grind noise, rising from -35 dB at 0 s to about -15 dB at 0.18 s. Start it at 0 s, not 0.03 s, so the first tenth sits near -40 dB rather than -56 dB.
Move the main clunk from 0.16 s to ~0.20 s and soften it. Cut the full-band click to ~5 ms and lower it 8-10 dB, with a lowpass at ~6 kHz. Increase the attack to ~0.15-0.2 s on the body layer.

Darken the tail: sweep a lowpass on the noise bed from ~3 kHz at 0.25 s down to ~600 Hz by 0.7 s, so the final-quarter centroid falls to ~250 Hz instead of ~930 Hz. Reduce the 2.4/3.6 kHz noise content by ~8 dB after 0.3 s.
Add rattle to the tail from 0.4 to 0.8 s: amplitude-modulate the 100-400 Hz noise with a 25-40 Hz pulse train at 50-70% depth, plus a small clank (a 450 Hz, 40 ms ring) at ~0.4 s, -15 dB.
Reduce the impact sub thump slightly (20-100 Hz, -3 dB) to keep sub at about 2.4% and bass near 28%. Lower the peak to about -3 dBFS and extend the tail fade to ~0.85 s to match A's -62 dB at 0.9 s.
Keep the total length at 1.06 s with roughly 0.2 s trailing silence.

review.summary: B matches A's length, mono format and silent gap layout, but fills the first half with dense, evenly spaced soft clicks and a loud, low-heavy bolt section, so the reload reads less like clean distinct foley hits and the stage pacing and weight differ.

differences.a: First half has a few distinct hits: a double clack at 0.05/0.15 s, quiet rattles, one big mag-seat slap at ~0.62-0.68 s, and a faint tick at 0.83 s.
differences.b: First half has about 9 evenly spaced similar clicks and ticks (0.05-0.83 s) with a typewriter-like, repetitive feel. No single dominant mag-seat hit.

differences.a: Hits are broadband from sub to 10 kHz with a low thump under each clack, mid-heavy (58% mid). Bass is nearly absent in measurement but the spectrogram shows vertical strokes down to 20 Hz.
differences.b: First half is thin and hissy with energy mostly above 1 kHz and little thump. The bolt section has a loud 40-150 Hz boom plus a ~250 Hz tone, which is a heavy sustained low body that A lacks.

differences.a: Noisy, gritty and percussive, with spectral flatness of 0.035 and a mostly impulsive texture.
differences.b: Flatness of 0.219 with sustained hissy noise beds between clicks, tonal artifacts (~1.2 kHz and ~4.5 kHz lines at 0.55 s, peaks at 7.8/9.2/12.6 kHz) and a ~250 Hz tone in the bolt.

differences.a: Sharp transients that decay fast (-20 dB in 0.09 s, -40 dB in 0.16 s), with gaps of near-silence between hits.
differences.b: Slower, smeared decays (0.13 s to -20 dB), with a continuous low-level noise bed (active fraction 0.70 vs 0.52). The bolt is a swollen blob about 0.15 s long instead of two distinct clacks.

review.summary: B has the right kind of sound: a loud, sub-heavy noisy blast with a debris tail, and the same length, peak time and band balance. It differs in the middle and the tail. Its debris is sparse, pitched, ringing clicks after a hard cutoff near 1.0 s, where A has a continuous rumbling roll-off, and B is a bit quieter overall.

differences.a: Continuous, smooth decay. Dense rumbling noise holds from 0.13 s to about 0.7 s, then falls steadily (-20 dB at 0.96 s, -40 dB at 1.93 s) with no gap before the rattles.
differences.b: Body is flat to about 0.75-1.0 s, then drops abruptly (tenth-envelope -14.6 to -34 dB) into isolated transients with near-silence between them. Reaches -40 dB sooner (1.72 s).

differences.b: Tail is about 12 discrete, widely spaced ping or clack hits. The spectrogram shows vertical streaks reaching up to 10 kHz and a gappy, ticking feel. They sound like pops or gunfire (per Qwen), not falling debris.

differences.a: Highs vanish quickly after about 0.7 s; the tail is almost entirely below 200 Hz, with centroid dropping to 23-52 Hz in later quarters.
differences.b: Every debris hit brings back broadband mid/high energy, so the centroid rises to about 1-3 kHz in later quarters. The tail is much brighter and thinner than A's.

review.summary: B matches A's length, loudness and broad band split, but its structure differs. It has one big opening hit, then a sagging middle and a dead gap near 1.85 s. A is a series of distinct growl bursts, including a second big roar at about 2.05 s. B reads as a synthetic, tonal, formant-banded drone rather than a rough vocal growl.

differences.a: Several distinct growl bursts: opening growl at 0.05 s, sustained roar 0.37-1.15 s, bark accent at about 1.25 s, second big roar 2.05-2.8 s, weak pulses near 2.83 s and 3.11 s.
differences.b: One big opening hit at 0.05-0.2 s, a sagging mid section and a weak low swell around 2.2-2.4 s. It does not read as a clear sequence of 2-3 roars or a bark accent.

differences.a: Moderate attack (0.08 s) with a rough growl onset. Several secondary onsets (9 detected) give a bursty, vocal rhythm.
differences.b: Sharp broadband blast at the start, with peak -2.6 dBFS and a much higher waveform spike than the rest. Only 4 onsets are detected, at 0.05, 0.37, 1.4 and 1.9 s. The later sections lack A's defined re-attacks.

differences.a: Rough, throaty, modulated vocal growl with formant-like harmonic ladders and a dense low body at 100-450 Hz. Spectral flatness is 0.001.
differences.b: Static horizontal bands at about 690 Hz, 1.1 kHz, 1.7 kHz and 2.5 kHz that hold for the whole clip, which sounds like a fixed-formant synth or drone. It sits on a broadband noise bed up to 10 kHz+. Qwen heard a sine and chirp with an electronic quality. Flatness is 0.008, noisier, and it does not read as a creature.

differences.a: Swells and drops. A loud roar at 0.4-1.1 s, a second roar at 2.05-2.8 s as the loudest sustained section, then a gradual fade. -40 dB is reached at 3.59 s.
differences.b: Level drops from the opening hit, with -40 dB at 1.67 s. There is a near-silent notch at about 1.85 s, then a weak second swell and a fade. The loudness range is 8 LU against A's 3.3.

differences.b: Centroid 1062 Hz, rolloff 1.79 kHz. Hiss and haze extend up to 10 kHz+ throughout, brighter and harsher. The band percentages happen to match, but the shape differs.

differences.a: The body energy sits at 100-450 Hz, with the biggest energy around 200-500 Hz in the second roar. Harmonics shift between bursts like a living voice.
differences.b: The body is more sub-heavy and bass-heavy in the opening hit, with a fixed 690 Hz band. No vocal pitch contour or per-burst variation.

review.summary: B is the right kind of sound: a ~2 s low growl with weak muttering phrases followed by a louder roar. Length, loudness and band balance match A closely. The main gaps are timing and structure: B has a late, short climax with an abrupt cut-off, and it adds a 2.6 kHz tone and hiss that A lacks.

differences.b: Second phrase builds gradually from ~1.2 s to a single spike near 1.65 s, then drops within ~0.15 s. It reads as a swell-and-burst rather than a sustained roar. The first half has an uneven bump near 0.2 s (-18 dB tenth) that is louder than A's opening.

differences.a: Starts almost immediately (0.01 s lead silence), is active 95% of the time, has a near-silent gap at 1.15-1.23 s, and ends with a 0.04 s tail.

review.summary: B is the right kind of sound: a sub-heavy giant footstep of the same length, loudness, band balance and onset count. Its envelope is more compact and cleaner than A, with a later start, a faster decay and almost no tail, and the top end is less continuous and less gritty.

differences.a: Dense energy from 0.02 s, peak at 0.14 s, then -40 dB at about 0.22 s after the peak. Decaying thumps keep going to about 0.4 s, with envelope around -34 to -45 dB through 0.3-0.7 s.
differences.b: Starts later and rises faster. Peak at 0.13 s, then -40 dB by 0.13 s. Energy falls into a near-silent gap around 0.26-0.30 s and becomes sparse after 0.35 s, so the body is shorter and punchier.

differences.a: Leading silence 0.01 s, trailing 0.03 s, active fraction 0.6. Lead-in rumble scuffs start at about 0.02 s, so the sound fills the 0.53 s clip.

differences.a: Quiet debris and rumble tail with sparse ticks to about 0.5 s, which gives the step some room and weight.

differences.a: Several staggered low pulses ramp up over 0.13 s from small scuffs, with a brief 5-10 kHz bright burst at about 0.16 s.
differences.b: Faster 0.08 s attack with discrete broadband clicks at about 0.10, 0.13, 0.19-0.21, 0.24 and 0.29 s that reach the top of the spectrum. They are brighter and more clicky and extend past 10 kHz.

differences.a: Dense, rumbly, organic texture with a continuous mid-band bloom of 100-1000 Hz scuffs (centroid by quarter 308/125/2152/4461 Hz).

differences.b: Steady, buzzy drone with stationary horizontal bands near 500, 900 and 1000 Hz and a tonal line at about 2.6 kHz. Reads more synthetic or mechanical, and Qwen heard metallic scraping and buzzing.

review.summary: B is the right kind of sound, a gated train of bright tonal beeps at the same length and loudness. It has a slower, uneven pulse rate (about 12 bursts against A's 13), a heavy low-frequency rumble under each beep, and a darker, less buzzy top end.

differences.a: Almost no energy below 1 kHz. Spectrum is clean and bright with a centroid of about 6.8 kHz, and the main lines are at 1.2 kHz, 4 kHz, 7.9 kHz and 9.3 kHz.
differences.b: Strong sub and bass smear below 200 Hz in every burst, brightest in the first burst and at about 0.4 s. The centroid is lower at about 5.3 kHz, and the peaks sit at 4.1 kHz, 7.3 kHz and 7.8 kHz.

differences.a: About 13 bursts, each roughly 40 ms on, evenly spaced with onsets near 0.08 s. Active fraction is 0.91, so the gaps are short.
differences.b: About 12 bursts with a slightly longer period, and the waveform shows uneven spacing with occasional extra-long gaps. Active fraction is 0.83, and the train looks looser and less dense.

differences.a: Pitch is constant across all bursts, so the tone is steady and mechanical.
differences.b: Per-burst pitch wobbles. Lines drift down to about 3.7 kHz on some bursts and up on the final bursts, so it sounds slightly warbly and less uniform.

differences.a: Buzzy, metallic, harmonic-rich square-like tone with a strong 1.2 kHz formant band and broadband gating clicks.
differences.b: Cleaner thin lines with a weaker 1.2 kHz body. The low rumble gives a thumpy, boing-like feel instead of a sharp electronic chirp.

differences.a: Hard gating with a near-instant attack and a sharp drop. Gaps sit about 20 dB or more down, and a tiny blip trails at about 0.52 s.
differences.b: Similarly gated, but the gaps are filled with low-frequency energy. The ending blip is louder and sits at 0.53 s.

differences.b: -24.5 LUFS, peak -14.9 dBFS, RMS -27.6 dBFS.

differences.b: No tail, ending abruptly on a burst, with no significant reverb.

review.summary: B matches A's length, onset count and onset times (14 onsets, ~0.07-1.89 s), loudness and general beepy-robotic role, but it is a sparse set of discrete beeps with silence between them. A is a continuous, dense texture with a constant 7.3 kHz whine, a broadband haze and a pitched warble cluster.

differences.a: Continuous bed: a constant 7.3 kHz whine across the whole sound, plus broadband noise haze and fine ticks between the main beeps.
differences.b: No continuous bed. Isolated beep bursts, with true silence (about -70 to -135 dB) in the gaps. The 7.1 kHz tone appears only inside some beeps.

differences.a: Active about 89% of the time. Level stays around -25 to -45 dB per tenth and the sound ends in a hard cutoff at 2.05 s.
differences.b: Active only about 54%. Levels drop to -50 to -70 dB between beeps and the sound fades out. A has a steady ratchet-like chatter, while B has gaps and stutters.

differences.a: Peaks at 7.27 kHz, 2.7 kHz and 1 kHz. Centroid is about 4.2 kHz, and every quarter of the sound stays bright (6.9, 3.4, 7.0, 6.0 kHz).
differences.b: Peaks at 1 kHz, 5.5 kHz and 7.1 kHz. Centroid is about 3.3 kHz. Quarters swing from 2.2 kHz to 6.7 kHz to 1.3 kHz, so the sound is uneven and some segments are dark.

differences.a: The 0.4-0.9 s cluster is three louder, vocal-like warbles with a fundamental of 800-1000 Hz and a harmonic ladder up to 5 kHz, stepping upward. There is another harmonic beep near 1.8 s.
differences.b: Clean, static-pitch beeps. The strongest are a ~1 kHz pair at 0.1-0.3 s and another at ~1.7 s. Higher beeps are pure tones near 3 and 5.5 kHz. There is no warble or rich harmonic ladder, and the loud section is in the wrong place (0.1-0.35 s rather than 0.4-0.9 s).

differences.a: Gritty, noisy, chirpy and organic-robotic, with a vocal-like babble.
differences.b: Clean, sine-like tones with sharp thin harmonics. Reads as UI or notification beeps rather than a turret chatter.

differences.a: Soft ticks about every 0.11 s on a bed, each decaying in about 0.11 s to -20 dB.
differences.b: Each beep has a sharp low thump and click at onset, plus a strong sub-bass/bass pulse (energy down to 20-100 Hz) that A does not have. Beeps are 60-100 ms plateaus with quick decays.

differences.a: Integrated -26.8 LUFS, peak -12.4 dBFS, loudest in the 0.3-0.9 s section.
differences.b: Integrated -26.8 LUFS, peak -12.7 dBFS, but loudest around 0.1-0.35 s. The loudness distribution over time differs.

differences.a: 2.24 s, with a cutoff at 2.05 s and 0.14 s of trailing silence. Onsets are regular.
differences.b: 2.24 s with onsets matching within about 30 ms. It has 0.06 s of leading silence and 0.24 s of trailing silence, with a decaying low-frequency tail rather than a hard cutoff.

change_notes: Add a continuous 7.27 kHz sine whine from 0 to 2.05 s at about -45 dB relative to the beep peaks, and cut it hard at 2.05 s (<5 ms fade). B's gaps should never fall below about -50 dB.

Rebuild the 0.4-0.9 s section as three loud warble beeps (about 120 ms each, gaps of 30-50 ms) with fundamentals of 800, 900 and 1000 Hz (stepping up), a sawtooth or FM source (ratio 2-3, index 2-4) to give a harmonic ladder to ~5 kHz, and +5 dB over the ticks. review.summary: B is the right kind of sound: a 1.46 s low-mid growl with matching loudness, band balance and a second pulse. But its envelope is wrong: a sharp transient hit at ~0.2 s, a steep drop at ~0.8 s instead of A's gradual decay, and a tonal, whistly upper register instead of A's smooth noisy growl.

differences.a: Gradual swell from a faint onset at 0.06 s to a peak at ~0.21 s. No distinct click; the body rises smoothly with a ragged amplitude.
differences.b: Sudden, loud burst at ~0.18-0.21 s that stands well above the surrounding body in the waveform and brightens the whole spectrum up to 10 kHz. It reads as a hit or punch rather than a swell.

differences.a: Stays high and ragged through ~0.6 s, dips near 0.65 s, has a second bump at 0.93 s, and decays slowly (-20 dB at 1.05 s, -40 dB at 1.21 s).
differences.b: Reaches -20 dB by 0.6 s, has a clear drop at ~0.8 s, then a quieter second section, and ends with ~0.11 s of silence. The main growl is shorter and the dynamics are more front-loaded.

differences.a: Centroid ~1.27 kHz, falling from ~1.1 kHz to ~0.6 kHz by the end as the sound darkens. Energy is dense at 100-450 Hz, with a warm roll-off.
differences.b: Centroid ~1.42 kHz and roughly flat across the sound (1.2-1.6 kHz). It stays brighter in the last quarter, so it does not darken toward the tail. Overall band percentages are nearly identical to A.

differences.a: Very low flatness (0.002) with a smooth, dense, gritty vocal growl and a continuous harmonic wash. No isolated spectral lines.
differences.b: Flatness 0.036, with stable horizontal bands at ~0.7, 1.2, 1.7 and 2.6 kHz. These sit as fixed formant or tonal lines that sound synthetic, whistly or vowel-like rather than a growl.

differences.a: Vertically striated vocal-fold growl texture, rough and organic, with noisy harmonics up to 5-8 kHz in the main peak.
differences.b: Similar low-frequency striations, but the upper range is a static tonal comb plus a bright burst. It sounds more like a synth or electronic voice than a creature.

differences.a: 1.463 s with 0.04 s trailing silence. Second pulse onset at 0.93 s; the active body runs to ~1.4 s.
differences.b: 1.46 s, but 0.11 s trailing silence and a second section that starts earlier and fades sooner. Active fraction 0.88 vs 0.95.

differences.a: Peak -16.9 dBFS, RMS -26.3 dBFS, active fraction 0.87, so a steady, present beep.

differences.a: Very tonal (flatness 0.004), with strong steady lines and a harmonic comb of buzz.

differences.b: Static lines at the same frequencies but no stepping or audible pitch change.

differences.b: More synthetic, buzzy/metallic tone with stable horizontal formant lines near 1.1, 1.7 and 2.5 kHz; flatness 0.024; reads as mechanical rather than creature.

differences.b: 3.93 s with ~1.0 s silence; main accent at 0.64 s.

review.summary: B is the right kind of sound, a bright electronic double-beep pair at the same 0.62 s length with matching partials and loudness. But its beeps are longer and more evenly spaced, and its low-end sustain is much heavier, so the crisp 'bi-dip' tick and the quiet tail of A are lost.

differences.a: Each group is a short main beep (~20 ms) followed by a quieter blip ~25 ms later, so the pair is very tight. The groups start at ~0.01 s and ~0.385 s.
differences.b: The two pulses in each group are ~60-70 ms long and start ~60 ms apart (0.0 and 0.07 s, then 0.38 and 0.44 s), so they read as two equal beeps, not a 'bi-dip'. The first group is also slightly early at ~0.0 s.

differences.a: Instant attack, ~20 ms plateau, -20 dB in 20 ms and -40 dB in 50 ms. Very staccato, with a quieter second blip.
differences.b: Pulses sustain ~50-60 ms with a gated, boxy shape. -40 dB takes ~130 ms. The two pulses are near equal in level, so there is no dynamic bi-dip.

differences.a: Almost no energy below 200 Hz except a brief thump at each onset. Band energy is mid 29%, presence 54%, air 17%.
differences.b: A continuous red low-frequency bed below ~200 Hz runs across the whole file, strongest at the start. The sustained bass/sub makes it muddier, with presence at 49% and a lower centroid (6.5 kHz against 6.8 kHz).

differences.a: A faint tonal tail around 1.2 kHz and 4 kHz and low rumble residue, with the main hits drying quickly. Between groups there is a barely audible tick at ~0.12-0.2 s.
differences.b: The gap between groups is completely empty above 300 Hz, with no residual tick or tail. The low bed lingers faintly instead and there is a weak pulse at ~0.6 s.

differences.a: Peak -14 dBFS, crest 21 dB, RMS -35 dB. Loudness comes from sharp transients.
differences.b: Peak -18.8 dBFS, crest 16 dB, with the same integrated loudness (-31.3 LUFS). Energy is spread over longer sustained pulses, so it has a weaker transient punch.

differences.a: Sharp click-like onset with a broadband burst and a low thump.

review.summary: B has the same overall structure as A: two ticks, a gap, a run of clacks and a heavy final clunk, all in 0.81 s at matching loudness. review.summary: B matches A's length, loudness and overall click-cluster rhythm, but it is much more tonal and synthetic. It has a sustained bed, steady resonant whistle lines, and a heavy sub thump in place of A's crisp, noisy metallic clacks. It reads as a digital ticking machine rather than a gun action being racked.

differences.b: Flatness is 0.39, and the spectrogram shows steady narrow tonal lines at ~1.36 kHz, ~3.7 kHz, ~7.8 kHz and ~9.2 kHz held over 0-0.06 s and 0.18-0.25 s. These read as beeps or whistles rather than metal impacts.

differences.a: Click-clack pairs with a small low thump (100-400 Hz) only on the heavier hits at 0.07, 0.19 and 0.33 s.

change_notes: Lower the master level by about 10 dB so the peak is about -13 dBFS and RMS about -29 dBFS. The brief's -1 dBFS ceiling is a cap, not the target; A sits much lower.
Remove or high-pass the sub-bass layer at 20-100 Hz (HPF at 500 Hz or higher, or delete the layer). Keep only about -60 dB of mid content if needed for small-speaker audibility.
Replace the blocky, gapped gating with a continuous plateau: attack in under 5 ms, level flat within ±3 dB from 0 to 0.155 s, then a 5-10 ms fade-out and a cut.

Add about 30 Hz amplitude modulation at 40-60% depth on the three partials (9.6, 13.1, 16.2 kHz). Use slightly detuned or phase-offset modulation per partial for the metallic buzz, and 4-5 gentle level bursts of ±3 dB.
Remove the 0.08-0.13 s broadband noise burst, or reduce it to a very quiet 8-16 kHz noise layer at -50 dB or lower relative to the tones.
Remove the clicks at 0.01 s and 0.18 s by adding 2-3 ms fades on every block edge. Then add a faint 0.16-0.26 s tail with thin high lines at about -55 to -65 dB.

review.summary: B is the right kind of sound, an explosive burst with a rumble and debris tail, with matching length, band balance and loudness. Its envelope is more distinct, with a dense body to ~1 s, then a sharp cutoff into sparse, isolated, bright pings that sound like ticking rather than A's continuous granular rumble.

differences.a: Smooth, continuous decay: -20 dB at 0.92 s, -40 dB at 2.32 s, with a long rumbling tail that fades steadily.
differences.b: Body holds to ~1.0 s, then drops abruptly to a very quiet floor (about -42 to -52 dB). -40 dB is reached at 1.4 s, so the tail is much shorter and more gated.

differences.a: 0.45-1.4 s has dense low-frequency thuds and granular debris pulses every 0.08-0.15 s. Later, sparse faint clicks sit over a continuous sub rumble.
differences.b: After 1.0 s there are only ~10 isolated, widely spaced bright debris pings over a near-empty bed, and no onsets are detected in the first second. They read as clock ticks (per Qwen) rather than rumbling debris.

differences.a: Centroid 854 Hz. The first 0.4 s is bright, noisy and crunchy up to ~10 kHz. The late tail collapses to ~35 Hz sub-only rumble.
differences.b: Overall centroid 707 Hz, rolloff 1.6 kHz versus A's 2.9 kHz. Centroid rises across the quarters (573, 1059, 2575, 1530 Hz) because the late tail is just bright pings with no sub bed, the reverse of A's trajectory.

differences.a: Fast attack, peak at 0.16 s, with a dense crunchy broadband burst and a narrow ~3 kHz tonal spike. Clipped.
differences.b: Peak at 0.13 s, a similar noisy burst but less bright at the top, no 3 kHz spike, and a quieter first tenth (-18 dB vs -10 dB). Roughly comparable impact.

differences.a: Continuous granular crackling rumble, chaotic and organic.
differences.b: Wide dark-to-bright sweeps and tonal hits with vertical streaks. Clean and gated with sparse pings, so it feels more like discrete events.

differences.a: -15.9 LUFS, peak +2.5 dBFS (clipped), RMS -15.4 dB.
differences.b: -18.1 LUFS, peak -1.3 dBFS, no clipping. About 2 LU quieter, within tolerance and the cleaner choice.

differences.a: 3.05 s with 0.32 s trailing silence. Sound fades out around 2.7 s.
differences.b: 3.05 s with 0.34 s trailing silence. Active fraction 0.68 vs 0.75, so audible content is slightly shorter.

Dense granular debris and thud pulses between 0.45 and 1.0 s

change_notes: Add a continuous sub rumble bed (20-120 Hz, low-passed noise plus a 40-60 Hz sine) from 0 to 2.6 s, with an exponential decay giving -20 dB at ~0.9 s and -40 dB at ~2.3 s. This removes the gated cutoff at 1.0 s, so the tail sits ~-30 to -40 dB until 2.3 s instead of -42 to -52 dB.
Remove the abrupt level drop at 1.0 s. Crossfade the body into the rumble bed over ~300 ms, and keep the body envelope around -20 dB at 0.9 s and -29 dB by 1.3 s.

Replace the sparse pings with dense granular debris: 8-15 ms noise grains (200-2000 Hz band-pass) at ~80-150 ms intervals from 0.45 to 1.4 s, with random amplitudes of -6 to -18 dB, thinning to one grain per ~300 ms after 1.4 s.

Reduce ping brightness and level. Keep post-1 s hits mostly under 2 kHz at about -12 dB relative to the burst, and soften their attacks (3-5 ms) so they don't read as clock ticks. Drop the late hits at 2.28 s and 2.57 s or make them very faint.

Brighten the first 0.4 s. Add a 0.3-0.4 s noise burst with a lowpass sweeping 10 kHz to 2 kHz, +4 dB above the current top end, to raise the rolloff toward ~2.5-3 kHz. Optionally add a short 3 kHz metallic ping at 0 s, -25 dB.
Keep the peak near -1 dBFS. Raise the overall level ~2 dB (target -16 LUFS), for example with a gentle soft clip at the burst, to match A's weight without clipping.

review.summary: B matches A's length, peak level, loudness and sub/bass weight, but it is a cleaner, more segmented set of low pulses with a thinner crunchy mid layer and an emptier tail. It reads as a heavy footstep, but less like one gritty stomp with a rumble tail.

differences.a: One continuous swell to a peak at 0.15s (attack ~0.14s), then a steady decay through 0.3s. Energy stays dense and rumbling from 0.05 to 0.32s, and the envelope is smooth.
differences.b: Splits into several discrete pulses at ~0.05, 0.13 and 0.25s, with a dip near 0.14-0.2s (envelope -35 dB at the 0.4 tenth). The hit has an uneven 'bump-bump-bump' stutter and a quicker attack (0.09s).

differences.a: Gritty, crunchy, debris-like rumble with dense mid texture (200 Hz-3 kHz) and scattered gravel-like energy through the body.
differences.b: Smoother, cleaner synthetic thump. The mid crunch is a short blob around 0.1-0.2s (~300 Hz-1 kHz) and is less dense, with stray vertical clicks at 0.25-0.36s that read as separate ticks and not a scrape.

differences.a: Rumble and debris continue to ~0.32s with a small bump at 0.22s, then fade to near silence, with only faint codec-like HF ticks after 0.43s.
differences.b: Body ends around 0.22s, followed by low-level periodic sub pulses (~86 Hz) to ~0.36s and a single vertical click at ~0.36s. Trailing silence is 0.17s versus 0.03s, so the sound feels shorter and tails off in a different way.

differences.a: Active fraction 0.6, with energy from ~0.02 to 0.32s and nearly no leading gap (0.01s).
differences.b: Active fraction 0.44, leading silence 0.04s, with the main body concentrated at 0.05-0.22s.

differences.a: Sub 65%, bass 25%. Broad low-frequency energy from 20 to ~200 Hz, with an 85% rolloff of ~129 Hz.
differences.b: Sub 65%, bass 23%, so the balance is nearly identical, but energy is concentrated in a band at ~60-100 Hz with a visible floor around 20-50 Hz. The rolloff is lower (65 Hz), so it is a bit more tonal and boomy and less broadband.

differences.a: Noisy and non-tonal, with a fairly flat low-frequency spread and no sharp tonal peak.
differences.b: A clearer tonal peak at ~86 Hz (a pitched boom) with a cleaner noise floor, and weaker upper-band noise above 2 kHz.

differences.a: Peak -2.9 dBFS, -22.7 LUFS.
differences.b: Peak -2.9 dBFS, -23.0 LUFS.

change_notes: Merge the pulses into one stomp: use a single sub thump (40-80 Hz sine with a slight downward pitch glide, 90 to 50 Hz over 150 ms) with ~100-120 ms attack, peak at 0.15s, then exponential decay reaching -20 dB at ~0.09s after the peak. Remove or reduce the separate hits at 0.05/0.13/0.25s to below -25 dB relative.

Add a continuous gritty mid layer: band-passed noise at 200 Hz-3 kHz (plus some granular gravel ticks of 5-15 ms at 20-40 per second) from 0.03s to 0.30s, shaped to follow the body envelope, with its level about -12 dB under the sub peak.

Fix the tail: add a low rumble (noise low-passed at ~150 Hz) decaying from 0.2s to 0.33s, with a small bump at ~0.22s of about -8 dB relative to the peak. Delete the stray click at 0.36s and the periodic 86 Hz pulses after 0.25s, or drop them below -50 dB.
Reduce the tonal quality: add a broadband 20-200 Hz noise component at about -6 dB relative to the sine, and detune or slow-modulate the 86 Hz peak so that it doesn't read as a tonal boom.
Shift the timing so the sound starts at ~0.01s (instead of 0.04s) and the body ends near 0.32s, leaving ~0.03s of trailing silence. Keep the peak at -3 dBFS and about -22.7 LUFS.

review.summary: B matches A's length, loudness, peak time and overall swell-and-fade envelope very closely, but it is built from a steady, more synthetic tone stack with static formant bands, lacking A's ragged noisy onset and rattling pulse tail. It is the right kind of sound, with a different texture and an off-pattern tail.

differences.a: Bright, noisy ragged breath blast in the first ~0.2 s (centroid ~1.4 kHz in the first quarter, energy up to 5-10 kHz) that darkens quickly; starts at about -16 dB.
differences.b: Starts quieter (-22 dB in the first tenth) with no distinct noisy blast. Spectrum is flat-bright from the start, with a small onset at 0.05 s and a slow build to the 0.54 s peak.

differences.a: Rough, guttural, vocal growl with irregular, organic modulation and broad harmonic smear. Flatness is ~0.001, but the spectrogram looks ragged and breathy.
differences.b: Reads as a synthetic stack of stationary harmonic bands (distinct lines near ~900 Hz, ~1.2 kHz, ~2.6 kHz and regular higher-harmonic striations). Flatness is 0.032, so it is noisier overall but more machine-like or buzzy than vocal.

differences.a: Strong 100-300 Hz body, formant band ~500-1500 Hz, very little above 2 kHz after the first 0.2 s; centroid ~954 Hz, rolloff85 ~1.4 kHz.
differences.b: Band energy is similar (low_mid 59% vs 61%), but a persistent 2.6 kHz band and lines up to 10 kHz plus bright content to ~1.8 s make it buzzier in the upper mids. Centroid stays ~1 kHz through the first half, and rolloff is slightly lower (1.2 kHz).

differences.a: Peak at 0.5 s, -20 dB at ~0.49 s after the peak, -40 dB at 1.37 s. The decline is gradual with a weak mid section.
differences.b: Peak at 0.54 s, -20 dB at 0.38 s, -40 dB at 1.25 s, so the fall is slightly faster. A step drop at ~0.9 s (about 10 dB, visible in the spectrogram) makes the second half feel like a different section.

differences.a: Rattling growl pulses at ~1.33 s and ~1.69 s as the voice sags; the second half is a weakening, wobbly growl.
differences.b: Onsets at 1.07, 1.15 and 1.86 s with a sudden block-like change at ~0.9 s and ~1.35 s. A bump near 1.5-1.8 s resembles a second pulse but is timed differently, with a clean stepped feel instead of a rattle.

differences.a: Falling or sagging growl: brightness and pitch sink over ~1.5 s, with formant movement.
differences.b: Largely static pitch bands, with only a slight downward centroid drift (1046 to 549 Hz). Little perceived pitch sag.

differences.a: Faint low rumble tail dying to silence at 2.18 s, with ~0.31 s near-silent end.
differences.b: Same trailing silence (0.31 s); the tail ends with a sharp vertical cutoff at ~1.9 s followed by a small dark blip to 2.0 s. Slightly more abrupt.

differences.a: -15.9 LUFS, peak -2.2 dBFS, crest 15.4 dB.
differences.b: -16.0 LUFS, peak -2.2 dBFS, crest 15.8 dB. Essentially matched.

differences.b: Mono, with a slight DC offset (-0.0018).

differences.b: 2.18 s one-shot; same total length and trailing silence.

change_notes: Add a 0-0.2 s breath/noise burst: band-passed noise 1.5-8 kHz, attack 10 ms, decay 150 ms, level about 6 dB above the body at the start, so the first tenth sits near -14 to -16 dB instead of -22.

Make the growl vocal and irregular: apply 25-40 Hz amplitude modulation with 30-50% depth plus random jitter (±5% pitch) on the 100-300 Hz fundamental; reduce distinct harmonic lines by adding 10-15% formant noise or detuned saw layers.

Add pitch sag: glide the fundamental from ~180 Hz at 0.3 s to ~90 Hz at 1.8 s (about -1 octave), and sweep the formant filter from ~1.2 kHz down to ~600 Hz so the centroid drops from ~1 kHz to ~450 Hz by the last quarter.

Replace the stepped drops with smooth curves: crossfade the 0.9 s and 1.35 s transitions over at least 150 ms and keep the -20 dB point at ~0.5 s (instead of 0.38 s) after the peak and -40 dB at ~1.37 s.
Move the late pulses to ~1.33 s and ~1.69 s as rattling bursts (30-60 ms, 150-600 Hz, about -8 dB below the body); remove the 1.07/1.15/1.86 s events.
Tame the 2.6 kHz band and the 5-10 kHz striations after 0.3 s by 10-15 dB with a gentle lowpass moving from 8 kHz at 0 s to 1.5 kHz by 1.0 s.
Fade the tail with a 150-250 ms exponential fade to avoid the cutoff at ~1.9 s, and high-pass at 20 Hz to remove the DC offset.
